Gina and Jon are friends who have chatted online since January 2023 about their careers, their love of dance, and the businesses they are building. Both lost their jobs that month: Jon was a banker, and Gina worked at DoorDash. Since then each has built a business while staying close to dance and supporting the other. Jon is building a dance studio, and Gina is building a clothing business. Their conversations are warm and encouraging, and they often close by promising to keep moving forward together.

On 20 January 2023, at about 4:04 pm, they caught up in person. Jon said he had lost his banking job on 19 January 2023 and planned to start a dance studio. He has loved dancing since childhood and sees it as both his passion and his escape. He wants to open the studio to teach others the joy dance brings him. He loves all dance styles but names contemporary as his favorite, calling it expressive and powerful. His dance crew took first place at a local competition in 2022, and he shared a photo of a man in a suit dancing from that event, saying he wants to bring that same intensity to others. He described his ideal studio as one by the water with an ocean view and yoga mats, and he shared a photo of a room like that.

Jon also described his routine. He rehearses after work with a small group of dancers who perform everything from contemporary to hip-hop. He was finishing choreography for a performance at a nearby festival in February 2023, and he shared a photo of dancers in white dresses on a stage, saying this group was the one performing. Gina asked whether he had time to rehearse while building the business and searching for a space. Jon said he hoped to find a place that would inspire them both.

Gina also lost her job at DoorDash in January 2023. Dance is her main stress relief, and she loves contemporary dance for being expressive and graceful. In the past she competed in several dance competitions and shows. Her favorite memory is her team winning first place at a regional competition when she was fifteen, performing a contemporary piece called "Finding Freedom," which she described as emotional and powerful. She shared a photo of a large open porch with a fireplace and a view of the water, and a photo of two people standing side by side.

Jon and Gina agreed to get together for a dance session. Jon invited Gina to see his moves "next Friday," and she said that worked. They also talked about taking a dance class together. The exact date of that Friday was never specified. The most likely date is 27 January 2023, but a later exchange on 29 January discusses the studio without mentioning that session, so whether it happened is unknown.

On 29 January 2023, at about 2:32 pm, they chatted online. Gina said things had been hectic because she had launched an ad campaign to grow her clothing store. She called starting her own store and taking risks both scary and rewarding, and she shared a photo of a store with clothes on display. Gina asked whether Jon had found the right spot for the studio. Jon said he was still searching but had found a place with great natural light, and that he had been to Paris "yesterday," which would be 28 January 2023. He shared a photo of a room with a blue floor and a pink wall, which he described as a bathroom. Gina said she had never visited Paris and had only been to Rome once.

Jon said the space he was considering is downtown, which makes it easy to reach, and that the natural light is a plus. He still needed to check its size and floor quality. He wants a good dance floor with enough bounce for himself and his students to dance safely. Gina said dance floors help prevent injuries and asked what flooring he liked. Jon said he wants Marley flooring, which is grippy but still lets dancers move, and is tough and easy to clean. Gina agreed that Marley sounded perfect. Jon described finding a space and preparing as a mix of exciting and nerve-wracking. Gina encouraged him to believe in himself, take breaks, and dance out stress. They agreed to keep chasing their goals, Gina saying good things were coming and Jon saying success was almost here.

On 1 February 2023, at about 12:48 am, they chatted again. Jon said his dance journey had been bumpy, but he was determined to make it work and was still searching for a studio location. Gina said she had emailed some wholesalers and one had replied yes that same day. She was thrilled because it meant she could expand her store and get closer to her customers. She shared a photo of a shopping mall with a glass entrance, which she presented as the store's new spot. Jon called it the perfect spot and shared a photo of a room with a mirror and a wooden floor.

Gina then shared a photo of a clothing store she had designed, full of clothes on display, and described it as cozy and inviting. She chose stylish but comfortable furniture and a chandelier for a glam feel, because she wants customers to feel they have found a cool oasis. Jon said he believed she could create the space she imagined. Gina said his support meant a lot. They agreed they would get through this together, and Gina told him hard work pays off eventually.

On 4 February 2023, at about 10:43 am, they chatted again. Gina said her store was doing great and called running it a wild ride. Jon said he was putting a lot of work into his business despite obstacles, and that some days did not go his way, but he was sure that if he kept pushing he would reach his dreams. Gina told him setbacks are opportunities for comebacks and promised her full support. Jon said searching for a studio location had been tricky, but he was determined to find the right spot.

Jon said he was rehearsing hard for an upcoming show because dancing brings him joy and fulfillment. He shared a photo of a woman in a gray dress doing a trick. He was also getting ready for a dance competition near him in March 2023, which he saw as a chance to show his skills and earn respect from the dance community. Gina wished him good luck, and Jon said he would not give up.

On 8 February 2023, at about 9:32 am, they chatted again. Gina shared a photo of a group of women posing with a giant balloon, saying she had found a cool new fashion piece for her store. Jon said he had already performed at the festival he had mentioned, that it was awesome, and that many people had complimented his moves. He shared a photo of a group of young girls in a dance studio. Gina asked what his favorite part of running his own studio was. Jon answered as though the studio were already running. He loves the freedom to create a space and help dancers of all ages and levels express themselves, and he finds it fulfilling to watch his students progress.

Gina said she had teamed up with a local artist for cool designs and shared a photo of a rack of clothes with a coat and a dress. She got the idea from a fashion magazine and wanted to give customers something different. Jon called her willing to take risks and said it was inspiring. Gina said taking risks is scary but is the only way to grow. Jon agreed and said taking risks had gotten him out of his secure 9-to-5 as a banker, and that the difficulties of his dance business have not been a walk in the park.

Jon shared a photo of a cartoon character with a quote about fear. Gina said the quote had kept her positive through tough times and had inspired a tattoo, which she showed in a photo of a woman on a balcony in a blue dress. She got the tattoo a few years earlier. It stands for freedom, meaning dancing without worrying what people think. Jon said dance gives him an escape to be himself, and he shared a photo of a woman in a tutu. Gina asked how he juggled dance and business goals. Jon said each passion gives him energy for the other: his dance moves pump him up for business goals, and business successes boost his drive on the dance floor. He called it a balancing act, but a fun one. Gina closed by saying they were there for each other.

On 16 March 2023, at about 2:35 pm, they chatted again in a new session. Jon said things had been hectic, and that he had started going to the gym the previous week to stay on track with his venture. Gina said she had been having tough times since losing her DoorDash job, but she had good news: her online clothing store was now open. She had been dreaming of this for a while and shared a photo of a computer screen showing a book and a pair of shoes. She wanted to blend her love of dance and fashion, which made the store a perfect match. Jon congratulated her and shared a photo of three young girls standing together with trophies.

Jon said losing his job had been hard, but he was living his dreams now, and that starting his business had brought new challenges at every turn. Gina said running her own business had had its ups and downs but had been an amazing ride. Jon said it had been a rollercoaster and that Gina's success inspired him. He said it helps that they both face the same challenges, like having a dance partner. Gina said they were on different paths, but it was nice to have someone rooting for them. Jon raised a toast to new heights and the trials that come with them, and shared a photo of two glasses of champagne.

On 23 March 2023, at about 7:28 pm, in what the record labels Session 7, they chatted again. Gina said her online store had been a roller coaster but rewarding, and she asked for tips on running a successful business. Jon advised her that brand identity is key, that she should build relationships with customers and let them know she cares, and that her positive energy would be contagious. Gina said building relationships and a strong brand image was something she was always working on.

Asked what keeps him motivated with his studio, Jon said seeing his students succeed does, and that her support means a lot to him. He shared a photo of a group of women doing a dance routine, which he described as a photo of the two of them from one of the dance classes, though the image shows only the women dancing. Gina said seeing his students grow must be fulfilling, and told him to keep going, never give up, and believe in himself. This session speaks of dance classes and students as current, but the memory does not confirm that a studio location was ever secured.

On 3 April 2023, at 1:26 pm, in Session 8, they chatted again. Jon said he had shut down his bank account. It was tough, but he felt he needed to do it for his business, and he believed it would help it grow. Gina said she had launched new offers and promotions on her online store to bring in customers, and that starting her business had been a wild ride, but she was not giving up. She said dance is her stress relief and fashion fuels her creativity, and she shared a photo of a man and woman doing a yoga pose, calling it a favorite dance session.

Gina said she could add dance-inspired items to her store, since she is passionate about both. Customers liked the new offers, and growing her customer base was the main focus. She was considering working with fashion bloggers and influencers over the next few months and planned to run more ads, with the goal of making her store a top destination for fashion fans.

Gina then asked what Jon had going for his studio. He said he was expanding its social media presence and offering workshops and classes to local schools and community centers. He was also hosting a dance competition the following month, which he described as a way to showcase local talent and draw attention to his studio. He asked whether Gina would come to the event and shared a photo of a stage with a projector screen. Gina said she would like to join in and show her support. Jon explained that his studio and other schools would bring their best moves to an evening of performances and judging, and he shared a photo of dancers on a stage. Gina said she was definitely in and shared a photo of a woman in a tutu. Jon said he could not wait to see her. They signed off with Gina telling him he had this and to believe in himself and keep pushing, and Jon saying he would not quit on his dreams.

On 9 April 2023, at about 10:33 am, in Session 9, they chatted again. Jon said he was turning his love of dance into a business and had put a great deal of time into the studio lately. His students were already doing well, and he was learning alongside them. He shared a photo of a group of dancers on a stage with a red background. Gina congratulated him and shared a photo of a display showing a dress and a flamingo. Jon said he was determined to make the studio work, and that losing his job, though tough, had given him the push he needed to do what he loves. Gina called tough times a gateway to awesome things and shared a photo of a red dress with gold accents on a mannequin.

Jon said that although it had been tough, he was living his true self. Dancing makes him happy, and sharing it with others brings him joy when he sees his students improve. He shared a photo of a woman doing a pole dance in a dance studio. Gina said he looked so happy when he danced. Jon said dance is his way of expressing himself and finding his happy place, and that he used to be scared of what people would think but learned that his own happiness matters most. He called the journey tough but also the best thing ever.

Gina recalled their dance classes and said she used to love spending time in the studio. She shared a photo of a group of young women in ballet attire and said it brought back many memories. Jon said he was glad dance held special meaning for both of them, and that he had loved taking lessons with his friends when he was younger. He thanked Gina for always being there for him. These references to shared classes suggest the two took lessons together in the past, though earlier sessions mention only a planned class.

Gina said she had his back and that dance helps people express themselves and find happiness. She shared a photo of a trophy with a glass globe on top and described it as one of her trophies from a dance contest. This is the same trophy photo Jon shared on 8 February 2023, so the record cannot confirm whose trophy it is. Jon said it looked awesome and thanked her for the support. Gina told him he had earned all the kudos for his hard work. Jon said he would keep pushing and would not let anything hold him back, and Gina said he was almost there.

As of the most recent session, Jon has been building a dance studio. He lost his banking job, has closed his bank account to focus on the business, and is expanding its social media presence, offering workshops to local schools and community centers, and planning a dance competition for the following month, which would be in May 2023. He has invited Gina, and she has said she will attend. As of April 2023 he speaks of teaching students and learning alongside them, but the memory never confirms that a permanent location was secured. The documented details about the space are the search itself, his preference for a downtown or ocean-view space with natural light, and his wish for Marley flooring. His dance crew took first place locally in 2022, he performed at a February 2023 festival, and he prepared for a March 2023 competition. He describes dance as his happy place and his way of being his true self.

Gina has been building her clothing business. She emailed wholesalers and secured a yes from one in February, designed a store with a cozy, glam feel, and launched an online store on 16 March 2023, with designs from a local artist. In April she was running promotions, planning collaborations with fashion bloggers and influencers, and expanding advertising. Her favorite dance memory remains her team's first-place regional win at age fifteen with "Finding Freedom," and her preferred style is contemporary. Her tattoo, which she got a few years before 2023, stands for freedom, meaning dancing without worrying what people think.

Both have repeatedly said they are there for each other, see their passions as mutually energizing, and describe their friendship as a kind of dance partnership. They have closed nearly every conversation with encouragement to keep pushing, believe in themselves, and never give up. The date of the dance session Jon proposed for "next Friday" in January is still not confirmed, and the record does not say whether the dance class they discussed ever took place.

This memory covers 19 conversations between Caroline and Melanie, who are friends and chat every few weeks, between 8 May 2023 and 22 October 2023. Caroline usually opens the conversations, and most of what follows concerns her life: her transition, her adoption plans, her career and her art. Melanie's life centers on her husband, her children, pets, pottery, painting, camping and running. Where a speaker says "last week" or "last Friday," the dates below are worked out from the session date.

Caroline is a trans woman who began transitioning about three years before May 2023, around 2020. She was born and grew up in Sweden, and she moved to her current city roughly four years before the May conversations. The friends she has known since that move are among her closest supports. In the first session, on 8 May 2023, she said she had gone to an LGBTQ support group the day before, on 7 May, and that hearing transgender people's stories had been powerful. The group made her feel accepted and gave her the courage to embrace herself. She said she planned to continue her education and look at career options, and that she was drawn to counseling or mental health work so she could support people facing similar struggles. Melanie encouraged her, saying her empathy would serve clients well. Melanie said she was swamped with work and her kids. She shared a painting of a lake sunrise she had made in 2022, and described painting as a way to express her feelings and relax after a long day.

In the second session, on 25 May 2023, Melanie reported that she had run a charity race for mental health the previous Saturday, around 20 May, and that it had made her think about caring for minds, including her own. She said that when she looks after herself, she can better look after her family. She described carving out daily me-time for running, reading and playing her violin. Caroline said she was researching adoption agencies, a long-held dream of giving a loving home to children who need one. She chose an agency partly because it helps LGBTQ+ people adopt, and she said that as a single parent she was up for the challenge. Melanie said her kids were excited for summer break and that the family was thinking about camping the next month.

By the third session, on 9 June 2023, Caroline had given a talk at her school the week before about her transgender journey and had encouraged students to get involved with the LGBTQ community. She said the event made her reflect on how far she had come since starting her transition. She described how the audience related to her story and became better allies. She also said that friends, family and mentors had been essential after a painful breakup, and she called them her rocks. She shared a photo from a meetup with friends the previous week. Melanie said her husband and kids keep her motivated, and she shared photos from their family outings. She revealed that she and her husband had been married five years, and she shared photos from their wedding day. Caroline congratulated her and wished her many happy years together.

In the fourth session, on 27 June 2023, Caroline showed a necklace with a cross and a heart, a gift from her grandmother in Sweden, who gave it to her when she was young. Caroline said it stood for love, faith and strength, and reminded her of her roots and her family's support. She also mentioned a hand-painted bowl that a friend had made for her eighteenth birthday ten years earlier. She told Melanie about an LGBTQ+ counseling workshop she had attended the previous Friday, around 23 June, where practitioners discussed therapeutic approaches for working with trans people. She said she was thinking of working specifically with trans people, helping them accept themselves and supporting their mental health. Melanie, meanwhile, had taken her family camping in the mountains the week before, around 20 June. They roasted marshmallows, went on a hike and enjoyed a wonderful view from the top. She said her two younger kids love nature.

Session five took place on 3 July 2023. Caroline said she had attended an LGBTQ+ pride parade the week before, which made her feel she belonged. The parade showed her how much the community had grown and made her want to use her story to help others, reinforcing her plan to pursue counseling and mental health work. She was also going to a transgender conference later that month. Caroline mentioned she was learning the piano. Melanie had signed up for a pottery class the day before, around 2 July. She called pottery like therapy, a way to express herself and get creative, and she shared a photo of a black and white flower bowl she had made in class.

Session six, on 6 July 2023, opened with Caroline saying she had been looking more deeply into counseling and mental health work, which she found tough but rewarding. Melanie had taken her kids to a museum the previous day, around 5 July, where they loved the dinosaur exhibit. Caroline said she was building a library for when she has children, with classics, stories from different cultures and educational books. Melanie named *Charlotte's Web* as a favorite from her childhood, saying it showed her how friendship and compassion can make a difference. Caroline said friends and family had been helping her with her transition, giving her love, guidance and acceptance, and that they had recently had a picnic together. Melanie then shared a photo of her family camping at the beach, a trip she said brought them closer.

On 12 July 2023, Caroline reported she had attended an LGBTQ conference two days earlier, on 10 July. She connected with people on similar journeys and felt totally accepted, and she said she wanted to help fight for trans rights and spread awareness. She said she was still looking into counseling and mental health jobs, and that she had struggled with mental health herself and had been helped by support, which made her want to help others. Melanie recommended a book she had read the previous year, one that reminded her to pursue her dreams. Caroline named *Becoming Nicole* by Amy Ellis Nutt as a favorite, a true story about a trans girl and her family that gave her hope for her own path. It taught her about self-acceptance and finding support. Melanie introduced her pets, a dog named Luna and a cat named Oliver, and mentioned she had just bought new pink running shoes. She said she had been running farther to de-stress and clear her mind. Caroline encouraged her to keep it up and stressed the importance of self-care.

Session eight, on 15 July 2023, covered a lot of ground. Melanie said she had taken her kids to a pottery workshop the previous Friday, around 7 July, where they all made their own pots, and she shared a photo of a cup with a dog face that one of her kids had made. The family had recently painted together, especially nature-inspired pictures, and she shared a painting of a sunset with a palm tree. Caroline said she had attended a council meeting for adoption the previous Friday, which was inspiring and emotional and made her even more determined to adopt. Melanie talked about flowers and their meaning, and she shared photos from her wedding, including a greenhouse ceremony. She said the best part was promising to be together forever. Caroline described a pride parade she had attended a few weeks before, where she felt accepted and celebrated. She said the best part of her journey had been realizing she could be herself without fear and having the courage to transition. Melanie said she was finding peace through creativity and family, and that her family had helped during a recent move. The two also discussed camping and hiking in the mountains and forests.

On 17 July 2023, Melanie said she had had a quiet weekend after camping with her family two weekends earlier. Caroline said she had joined a mentorship program for LGBTQ youth the previous weekend, around 15 July. She described mentoring a transgender teen on confidence and positive strategies. The two had attended a pride event together the previous month, in June. Caroline said the best part was watching her mentee's face light up at the support around them. Caroline also said she was planning an LGBTQ art show with her paintings the next month, in August, and shared a painting of a tree with a bright sun, inspired by a visit to an LGBTQ center. Melanie said she and her kids had just finished another painting like the last one.

On 20 July 2023, Caroline told Melanie she had joined a new LGBTQ activist group the previous Tuesday, 18 July. The group, "Connected LGBTQ Activists," holds regular meetings, plans events and campaigns, and supports its members. Caroline had missed her city's pride parade the weekend before, around 15 and 16 July, but found it a powerful reminder that the fight for equality continues. Melanie shared photos from a family beach trip, saying her family goes to the beach only once or twice a year. She described camping trips as the highlight of her summer, and she recalled a camping trip the previous year when the family saw the Perseid meteor shower, which she called a treasured memory. She also said her youngest child had recently taken her first steps, a moment that made her realize how fleeting life can be.

On 14 August 2023, Melanie said she had celebrated her daughter's birthday the night before with a concert by Matt Patterson, whose voice and songs she praised. Caroline said she had attended a pride parade the previous Friday, 11 August, full of energy and love, which reminded her to keep standing up for equality. Caroline described her art as an expression of her trans experience and a way of helping people understand the trans community. She showed a painting titled "Embracing Identity," about finding comfort and love in being yourself and the journey toward acceptance. Caroline said art had helped her explore her transition and her changing body, and that it taught her to accept the beauty of imperfection. Melanie told her that art can be healing and connective.

Session twelve, on 17 August 2023, opened with Caroline describing a hike where she had run into a group of religious conservatives who said something that really upset her. The experience made her realize how much work remains for LGBTQ rights, and she said supportive people around her helped. Melanie apologized and said strong support helps. She then shared a colorful pottery bowl she had just finished, saying painting helped her express her feelings. Caroline also recalled a Pride fest the two had attended together the year before. Melanie suggested a family outing for the summer, and Caroline proposed a trip just for the two of them to catch up and explore nature. They agreed to plan something special, though no plan was settled.

On 23 August 2023, Caroline said that she had taken the first step toward becoming a mom that week by applying to adoption agencies, after attending an adoption advice and assistance group. She described the decision as big, exciting and a little nerve-wracking. She introduced her pet, a guinea pig named Oscar. Melanie told her about their dog and cats, including a new cat named Bailey, and said Oliver had once hidden a bone in her slipper. Caroline shared that she used to go horseback riding with her dad as a child, and that she had always loved horses. Melanie shared a painting of a horse she had made on a wooden wall. Caroline said she had recently painted a self-portrait, a woman with a blue face, and that painting helped her feel liberated, empowered and true to herself. Melanie wished her the best on her adoption journey.

John and Maria are friends who reconnected in December 2022 after a long gap and have kept in touch across five chats, the most recent on 28 January 2023. Maria is generally the encourager, and John often thanks her for her support and tells her she is an awesome friend.

Their first conversation took place on 17 December 2022 at 11:01 am. John said that the day before, 16 December, he had returned from a family road trip that he had enjoyed. Maria said she had been busy volunteering at a homeless shelter and keeping fit, and that she had just started aerial yoga, which she loves. John said he does kickboxing, which gives him a lot of energy, and Maria called it a good way to stay in shape and de-stress. The conversation then turned to politics. John said his main goal is to get into local politics because he loves helping the community and making it better. His two main focuses are improving education and infrastructure. This interest came from growing up, when he saw how a lack of education and crumbling infrastructure affected his neighborhood. He does not want future generations to face the same problems, and he believes schools and infrastructure should be funded properly. He shared a photo of a group of men working on a building, which he described as a school from last year, taken after it received funding. He said the money paid for needed repairs and renovations, making the learning environment safer and more modern for students, and that he had been involved in that project. His next steps were to talk with local leaders and organizations, gather support, and collect ideas. Maria asked him to keep her posted on how the campaign went, and John agreed.

Deborah and Jolene first met in a chat on 23 January 2023 at 4:06 pm. Jolene said her week had been busy because she had just finished an electrical engineering project that took a lot of work. Deborah said that the previous week she had visited her mother's old house, a place full of memories. Her mother had passed away a few years before that session. Deborah shared a photo of herself and her mother, both in wheelchairs and hugging, which she described as their last photo together. Jolene said her own mother passed away in 2022 and shared a photo of her room in her mother's house, which has a bench and a window. Deborah said her mother's house also had a special bench by the window where her mother liked to sit every morning to take in the view. Deborah sometimes sits there herself because it helps her stay connected to her mother. Jolene agreed that staying connected is important and shared a photo of a heart-shaped pendant with a bird on it, which her mother gave her in Paris in 2010 and which reminds her of her mother. Deborah also has a pendant that reminds her of her mother. Jolene said her jewelry has a symbol representing freedom, a reminder to pursue her goals without being held back. Deborah said one of her goals is to keep teaching yoga and supporting her community, because she is passionate about helping people find peace and joy through it. Yoga helped her find peace during a rough time, and she now wants to share that with others. Jolene called this truly inspiring. Deborah then had to leave, and Jolene said she looked forward to the next chat.

In a second session on 27 January 2023 at 9:49 am, Deborah told Jolene that her dad had passed away two days earlier, around 25 January, and that his sudden death had left the whole family shell-shocked. She said she was channeling her grief into spending more time with family, cherishing memories, and living life fully. She shared a photo of a woman hugging another woman who sat on a couch. Jolene expressed sympathy and asked how the family was coping. Deborah said that looking back on good memories was comforting and that photos give her peace in hard times. She shared a photo of her parents' wedding in 1993, and Jolene called them a beautiful couple. Deborah said that she and her husband are trying to be as good a family as her parents were. Asked what she values in her relationship, Deborah said love and openness have kept the two of them close all these years, and that being there for each other has made them both happy. On 26 January she had received a handwritten letter from the members of her yoga group, who thanked her for the positive influence she had on them. She shared a photo of the note, and said such moments remind her why she is so passionate about yoga. Asked where she most often practices, she shared a photo of a living room with a television and a window, which is her old home, where she goes now and then for her mother. Sitting in the spot by the window gives her peace, and she can feel her mother's presence there. She shared a photo of that window seat. Her mother would sit there every night with a book and a smile, since reading was one of her hobbies and it was one of her favorite spots in the house. Deborah shared a photo of a view of the sky from an airplane window, and said that travel was also her mother's great passion.

Jolene then shared a photo of her pet snake Susie, saying snakes always calm her and make her happy. Deborah said pets brighten life and asked for a fun moment with a pet. Jolene described how her second snake, Seraphim, slinked out of her cage while she was playing video games and coiled up next to her, and shared a photo of Seraphim with a blanket and "sly eyes." She said she bought Seraphim a year earlier in Paris. Jolene then shared a photo of herself and her partner gaming the previous week, playing the game "Detroit" on a console, with a dog watching TV from the bed. Both are crazy about gaming. Deborah asked whether her partner taught her to play; Jolene said she learned on her own even as a child. Asked whether she plays old or new games, Jolene said she and her partner plan to play "The Walking Dead" next Saturday. The session ended with Deborah telling Jolene to keep spreading good vibes, and Jolene saying goodbye.

Session 1 (8 May 2023): Caroline and Melanie caught up. Caroline attended an LGBTQ support group on 7 May 2023, which she found very powerful. She was especially moved by the transgender stories and said the group made her feel accepted and gave her courage to embrace who she is. She shared a photo of a dog walking past a wall with a painting of a woman. Caroline plans to continue her education and explore career options, leaning toward counseling or mental health work so she can support people facing similar issues. Melanie encouraged her, saying her empathy would make her a great counselor. Melanie is busy with her kids and work. She paints as a creative outlet and a way to relax and express her feelings. She shared a photo of a sunset over a lake she painted last year, which is special to her. Caroline admired the colors. Caroline headed off to do research and Melanie went swimming with her kids.

Session 2 (25 May 2023): Melanie ran a charity race for mental health on Saturday 20 May 2023, which she found rewarding and thought-provoking. It made her think more about caring for our minds. She now sees self-care as important and a personal journey. She carves out daily me-time for running, reading, or playing her violin, which refreshes her and helps her stay present for her family. Her kids are excited for summer break, and her family was thinking about camping the next month (June 2023). Melanie asked Caroline about her summer plans.

Caroline is researching adoption agencies, a long-held dream to build a family and give a loving home to children who need one. She chose an agency because it helps LGBTQ+ people adopt, and she was drawn to its inclusivity and support. She shared a photo of the agency's sign. She knows it will be tough as a single parent but feels up for the challenge. She is grateful for support from friends and mentors and sees the hard work now as the step to making her dream real. Melanie is encouraging and sees Caroline as caring, kind, and someone who will be a wonderful mom.

Session 3 (9 June 2023): Caroline described a school event the week before (early June 2023) where she spoke about her transgender journey and encouraged students to get involved in the LGBTQ community. She said it was awesome, that the audience related to her and seemed inspired to be better allies, and that she felt powerful giving the talk. She reflected on how far she has come since she started transitioning three years ago (around 2020). She said conversations about gender identity and inclusion are necessary, and that she is thankful to give a voice to the trans community. She said she has been blessed with loads of love and support and wants to pass it on, and that she will keep using her voice to make change. Melanie strongly encouraged her, calling her brave and inspiring.

Caroline's support system: friends, family and mentors are her "rocks." She has known her closest friends for about 4 years, since she moved from her home country (Sweden, revealed in Session 4). They helped her especially after a tough breakup. She shared a photo of a family posing in a yard from when they met up the previous week. She asked Melanie who supports her.

Melanie's family: she is lucky to have her husband and kids, who keep her motivated. She shared a family photo of herself, her husband and a little girl in front of a waterfall. She has been married 5 years (since about 2018) and shared a wedding photo of herself in a wedding dress holding a bouquet. Caroline congratulated her and her husband. Melanie shared a photo of herself and her husband sitting on a blanket eating food, describing a fun day with games, good food, and hanging out together. She cherishes time with family because it's when she feels most alive and happy. Caroline agreed that family is everything.

Session 4 (27 June 2023): Caroline reconnected after a long gap ("Long time no talk") and said a lot had been going on in her life. She shared a photo of a necklace with a cross and a heart, a gift from her grandmother in Sweden (her home country) when Caroline was young. It stands for love, faith and strength and reminds her of her roots and her family's love. Caroline also treasures a hand-painted bowl that a friend made for her 18th birthday about ten years earlier (around 2013). It reflects art and self-expression. She shared a photo of a stack of patterned bowls. Melanie shared a photo of a stack of bowls with different designs.

Melanie took her family camping in the mountains the week before (around 19–23 June 2023). They explored nature, roasted marshmallows, and went on a hike with a great view from the top. The two younger kids love nature. Melanie said these moments together were special and that she will never forget them.

Caroline has been looking into counseling and mental health as a career, wanting to help people who have been through similar experiences to hers. She shared a photo of a bookshelf. She is still working out the details but is considering working with trans people, helping them accept themselves and supporting their mental health. On Friday 23 June 2023, she attended an LGBTQ+ counseling workshop covering therapeutic methods and how best to work with trans people. She was moved by how passionate the professionals were about creating a safe space for people like her. She said her own journey and the support she received, including counseling and support groups, improved her life and made her care more about mental health and self-understanding. She now wants to create a safe, inviting place for people to grow. Melanie praised her dedication, said she is making a big impact, and shared a photo of a book-filled bookshelf.

Session 5 (3 July 2023): Caroline said that last week (around 24–28 June 2023) she attended an LGBTQ+ pride parade. Everyone was happy, it made her feel like she belonged, and it showed her how much the community has grown. It motivated her to use her own story to help others. She is still set on counseling and mental health as the path, and she is excited to give back. Melanie congratulated her.

Melanie said she signed up for a pottery class on 2 July 2023 ("yesterday" relative to the session). She described pottery as like therapy, a way to express herself and get creative, and said making it is calming. She shared a photo captioned as a person holding a frisbee, which seems to be a mislabel, and then a photo of a bowl with a black and white flower design that she made in her class. She said it took work but she is proud of it. She said pottery is a huge part of her life, helps her express her emotions, and brings her a lot of joy. She said she is excited to see where pottery takes her.

Caroline said she is learning the piano as her own creative outlet. She is going to a transgender conference in July 2023, which she is excited about because she wants to meet others in the community and learn more about advocacy. She said she would keep Melanie posted.

Current state (as of 3 July 2023): Caroline is pursuing further education and a counseling/mental health career focused on working with trans people. She attended an LGBTQ+ counseling workshop on 23 June 2023 and an LGBTQ+ pride parade in late June 2023. She is learning piano and has a transgender conference coming up in July 2023. She is still researching LGBTQ+-inclusive adoption agencies toward building a family as a single parent, and she is public about her transgender journey through speaking engagements. Her close friends, family and mentors remain her main support. Melanie is balancing work and a busy family life with her husband and kids. She practices daily self-care (running, reading, violin), ran a mental health charity race on 20 May 2023, took her family camping in the mountains around 19–23 June 2023, and started a pottery class on 2 July 2023.

Calvin and Dave are friendly acquaintances who have talked three times so far, on 23 March, 26 March, and 20 April 2023. Their first recorded conversation was on 23 March 2023 at 11:53 am, though Calvin's opening line ("How's it going since we talked?") suggests they had spoken before. In that session, Dave described recently attending a classic car event, which he called a car lover's paradise, where he admired many classic cars and talked with their owners about their stories. Calvin said he had just gone through a big life change and shared a photo of a building with a sign on the front, which he called his new mansion. He tied the change to excitement about learning Japanese culture and expanding himself. Calvin has never been to Japan but is fascinated by its traditions and eager to taste the culture. He planned to leave for Japan in April 2023, and his agent had found him a place to stay there. He shared a photo of a cozy living room with a couch, a table, and a television. His Japan plans included exploring the city, trying local cuisines, and perhaps collaborating with local musicians. He expected to stay a few months and then travel on to Boston. Dave has been spending a lot of time at a beautiful, calming park with a lake and a few boats, and he shared a photo of it. Calvin has never been there but said he would check it out when he is back. Dave offered further trip recommendations, and Calvin said he would ask for help if needed. Nothing in that session gave a specific return date or the exact nature of Calvin's life change beyond the move and the mansion photo.

In the second session, on 26 March 2023 at 4:45 pm, Calvin opened by saying it had been a few days since they last talked and that he had news. He had just gotten a new luxury car, which was a dream come true. He called it a rockstar ride, super smooth and powerful, and said each time he steps in it feels like an adrenaline rush. He shared a photo of a red sports car parked on the side of the road, taken on 25 March when he first took it for a ride. He said he felt he deserved it after a lot of hard work and was on cloud nine. Dave asked whether it was his first one, but Calvin's replies implied it was his first luxury car, though this was not explicitly confirmed. Dave shared that the previous weekend (around 18 to 19 March 2023) he went to a music festival in Boston, which he enjoyed. He said there were many cool bands, the atmosphere was electric, and it reminded him why he loves music. He shared a photo of a large crowd at a concert. His favorite act was Aerosmith, whose performance he found incredible. It was the first time he saw them live. He shared two photos from their set: one showing a concert stage with a large eagle, and another of two people on stage with guitars and a microphone. He said the lead singer was jamming to one of their hits. Dave did not get to hang out with the band after the show, but said seeing them live was enough. Calvin said he had written new tunes and had studio sessions the previous week, and he was excited to collaborate and share the music. Dave said he looked forward to hearing the new songs and asked Calvin to keep him updated on the collaborations. Calvin agreed. The session ended with both wishing each other well, Dave telling Calvin to stay safe and enjoy the collaborations, and Calvin saying goodbye.

The third session took place at 4:15 pm on 20 April 2023, and Calvin opened with "Long time no see," about three and a half weeks after the last session. He said he had just been to an awesome music event in Tokyo. When Dave asked whether he had seen any bands, Calvin said he did not see any bands there but met many talented artists and industry people, which he found enriching. He said he learned a lot and got good advice from music professionals. A producer told him to stay true to himself and sound unique, which got him thinking about where he wants his music to go. Calvin said he dreams of touring the world, performing for different people and connecting with them, and hopes his music can reach a global audience and make an impact. He said he is looking forward to an upcoming trip to Boston after he finishes the Frank Ocean tour, and that he has heard the Boston music scene is awesome. Dave offered to show him around town and all the cool spots, naming Paradise Rock, House of Blues, and Fenway Park as places with a great music scene. Dave said he would be in the front row when Calvin performs. Dave shared a photo of a city skyline with a boat in the water. Calvin said Boston looked great and thanked him for the tips. Dave said that last weekend (around 15 to 16 April 2023) he went to a car show. He said classic cars are charming, that the dedication people put into restoring them is amazing, and that this is why he is so into auto engineering. He said he could not wait to show Calvin some classic cars in Boston. He then shared a photo of a green Mustang parked in a field of grass. Calvin replied that the car looked great and shared a photo of a red sports car on display at a show, saying he had put a lot of work into it. Dave asked whether Calvin had had a chance to explore Boston beyond the gigs. Calvin said he had not yet, because he had been busy with rehearsals and travel, but he looked forward to exploring the city, trying good food, and visiting popular attractions. He suggested grabbing a bite together when he is there, and Dave agreed to show him his favorite spots. The session ended with both looking forward to the visit, Dave saying he could not wait to show Calvin the music and food in Boston, and "See you soon!"

Calvin's stated interests across the sessions are Japanese culture, music (he writes songs, does studio work, hoped to work with local musicians in Japan, and now dreams of touring internationally), and luxury cars. By 20 April he was in Tokyo, and he has not yet confirmed a return date or the exact arrival date for Boston, though the trip is planned to follow the Frank Ocean tour. Dave's interests include classic cars and auto engineering, live music (especially Aerosmith), and the calming park with a lake. Dave has also become a host-like figure for the Boston visit, offering to show Calvin around, recommend venues, and attend his performances. Calvin and Dave have agreed to keep each other updated. Dave asked for updates on Calvin's collaborations, and Calvin promised to share his new music. Nothing in these sessions confirms the specific nature of Calvin's life change beyond the move and the mansion photo, or whether the red sports car shown on 26 March is the same one he later displayed at the show.

Gina and Jon are friends who have chatted online since January 2023 about their careers, their love of dance, and the businesses they are building. Both lost their jobs that month: Jon was a banker, and Gina worked at DoorDash. Since then each has built a business while staying close to dance and supporting the other. Jon is building a dance studio, and Gina is building a clothing business. Their conversations are warm and encouraging, and they usually close by promising to keep moving forward together. The record runs through ten sessions, the most recent on 25 April 2023.

The first conversation took place in person on 20 January 2023, at about 4:04 pm. Jon said he had lost his banking job the day before, on 19 January, and planned to start a dance studio. He has loved dancing since childhood and sees it as both his passion and his escape. He wants to open the studio to teach others the joy dance brings him. He loves all dance styles but names contemporary as his favorite, calling it expressive and powerful. His dance crew took first place at a local competition in 2022, and he shared a photo of a man in a suit dancing from that event, saying he wants to bring that same intensity to others. He described his ideal studio as one by the water with an ocean view and yoga mats, and he shared a photo of a room like that. He also rehearses after work with a small group of dancers who perform everything from contemporary to hip-hop. He was finishing choreography for a February 2023 festival performance, and he shared a photo of dancers in white dresses on a stage, saying this was the group performing. He hoped to find a space that would inspire them both.

Gina also lost her job at DoorDash in January 2023. Dance is her main stress relief, and she loves contemporary dance for being expressive and graceful. In the past she competed in several dance competitions and shows. Her favorite memory is her team winning first place at a regional competition when she was fifteen, performing a contemporary piece called "Finding Freedom," which she described as emotional and powerful. She shared a photo of a large open porch with a fireplace and a view of the water, and a photo of two people standing side by side.

Jon and Gina agreed to get together for a dance session. Jon invited Gina to see his moves "next Friday," and she said that worked. They also talked about taking a dance class together. The exact date of that Friday was never specified. The most likely date is 27 January 2023, but a later exchange on 29 January discusses the studio without mentioning any session, so whether it happened is unknown. The record also never confirms whether the dance class they discussed ever took place.

On 29 January 2023, at about 2:32 pm, they chatted online. Gina said things had been hectic because she had launched an ad campaign to grow her clothing store. She called starting her own store and taking risks both scary and rewarding, and she shared a photo of a store with clothes on display. She asked whether Jon had found the right spot for the studio. He shared a photo of a room with a blue floor and a pink wall, which he described as a bathroom. Gina said she had never visited Paris and had only been to Rome once. He wants a good dance floor with enough bounce for himself and his students to dance safely, and he prefers Marley flooring, which is grippy but still lets dancers move, and is tough and easy to clean. Gina agreed that Marley sounded perfect. Jon described finding a space and preparing as a mix of exciting and nerve-wracking. Gina encouraged him to believe in himself, take breaks, and dance out stress, and they agreed to keep chasing their goals.

On 1 February 2023, at about 12:48 am, they chatted again. Jon said his dance journey had been bumpy, but he was determined to make it work and was still searching for a studio location. Gina said she had emailed some wholesalers and one had replied yes that same day. She was thrilled because it meant she could expand her store and get closer to her customers. She shared a photo of a shopping mall with a glass entrance, which she presented as the store's new spot. Jon called it the perfect spot and shared a photo of a room with a mirror and a wooden floor. Gina then shared a photo of a clothing store she had designed, full of clothes on display, and described it as cozy and inviting. She chose stylish but comfortable furniture and a chandelier for a glam feel, because she wants customers to feel they have found a cool oasis. Jon said he believed she could create the space she imagined, and they agreed they would get through this together.

On 4 February 2023, at about 10:43 am, they chatted again. Gina said her store was doing great and called running it a wild ride. Jon said he was putting a lot of work into his business despite obstacles, and that some days did not go his way, but he was sure that if he kept pushing he would reach his dreams. Deborah and Jolene are two people who chat with each other across several sessions. Their first conversation took place on 23 January 2023 at 4:06 pm. Jolene said her week had been busy because she had just finished an electrical engineering project that took a lot of work. Deborah said that the previous week she had visited her mother's old house, a place full of memories. Her mother had passed away a few years before that session. Deborah shared a photo of herself and her mother, both in wheelchairs and hugging, which she described as their last photo together. Jolene said her own mother passed away in 2022 and shared a photo of her room in her mother's house, which has a bench and a window. Deborah said her mother's house also had a special bench by the window where her mother liked to sit every morning to take in the view. Deborah sometimes sits there herself because it helps her stay connected to her mother. Jolene agreed that staying connected is important and shared a photo of a heart-shaped pendant with a bird on it, which her mother gave her in Paris in 2010 and which reminds her of her mother. Deborah also has a pendant that reminds her of her mother. Jolene said her jewelry has a symbol representing freedom, a reminder to pursue her goals without being held back. Deborah said one of her goals is to keep teaching yoga and supporting her community, because she is passionate about helping people find peace and joy through it. Yoga helped her find peace during a rough time, and she now wants to share that with others. Jolene called this truly inspiring. Deborah then had to leave, and Jolene said she looked forward to the next chat.

In a second session on 27 January 2023 at 9:49 am, Deborah told Jolene that her dad had passed away two days earlier, around 25 January, and that his sudden death had left the whole family shell-shocked. On 26 January she had received a handwritten letter from the members of her yoga group, who thanked her for the positive influence she had on them. She shared a photo of the note, and said such moments remind her why she is so passionate about yoga. Asked where she most often practices, she shared a photo of a living room with a television and a window, which is her old home, where she goes now and then for her mother. Sitting in the spot by the window gives her peace, and she can feel her mother's presence there. She shared a photo of that window seat. Her mother would sit there every night with a book and a smile, since reading was one of her hobbies and it was one of her favorite spots in the house. Deborah shared a photo of a view of the sky from an airplane window, and said that travel was also her mother's great passion.

Later in that same session, Jolene shared a photo of her pet snake Susie, saying snakes always calm her and make her happy. Deborah said pets brighten life and asked for a fun moment with a pet. She said she bought Seraphim a year earlier in Paris. Jolene then shared a photo of herself and her partner gaming the previous week, playing the game "Detroit" on a console, with a dog watching TV from the bed. Both are crazy about gaming. Deborah asked whether her partner taught her to play; Jolene said she learned on her own even as a child. Asked whether she plays old or new games, Jolene said she and her partner plan to play "The Walking Dead" next Saturday. The session ended with Deborah telling Jolene to keep spreading good vibes, and Jolene saying goodbye.

John and Maria are friends who reconnected in December 2022 after a long gap. They have had six conversations, the most recent on 5 February 2023 at 2:33 pm. Their talks center on John's goal of getting into local politics, with education and infrastructure as his two main focuses, along with the volunteer work, fitness, and family life both describe. Maria is usually the encourager, and John often thanks her and calls her an awesome friend. By February 2023, John also described a food drive for unemployed neighbors and a desire to serve his country.

The first conversation took place on 17 December 2022 at 11:01 am. John said he had returned from a family road trip on 16 December and had enjoyed it. Maria said she had been volunteering at a homeless shelter and keeping fit, and that she had just started aerial yoga, which she loves. John said he does kickboxing, which gives him energy, and Maria called it a good way to stay in shape and de-stress. The conversation then turned to politics. John said his main goal is to enter local politics because he loves helping the community. His two focuses are improving education and infrastructure. This interest grew out of his childhood, when he saw how a lack of education and crumbling infrastructure affected his neighborhood. He does not want future generations to face the same problems, and he believes schools and infrastructure should be funded properly. He shared a photo of men working on a building, which he described as a school from last year that received funding for repairs and renovations, and said he had been involved in that project. His next steps were to talk with local leaders and organizations, gather support, and collect ideas. Maria asked him to keep her posted, and John agreed.

The second conversation took place on 22 December 2022 at 6:10 pm. Maria said she had donated her old car to the homeless shelter on 21 December and asked how the campaign was going. John said it had been an interesting ride and that he had been networking to get people's input. He had recently talked with someone whose stories fired up his passion for improving education in their area. He said investing in future generations is key, because they need the right tools to succeed. Maria encouraged him throughout, telling him she believed in his power to make a positive difference, that his passion inspired her, and that she was there for him. John said her help made him more determined.

The conversation then turned to family and friends. John shared a photo of a family picnic and said his family is the reason he never gives up. Their love gives him strength, keeps him centered, and reminds him why he is passionate about making a positive impact. He called them his rock in tough times. He also shared photos of his family at a playground, at the dinner table, and with homemade pizzas and salads, saying they love playing together and that good food and conversation keep them close. Maria said her family is small, but she loves spending time with her friends, who often watch movies, hike, and join her for game nights. She said quality connections matter most to her, and she mentioned that she had recently made peach cobbler. Both agreed that making memories with loved ones matters. John ended by saying he was off to do taekwondo, which he practices alongside kickboxing.

The third conversation took place on 1 January 2023 at 8:30 pm. John said he had joined a service-focused online group the previous week and found it emotional. Its members' stories opened his eyes to new perspectives and gave him a sense of connection and purpose. Maria called it great to see him finding a supportive community. John said the group shares stories, advice, and encouragement. When Maria asked whether he had met any members in person, he shared a photo of a Santa-themed poster and said the group had held in-person events, including handing out food and supplies at a homeless shelter, and a toy drive for kids in need. Seeing people's smiles showed them they had made a real difference. The group was brainstorming ways to help underserved communities access education, mentorship, job training, and resume building. Maria said empowering people through education and mentorship is crucial. John thanked her for her support and then revealed that he had recently failed a military aptitude test, which left him stressed. Maria said she was there for him and had his back. Maria then shared a photo of a sunset over the ocean, which she had taken at the beach in December 2022. She said nature's beauty reminds her to slow down and enjoy small things. John said it reminded him of the film camera he had as a kid, and he closed by saying nature helps people remember small joys when life gets busy.

The fourth conversation took place on 9 January 2023 at 7:06 pm. Maria said she had become friends with a fellow volunteer, and they both love helping others. John said he had been busy with work and family, but the previous week he had an unexpected incident on his way home that left his car's windshield broken. Maria expressed concern and was glad he was all right. John shared a photo of a tattoo with a quote that reminds him to stay strong in tough times. He said he handled the incident by staying calm and asking for assistance, and afterward he felt relieved and grateful. Maria encouraged him to appreciate what he has. Asked how he calms down, John said he likes to watch the sunset, which reminds him to enjoy small things.

Maria then asked about his political goals. John said he had been looking into local politics, talking to community leaders, and learning about his neighborhood's needs and hopes. He found it informative and said he felt optimistic. Maria praised his dedication and said she had been taking notes on local politics in her notebook. John said her help had given him new ideas. His next step was a community meeting the following week to discuss education and infrastructure upgrades. Maria wished him luck and hoped his concerns would be heard. John said he would stick up for the community, and Maria called his speaking out admirable. John shared a photo of people working around a table with a laptop and a photo of two people shaking hands, saying they could achieve great things by joining forces. Maria agreed that uniting is essential and said they could bring positive changes to the neighborhood as a team. John thanked her for being an awesome friend, and both agreed they made a great team.

The fifth conversation, Session 5, took place on 28 January 2023 at 1:17 pm. John said he had attended the community meeting. He found it interesting to hear everyone's worries, and it made him realize how crucial the upgrades are, especially for children. He said he was upset by the state of education and asked Maria how she thought things could be improved. Maria said they should fight for more money and resources for schools and raise awareness of why education matters for everyone. John said education is essential for a successful society and that it breaks his heart that children do not have what they need. Maria said it is not right that some kids get everything they need while others have nothing. In this part of the conversation John said, "My kids have so much and others don't." It is not entirely clear whether he meant his own children or children in general, and earlier chats refer to his family only in broad terms. Both agreed they needed to do something about it.

Maria then said that the previous week she had volunteered at a shelter during an event for kids and shared a photo of volunteers in green aprons. She said her aunt had believed in volunteering and had helped her family when they were struggling, which inspired her to help too. She said it makes her happy to brighten someone's day. John asked which moment had stood out most. Maria described a sad little girl of about eight sitting alone. She sat with her, and the girl told her she had no other family, which broke Maria's heart. Maria gave her comfort and a listening ear, and they ended up laughing together. John called it a touching moment. He shared a photo of a little girl kissing a doll, saying it reminded him of a doll he had as a child that always made him feel better, and that it reminds him to look out for others who are feeling down. Maria said spreading kindness can make a real difference, and John agreed that you never know the difference a kind gesture can make.

The sixth conversation took place on 5 February 2023 at 2:33 pm, after about a week's gap. Maria said that on Friday, 3 February, she had challenged herself by doing a charity event, and she felt the power of collective effort to help people in need. Serving meals and seeing people's gratitude was heartwarming. She asked John what had made him get into politics. He answered that he feels a strong urge to serve his country and community, and that running for office was his chance to make an impact. This framing differs somewhat from his earlier explanation, which centered on education, infrastructure, and the struggles he saw in his neighborhood. Maria said that at the event she had talked with a man named David, whose story of hardship humbled her. She said she linked him afterward with a nearby organization offering housing and support for homeless individuals. John said it was important to help people find what they need and asked whether she had ever needed help herself. Maria said that when she was younger, her family had money problems and relied on outside help from her aunt, which taught her the importance of helping others who struggle.

John then said he had just started helping with a community food drive for people who had lost their jobs. He said seeing the effect of unemployment on his neighbors had made him decide to act, and that unemployment in the community was the reason he started the initiative. He shared several photos of the effort and said the group had been overwhelmed by the response from volunteers. Maria praised his efforts and offered to help with networking or at future events, and John said her help would be appreciated. Maria said that whenever he needed help he should let her know. John said her support meant a lot and thanked her for always being there. Maria said he was a great friend and that she would always be there for him. John closed by saying friendship meant a lot to him and that they could work toward a shared goal together.

Several things are worth keeping in mind. Maria is consistently supportive, offering help with his campaign and sharing her own experiences with volunteering, her aunt's help during hard times, and her recent charity event. John's stated goal has been local politics focused on education and infrastructure, but by February 2023 he also describes a food drive for unemployed neighbors and a desire to serve his country. He mentioned failing a military aptitude test in January, but later conversations do not connect that to his plans. Some photo descriptions do not match the surrounding text, such as the David photo and the Thanksgiving-themed flyer, so captions should be read with caution. Facts about John's children are also unclear, especially the "My kids have so much" remark. Future conversations are likely to continue around John's community work and political plans, Maria's volunteering, and their shared emphasis on family, friendship, and making a difference.

Sam and Evan are longtime acquaintances who have been catching up across nine sessions in 2023, from 18 May through 27 August. Sam's health and habits have been the main thread since May, and Evan has repeatedly offered encouragement, practical tips, and his own health story as a model. Evan's personal life became a major topic by August, when he began describing a new relationship with a Canadian woman whom he calls his "SO." His family's news, especially his son's soccer injury, came up in mid-August. His painting classes and winter sports came up on 19 August, and on 27 August he reported a twisted knee. Evan's photos often do not match his descriptions, and several of his accounts shift from one session to the next. Those discrepancies are noted where they matter.

The first session took place in person on 18 May 2023 at 1:47 pm, after a long gap in contact. Evan had recently bought a new Prius, after his old car broke down, was repaired, and was then sold. Shortly before the meeting he had returned from a family trip to the Rockies, where they hiked the trails during the week before 18 May. He shared a photo of a lake with rocks and mountains behind it. Evan said he had painted in watercolor for a few years, after a friend introduced him to the medium and gave him early advice, and he described painting as a great stress-buster. He shared a photo of his watercolor of a desert cactus.

Sam said they loved hiking but had not gone in ages. Their most special hike was with their dad when Sam was ten, covering a good distance, which Sam still treasures. Sam shared a photo of a man and a child walking through a forest, presumably the two of them. Sam had no hobbies yet but was considering painting, and shared a photo of a paint set in a store. Neither had tried painting, though both were keen. Evan encouraged Sam to keep trying new things until one sparked excitement, and said he was "super pumped" for them. They agreed to catch up again soon, and Sam promised to keep Evan posted on new hobbies. No date for the next meeting was set.

The second session took place by text on 24 May 2023 at 7:11 pm. Evan said that on the weekend of about 20 and 21 May he had taken his family on a road trip to Jasper, Alberta, driving the Icefields Parkway and seeing glaciers and lakes. He shared a photo that he said showed a glacier, but it actually shows a person holding a book in front of a lake, with no glacier visible. Sam said they had never been to Jasper and that it looked breathtaking.

Sam then said their week had been tough. A few days earlier, a check-up with their doctor had shown their weight was not where it should be, which Sam called pretty eye-opening. Evan said it is never too late to make positive changes. When Sam asked for tips on breaking old habits, Evan recommended finding a fitness routine one truly enjoys and making small, smarter dietary choices, which add up. Sam said they had been looking for a hobby to stay motivated and asked whether painting would help them de-stress. Evan said yes, painting relieves stress and builds creativity, but it would not solve Sam's weight problem, so exercise was also needed. Sam said they would try painting and report back, and Evan told them not to put too much pressure on themselves. Sam has not yet reported back on painting.

The third session took place by text on 6 June 2023 at 3:55 pm. Evan said life had been a rollercoaster. The previous week he had a sudden heart palpitation episode, a serious wake-up call about his lifestyle. He shared a photo of a person holding a bottle of medicine. Sam said they were glad Evan was feeling better and that they were trying to eat healthier. Evan said he was being extra careful, trying to eat less processed food and fewer sugary snacks, though he admitted he loved ginger snaps. He asked whether Sam had made diet changes. Sam said no, though they still enjoyed soda and candy and knew it was not the best habit.

Evan said small changes can have a big impact later and suggested swapping soda for flavored seltzer water and candy for dark chocolate with high cocoa content. Sam agreed to try. Evan shared a photo of a bearded man holding a dumbbell and said exercise clears the mind. Sam asked for help getting started, and Evan offered to get together and show Sam some basic exercises. No date for that get-together has ever been set. Sam then described a frustrating supermarket trip, where the self-checkout machines were all broken, and Evan said he was sorry. Sam said take care and ended the chat.

The fourth session took place by text on 27 July 2023 at 10:52 am. Sam said friends had mocked Sam's weight the previous Friday, which hurt and made Sam realize they needed to change. Evan apologized, said progress takes time, and offered to work on it together. Evan said he had struggled with his own health a few years earlier but had stuck with it. He shared a photo he described as his gym membership card, though it shows a set of five cards reading "let it shine." He said diet and lifestyle changes also matter.

When Sam asked what had made the biggest difference for him, Evan said cutting sugary snacks and eating more vegetables and fruit had helped a lot, and he shared a photo of a table full of fresh produce. Sam said they were reducing soda and candy and were determined, though it was tough. Evan recommended flavored seltzer as an alternative to soda and mentioned a mystery novel he could not stop thinking about. Sam asked for low-calorie snack ideas and the novel's title. Evan suggested seltzer with air-popped popcorn or fruit. He said the novel was *The Great Gatsby*, though he had earlier called it a mystery, and his photo showed fruit and a bottle of alcohol rather than a book. Sam said they would read it sometime and that they wanted to focus on progress, not perfection.

Evan asked whether Sam had thought about exercise, which he said was just as important as eating right. Sam said that starting the next day, 28 July, they would go to the gym and exercise regularly. Evan told Sam to keep going and have fun, and Sam thanked him several times. Sam has not mentioned painting since the second session, and it is unclear whether they ever started. Whether the gym routine began on 28 July has never been confirmed.

The fifth session took place by text on 7 August 2023 at 7:52 pm. Evan said that the previous week he had traveled to Canada and met an awesome Canadian woman, which he described as something out of a movie. He said being with her made him feel alive. He shared a photo of a couple holding hands in the snow. Sam congratulated him and said they were sorry he had been dealing with health issues, which can make it hard to enjoy things. Evan said the relationship was a welcome change and that his health struggles had made him appreciate good moments more. He shared a photo of a woman and a child on a swing set, and Sam said his kids seemed to be having a great time.
