Calvin and Dave are friendly acquaintances with eight recorded conversations: on 23 March, 26 March, and 20 April 2023, then 1 May, 3 May, 16 May, 31 May, and 9 June 2023. Their exchanges are warm and encouraging, and they have repeatedly talked about meeting in Boston, where Calvin is expected to perform and Dave has offered to show him around.

The first conversation took place at 11:53 am on 23 March 2023, though Calvin's opening line, "How's it going since we talked?", suggests they had spoken before. Dave described a classic car event he called a car lover's paradise and a calming park with a lake and boats where he had been spending time. Calvin said he had just gone through a big life change and shared a photo of a building he jokingly called his new mansion. The change was never explained beyond a planned move to Japan in April 2023, where his agent had found him a place to stay. He hoped to explore the city, try local cuisines, perhaps collaborate with local musicians, and then travel on to Boston. No return date was given. He had never visited the park Dave described but said he would check it out when he was back.

The second session took place at 4:45 pm on 26 March 2023. Calvin announced a new red sports car he first drove on 25 March, calling it a dream come true and a rockstar ride after hard work. His replies implied it was his first luxury car, but this was never explicitly confirmed. Dave said he had attended a music festival in Boston around 18 to 19 March, where seeing Aerosmith live for the first time was incredible, and he shared two performance photos. Calvin said he had written new tunes and had studio sessions the previous week, and he agreed to share the songs. Dave asked to hear them and to be kept updated.

The third session took place at 4:15 pm on 20 April 2023. Calvin opened with "Long time no see" and said he had just been to an awesome music event in Tokyo. He had not performed there but had met talented artists and industry people, and a producer told him to stay true to himself and sound unique. Calvin dreams of touring the world and reaching a global audience, and he was looking forward to Boston after finishing the Frank Ocean tour. Dave offered to show him around, recommended Paradise Rock, House of Blues, and Fenway Park, and promised to be in the front row at his performance. Dave also described a car show from around 15 to 16 April. Calvin replied with a photo of a red sports car on display, saying he had put a lot of work into it. He had not yet explored Boston because of rehearsals and travel, and he suggested a meal together when he arrived. The session closed with "See you soon!"

The fourth session took place at 6:24 pm on 1 May 2023. Dave opened with "long time no see" and announced that he had finally opened his own car maintenance shop, a dream come true. He shared a photo of a car dealership, and Calvin praised his guts and ambition. Dave said the shop was a step toward classic car work, which he loves, and that he had restored one the previous year. He works on everything from routine maintenance to full classic restorations. He invited Calvin to visit the shop, and Calvin said he would love to. Calvin then shared a gold necklace with a diamond pendant, given to him by another artist, which reminds him why he keeps hustling as a musician. Nothing indicates when he received it.

The fifth session took place at 1:16 pm on 3 May 2023. Dave opened with "Long time no talk," although only two days had passed. He said he was teaming up with a local garage and shared a photo of himself working on a car engine, which sits awkwardly with his earlier account of running his own shop. He hoped to keep learning about auto engineering and someday build a custom car from scratch. Calvin said long drives in "[this car]," an unfilled placeholder, help him clear his head, and he shared a photo of a red sports car on a road. He said he had been loving getting to know Japanese culture, suggesting he was still in Japan, though this was not stated. He said his creativity was frozen, and Dave suggested immersing himself in things he loves and taking a break from music. Calvin said the break was helping him get his mojo back.

The sixth session took place at 11:50 am on 16 May 2023. Calvin opened with "Long time no chat!" and reported that about a week earlier his place had been flooded. He saved his music gear and favorite microphone and was waiting for insurance before repairs could begin. He shared a photo of his music studio with a keyboard, a synthesizer, and other equipment. Dave expressed sympathy and offered help. He then said he had opened his car shop "last week" and celebrated with friends, which conflicts with the 1 May session. Calvin said he had an upcoming Tokyo performance later that month, hoping to reach a new audience. Dave asked to be told how it went and said he wanted to visit Tokyo soon. Neither session specifies the performance date or venue.

The seventh session took place at 6:06 pm on 31 May 2023. Calvin said touring with Frank Ocean the previous week had been wild and that Tokyo was unreal, with an insane crowd. Dave shared a photo of a man working on a car engine, saying it was his neighbor's car, which he had fixed himself. Calvin asked whether it was the car Dave had been fixing for a friend, and Dave did not clearly answer. Both agreed that working on cars is calming, and Dave said fixing things gives him purpose and a sense of achievement. Calvin said performing fuels his soul and that he was buzzing to perform in Boston for folks from home. Dave called the Boston music scene awesome and promised to cheer him on. Calvin said he would fill Dave in on the details when he got back. He did not mention the flood, the studio repairs, or the new songs he had promised to share.

The eighth session took place at 2:31 pm on 9 June 2023. Calvin said he had met with the creative team for his album the previous day, a long but awesome session. Dave shared a photo of a pond with a boat surrounded by trees, and Calvin replied with a photo of a recording studio with a large window and a desk, calling it a wonderful studio. This is the first working studio he has shown since the flood, though he did not say the repairs were finished. Dave said he had been exploring parks on weekends and asked for chill spots in Boston. Calvin said he had never been to Boston before, though he had heard the parks were amazing, and that he could not wait to visit next month. This conflicts with his earlier planning and with the idea that he had only not yet explored the city because of rehearsals and travel. Dave said Boston parks are awesome in spring and that he had gone for a stroll the previous Friday, which walks recharge him for the week ahead. Calvin asked whether Dave had been hiking, and Dave said he had not but described nature as clearing the mind. Calvin said he had never been to the mountains but was keen to escape and de-stress. Dave announced he had booked a trip to a mountainous region for next month, which would be July 2023. Calvin asked him to take lots of pictures and show them when he got back. They closed with "See you soon" and "Take care" from both sides.

Calvin's stated interests are Japanese culture, music, and luxury cars. He writes songs, does studio work, hoped to collaborate with local musicians in Japan, and dreams of touring internationally. He is now working on an album with a creative team. His home studio was damaged by a flood in early May 2023, and by 9 June he was sharing a photo of a functioning studio, though no repair details were given. He described a red sports car as his first luxury car, which was never confirmed. He was in Tokyo by 20 April, was getting to know Japanese culture by 3 May, and was preparing for a Tokyo performance by 16 May. By 31 May he described the Frank Ocean tour and a Tokyo show as already past, though earlier he had described the tour as still ahead of Boston. He has not confirmed an exact Boston arrival date. He has also said he is keen to try hiking in the mountains.

Dave's interests include classic cars, auto engineering, live music, and now hiking and mountain travel. He first saw Aerosmith live in March 2023 at a Boston festival. He spends time at a calming park with a lake and boats, and he has been exploring parks on weekends. He opened his own car maintenance shop by 1 May, though he described it as newly opened again on 16 May. By 3 May he was working with a local garage and hoping to build a custom car someday. He restored a classic car the previous year. By 31 May he described repairing a neighbor's car. On 9 June he said he had booked a mountain trip for July 2023. He appears to be based in or near Boston, since he recommended local venues earlier. He has become a host-like figure for Calvin's Boston visit, offering to show him around, promising to attend his performances, and inviting him to the shop. He also gives practical advice on creative blocks, relaxation, and recovery from setbacks.

Several threads remain open. Calvin's life change beyond the move and the mansion photo was never explained. It is unconfirmed whether the red sports car shown on 26 March is the same one shown on 20 April or the one he drove on 3 May. Calvin has not visited the park Dave described and has not shared the new songs he promised. The studio's repair status is unclear, though the 9 June photo suggests it is usable. Calvin's Tokyo performance date and venue were never given. His claim on 9 June that he had never been to Boston conflicts with earlier planning, and his arrival date is still only "next month." Dave's shop timing and garage partnership are inconsistent across sessions, and his 31 May messages describe a neighbor's car where Calvin called it a friend's. Several photos were described in ways that do not match their captions, so their exact content should be treated with caution. Calvin's "[this car]" reference on 3 May is unresolved. It is also unclear whether Dave's July mountain trip will affect the timing of Calvin's Boston visit.

The relationship is warm and supportive, centered on shared interests in music, cars, nature, and each other's progress. Both regularly encourage each other's ambitions, offer practical advice, and plan to meet in Boston. Dave offered help after the flood, and Calvin asked to be kept posted on the Tokyo performance. On 9 June they discussed Calvin's album, Boston parks, and Dave's upcoming mountain trip. Dave asked for pictures from the trip, and Calvin said he could not wait to visit Boston. The most recent exchange, on 9 June 2023, ended with both promising to see each other soon.

The memory covers two speakers, Nate and Joanna, who chatted across four sessions between 21 January and 25 February 2022. Nate is a video game competitor who keeps a pair of turtles and has become a home baker of dairy-free desserts and ice cream. Joanna is a screenwriter who cannot eat dairy, is allergic to most reptiles and furred animals, and has a screenplay out for film festival consideration. Their conversations are friendly and casual, and they often praise each other's work. Each has at times recommended films or foods to the other, and each has promised to report back on what they tried, so several threads stay open across the sessions.

In the first session, on 21 January 2022 at 7:31 pm, Nate opened by greeting Joanna after a long gap and asking whether anything fun was going on. Joanna said she had been working on a project that had been pretty cool and asked about his projects or hobbies. Nate said he had won his first video game tournament the previous week. The game was Counter-Strike: Global Offensive, a team shooter, and he said he and his teammates had a blast right to the very end. Nate's main hobbies are playing video games and watching movies. He especially likes action and sci-fi films and says the visual effects are what draw him in. He also said he loves watching classics. Joanna listed her hobbies as writing, reading, watching movies, and exploring nature. She noted that the two of them share similar interests. She described her own favorite genres as dramas and romantic comedies, and said she likes getting immersed in the feelings and plots of a film. Nate said movies can be very powerful and asked for recommendations.

Joanna recommended a romantic drama about memory and relationships and shared a photo of its poster, which shows a man and a woman sitting on a bench. She said she first watched it around three years before that session, bought a physical DVD copy, and has rewatched it a few times. It is one of her favorites, and she praised both its concept and its acting. She shared a second photo of the DVD sitting on a table with a blurry background. Nate said he might check it out soon and asked whether she knew the film well. Joanna asked him to tell her what he thought. Nate never confirmed whether he had watched it, so that remains open.

In the second session, on 23 January 2022 at 2:01 pm, Joanna opened by saying she hadn't talked to Nate in a few days and that crazy things had happened to her. She said she had finally finished her first full screenplay and printed it the previous Friday, which was 21 January. She had been working on it for a while and said it was a relief to have it done. She shared a photo of a book with a page of text on it. The screenplay is a mix of drama and romance. Nate asked how she felt now that it was finished and whether she had new plans for it. Joanna described a rollercoaster of emotions: relief, excitement, and some anxiety. Her plan was to submit the screenplay to film festivals and hope that producers and directors would check it out. Nate told her it sounded like a wild experience and wished her well.

In the same session, Nate said he had had his two turtles for three years and that they bring him tons of joy. He shared a photo of a turtle and a baby turtle sitting on a rock. He said that keeping small animals around helps calm him when things are important and he feels nervous, and he recommended that Joanna consider a pet for times of stress. Joanna said they looked adorable and asked how long he had had them. She said she would think about getting pets of her own if she could find ones she wasn't allergic to. She then asked what Nate had been up to. He said he had started hanging out with some people outside his usual circle at the tournament, and that they were pretty cool. Joanna asked whether it was a weird relationship, since they were competitors. Nate said it was a little awkward at times, since some players are more competitive than others, so he tends to stick with the chiller people there. He said he doesn't expect to win big and simply likes playing for fun. He would cheer on his rivals even if they beat him.

Nate then asked how bad Joanna's allergy was. She said it was really bad, that her face gets puffy and itchy around certain animals, and that she has always stayed away from them. Nate asked what she was allergic to. She said she is allergic to most reptiles and animals with fur, and that it can be a bit of a drag, but she finds other ways to be happy. She said writing and hanging out with friends bring her joy, since writing lets her express herself through stories and time with friends lets her have a good time. Nate said he was glad she had other things to help her through anxiety despite not being able to have animals. Joanna said writing lets her create wild worlds with awesome characters, is a great way to express her feelings, and that she could not imagine life without it.

In the third session, on 7 February 2022 at 9:27 am, Joanna said the screenplay she had sent to a film festival had been on her mind all day, every day. She was bouncing between relief, excitement, and worry, and she hoped a producer or director would fall in love with it and bring it to the big screen. Nate said it was a big deal, sent positive vibes, and hoped someone would like it enough to get it on the big screen. Joanna thanked him and said she had put a lot of effort into the screenplay and was crossing her fingers. She asked Nate whether anything new was happening in his life. Nate said not much had changed, but he had just discovered that he could make coconut milk ice cream and had given it a try. He was proud of it, since it turned out pretty good. He shared a photo of a bowl of it with a spoon in it. He described it as rich and creamy and said it might become his new favorite snack. He said he would try again and planned to experiment with different flavors and toppings. Joanna asked whether he would make it again, and he said it could be fun. When she asked about his favorite flavors for dairy-free desserts, he said he loves coconut milk and also enjoys chocolate and mixed berry flavors.

Joanna said those flavors sounded great and that she was tempted to try dairy-free desserts herself. She shared a photo of a piece of cake with berries on a plate. Nate said he had made a dairy-free chocolate cake with berries on it the other day and thought she might like it. Joanna said it sounded yummy, called him talented, and said she should try making one herself or pay him a visit and try one. Nate said he always enjoys experimenting in the kitchen, and Joanna said his cooking skills are awesome. She then asked whether he had seen any good movies lately. He said he hadn't, and asked for recommendations. Joanna said she had just watched "Little Women," which she found amazing. She described it as a great story about sisterhood, love, and reaching for your dreams, and called it a must-see. Nate said he would add it to his list and thanked her. Joanna said she was always happy to give movie recommendations. Nate joked that he would give her a shout whenever he ran out of things to watch, and Joanna asked him to let her know what he thought once he finished it. Nate promised she would be the first to know. The two then ended the conversation with friendly goodbyes.

In the fourth session, on 25 February 2022 at 1:07 pm, Nate apologized for not having been around. He said he had made some ice cream for a friend, who loved it. He had made a chocolate and vanilla swirl and shared a photo of a person holding a chocolate and vanilla ice cream cone. Joanna said it looked delicious but that she can't have dairy, so she couldn't have any. She asked whether he had a dairy-free recipe she could try. Nate said he knew one that uses coconut milk and offered to send it. Joanna said she was definitely keen to try it and was always up for something sweet. She promised to keep him posted on how it turned out, and she told him she loved his creations.

In that session, Joanna also said she could not stop thinking about the screenplay, so she had just started writing another one while she waited to hear back about how the first one had done. The new script is about a thirty-year-old woman on a journey of self-discovery after a loss. Joanna said it was somewhat similar to the last one, but that this was the kind of thing she was inspired to write about. The main character is dealing with loss and trying to figure out who they are, and they take a road trip to heal and grow. Joanna said the story is her own and was inspired by personal experiences and her own journey of self-discovery. Nate said that took guts and that he could not wait to see it all come together. He also said he was pumped to see how the first screenplay would do. Joanna said she was still hoping her screenplay would get noticed and make it to the screen, and Nate wished her luck and said he hoped it would find a fan and be given its due.

Several details have shifted or sharpened over time. In January, Joanna described her allergies only in terms of pets, but by February she said she cannot have dairy, which matters because Nate's desserts and ice cream are dairy-free or made with dairy. Nate's turtles have been a steady part of his life since late January, when he said he had had them for three years. Joanna's screenplay has moved from completion on 21 January to submission to film festivals, then to waiting for a response, and she has since begun a second project. Nate has gone from being a competitor who played for fun to a more social player who has made new friends and grown into an enthusiastic home baker. His baking progressed from coconut milk ice cream in early February to a dairy-free chocolate cake with berries, and then to chocolate and vanilla swirl ice cream for a friend in late February. Movie recommendations have passed back and forth. Joanna suggested the memory-themed romantic drama in January and "Little Women" in February, and Nate asked for suggestions and promised to report back. Whether Nate has watched either film, and what he thought of them, has not been confirmed in any session. Joanna also said she would send Nate's coconut milk recipe feedback once she tried it, and that promise has not been followed up. Whether Joanna has tried any of Nate's desserts in person has not been confirmed either. Joanna has said she might pay Nate a visit to try one, but no plan was set. Finally, Joanna's question about getting a pet has not been resolved. She said she would think about it and might find something she is not allergic to, but she has not said she has done so.

The memory covers eight conversations between Caroline and Melanie, friends who keep in touch by chat and share photos. The sessions took place on 8 May, 25 May, 9 June, 27 June, 3 July, 6 July, 12 July, and 15 July 2023. Relative dates below are worked out from each session date. Both women write warmly and informally, and Melanie typically responds to Caroline's news with encouragement and short questions.

Caroline is a trans woman who moved from Sweden, her home country, about four years before June 2023. She began transitioning three years before June 2023. In the first session (8 May), she said she had attended an LGBTQ support group on 7 May 2023 and found it very powerful. The transgender stories she heard made her feel accepted and gave her the courage to embrace herself. She planned to continue her education and was drawn to counseling and mental health work so she could support people facing similar issues. Melanie praised her empathy and said she would make a great counselor. Melanie opened that session by saying she was swamped with her kids and work, and she shared a painting of a lake sunrise she had made the previous year, which is special to her. She described painting as a way to express her feelings and relax.

By the second session (25 May), Caroline was researching adoption agencies, a long-held dream of building a family and giving a loving home to children who need one. She chose an agency that helps LGBTQ+ people adopt because of its inclusivity and support. She said she felt hopeful and was up for the challenge of single parenthood, and she credited friends and mentors for their encouragement. In the same session, Melanie said she ran a charity race for mental health on Saturday, 20 May 2023. It made her realize how important self-care is. She has begun taking daily me-time for running, reading, or playing her violin, which she called a work in progress. Her family was considering a camping trip the following month.

In the third session (9 June), Caroline described speaking at a school event "last week," in the days just before 9 June. She talked about her transgender journey and encouraged students to get involved in the LGBTQ community. She said many listeners seemed inspired to become better allies, and that sharing her story helps build understanding and a supportive community. Melanie called her brave, and both agreed they wanted to spread love and understanding together. Caroline named her friends, family, and mentors as her "rocks." She had met friends "last week," and she had known them four years, since her move. They were especially important to her after a tough breakup. Melanie said she was lucky to have her husband and kids, who keep her motivated. She shared a photo of herself, her husband, and a little girl in front of a waterfall, and said they had been married five years. She also shared a wedding photo and described a recent family day out with games and good food.

In the fourth session (27 June), Caroline shared a photo of a necklace with a cross and a heart, a gift from her grandmother in Sweden that stands for love, faith, and strength. She also treasures a hand-painted bowl a friend made for her 18th birthday ten years earlier. Melanie said she had taken her family camping in the mountains "last week," in the days before 27 June. They hiked, roasted marshmallows, and enjoyed the view, and the two younger kids loved nature. Caroline said she was looking into counseling as a career, possibly working with trans people. On Friday, 23 June 2023, she attended an LGBTQ+ counseling workshop on therapeutic methods, and she was inspired by the professionals' passion for creating safe spaces.

In the fifth session (3 July), Caroline said that "last week," in the days just before 3 July, she attended an LGBTQ+ pride parade. It made her feel she belonged and showed how much the community has grown. It also motivated her to use her story to help others, and she remained committed to counseling and mental health work. Melanie said she had signed up for a pottery class "yesterday," which is 2 July, and described pottery as a kind of therapy. She shared a photo of a bowl with a black and white flower design that she made in class. Caroline said she was learning piano, and she mentioned a transgender conference she planned to attend that month, July 2023, to learn about advocacy.

In the sixth session (6 July), Caroline said she had been looking more into counseling and mental health work, which she found tough but rewarding. Melanie said that "yesterday," which is 5 July, she took her kids to a museum, where they loved the dinosaur exhibit. Caroline said she was building a children's library for the future, with classic, multicultural, and educational books. Melanie said she had loved *Charlotte's Web* as a child. Caroline said a picnic with friends "last week" showed how much her friends and family support her transition, giving her love, guidance, and acceptance. Melanie shared a photo of her family camping at the beach and said it brings them closer.

In the seventh session (12 July), Caroline said she attended an LGBTQ conference "two days ago," which is 10 July. She felt accepted there and became more committed to fighting for trans rights and spreading awareness. She explained that she had struggled with her own mental health, and the support she received showed her how much a support system matters, which is why she wants to help others through counseling. Melanie shared a photo of a book she read last year about pursuing dreams. Caroline named *Becoming Nicole* by Amy Ellis Nutt as her favorite guiding book, a true story about a trans girl and her family, which taught her self-acceptance and how to find support. Melanie introduced her dog, Luna, her cat, Oliver, and a pair of new pink running shoes. She said she had been running farther to de-stress, and that it was improving her mental health.

In the eighth session (15 July), Melanie said that "last Fri," which is 7 July, she took her kids to a pottery workshop where they all made pots. They also paint nature scenes together, including a sunset with a palm tree from "last weekend," which is 8 to 9 July. Melanie said she appreciates small things, such as a field of purple flowers they found. Caroline said that "last Friday," which is 7 July, she attended an adoption council meeting that was inspiring and emotional, and it made her more determined to adopt. Melanie said flowers represent growth and beauty, and she shared wedding photos from a greenhouse ceremony and a beach, saying that marrying her partner and promising to be together forever was the best part. Caroline said that a pride parade she attended "a few weeks ago" made her feel proud and less alone. Her best part was realizing she could be herself without fear and finding the courage to transition. Melanie said creativity and family keep her at peace, and that her family had supported her through a recent move, though she did not give details. Melanie also shared photos of a family camping trip in the forest and said they enjoy hiking in the mountains together. The two ended warmly, thanking each other for their friendship.

Across these sessions, both women emphasize self-care, family, and creative expression. Caroline moved from exploring counseling to actively studying it, from adoption research to attending a council meeting, and she took on a growing public role through school talks, a pride parade, and conferences. Melanie moved from her charity race and new me-time routine to pottery, painting, running, and family outings, always balancing family, work, and well-being.

SUMMARY

Caroline and Melanie are friends who check in every few weeks and share photos of their art, pets, families and outings. Caroline is a trans woman who moved to her current city from Sweden about four years before the first session, and she began transitioning around three years before June 2023. Her friends, family and mentors have been central to that process. Melanie is a married mother of several children, including a younger daughter and a son, and she names her husband and kids as her main motivation.

Caroline's career goal grew steadily. In May 2023 she was thinking about continuing her education toward counseling or mental health work. Over the summer she attended an LGBTQ+ counseling workshop, a pride parade, and a transgender conference. She spoke at a school event about her transition, began mentoring a transgender teen, and in late July joined an activist group called "Connected LGBTQ Activists." In August she started volunteering at an LGBTQ+ youth center and planned a talent show for the kids.

Caroline's adoption plans run through the whole record. In late May she was researching agencies, choosing one that works with LGBTQ+ applicants, and she said she expects to parent as a single parent. In mid-July she attended an adoption council meeting. In August she applied to agencies, calling it the first step toward becoming a mom. In October she contacted her mentor for advice and started preparing references, financial records and medical checks. On 22 October 2023 she reported passing the adoption agency interviews, which is the latest state of her plans. She is also building a children's library and keeps a guinea pig named Oscar.

Art is central to Caroline's life. She has painted since about age 17, and she said she has played acoustic guitar for about five years. She describes painting as therapeutic and as a way to explore her identity. Her works include a self-portrait, a piece called "Embracing Identity," and a red-and-blue painting about her path as a trans woman. She planned LGBTQ art shows for August and the following month. She recommended the book "Becoming Nicole" by Amy Ellis Nutt, which she said taught her about self-acceptance. Her favorite song is "Brave" by Sara Bareilles. She also described some friendships changing: a few close friends could not handle her transition, while others stayed supportive.

Melanie's life centers on family, nature and creative outlets. In May 2023 she had recently run a charity race for mental health and was building daily me-time around running, reading and playing violin. She later said she started playing clarinet when she was young. Over the summer she signed up for a pottery class, took her children to a pottery workshop, and went camping several times. Family trips included the mountains, the beach, a forest campfire, and a Perseid meteor shower the year before. In August she volunteered with her family at a homeless shelter. She attended a concert by "Summer Sounds" and a concert by Matt Patterson at her daughter's birthday celebration.

Melanie's household includes a dog named Luna and a cat named Oliver, and in August she mentioned another cat, Bailey. She remembered the day her youngest took her first steps. She and her husband married about five years before June 2023, and she described the wedding as full of love and joy. In October 2023 a family road trip was disrupted when her son was in a car accident. He was fine, and the family later enjoyed the Grand Canyon.

Melanie also had setbacks. In mid-October she said she got hurt the previous month and had to take a break from pottery, which she uses for self-expression and peace. She was reading the book Caroline had recommended and painting to stay busy. After a friend adopted the previous year, she said she was considering adoption herself, and Caroline offered to help if she pursued it.

The two women support each other's goals. Caroline praises Melanie's painting, pottery and family life, while Melanie affirms Caroline's advocacy, art and adoption plans. By late October 2023 Caroline is further along toward becoming a parent, while Melanie is recovering from her injury, adjusting after her son's accident, and returning to the creative activities that calm her.

Caroline and Melanie are close friends who check in on each other's lives across sessions from May to June 2023. Caroline is a transgender woman who moved from Sweden about four years before June 2023. She has a supportive circle of friends, family, and mentors, and she is single, having gone through a tough breakup before June 2023. Melanie is married and has kids, including two younger children. Her husband and kids are her main motivation.

In the first session (8 May 2023), Caroline said she had attended an LGBTQ support group the day before, which she found powerful. The stories shared there were inspiring to her. The group made her feel accepted and gave her courage to embrace herself. She said she planned to continue her education and look into career options, particularly counseling or mental health work, because she wanted to support people with similar struggles. She shared a photo of a dog walking past a wall with a painting of a woman. Melanie said Caroline would be a great counselor because of her empathy and understanding. Melanie shared a painting she had made of a lake sunrise the previous year, which is special to her. She described painting as a way to express her feelings and relax after a long day.

By the second session (25 May 2023), Melanie had run a charity race for mental health the previous Saturday, around 20 May, and found it rewarding and thought-provoking. She said she was learning that self-care matters, and she set aside daily me-time for running, reading, or playing the violin. She said this helped her stay present for her family. She mentioned that her family was thinking about camping the following month, and that her kids were excited about summer break. Caroline said she was researching adoption agencies and had a long-held dream of having a family and giving a loving home to children in need. She chose an agency because it supports LGBTQ+ people with adoption, and she shared a photo of the agency's sign. She expected single parenthood to be tough but said she was ready for the challenge and felt hopeful. She thanked her friends and mentors for their support.

In the third session (9 June 2023), Caroline reported that the previous week she had given a talk at a school about her transgender journey and encouraged students to get involved in the LGBTQ community. She said she felt powerful giving the talk and that the audience related to what she shared and wanted to become better allies. She said it made her reflect on how far she had come since she began transitioning three years earlier. She wanted to give a voice to the trans community and promote understanding and acceptance. Caroline said her friends, family, and mentors were her main sources of motivation and strength, and that their help had been especially important after a painful breakup. She shared a family photo from when they met up the week before. Melanie shared that she and her husband had been married for five years and that the family spent a fun day playing games, eating, and spending time together. Melanie said she wanted to be courageous for her family, who motivate her and give her love.

In the fourth session (27 June 2023), Caroline showed a necklace with a cross and a heart, a gift from her grandmother in Sweden that stands for love, faith, and strength. It reminds her of her roots and the support she gets from her family. She also mentioned a hand-painted bowl that a friend made for her 18th birthday ten years earlier, which reminds her of art and self-expression. Melanie said she had taken her family camping in the mountains the previous week, where they explored nature, roasted marshmallows, and hiked to a view she called amazing. She said the trip was a special family moment she would not forget. Caroline said she had recently been looking into counseling and mental health as a career and had attended an LGBTQ+ counseling workshop the previous Friday, around 23 June. The workshop covered different therapeutic methods and how to work well with trans people. She said she was still working out the details but was considering working with trans people to help them accept themselves and support their mental health. She said counseling and support groups had improved her own life, which is why she now cares more about mental health. Melanie congratulated her on pursuing what she cares about.

Across the sessions, Caroline's plans moved from exploring careers, to adoption research, to a clearer focus on counseling and mental health work with trans people. Melanie's life stayed centered on her family, her charity and self-care efforts, and her creative outlets such as painting and playing the violin.

Audrey wished him the best and looks forward to hearing where he and his future dog spend time. Andrew said he would keep her posted, and they said goodbye.

On 16 April 2023 at about 4:19 pm, in a third session, Andrew said he had missed chatting. He and his girlfriend had tried a new cafe in the city the previous weekend. Andrew said he was glad they bring her so much joy.

Taken together, the conversations show a steady theme: Andrew values nature and animals, and Audrey's dogs are central to her life. Deborah shared a photo of their last photo together, two women in wheelchairs hugging. She described a bench by the window where her mother sat every morning, and she sometimes sits there to feel close to her. She keeps a pendant that reminds her of her mother and wears her mother's gold-chained amulet when she reflects by the water near that house. Her mother loved travel, flowers, and art. On 27 January Deborah wrote that her father had died around 25 January. His sudden death left the family shell-shocked, and she and her husband are trying to be as good a family as her parents were. That week her yoga group gave her a handwritten note thanking her for her positive influence. Her neighbor Anna became a close friend, after they met at a park yoga class on 31 January and bonded at a class on 3 February. Anna wears a pendant in memory of her own mother. Deborah named a park with a forest trail and nearby beach as favorite places for peace. On 22 February she said she had lost a friend, Karlie, the week before, and found comfort in a calm garden of roses and dahlias. She shared the last photo she had taken with Karlie, two women on a motorcycle on a dirt road. Her routine is mornings for meditation, yoga, and teaching, and evenings for loved ones. On 13 March she started a neighborhood yoga class. By 9 July she had started a running group with Anna and was organizing workshops on mindfulness and self-care. She runs her two cats each morning and evening. On 1 August she described a community cleanup project she was raising funds for, and on 12 August she said she had made a meditation guide for her retreat. On 16 August she led a meditation yoga session at a local care home. On 21 August she visited the special bench near her mother's house, where the two once talked about dreams and watched sunsets in silence, and she brought flowers because her mother loved them. On 24 August she described a yoga retreat near her mother's place as life-changing. On 26 August she shared photos of her cats: Luna, a five-year-old she adopted from a shelter, and Max, an eight-year-old who was her mother's cat and whom she took in when her mother died. On 30 August she named a lake with trees as a favorite spot for reflecting and letting go, and shared a handwritten note from a friend who had died, quoting "Let go of what no longer serves you." On 3 September she said a community event had inspired her, that her yoga friends had become her second family, and she shared an old photo of herself with her mum, her biggest fan, who often came to classes. On 8 September a storm forced her to cancel a yoga getaway. She was bummed but found comfort in her work and time at home. In mid-September she reconnected with her mother's old friends, whose stories made her tear up and helped her appreciate her mother more. She said the beach in one of her photos is where she got married and discovered her love of surfing, and that it is always filled with joy and peace. She called yoga on the beach the perfect way to take care of herself. Her husband once liked detective games and spending time outdoors, and they used to play games together.

Jolene's mother died in 2022. In her first session she shared a photo of a room with a bench and a window in her mother's house, along with a heart-shaped bird pendant her mother gave her in Paris in 2010. She wears jewelry with a symbol of freedom to remind herself to pursue her goals. She keeps pet snakes, which calm her. Susie, adopted two years before August 2023 when Jolene felt lonely, and Seraphim, bought a year earlier in Paris, are her favorites. On 15 September she confirmed that the snake in her photo was Susie. Jolene and her partner are both avid gamers. Her parents gave her a Nintendo console when she was ten, which started her love of video games. Her dad was supportive, and her mom played games with her, especially "Monster Hunter: World." On 19 August she bought a black Xbox console for her partner and recommended Zelda: Breath of the Wild, Animal Crossing: New Horizons, and Overcooked 2. Their favorite game together is "It Takes Two."

Jolene is an engineering student. In early February she called a robotics project from her engineering professor tough but fun. On 4 February she reported that she had designed and built a sustainable water purifier for a rural community, and seeing it deliver clean water felt deeply satisfying. On 9 February a mini retreat gave her an idea for a volunteer program in which engineers teach STEM to underprivileged kids, though she had not yet contacted any schools. On 2 March she said exams were weighing on her and admitted she needed to be more mindful of her stress. Deborah advised breaking work into smaller pieces and promised her a yellow mug with an encouraging handwritten message. On 22 March Jolene said she was using the Pomodoro Technique but still struggled to prioritize, so Deborah introduced the Eisenhower Matrix, which helped. On 28 March Jolene reported a breakthrough on her project. She finds lavender and rosemary scents relaxing and listens to Nils Frahm and Olafur Arnalds during practice, and Deborah recommended the track "Savana" and the album "Sleep." On 25 February she had said she was balancing engineering school with her partner's video games and setting aside time for yoga and meditation, which he had begun joining. The two have been together three years, are not yet married, and met in an engineering class in college. On 6 June Jolene returned after a long silence. She had finished the tough engineering project and was interning at a well-known engineering firm. She found work-life balance hard, and she had practiced yoga and meditation sporadically for about three years. On 26 June she had just bought a new aquarium for Seraphim and said she sometimes felt overwhelmed by pushing herself to succeed. On 1 August she said a huge setback with her project had left her frustrated and depressed, and that video games and Susie helped. On 12 August she said meditation had helped her recover her clarity after losing work files, and she described a prototype for a more affordable aerial surveillance system. On 16 August she said she was struggling to juggle engineering, her relationship, and personal growth, and had started a bullet journal, which she found satisfying. On 21 August she said her favorite yoga pose is savasana and that she was finding her zen again. On 24 August she presented at a virtual conference and received positive feedback that confirmed she was on the right track. On 26 August she said her mother always told her never to give up and stressed helping others, and her partner's father taught them determination. Her two goals are renewable energy such as solar power to help communities, and clean water for people with limited access. She and her partner were planning a meditation retreat together. On 30 August she said she meditates at a nearby pond with lily pads, where she makes sense of things and reduces stress. On 3 September she said she and her partner take short trips to the beach to relax, and that she had many finals that month and was considering a trip afterward to recharge.

Jolene and her partner have been traveling and seeking calm. On 30 August she said they had just returned from Rio de Janeiro, where they took yoga classes, visited an old temple, and ate at many cafes. On 6 September she signed up for a meditation course at a retreat near a lake and shared a photo of a building with a curved roof on a hill. On 12 September she said that the previous weekend she and her partner had gone on a few-week meditation retreat in Phuket, which helped her find inner peace. She realized the importance of relaxation and balance alongside her studies. One session stood out to her, about releasing expectations and savoring the present. She said she usually gets so consumed with hitting her goals that she forgets to appreciate the ride. She now tries to be more mindful and grateful for small things like sunshine and good coffee. On 15 September she said she had shared her love of yoga with her partner, and that they had tried a new style of meditation in Thailand using flowers. She creates a serene yoga space with candles, oils, and soft music, and she said her room is her little haven for rest and recharging.

Deborah and Jolene have supported each other throughout. Deborah has encouraged Jolene through her mother's death, engineering work, exam stress, internship, and setbacks, and has offered practical advice on self-care, breathing, time management, and mindfulness. Jolene offered sympathy after Deborah's father and her friend Karlie died, and has shown steady interest in Deborah's yoga, travels, pets, and community work. Jolene has returned to yoga and meditation, sometimes with her partner, though gaming remains a shared pastime. Deborah has grown closer to Anna, widened her practice into the neighborhood and care homes, and taken up running.

Their most recent sessions were lighter and centered on plans. On 6 September Deborah shared a photo of a beach sunrise, and Jolene said beach walks relax her and hoped they might someday watch the sunrise together. On 8 September they tried to set up a coffee date. Jolene first proposed a Wednesday at 4 pm, but Deborah had other plans, so they settled on a Friday at 5 pm, which Deborah described as "next week." Jolene needed to sort books from a bookcase first, and Deborah jokingly asked her to bring some interesting books. Deborah also mentioned a cat-themed card game she had played and said they would play it with Jolene someday. Both women close their chats warmly and say they want to stay in touch.

Jon and Gina are friends who check in on each other's businesses and encourage each other through setbacks. This memory covers their conversations from January 2023 through 13 June 2023. Photos shared in the sessions are known only through the speakers' words and short captions. I have not confirmed what the images show.

Background: Both lost their jobs in January 2023. Jon was a banker, and Gina worked at Door Dash. Jon is building a dance studio offering classes, workshops, and now one-on-one mentoring. Gina runs an online clothing business and has developed a video presentation on styling her fashion pieces.

Jon's timeline:
- 20 January 2023: He decided to open a dance studio because he is passionate about dancing. Contemporary is his top pick. He was finishing choreography for a festival.
- 29 January 2023: He described a downtown location that is easy to reach and has natural light, and said he is after Marley flooring.

- 24 April 2023 (reported 25 April): He showed his studio at a fair, which was stressful and great, and he got some possible leads. He said confidence matters for business success.
- 25 April 2023: He said he has been feeling low on confidence.

- 13 June 2023: He said he is "prepping for my dance studio more than ever." He is working with young dancers and wants the studio to be a place of support and encouragement. Besides classes and workshops, he is offering one-on-one mentoring and training. He uses a whiteboard to track goals and color-codes achievements. He asked to see Gina's styling presentation and said he won't give up.

- 1 February 2023: A wholesaler agreed to work with her, which lets her expand the store and get closer to customers.
- 4 February 2023: She said the store is doing great.
- 16 March 2023: She said her online clothes store is open.
- 3 April 2023: She launched new offers and promotions and said she is not giving up. She planned to work with fashion bloggers and influencers and run more ads. She said she is definitely attending Jon's competition.
- 9 April 2023: She told Jon he is almost there.
- 25 April 2023: She said she started her own online clothing store "not so long ago." She advised Jon to focus on why he started and said she has faith in him.
- 11 May 2023: She said she had a design internship interview "yesterday" (10 May 2023), which she called "so cool." She said she is proud of Jon and agreed to watch his routine.
- 27 May 2023: She said she was accepted for a part-time fashion internship in the fashion department of an international company. She felt excited and kinda nervous, and said it will be a big change.
- 13 June 2023: She said she is proud of Jon for starting his own business and for staying hopeful. She has developed a video presentation on styling her fashion pieces and said she would send it to Jon "later." She said she had a mentor when she was learning to dance. She shared several photos, including one described as a group of young girls in blue outfits and another described as a dance class. She encouraged Jon to stay positive and not quit.

Discrepancies and open points:
- On 16 March 2023, Gina said her online store was already open. On 25 April 2023, she said she started it "not so long ago." The sessions do not explain this, so do not treat the exact start date as settled.
- The 10 May 2023 design internship interview and the 27 May 2023 internship acceptance may or may not be the same opportunity. The sessions do not say.
- There was a gap in contact between 11 May and 27 May 2023.

- Both consistently encourage each other. The latest exchange (13 June 2023) was warm and supportive, and both spoke about not giving up.

Calvin and Dave are friends who chat periodically, share photos, and trade news about their work and hobbies. Calvin's messages are enthusiastic and often exaggerated, full of exclamations, phrases like "so cool" and "can't wait," and frequent references to dreams coming true. Dave's messages are warmer and more measured, centered on cars, restoration, parks, and his band. Both usually congratulate each other before turning back to their own lives, and both close by offering encouragement or proposing a time to meet. Across twenty-four sessions from March to October 2023, their conversations moved from life changes and travel plans to music careers, car projects, and plans to see each other in Boston.

In March, Calvin announced a major life change, shared a photo of a building he called his new mansion, and said he was heading to Japan in April before going on to Boston. Dave said having a place to stay was key. Calvin promised to visit when he was back. On 26 March, Calvin said he had bought a red sports car that made him feel like a rockstar. Dave said his favorite band was Aerosmith, whom he had seen live. On 20 April, Calvin described a Tokyo music event where a producer advised him to stay true to himself, and he said he looked forward to Boston after the Frank Ocean tour. Dave offered to show him the Boston music scene, including Paradise Rock Club, House of Blues, and Fenway Park, along with classic cars, and they agreed to share a meal there.

On 1 May, Dave announced he had opened his own car maintenance shop, a dream come true and a step toward working on classic cars. He invited Calvin to visit. On 3 May, Dave said he was teaming up with a local garage. Calvin said long drives in his red sports car helped him relax, but his creativity felt frozen, so Dave suggested immersing himself in music he loved. On 16 May, Calvin reported that his home had flooded the previous week. He had saved his music gear and favorite microphone, but repairs were waiting on insurance. Dave offered help. The exact date of Dave's shop opening is unclear across sessions. On 31 May, Calvin said touring with Frank Ocean had been wild and that he was excited to perform in Boston for people from home. The two agreed that fixing things was therapeutic.

On 9 June, Calvin met with the creative team for his album. Dave had booked a mountain trip for July, and Calvin said he could not wait to visit Boston in July. On 21 June, Calvin described a small car accident in which no one was hurt. Repairs took a week and cost less than he feared. He also shared a photo of a small Japanese town with a mountain behind it that he hoped to visit. Dave said he had recently joined a rock band. On 7 July, Calvin said his car was fixed, and Dave said he hoped to visit Japan one day. Calvin said he was working on collaborations with Japanese artists. On 21 July, Dave returned from a road trip that reminded him why he loved cars. Calvin described turning his mansion into a recording studio, a long-held dream, and said collaborating kept him motivated.

On 3 August, Calvin said he had taken his Ferrari in for service, which was stressful because he was attached to it. On 11 August, Dave said he had been picked for a car mod workshop and was working on a classic muscle car. He shared a photo of a silver Corvette with a modern twist. Dave offered to help with Calvin's music work, and Calvin politely said he was too busy. On 14 August, Dave said he had attended a car restoration workshop in San Francisco. Calvin said he had recently toured with a well-known artist, ending with a show in Japan. On 22 August, Calvin announced a deal to keep collaborating with Frank Ocean, which he called a dream come true. He said they had met at a Tokyo music festival and recorded a song at his mansion. He said his tour was ending and that he was heading to Boston. On 31 August, Calvin said he had started shooting a video for his new album on a Miami beach. Dave offered help with props, and Calvin shared a photo of a custom octopus-design guitar made by a Japanese artist friend.

On 2 September, Dave said he had returned from San Francisco and found giving old cars new life deeply satisfying. Calvin shared a photo of a boarding pass for his flight to Boston, and they agreed to catch up there. On 13 September, Calvin apologized for the gap and said his album had dropped on the 11th. His next step was a tour, though he did not name cities. Dave said he would love to show Calvin his garage, and Calvin said he would take him up on it. On 15 September, Dave said he and his band had been jamming. Calvin shared a photo of a Ratatouille poster, one of his favorites. On 22 September, Dave said a vintage Mustang engine he thought he had fixed made a weird noise when started. Calvin said his trip to Japan had been incredible and that he was already longing to go back, which sits awkwardly with his earlier descriptions of living there. Calvin also named "California Love" as a song he used to sing with his dad on road trips. Dave suggested a jam session, and Calvin agreed.

The October sessions add new detail, some of it inconsistent. On 4 October, Calvin said that the day before he had met incredible artists in Boston and talked about working together. Dave said he was restoring a Ford Mustang he had found in a junkyard, a project that differs from the noisy-engine Mustang he described in September. The session became a long exchange of encouragement about hard work and small wins. On 8 October, Dave said he had gone to a car show the previous Friday and had restored and modified a car himself, adding a custom exhaust and performance upgrades. He said restoration was now his job, which had been his goal since childhood. On 15 October, Dave said a competing car maintenance shop had won a deal his team had pursued for months, and he asked whether he was wasting his time. Calvin encouraged him to keep pushing. Dave then described a music festival whose headliner was The Fireworks. Calvin announced that he had gotten a new black Ferrari the previous week. On 19 October, Calvin said he had started touring with Frank Ocean and had shared stage photos, including one from a Tokyo concert. He said he had first met Frank at a festival in August of the previous year, which conflicts with his earlier account of a Tokyo festival in August. Calvin said he would be heading to Tokyo next month after the tour ends, and he mentioned Shibuya Crossing, Shinjuku, and ramen. Dave shared a photo of a ramen bowl he had eaten in Boston.

Several things changed over time. In March, Calvin was planning a move to Japan and then Boston. By April he was in Tokyo, and by mid-May he was performing there. His home flooded in May. He described touring with Frank Ocean at different points, and the timing is inconsistent across sessions. By June he was working on an album, and by summer he described his Japanese mansion as both home and studio. In August he referred to a Ferrari, which may or may not be the red sports car he showed in September. By late August he had a continuing collaboration deal with Frank Ocean, was filming in Miami, and had booked a flight to Boston, though he had not confirmed arriving there. His album was released on 11 September. In October he said he had met artists in Boston, bought a black Ferrari, and started a tour.

Dave's life also developed. In March he was enjoying parks, car events, and a Boston music festival. In May he teamed up with a local garage and opened his own shop, though the shop is not mentioned again after July, when he described corporate demands at work that sit uneasily with owning a shop. In July he took a road trip and joined a rock band. In August he was selected for a car mod workshop, attended a San Francisco restoration workshop, and worked on a car with a broken engine. In September he was rehearsing with his band and troubleshooting a Mustang. In October he restored a junkyard Mustang, described restoration as his job, and lost a business deal to a competitor.

Throughout the conversations, Calvin focused on music, collaborations, touring, cars, and reaching a global audience, while Dave focused on cars, restoration, parks, music festivals, and his band. Both encouraged each other through photos and messages. Caroline and Melanie are friends who check in every few weeks. Their conversations center on mental health, self-care, identity, family, and the futures they are building. They share photos, celebrate each other's progress, and encourage each other's goals. Eight sessions are recorded, from 8 May 2023 to 15 July 2023.

Caroline is a transgender woman who started transitioning about three years before June 2023. She moved from Sweden about four years earlier, around when her friendships with her current group began. After a painful breakup, her friends and mentors helped her through. She calls them her "rocks" and says family is everything to her. Melanie has been married to her husband for about five years and has young kids. She works, looks after the family, and makes time for running, reading, playing the violin, and painting. She has a dog named Luna and a cat named Oliver.

The first session took place on 8 May 2023. Melanie said she had been swamped with work and kids. Caroline said that on 7 May she attended an LGBTQ support group, where other trans members' stories gave her courage to embrace who she is. She plans to continue her education and is drawn to counseling or mental health work to support people facing similar issues. Melanie said her empathy would make her a great counselor. Melanie shared a 2022 painting of a lake at sunset, which she calls a lake sunrise and which is special to her. Both agreed that looking after yourself is vital.

The second session took place on 25 May 2023. Melanie said that around 20 May she ran a rewarding charity race for mental health. She sets aside daily me-time for running, reading, or violin, which she called a work in progress and which helps her care for her family. The family was planning a June camping trip. Caroline said she was researching adoption agencies, a long-held dream to build a family and give a loving home to a child in need. She chose an agency supporting LGBTQ+ adoptive parents and feels ready, though she knows single parenthood will be tough. Melanie said she would be an awesome mom.

The third session took place on 9 June 2023. Caroline described a school talk she gave in early June about her transgender journey, encouraging students to join the LGBTQ community. She wants to keep lifting others up with her voice. She named her friends, family, and mentors as her motivation, and said her friends of four years were especially important after the breakup. Melanie said her husband and kids keep her motivated, and she shared family photos, including her wedding photo.

The fourth session took place on 27 June 2023. Caroline shared a necklace with a cross and a heart, a gift from her grandmother in Sweden that symbolizes love, faith, and strength, and a hand-painted bowl a friend made for her eighteenth birthday. Melanie said her family camped in the mountains around 20 June, roasting marshmallows and hiking to a view she called amazing. Caroline said she is looking into counseling, possibly working with trans people to help them accept themselves. On 23 June she attended an LGBTQ+ counseling workshop and was moved by the professionals' passion for creating safe spaces. Melanie congratulated her.

The fifth session took place on 3 July 2023. Caroline described an LGBTQ+ pride parade in late June where she felt she belonged. It motivated her to use her story to help others and keeps her leaning toward counseling. Melanie said she signed up for a pottery class on 2 July, which feels like therapy, and shared a photo of her bowl. Caroline said she is learning piano and would attend a transgender conference later in July to meet people and learn about advocacy. Melanie told her to stay safe.

The sixth session took place on 6 July 2023, after a gap. Caroline said she is looking more into counseling or mental health work, which she finds tough but rewarding. She is also building a children's library to read to her future kids. Melanie said that on 5 July she took the kids to a museum, where they were most excited about the dinosaurs. Her favorite childhood book was Charlotte's Web, which taught her how friendship and compassion make a difference. Caroline said this made her appreciate the friends and family helping with her transition. They had a picnic the previous week, and Melanie shared a beach campfire photo, saying camping brings the family closer. The adoption plan, the July conference, and piano did not come up.

The seventh session took place on 12 July 2023. Caroline said she attended an LGBTQ conference around 10 July, where she met people with similar journeys, felt totally accepted, and became committed to fighting for trans rights and spreading awareness. This is likely the July conference from session five. She is still exploring counseling and mental health jobs because she wants people to have someone to talk to. She said she had struggled with mental health herself and wants to help others as she was helped. Her favorite book is "Becoming Nicole" by Amy Ellis Nutt, a true story about a trans girl and her family, which taught her self-acceptance and that tough times do not last. Melanie shared a book cover with a gold coin and said a book she read reminded her to pursue her dreams. She introduced Luna and Oliver with photos and shared new pink running shoes, saying she has been running farther to de-stress. She said her mental health has improved.

The eighth session took place on 15 July 2023, a Saturday, and covered the past week. Melanie said she took her kids to a pottery workshop "last Friday," probably 14 July, where they made pots and clay sculptures. She shared a photo of a dog-faced cup one child made. She also described painting nature scenes with the kids, including a sunset with a palm tree, and said she is learning to appreciate small things. Caroline reported attending an adoption council meeting "last Friday," which she found inspiring and emotional and which made her even more determined to adopt. This is the first concrete adoption step since session four. Melanie said her future family would be lucky to have her. Melanie called flowers symbols of growth and joy, and said flowers were central to her wedding decor, a day she described as full of love and joy. Caroline said she wished she had known her then. Asked about her favorite part, Melanie said promising to stay together forever with her husband. Caroline returned to the pride parade from "a few weeks ago," describing feeling accepted, proud, and part of a community, and calling the best part realizing she can be herself without fear. Melanie said creativity and family keep her at peace. She said her family supported her through a recent move and enjoys camping, hiking, and forest outings. The session ended with both thanking each other for their friendship.

Several threads remain open. Caroline is still pursuing adoption through an agency supporting LGBTQ+ adoptive parents and plans to raise a child as a single parent. She reported in session eight that the council meeting strengthened her resolve. Her children's library may be tied to this plan, though she has not said so directly. She is actively exploring counseling and mental health work, especially supporting trans people, but has not named a specific program or job. Her conference around 10 July strengthened her advocacy. She has not mentioned piano since session five, and she is still considering further education. She sees her friends and family as the foundation of her transition, and her pride parade has become a central story of belonging. Melanie has built regular me-time into her routine, started pottery she finds therapeutic, and takes longer runs in new shoes. Painting and pottery with her kids now give her peace too. She remains a devoted mother and wife, with family outings, camping, hikes, and her pets central to her life. Both see self-care, community, and family as central to how they want to live. Melanie affirms Caroline's path toward counseling and adoption, and Caroline cheers on Melanie's running, pottery, painting, and family life.

The memory covers twelve conversations between Caroline and Melanie, friends who keep in touch by chat and share photos. The sessions took place on 8 May, 25 May, 9 June, 27 June, 3 July, 6 July, 12 July, 15 July, 17 July, 20 July, 14 August, and 17 August 2023. Relative dates below are worked out from each session date. Both write warmly and informally, and Melanie usually answers Caroline's news with encouragement and short questions.

Caroline is a trans woman who moved from Sweden, her home country, about four years before June 2023, and began transitioning three years before June 2023. In the first session (8 May), she said an LGBTQ support group she attended on 7 May 2023 had been very powerful, and that the transgender stories she heard gave her the courage to embrace herself. She planned to continue her education toward counseling and mental health work so she could support people facing similar issues, and Melanie said she would make a great counselor. Melanie, who was swamped with kids and work, shared a painting of a lake sunrise she had made the previous year and described painting as a way to express feelings and relax. By 25 May, Caroline was researching adoption agencies, a long-held dream of giving a loving home to children, and she chose one that helps LGBTQ+ people adopt. She felt hopeful about single parenthood. Melanie had run a charity mental health race on Saturday, 20 May 2023, which showed her how important self-care is, and she had started daily me-time for running, reading, or playing violin.

On 9 June, Caroline described speaking at a school event "last week" about her transgender journey, encouraging students to join the LGBTQ community. Melanie called her brave, and they agreed to spread love and understanding together. Caroline named her friends, family, and mentors as her "rocks," especially friends she had known since her move four years earlier, who mattered greatly after a tough breakup. Melanie said she was lucky to have her husband and kids, married five years, and shared a family photo in front of a waterfall. On 27 June, Caroline shared a necklace with a cross and a heart, a gift from her grandmother in Sweden representing love, faith, and strength. Melanie had taken her family camping in the mountains "last week." Caroline was looking into counseling, possibly with trans clients, and on Friday, 23 June 2023, she attended an LGBTQ+ counseling workshop on therapeutic methods, inspired by the professionals' passion for creating safe spaces.

On 3 July, Caroline said that "last week" she attended an LGBTQ+ pride parade that made her feel she belonged and motivated her to use her story to help others. She was learning piano and planned to attend a transgender advocacy conference that month. Melanie had signed up for a pottery class "yesterday" (2 July), calling pottery a kind of therapy. On 6 July, Caroline found counseling work tough but rewarding and was building a children's library of classic, multicultural, and educational books. Melanie said "yesterday" (5 July) she took the kids to a museum with a dinosaur exhibit, and that she had loved *Charlotte's Web* as a child. Caroline said a picnic with friends "last week" showed how much they support her transition.

On 12 July, Caroline said she attended an LGBTQ conference "two days ago" (10 July), where she felt accepted and more committed to trans rights. She had struggled with her own mental health, and that support is why she wants to help others through counseling. Her favorite guiding book is *Becoming Nicole* by Amy Ellis Nutt, a true story about a trans girl and her family. Melanie introduced her dog Luna, her cat Oliver, and new pink running shoes, and said running farther was helping her de-stress. On 15 July, Melanie said "last Fri" (7 July) her kids made pots at a pottery workshop, and "last weekend" (8 to 9 July) they painted a sunset with a palm tree. Caroline said "last Friday" (7 July) she attended an inspiring and emotional adoption council meeting that made her more determined to adopt. She also said a pride parade "a few weeks ago" made her feel proud and less alone.

On 17 July, Melanie said she had a quiet weekend after a family camping trip "two weekends ago." Caroline joined a mentorship program for LGBTQ youth "last weekend" (15 to 16 July) and mentors a transgender teen, and they are building confidence together. Caroline said the best moment at a June 2023 pride event was seeing her mentee's face light up at the support there. She also previewed a painting of a tree with a bright sun, made after visiting an LGBTQ center to capture unity and strength, for an LGBTQ art show she planned for August. Melanie said she and her kids had just finished another painting.

On 20 July, Caroline said she had joined an LGBTQ activist group called "Connected LGBTQ Activists" "last Tues" (18 July), which holds regular meetings and plans events and campaigns. She had missed her city's pride parade "last weekend" (15 to 16 July), but it reminded her that the community is not alone in fighting for equality. Melanie said the family had recently gone to the beach, and that seeing the kids so happy was the best part. Their annual family camping trip, with marshmallows and campfire stories, is the highlight of their summer. Melanie's best camping memory was watching the Perseid meteor shower on a trip "last year" (2022).

On 14 August, Melanie said "last night" (13 August) the family celebrated her daughter's birthday with a concert by Matt Patterson. Caroline had attended a pride parade "last Friday" (11 August), which made her proud and more determined to keep fighting for equality. Asked how she stays inclusive as an artist, Caroline said her art expresses her trans experience and helps people understand the trans community. She shared "Embracing Identity," a painting of a woman on a journey of acceptance, meant to show warmth, love, and self-acceptance. Art has helped her explore her transition and her changing body, and it has taught her to accept the beauty of imperfections.

On 17 August, Caroline said that "recently" she ran into religious conservatives on a hike who upset her, which showed her how much work remains for LGBTQ rights. Melanie shared a colorful bowl, her latest pottery project. The two agreed that happy moments and supportive friends make hard times bearable. Melanie suggested a family outing this summer, and Caroline proposed either that or a trip just the two of them to explore nature. They agreed to plan something special, and Melanie said she would start thinking about what they could do.

Her art has become a way to tell her trans story. Melanie has moved from her charity race and me-time routine to pottery, painting, running, and family outings, always balancing family, work, and well-being. Their latest plan is a summer outing, either with the whole family or just the two of them.
