Evan and Sam have been talking since at least 18 May 2023, across sixteen sessions running to 9 November 2023. Their conversations trace Sam's move toward healthier habits and Evan's role as encourager. Sam usually asks for advice and support, while Evan shares his own experiences, photos, painting, and practical tips.

On 18 May 2023, Evan said he had just returned from a Rockies trip in a new Prius and shared a lake photo. Sam said he loved hiking but had not done it in ages, recalling a hike with his dad at age ten, one of the more personal details he has shared. He had no hobbies yet but was considering painting, which Evan said he had done in watercolor for years as a stress-buster. On 24 May, Evan described a road trip to Jasper and the Icefields Parkway. Sam said a doctor's check-up had shown his weight was off target. Evan said it is never too late to change, that an enjoyable fitness routine and smarter diet choices had worked for him, and that painting would not help weight, so Sam should exercise too.

On 6 June, Evan disclosed a sudden heart palpitation episode that was a serious wake-up call. Sam said he still drank soda and ate candy. Evan, who was cutting back on sugary snacks though he loved ginger snaps, suggested flavored seltzer and high-cocoa dark chocolate, and offered to show Sam basic exercises. On 27 July, Sam said friends had mocked his weight, which hurt and pushed him to change. Evan described his gym membership card as a reminder of his own commitment, said cutting sugary snacks and eating more produce had made the biggest difference, and suggested air-popped popcorn or fruit. Sam said he would start going to the gym the next day.

On 7 August, Evan mentioned meeting an incredible Canadian woman, admitted ginger snaps were still his weakness, and said his family had motivated his two-year healthy road. He shared a bonsai tree that symbolized strength for him and a fitness watch, which Sam said he was thinking of buying. On 13 August, Evan said he had just returned from a Canadian vacation with his new partner, where they had hiked and biked. Sam said things had been hard and had hurt his health, but Evan's support meant a lot, and he shared a quote that progress matters more than perfection. On 15 August, Evan's son hurt his ankle in a soccer accident. Sam said a recent doctor's appointment had felt like a wake-up call and that he was taking a cooking class, and he offered a roasted vegetable recipe.

On 19 August, Sam said he was on a diet, living healthier, and had more energy, and he shared a grilled chicken and vegetable stir-fry recipe. Evan said he had started watercolor classes to meet like-minded people, especially loving landscapes, and mentioned a skiing trip in Banff, hoping Sam might join him someday. Sam said he would love to try skiing but was not sure his body could handle it, a hint at a physical limitation that has recurred. On 27 August, Sam said he had started a new diet and exercise routine the previous Monday and felt great. Evan had twisted his knee and was swimming while waiting for physical therapy. He recommended a lake about two hours away, and Sam said he would plan a day trip there.

On 11 September, Sam shared a before-and-after photo and said he wanted to motivate others, but admitted cravings for sugary drinks and snacks, usually triggered by stress, boredom, or comfort. Evan said painting or going for a drive helped him de-stress and offered to recommend painting supplies, and they agreed to plan a painting session the following Saturday. On 6 October, Sam said he had started eating healthier. Evan had hurt his knee again playing basketball with the kids, and said painting had kept him busy. Sam said he was still learning to draw but loved journaling and creative writing, and he mentioned frustration with his new phone's navigation app.

On 8 October, Sam said his doctor had told him on Monday, 2 October, that his weight was a serious health risk. He admitted he had made jokes about it but said it was really hitting him. Evan said he had started lifting weights a year earlier, advised finding a trainer for good form, and urged Sam to start small and be patient. Sam said he would find someone and keep Evan posted.

On 14 October, Sam said he had had a rough week after buying unhealthy snacks and felt guilty, and he shared a photo of a person holding sodas. Evan shared a sunset painting he had just finished. Sam mentioned work stress and asked for outdoor ideas, and Evan suggested kayaking. Sam later said he and his friend were kayaking on a lake while traveling through Lake Tahoe, and Evan called it an awesome pick. On 17 October, Sam said he had missed their chats and had gone to the ER the previous weekend with severe stomachache, diagnosed as gastritis. He called it a wake-up call to prioritize nutrition and regular exercise, and said his phone troubles were adding stress. Evan said he had been focusing on fitness and had met another lost tourist. He advised setting goals, finding an enjoyable exercise, and getting a workout buddy, and they agreed to plan a hike soon.

On 25 October, Sam said his new routine was tough and his family was pressuring him. Evan said he had just come back from a morning walk and that encouragement should not add stress. Sam admitted he got impatient for fast results. Evan said he had changed his diet and started walking regularly two years earlier, and shared a photo of himself at a table of fruits and vegetables. He said focusing on well-being rather than quick results made the biggest difference, and urged Sam to take it one day at a time and celebrate small victories.

On 9 November, Sam said he had become a Weight Watchers coach in his group, a big accomplishment he felt proud of, and Evan congratulated him warmly. Evan apologized for missing events, citing personal challenges, and shared a photo of a 1968 Kustom K-200A vintage guitar, a gift from a close friend. He revealed he had lost his job the previous month when his company downsized, and said he was job hunting but staying hopeful. Sam offered to listen and help. Evan also shared a sunset photo from a peaceful beach spot near his home, which he had visited the previous Friday, and they agreed to visit it together the following month, in December 2023.

Several things changed across these sessions. In May, Sam was exploring painting and had not yet changed his habits. By early June he was thinking seriously about diet and exercise, and by late July he had committed to cutting back on soda and candy and to going to the gym. Caroline and Melanie are friends who check in every few weeks. Their conversations center on mental health, self-care, identity, family, and the futures they are building. They share photos, celebrate each other's progress, and encourage each other's goals. Nine sessions are recorded, from 8 May 2023 to 17 July 2023.

Caroline is a transgender woman who started transitioning about three years before June 2023. She moved from Sweden about four years earlier, around when her current friendships began. After a painful breakup, her friends and mentors helped her through, and she calls them her "rocks." Family is everything to her. She keeps a necklace from her grandmother in Sweden, with a cross and a heart symbolizing love, faith, and strength. Melanie has been married for about five years and has young kids. She works, looks after the family, and makes time for running, reading, violin, and painting. She took up pottery in July 2023. She has a dog named Luna and a cat named Oliver.

The first session took place on 8 May 2023. Melanie said she had been swamped with work and kids. Caroline said that on 7 May she attended an LGBTQ support group, where other trans members' stories gave her courage to embrace who she is. She plans to continue her education and is drawn to counseling or mental health work. Melanie said her empathy would make her a great counselor. Melanie shared a 2022 lake sunset painting that is special to her. Both agreed that looking after yourself is vital.

The second session took place on 25 May 2023. Melanie said that around 20 May she ran a rewarding charity race for mental health. She sets aside daily me-time for running, reading, or violin, a work in progress that helps her care for her family. The family planned a June camping trip. Caroline said she was researching adoption agencies, a long-held dream, and chose one supporting LGBTQ+ adoptive parents. She feels ready, though she knows single parenthood will be tough. Melanie said she would be an awesome mom.

The third session took place on 9 June 2023. Caroline described a school talk she gave in early June about her transgender journey, encouraging students to join the LGBTQ community. She wants to keep lifting others up and named her friends, family, and mentors as her motivation. Melanie said her husband and kids keep her motivated, and she shared family photos, including her wedding photo.

The fourth session took place on 27 June 2023. Melanie said her family camped in the mountains around 20 June, roasting marshmallows and hiking to an amazing view. Caroline shared the necklace and a hand-painted bowl a friend made for her eighteenth birthday. She is looking into counseling, possibly working with trans people to help them accept themselves. On 23 June she attended an LGBTQ+ counseling workshop and was moved by the professionals' passion for creating safe spaces. Melanie congratulated her.

The fifth session took place on 3 July 2023. Caroline described a late June pride parade where she felt she belonged, which motivated her to use her story to help others. Melanie said she signed up for a pottery class on 2 July, which feels like therapy, and shared a photo of her bowl. Caroline said she is learning piano and would attend a transgender conference later in July to learn about advocacy. Melanie told her to stay safe.

The sixth session took place on 6 July 2023, after a gap. Caroline said she is looking more into counseling or mental health work, which is tough but rewarding, and she is building a children's library to read to her future kids. Melanie said that on 5 July she took the kids to a museum, where they loved the dinosaurs. Her favorite childhood book was Charlotte's Web. Caroline said this made her appreciate the friends and family helping with her transition. Melanie shared a beach campfire photo, saying camping brings the family closer. The adoption plan, the July conference, and piano did not come up.

The seventh session took place on 12 July 2023. Caroline said she attended an LGBTQ conference around 10 July, where she felt totally accepted and became committed to fighting for trans rights. She is still exploring counseling because she wants people to have someone to talk to, and she said she had struggled with mental health herself. Her favorite book is "Becoming Nicole" by Amy Ellis Nutt, which taught her self-acceptance and that tough times do not last. Melanie shared a book cover with a gold coin and said a book had reminded her to pursue her dreams. She introduced Luna and Oliver with photos, shared new pink running shoes, and said her mental health has improved.

The eighth session took place on 15 July 2023, a Saturday. Melanie said she took her kids to a pottery workshop "last Friday," probably 14 July, and shared a photo of a dog-faced cup one child made. She also described painting nature scenes with the kids, including a sunset with a palm tree. Caroline reported attending an adoption council meeting "last Friday," which was inspiring and emotional and made her more determined to adopt. This is the first concrete adoption step since session four. Melanie called flowers symbols of growth and joy and said they were central to her wedding decor. Asked her favorite part of the day, she named promising to stay together forever with her husband. Caroline returned to the pride parade, calling the best part realizing she can be herself without fear. Melanie said creativity and family keep her at peace, and that her family enjoys camping and hiking. Both thanked each other for their friendship.

The ninth session took place on 17 July 2023, a Monday, at 2:31 pm. Melanie said she had a quiet weekend after camping with her family two weekends earlier. Caroline said she joined a mentorship program for LGBTQ youth the previous weekend, probably 15 or 16 July, and finds it rewarding. She mentors a transgender teen on confidence and positive coping strategies, which she says is paying off. The two attended a pride event "last month," most likely the late June parade, where the best moment was seeing her mentee's face light up. Caroline shared a photo of a woman holding a rainbow umbrella. She announced an LGBTQ art show of her paintings for August 2023 and previewed two works: a blue and yellow design, and a tree with a bright sun behind it, painted after visiting an LGBTQ center to capture unity and strength. Melanie praised the vivid colors and said she and her kids had just finished another painting like their last one.

Several threads remain open. Caroline is still pursuing adoption through an agency supporting LGBTQ+ adoptive parents and plans to raise a child as a single parent. The council meeting strengthened her resolve. Her children's library may be tied to this plan, though she has not said so directly. She is actively exploring counseling and mental health work, especially supporting trans people, but has not named a specific program or job. She has not mentioned piano since session five and is still considering further education. Her events and her new mentoring role have deepened her advocacy, and her August art show extends her work into art. She sees her friends and family as the foundation of her transition.

Melanie has built regular me-time into her routine, started pottery she finds therapeutic, and takes longer runs in new shoes. Painting and pottery with her kids now give her peace too, and they continued painting together in July. She remains a devoted mother and wife, with family outings, camping, hikes, and her pets central to her life. Both see self-care, community, and family as central to how they want to live. Melanie affirms Caroline's path toward counseling, adoption, and mentoring, and Caroline cheers on Melanie's running, pottery, painting, and family life.

Sam and Evan are friends who have now talked eight times. Their conversations are friendly and enthusiastic. Evan is usually the supportive, encouraging voice, and Sam is the one looking for direction. Sam has moved from exploring hobbies toward a committed focus on his health, while Evan's news has shifted from travel and family to a health scare, a new romance, his son's injury, and most recently a painting class and skiing.

The first conversation took place on 18 May 2023 at 1:47 pm. Evan had just returned from a family hiking trip to the Rockies, taken roughly 8 to 14 May, and shared a photo of a lake with mountains behind it. He had bought a new Prius after his old car broke down, and said he would repair and sell the old car, so its fate is unclear. Sam loves hiking but has not done it in ages, and treasures a memory of hiking with his dad at age ten. Sam was thinking of trying painting, which he had never done. Evan's main hobby was watercolor, which he called a great stress-buster. Evan once signed off with "Take it easy, Evan!" addressed to Sam, apparently a slip of the name.

The second conversation took place on 24 May 2023 at 7:11 pm. Evan described a family road trip to Jasper along the Icefields Parkway, probably 20 to 21 May. His photo labeled a glacier shot actually showed a person holding a book in front of a lake. Sam said a doctor check-up showed his weight was not in a good range. Evan said it is never too late to change and suggested an enjoyable fitness routine plus smarter eating. When Sam asked whether painting would help, Evan said it relieves stress but would not solve his weight problem. Sam said he would try painting and report back, and has not yet done so.

The third conversation took place on 6 June 2023 at 3:55 pm. Evan opened with "Long time no talk!" and described a sudden heart palpitation scare the previous week that had been a serious wake-up call. Sam said he was trying to eat healthier, though he admitted he had made no diet changes and still drank soda and ate candy. Evan said he was cutting back on sugary snacks, though he loves ginger snaps, and suggested flavored seltzer and high-cocoa dark chocolate. Evan offered to work out with Sam, and Sam agreed to try. Painting did not come up.

The fourth session took place on 27 July 2023 at 10:52 am and was the most serious so far. Sam said friends had mocked his weight the previous Friday, probably around 21 July, and it had hurt enough to make him realize he needed to change. Evan apologized, said progress takes time, and said they would work on it together. He shared that he had struggled with his health a few years earlier, and posted a photo of five cards reading "let it shine," which he called his gym membership card. He said diet matters as much as exercise and recommended low-calorie snacks such as air-popped popcorn or fruit. He described a mystery novel, then named The Great Gatsby, which is not really a mystery. His photo of fruit and a bottle of alcohol also did not match his snack advice. Sam said he would start the gym from 28 July.

The fifth session took place on 7 August 2023 at 7:52 pm. Evan said that the previous week he had traveled to Canada, where he met an awesome Canadian woman, and shared a photo of a couple holding hands in the snow. Sam congratulated him and said he was sorry Evan had been dealing with health issues. Evan said he had been prioritizing his health for about two years and admitted ginger snaps are his weakness. Sam asked whether a fitness watch was worth ordering. Evan said his family motivates him and the watch would be a constant reminder of progress. The two closed on small steps, and Sam's sign-off, "Great chatting with you, Sam!", used the wrong name, another slip. Evan ended with "Catch ya later!"

The sixth session took place on 13 August 2023 at 4:09 pm, eight days after the last talk, though Evan again opened with "Long time no talk!" He said he had just returned from a "rad vacay" in Canada with his new significant other, and that they had tried hiking and biking. His photo of a tent in a grassy field does not clearly show either activity. Sam said things had been challenging lately and some of it had been hard on his health, without details. He shared a notepad quote that had been keeping him motivated: "Don't fear it, just take the first step." Evan urged him to celebrate small wins. No update on painting, the gym, or the fitness watch came up.

The seventh session took place on 15 August 2023 at 4:20 pm, only two days after the last talk. Evan said his son had hurt his ankle in a soccer accident the previous Saturday, probably 12 August, and that he had been caring for the boy and taking him to the doctor. He shared a photo of a person with a cast on their foot, which does not clearly show his son. Sam said a rough week and a doctor's appointment had been a wake-up call, and that he was now taking a cooking class. He shared a photo of grilled salmon and vegetables he had made around 14 August. Evan said it was okay to feel overwhelmed and to keep moving forward slowly, and Sam said the encouragement meant a lot. Evan did not mention his Canadian partner.

The eighth session took place on 19 August 2023 at 6:17 pm, four days after the seventh. Sam opened with big news: he was on a diet and living healthier, which had been tough but he was determined. He shared a photo of spinach, avocado, and strawberries, and said he had more energy and less sluggishness after eating. He then shared a grilled chicken and veggie stir-fry with a homemade sauce, though the recipe card photo showed a drawing of a vase of flowers, an odd match for a recipe. Evan said he had started a painting class a few days earlier and was really enjoying it. This conflicts with the earlier record, in which watercolor was already his long-standing hobby. Evan said a friend had once given him a painting that inspired him to begin, and that he joined the class to find like-minded people. He shared photos of a forest scene on an easel, a cloth with what looked like eyeliners rather than painting supplies, a sunset over the ocean, and a tree with pink flowers. He said these scenes reminded him of road tripping in his "trusty car," and shared a photo of a truck in a forest, though he had bought a new Prius. Evan said last month he had driven somewhere with amazing views and shared a photo of a person skiing. Sam asked whether he had skied in Banff, and Evan said he could not wait to go back next year. He listed skiing, snowboarding, and ice skating as favorites and invited Sam to join him someday. Sam said he was not sure his body could handle skiing and thanked Evan for his understanding. The skiing timing is doubtful, since "last month" would be July, and the August Canada trip was described as hiking and biking. Sam gave no health details, and the gym and painting trial did not come up.

Taken together, the eight sessions show Evan as a steady source of encouragement. He has shared his health history, watercolor hobby, family life, love of hiking and travel, a new relationship with a Canadian woman, his son's injury, and now a painting class and skiing. He has offered practical advice about seltzer, dark chocolate, exercise, and small daily choices. Sam has moved from curiosity about hobbies to a committed focus on his health. He has cut back on soda and candy, planned a gym routine from 28 July, considered a fitness watch, taken a cooking class, and, as of 19 August, reported more energy on a healthier diet. Whether he started painting or the gym routine remains unconfirmed. He has been vague about health specifics since the sixth session, so his progress is best described as sincere effort without measurable detail.

Several of Evan's details do not match his photos or each other and should be treated with caution. These include the glacier shot with a person and book, The Great Gatsby described as a mystery, the snack advice paired with alcohol, the tent offered as hiking evidence, the cast photo, the eyeliners in the painting-supplies photo, the skiing "last month," the truck photo despite the new Prius, and the conflicting accounts of how long he has been painting. Name slips have appeared in both directions at sign-off, and Evan has used "long time no talk" even when little time had passed. The friendship's most consistent thread remains Evan's steady encouragement and Sam's determination to take his health seriously.

Deborah and Jolene first spoke on 23 January 2023, when Deborah greeted Jolene and asked about her week. Their chats have stayed friendly and personal, often turning to loss, family, and what keeps each of them going, and both have shared many photos. The record runs from January through 20 September 2023, with gaps in early and mid-March, from April to June, and from late July to mid-August.

Deborah teaches yoga to support her community and to help people find peace and joy through the practice. Yoga helped her through a rough time, which is why she wants to share it. In January 2023 she visited her late mother's old house, which is full of memories. Her mother had died a few years earlier. Deborah shared a photo of their last photo together, two women in wheelchairs hugging. She described a bench by the window where her mother sat every morning, and she sometimes sits there to feel close to her. She wears a pendant that reminds her of her mother and her mother's gold-chained amulet when she reflects by the water near that house. Her mother loved travel, flowers, and art, cooked lovingly for the family, baked pineapple birthday cakes for Deborah as a child, and sang her lullabies. On 27 January Deborah wrote that her father had died around 25 January. His sudden death left the family shell-shocked, and she and her husband are trying to be as good a family as her parents were. That week her yoga group gave her a handwritten note thanking her for her positive influence.

Her neighbor Anna became a close friend after they met at a park yoga class on 31 January and bonded at a class on 3 February. Anna wears a pendant in memory of her own mother. Deborah named a park with a forest trail and a nearby beach as favorite places for peace. On 22 February she said she had lost a friend, Karlie, the week before, and found comfort in a calm garden of roses and dahlias.

Deborah's routine is mornings for meditation, yoga, and teaching, and evenings for loved ones. On 13 March she started a neighborhood yoga class, and by 9 July she had started a running group with Anna and was organizing workshops on mindfulness and self-care. She cares for her two cats, Luna, a five-year-old she adopted from a shelter, and Max, an eight-year-old who was her mother's cat and whom she took in when her mother died. On 1 August she described a community cleanup project she was raising funds for, and on 12 August she said she had made a meditation guide for her retreat. On 16 August she led a meditation yoga session at a local care home. On 21 August she visited the special bench near her mother's house, where the two once talked about dreams and watched sunsets in silence, and she brought flowers because her mother loved them. On 24 August she described a yoga retreat near her mother's place as life-changing. On 30 August she named a lake with trees as a favorite spot for letting go. On 3 September she said her yoga friends had become her second family. On 8 September a storm forced her to cancel a yoga getaway, and she found comfort in her work and time at home. In mid-September she reconnected with her mother's old friends, whose stories helped her appreciate her mother more. The beach in one of her photos is where she got married and discovered her love of surfing.

On 10 September Deborah sat on the bench at her mother's house again, feeling her mother's presence. On 16 September she and her neighbor ran a free gardening class for the community, which she said brought people together. On 20 September she described a music festival with her friends where dancing felt freeing and reminded her of her mother's lullabies. She also recalled a blossom tree near her home that filled her with awe each spring and gave her hope for growth even in tough times.

Jolene's mother died in 2022. In her first session she shared a photo of a room with a bench and a window in her mother's house, along with a heart-shaped bird pendant her mother gave her in Paris in 2010. She wears jewelry with a symbol of freedom to remind herself to pursue her goals. She keeps pet snakes, which calm her. Susie, adopted two years before August 2023 when Jolene felt lonely, and Seraphim, bought a year earlier in Paris, are her favorites. On 15 September she confirmed that the snake in her photo was Susie.

Jolene and her partner are both avid gamers. Her parents gave her a Nintendo console when she was ten, which started her love of video games, and her mom played with her, especially "Monster Hunter: World." On 19 August she bought a black Xbox for her partner and recommended Zelda: Breath of the Wild, Animal Crossing: New Horizons, and Overcooked 2. Their favorite game together is "It Takes Two."

Jolene is an engineering student. In early February she called a robotics project from her professor tough but fun. On 4 February she reported that she had designed and built a sustainable water purifier for a rural community, which felt deeply satisfying. On 9 February a mini retreat gave her an idea for a volunteer program in which engineers teach STEM to underprivileged kids, though she had not yet contacted any schools. On 25 February she said she was balancing engineering school with her partner's video games and setting aside time for yoga and meditation, which he had begun joining. On 2 March she said exams were weighing on her. Deborah advised breaking work into smaller pieces and promised her a yellow mug with an encouraging message. On 22 March Deborah introduced the Eisenhower Matrix, which helped Jolene prioritize. On 28 March Jolene reported a breakthrough on her project. She finds lavender and rosemary scents relaxing and listens to Nils Frahm and Olafur Arnalds during practice, and Deborah recommended the track "Savana" and the album "Sleep." The couple has been together three years, are not yet married, and met in an engineering class in college.

On 6 June Jolene returned after a long silence. She had finished the tough project and was interning at a well-known engineering firm, but she found work-life balance hard. On 26 June she had just bought a new aquarium for Seraphim and said she sometimes felt overwhelmed by pushing herself to succeed. On 1 August a huge setback with her project left her frustrated and depressed, and video games and Susie helped. On 12 August meditation helped her recover her clarity after she lost work files, and she described a prototype for a more affordable aerial surveillance system. On 16 August she said she was struggling to juggle engineering, her relationship, and personal growth, and had started a bullet journal, which she found satisfying. On 21 August she said her favorite yoga pose is savasana. On 24 August she presented at a virtual conference and received positive feedback. On 26 August she said her mother always told her never to give up, and her partner's father taught them determination. Her goals are renewable energy such as solar power to help communities, and clean water for people with limited access. On 30 August she said she meditates at a nearby pond with lily pads, where she makes sense of things. On 3 September she said she had many finals that month and was considering a trip afterward to recharge.

Jolene and her partner have been traveling and seeking calm. On 30 August she said they had just returned from Rio de Janeiro, where they took yoga classes and visited an old temple. On 6 September she signed up for a meditation course at a retreat near a lake. On 12 September she said that the previous weekend they had gone on a few-week meditation retreat in Phuket, which helped her find inner peace and showed her the importance of balance. She said she often gets so consumed with her goals that she forgets to appreciate the ride. On 15 September she said she had shared her love of yoga with her partner, and that they had tried a flower-based meditation in Thailand. The same day she said they had tried a scuba diving lesson the previous Friday and found a dive spot they could explore together. She creates a serene yoga space with candles, oils, and soft music, and calls her room her little haven. She enjoys reading, and once read a self-discovery book in her bathroom that resonated with her deeply. On 17 September she said she had just started learning to surf but had not yet gone out. On 20 September she shared a photo from a music festival the previous year, and said they had just returned from a yoga retreat where the sunrise lit up the sky. She also described a hike that ended at a waterfall oasis, where her worries disappeared, and said she planned to get back into nature the next month.

Deborah and Jolene have supported each other throughout. Deborah has encouraged Jolene through her mother's death, engineering work, exam stress, internship, and setbacks, and has offered practical advice on self-care, breathing, time management, and mindfulness. Jolene offered sympathy after Deborah's father and her friend Karlie died, and has shown steady interest in Deborah's yoga, travels, pets, and community work. Jolene has returned to yoga and meditation, sometimes with her partner, though gaming remains a shared pastime. Deborah has grown closer to Anna, widened her practice into the neighborhood and care homes, and taken up running.

Their most recent sessions have been lighter and centered on plans and shared interests. On 6 September Deborah shared a photo of a beach sunrise, and Jolene said she hoped they might someday watch the sunrise together. On 8 September they tried to set up a coffee date, and settled on a Friday at 5 pm, which Deborah described as "next week." Jolene needed to sort books from a bookcase first, and Deborah jokingly asked her to bring some interesting ones. On 17 September they talked about reading, cozy nooks, and surfing. Deborah said she had not yet tried scuba diving, and Jolene invited her to try surfing together, with a day to be chosen next month. Both women close their chats warmly and say they want to stay in touch.

The memory covers sixteen conversations between Caroline and Melanie, friends who keep in touch by chat and share photos. The sessions took place on 8 May, 25 May, 9 June, 27 June, 3 July, 6 July, 12 July, 15 July, 17 July, 20 July, 14 August, 17 August, 23 August, 25 August, 28 August, and 13 September 2023. Relative dates below are worked out from each session date. Both write warmly and informally, and Melanie usually answers Caroline's news with encouragement and short questions.

Caroline is a trans woman who moved from Sweden, her home country, about four years before June 2023, and began transitioning three years before June 2023. In the first session she said an LGBTQ support group she attended on 7 May 2023 had been very powerful, and she planned to continue her education toward counseling and mental health work. By 25 May she was researching adoption agencies, a long-held dream, and chose one that helps LGBTQ+ people adopt. On 9 June she described speaking at a school event "last week" about her transgender journey. She named her friends, family, and mentors as her "rocks," especially friends she had known since her move, who mattered greatly after a tough breakup. On 27 June she shared a necklace with a cross and a heart, a gift from her grandmother in Sweden. On 3 July she attended a pride parade "last week" that made her feel she belonged, and she was learning piano. On 6 July she was building a children's library of classic, multicultural, and educational books. On 12 July she attended an LGBTQ conference "two days ago" (10 July), where she felt accepted. Her favorite guiding book is *Becoming Nicole* by Amy Ellis Nutt. On 15 July she attended an adoption council meeting "last Friday" (7 July) that made her more determined to adopt. On 17 July she joined a mentorship program for LGBTQ youth "last weekend" and mentors a transgender teen. She also previewed a painting of a tree with a bright sun, made after visiting an LGBTQ center, for an LGBTQ art show she planned for August. On 20 July she said she had joined an activist group called "Connected LGBTQ Activists" "last Tues" (18 July).

On 14 August she said a pride parade "last Friday" (11 August) made her proud and more determined to keep fighting for equality. She explained that her art expresses her trans experience, and she shared "Embracing Identity," a painting of a woman on a journey of acceptance. On 17 August she said that "recently" religious conservatives she met on a hike had upset her, which showed how much work remains for LGBTQ rights. On 23 August she reported that "this week" she applied to adoption agencies after getting help from an adoption advice group, calling the step exciting but nerve-wracking. Her pet is Oscar, a guinea pig. She shared a self-portrait "last week" (about 16 August) with a blue face, saying painting made her feel liberated and empowered. On 25 August she said that "last week" she got into a bad spot with some people while hiking and tried to apologize. She also painted a sunset after a beach visit that she found calming. She described a rainbow flag mural and an eagle mural as meaningful, and she made a stained glass window for a local church about time changing lives and her own journey as a transgender woman. She found a rainbow sidewalk for Pride Month that reminded her love and acceptance are everywhere. She is putting together an LGBTQ art show "next month" (September) where she will show her paintings. On 28 August she said she had been volunteering at an LGBTQ+ youth center, sharing her own story with young people, and would keep volunteering there. The center is planning a talent show for the kids "next month." She has played acoustic guitar for about five years, and she named "Brave" by Sara Bareilles as a song with deep meaning for her. On 13 September she said she spent "last weekend" (9 to 10 September) biking with friends. She has made art since about age 17 and finds it empowering and cathartic. Her red and blue painting represents the binary gender system and a rejection of rigid thinking, and it is a reminder to love her authentic self. She said her transition changed her relationships: some close friends kept supporting her, a few could not handle it, and her relationships now feel more genuine. She has not tried pottery yet but is open to it.

Melanie had run a charity mental health race on Saturday, 20 May 2023, which showed her how important self-care is, and she had started daily me-time for running, reading, or playing violin. In the first session she was swamped with kids and work, and she shared a lake sunrise painting from the previous year, describing painting as a way to express feelings and relax. On 9 June she called Caroline brave, and they agreed to spread love and understanding together. She said she was lucky to have her husband and kids, married five years. On 27 June she said her family had gone camping in the mountains "last week." On 3 July she signed up for a pottery class "yesterday" (2 July), calling pottery a kind of therapy. On 12 July she said running farther was helping her de-stress. On 15 July she said her kids made pots at a pottery workshop "last Fri" (7 July). On 20 July she said the family had recently gone to the beach, and their annual family camping trip, with marshmallows and campfire stories, is the highlight of their summer. On 14 August she said the family celebrated her daughter's birthday "last night" (13 August) with a concert. On 17 August she shared a colorful bowl, her latest pottery project, and the two agreed that happy moments and supportive friends make hard times bearable. She suggested a family outing this summer, and Caroline proposed that or a trip just the two of them. On 23 August Melanie congratulated Caroline on the adoption applications and mentioned her two cats, Oliver and Bailey, and her dog. On 25 August she said she made a plate in pottery class "yesterday" (24 August), and she described a day volunteering with her family at a homeless shelter that made her feel they could make a difference. She shared a sunflower painting and said autumn was inspiring her to plan more paintings. On 28 August she said she had taken her kids to a park "yesterday" (27 August). She shared a concert photo from a show by the band "Summer Sounds," and she said music brings people together. She plays clarinet, which she uses for self-expression and relaxation, and she named Bach, Mozart, and Ed Sheeran's "Perfect" as favorites. On 13 September she said she had gone camping with the kids "a few weeks ago," where they explored the forest, hiked, and roasted marshmallows. She has been into art for seven years and calls painting and pottery her real muses. She also described a café visit "last weekend" (9 to 10 September) and explained that a sign on the door was only a precaution.

Across these sessions, both women emphasize self-care, family, and creative expression. Caroline has moved from researching counseling and adoption to applying to adoption agencies, attending council meetings, and taking on a public role through school talks, pride parades, a mentorship program, a youth center, and an activist group. Her art has become a way to tell her trans story, and she has described her relationships as more genuine after some friendships changed. This memory covers 32 conversations between Maria and John from 17 December 2022 to 16 August 2023. They are friends who check in regularly, encourage each other, and often talk about community service, family, and nature.

John's main goal is public service. In December 2022 he said he wanted to get into local politics, focusing on education and infrastructure, shaped by growing up in a neighborhood with poor schools and crumbling roads. In January 2023 he joined a service-focused online group that helped him brainstorm programs offering underserved communities education, mentorship, job training, and resume building. He had failed a military aptitude test earlier, but in early March he retook it and got strong results, which drew him toward serving his country. He announced in late February that he was running for office again, and in early May he said he had decided to run after an earlier attempt that did not succeed. He attended a community meeting on education and infrastructure in late January, blogged about education reform in April, and in July organized a meeting about solutions after a flood damaged homes in his old neighborhood. He has also led a petition supporting military veterans, hosted a party where veterans shared their stories, and joined a veterans' rights march in early July.

John's family is central to his life. He is married, and he often refers to his wife as "the missus." They have several children, including a son named Kyle, who was one as of March 2023, and a daughter named Sara. Their photos often show picnics, swings, and dinners at home. The family started boot camps three times a week in April, enjoyed a live music event in June, and visited a military memorial in August. Their favorite activities include hiking, picnics, board games, and movie nights. John's dog Max, who had been part of the family for ten years, died in early June 2023. In August John shared camping photos of Max from the previous summer, and the family discussed adopting a rescue dog.

John's work life changed a lot. He finished a university degree in late March 2023 and considered a career in policymaking. He began a weekend beginner's yoga class with a colleague, and in late June he was promoted to assistant manager after many hurdles, including self-doubt, which he marked with a golden trophy. In late July he described his new job as going well. In early August he lost that job when his mechanical engineering company struggled, and he later mentioned a possible hardware role at a tech company. He joined a volunteer firefighting brigade in late July, and by mid-August he was describing a call-out where his team helped rescue a family from a burning building. He also organized a 5K charity run for veterans and their families and worked with a local organization supporting victims of domestic abuse. In mid-August he began volunteering as a school mentor. Earlier he had felt stuck and questioned whether he was making a real impact, so he planned to research volunteering groups.

Maria's life is equally full of volunteering. She began volunteering at a homeless shelter after her aunt, who believed in helping others, supported her family during hard times when Maria was young. In December 2022 she donated her old car to the shelter. In early 2023 she served meals at a charity event, where she met a man named David and linked him to a housing organization. In February she met Jean, a woman who had faced divorce, job loss, and homelessness yet stayed hopeful. In early April she completed a 5K charity run for the shelter and later gave talks there. She planned a ring-toss tournament and helped organize a chili cook-off fundraiser, which John helped promote. In June she began volunteering monthly at a local dog shelter. In late July she baked for the shelter, and in August she worked the front desk, where she received a medal and a letter of gratitude from a resident named Laura.

Maria has a small family, and she has spent time with her mother and siblings. She also enjoys cooking, from peach cobbler to banana split sundaes. She took creative writing and poetry classes in 2023, and she has traveled to England, where she was inspired by castles, and to Spain, where she tried surfing for the first time. Her grandmother died in early 2023, which was very hard for her. In May she joined a nearby church to feel closer to her faith and community, and she bought a cross necklace for that reason. In June she joined a gym and began kundalini yoga, and she has long enjoyed aerial yoga. In early July she and her cousin were in a car accident after another car ran a red light, but everyone was okay. Her cousin had also recently lost her home, and Maria helped her find a new place. In August she got a puppy named Coco, and later she adopted a black puppy named Shadow, and the two dogs get along well.

John and Maria often check in, encourage each other's goals, and celebrate each other's achievements. Both describe their friendship as a team and say they want to keep making a difference together. By mid-August 2023, John was serving with the firefighting brigade and mentoring students, while Maria was volunteering at the shelter and caring for her two dogs. Their shared photos of sunsets, nature, and family life reflect the same outlook they bring to their work.

Caroline and Melanie are friends who check in every few weeks. Their conversations center on mental health, self-care, identity, family, and the futures they are building. They share photos, celebrate each other's progress, and encourage each other's goals. Ten sessions are recorded, from 8 May 2023 to 20 July 2023.

Caroline is a transgender woman who started transitioning about three years before June 2023. She moved from Sweden about four years earlier, around when her current friendships began. After a painful breakup, her friends and mentors helped her through, and she calls them her "rocks." Family is everything to her. She keeps a necklace from her grandmother in Sweden, with a cross and a heart symbolizing love, faith, and strength. Melanie has been married for about five years and has young kids. She works, looks after the family, and makes time for running, reading, violin, and painting. She took up pottery in July 2023. She has a dog named Luna and a cat named Oliver.

The first session took place on 8 May 2023. Melanie said she had been swamped with work and kids. Caroline said that on 7 May she attended an LGBTQ support group, where other trans members' stories gave her courage to embrace who she is. She plans to continue her education and is drawn to counseling, and Melanie said her empathy would make her a great counselor. Both agreed that looking after yourself is vital.

The second session took place on 25 May 2023. Melanie said that around 20 May she ran a rewarding charity race for mental health, and she sets aside daily me-time for running, reading, or violin. The family planned a June camping trip. Caroline said she had chosen an adoption agency that supports LGBTQ+ adoptive parents, a long-held dream. She feels ready, though she knows single parenthood will be tough.

The third session took place on 9 June 2023. Caroline described a school talk she gave in early June about her transgender journey, encouraging students to join the LGBTQ community. She named her friends, family, and mentors as her motivation to keep lifting others up. Melanie said her husband and kids keep her motivated, and she shared family photos.

The fourth session took place on 27 June 2023. Melanie said her family camped in the mountains around 20 June and hiked to an amazing view. Caroline shared a hand-painted bowl a friend made for her eighteenth birthday. She is looking into counseling, possibly working with trans people to help them accept themselves, after attending an LGBTQ+ counseling workshop on 23 June.

The fifth session took place on 3 July 2023. Caroline described a late June pride parade where she felt she belonged, which motivated her to use her story to help others. Melanie said she signed up for a pottery class on 2 July, which feels like therapy. Caroline said she is learning piano and would attend a transgender conference later in July.

The sixth session took place on 6 July 2023, after a gap. Caroline is looking more into counseling and building a children's library for her future kids. Melanie took the kids to a museum on 5 July, where they loved the dinosaurs, and her favorite childhood book was Charlotte's Web. The adoption plan, the July conference, and piano did not come up.

The seventh session took place on 12 July 2023. Caroline attended an LGBTQ conference around 10 July, where she felt totally accepted and became committed to fighting for trans rights. She is still exploring counseling because she wants people to have someone to talk to, and she said she had struggled with mental health herself. Her favorite book is "Becoming Nicole" by Amy Ellis Nutt. Melanie introduced Luna and Oliver with photos, shared new pink running shoes, and said her mental health has improved.

The eighth session took place on 15 July 2023, a Saturday. Melanie said she took her kids to a pottery workshop "last Friday," probably 14 July, and they painted nature scenes together. Caroline reported attending an adoption council meeting that same Friday, which was inspiring and emotional and made her more determined to adopt. This was the first concrete adoption step since session four. Melanie called flowers symbols of growth and joy, and she said creativity and family keep her at peace. Caroline returned to the pride parade, calling the best part realizing she can be herself without fear. Both thanked each other for their friendship.

The ninth session took place on 17 July 2023, a Monday, at 2:31 pm. Melanie said she had a quiet weekend after camping with her family two weekends earlier. Caroline said she joined a mentorship program for LGBTQ youth around 15 or 16 July and mentors a transgender teen on confidence and coping strategies. She also announced an LGBTQ art show of her paintings for August 2023, previewing a blue and yellow design and a tree with a bright sun, painted after visiting an LGBTQ center. Melanie praised the vivid colors and said she and her kids had just finished another painting.

The tenth session took place on 20 July 2023, a Thursday, at 8:56 pm. Caroline said she joined a new LGBTQ activist group called "Connected LGBTQ Activists" on Tuesday, 18 July. She described regular meetings and planned events and campaigns. She also said her city held a pride parade "last weekend," around 15 or 16 July, and that she missed it. This is a separate event from the late June parade she attended earlier. Melanie shared family photos and memories: a recent beach trip where the kids flew a kite, summer camping trips with marshmallows and campfire stories, and watching the Perseid meteor shower on a camping trip last year. She also named her youngest daughter's first steps as a moment she will never forget. Caroline celebrated these milestones with her.

Several threads remain open. Caroline is still pursuing adoption through an agency that supports LGBTQ+ adoptive parents and plans to raise a child as a single parent. The council meeting strengthened her resolve. Her children's library may be tied to this plan, though she has not said so directly. She is exploring counseling and mental health work, especially supporting trans people, but has not named a specific program or job. She has not mentioned piano since session five and is still considering further education. Her advocacy has grown through the July conference, her mentoring role, and the new activist group, and her August art show extends that work into painting. She sees her friends and family as the foundation of her transition.

Melanie has built regular me-time into her routine, started pottery she finds therapeutic, and takes longer runs in new shoes. Painting and pottery with her kids bring her peace, and she remains a devoted mother and wife, with beach days, camping, hikes, and her pets central to her life. Both see self-care, community, and family as central to how they want to live. Melanie affirms Caroline's path toward counseling, adoption, and mentoring, and Caroline cheers on Melanie's running, pottery, painting, and family life.

Calvin and Dave are friends who chat periodically, share photos, and trade news about their work and hobbies. Calvin's messages are enthusiastic and often exaggerated, full of exclamations, "so cool," and references to dreams coming true. In October they became more repetitive, leaning on "awesome" and "you got this." Dave's messages are warmer and more measured, centered on cars, restoration, parks, photography, and his band. Both usually congratulate each other before turning to their own lives, and both close by offering encouragement or proposing a time to meet. Across twenty-eight sessions from March to November 2023, their conversations moved from life changes and travel plans to music careers, car projects, and plans to see each other in Boston.

In March, Calvin announced a major life change, shared a photo of his new mansion, and said he was heading to Japan in April before going on to Boston. Dave said having a place to stay was key, and Calvin promised to visit. On 26 March, Calvin said he had bought a red sports car that made him feel like a rockstar, and Dave said his favorite band was Aerosmith. On 20 April, Calvin described a Tokyo music event where a producer advised him to stay true to himself. Dave offered to show him the Boston music scene, including Paradise Rock Club, House of Blues, Fenway Park, and classic cars, and they agreed to share a meal there.

On 1 May, Dave announced he had opened his own car maintenance shop, a step toward working on classic cars, and invited Calvin to visit. On 3 May, he said he was teaming up with a local garage. Calvin said long drives helped him relax but his creativity felt frozen, so Dave suggested immersing himself in music he loved. On 16 May, Calvin reported that his home had flooded the previous week. He had saved his music gear and favorite microphone, but repairs were waiting on insurance, and Dave offered help. The exact date of Dave's shop opening is unclear across sessions. On 31 May, Calvin said touring with Frank Ocean had been wild and that he was excited to perform in Boston for people from home. The two agreed that fixing things was therapeutic.

On 9 June, Calvin met with the creative team for his album. Dave had booked a mountain trip for July, and Calvin said he could not wait to visit Boston. On 21 June, Calvin described a small car accident in which no one was hurt, and he shared a photo of a small Japanese town with a mountain behind it that he hoped to visit. Dave said he had recently joined a rock band. On 7 July, Calvin said his car was fixed and that he was working on collaborations with Japanese artists, and Dave said he hoped to visit Japan one day. On 21 July, Dave returned from a road trip that reminded him why he loved cars. Calvin described turning his mansion into a recording studio, a long-held dream.

On 3 August, Calvin said he had taken his Ferrari in for service, which was stressful because he was attached to it. On 11 August, Dave said he had been picked for a car mod workshop and was working on a classic muscle car. Dave offered to help with Calvin's music work, and Calvin politely said he was too busy. On 14 August, Dave said he had attended a car restoration workshop in San Francisco, and Calvin said he had recently toured with a well-known artist, ending with a show in Japan. On 22 August, Calvin announced a deal to keep collaborating with Frank Ocean, which he called a dream come true. He said they had met at a Tokyo music festival and recorded a song at his mansion, and that his tour was ending and he was heading to Boston. On 31 August, Calvin said he had started shooting a video for his album on a Miami beach, and Dave offered help with props.

On 2 September, Dave said he had returned from San Francisco and found giving old cars new life deeply satisfying. Calvin shared a boarding pass for his flight to Boston, and they agreed to catch up there. On 13 September, Calvin apologized for the gap and said his album had dropped on the 11th, with a tour next, though he did not name cities. Dave said he would love to show Calvin his garage, and Calvin said he would take him up on it. On 15 September, Dave said he and his band had been jamming. On 22 September, Dave said a vintage Mustang engine he thought he had fixed made a weird noise. Calvin said his trip to Japan had been incredible and that he was already longing to go back, which sits awkwardly with his earlier descriptions of living there. He also named "California Love" as a song he used to sing with his dad. Dave suggested a jam session, and Calvin agreed.

The October sessions add new detail, some of it inconsistent. On 4 October, Calvin said he had met incredible artists in Boston the day before. Dave said he was restoring a Ford Mustang found in a junkyard, which differs from the noisy-engine Mustang he described in September. On 8 October, Dave said he had restored and modified a car himself at a car show, and that restoration was now his job, a goal since childhood. On 15 October, Dave said a competing shop had won a deal his team had pursued for months, and he asked whether he was wasting his time. Calvin encouraged him to keep pushing. Calvin also announced a new black Ferrari. On 19 October, Calvin said he had started touring with Frank Ocean and shared stage photos, including one from a Tokyo concert. He said he had first met Frank at a festival in August of the previous year, which conflicts with his earlier account of a Tokyo festival that August. He planned to head to Tokyo next month after the tour, mentioning Shibuya Crossing, Shinjuku, and ramen.

On 23 October, Dave asked how the tour was going and how Calvin balanced fame with his personal life. Calvin said the tour was energizing but sometimes overwhelming, and that friends and team kept him on track. He said struggles people face pushed him to dig deeper into his music, which he called his own form of therapy. Dave said cars were his oasis of calm and shared a photo of his tidy garage. He explained that his interest began at ten, when he asked to fix an old car in a neighbor's garage. He said he had restored a car the year before and sold it to a collector, and he was now working on a black car. He called patience and attention to detail the hardest parts of restoration, and Calvin compared that to crafting a well-made rap song. The session also featured concert photos, and Dave closed by hoping to see Calvin soon.

On 25 October, Calvin said he had had a great time in Boston the day before with a high school friend. Dave recommended a spot for admiring nature and mentioned a conference in Detroit that taught him a lot. He said he was now an automotive engineer, and he traced his start to his father taking him to his first car show at ten. That is a different origin from the neighbor's-garage story he gave two days earlier. Calvin shared a photo of himself performing as a DJ with someone he admired, calling it a dream come true and a reminder that music was his passion and purpose. The two agreed to keep inspiring each other.

On 29 October, Calvin said he had attended a networking event to meet more artists, which he hoped would grow his fan base. Dave, who said he had recently become interested in photography, shared a sunset photo of a Boston skyline with a clock tower, taken the previous month. Calvin said he had visited Boston a few years earlier. Dave said he had just finished restoring his car project and invited Calvin to see it. Calvin said his album was almost finished and promised previews, which conflicts with the September release. He asked to catch up when Dave was free.

On 2 November, Calvin said that the previous week he had thrown a party at his Japanese house to celebrate his new album, and he shared photos of guests dancing and a crowd on a stage. Dave congratulated him and asked what it was like to be cheered on. Dave then said he had started a blog about car mods and asked for tips. He shared photos of a blue Subaru he had modified, said the blog had inspired readers to start DIY projects, and described the labor of polishing its headlights. He also said he had found a red car in bad shape the previous week and spent a long time restoring it. He shared the logo of a rock band he had long admired and had joined. Calvin showed his recording studio and a relaxation room with a TV, saying he mostly watches music videos, concerts, and documentaries about artists. Dave said he writes lyrics in a notebook, listens to vinyl while working on cars, and has been getting into classic rock. He then signed off to return to work, and Calvin wished him luck.

Several things changed over time. In March, Calvin was planning a move to Japan and then Boston. By April he was in Tokyo, and by mid-May he was performing there. His home flooded in May. He described touring with Frank Ocean at different points, and the timing is inconsistent across sessions. By June he was working on an album, and by summer he described his Japanese mansion as both home and studio. In August he referred to a Ferrari, which may or may not be the red sports car he showed in September. By late August he had a continuing collaboration deal with Frank Ocean, was filming in Miami, and had booked a flight to Boston. His album was released on 11 September, yet in late October he still described it as nearly finished, and in early November he celebrated its release at a party in Japan. In October he said he had met artists in Boston, bought a black Ferrari, and started a tour.

Dave's life also developed. In March he was enjoying parks, car events, and a Boston music festival. In May he teamed up with a local garage and opened his own shop, though the shop is not mentioned again after July, when he described corporate demands at work that sit uneasily with owning a shop. In July he took a road trip and joined a rock band. In August he was selected for a car mod workshop and attended a San Francisco restoration workshop. In September he was rehearsing with his band and troubleshooting a Mustang. In October he restored a junkyard Mustang, described restoration as his job, lost a business deal to a competitor, and took up photography. By late October he was an automotive engineer who had attended a conference in Detroit, and in early November he had started a car mod blog.

Throughout the conversations, Calvin focused on music, collaborations, touring, cars, and reaching a global audience, while Dave focused on cars, restoration, parks, music festivals, photography, and his band. Both encouraged each other through photos and messages.

Several plans remain open. Dave offered to show Calvin around Boston, and Calvin hoped they would share a meal when he arrived, though he has not confirmed that visit after his October Boston meetings and his visit the day before 25 October. Dave invited Calvin to see his garage and finished car, and Calvin said he would take him up on it. Calvin promised to share album previews, podcast, and collaboration news, and hoped to try skiing and visit the Japanese mountain town. He planned to be in Tokyo in November and said he would share a photo of his new Ferrari. Dave offered help with props for the Miami video and wants to visit Japan one day. The two planned a jam session together, and Calvin said he would let Dave know when he was free for a catch-up.

SUMMARY

Caroline and Melanie are close friends who check in with each other across sessions from May to August 2023. Caroline is a transgender woman who moved from Sweden about four years before June 2023 and began transitioning about three years before then. Her friends, mentors, and support network have been central to her wellbeing, including after a painful breakup. Melanie is a mother whose family is her main motivation. Her household includes her husband, her kids (one of whom had a birthday concert in August 2023), a dog named Luna, and a cat named Oliver.

In May 2023, Caroline said an LGBTQ support group made her feel accepted and gave her courage to embrace herself. She wanted to pursue counseling or mental health work. She was also researching adoption agencies, a long-held dream, and chose one that helps LGBTQ+ people adopt. Melanie ran a charity race for mental health and described it as rewarding. Her family was planning a camping trip the following month.

In June 2023, Caroline spoke at a school about her transgender journey and encouraged students to join the LGBTQ community. It made her reflect on how far she had come. On 9 June, Caroline said she had known these friends for four years, and Melanie replied that it had been five. On 27 June, Caroline showed a necklace from her grandmother in Sweden, made by a friend for her 18th birthday. She had attended an LGBTQ+ counseling workshop and was considering working with trans people on self-acceptance and mental health.

In early July 2023, Caroline attended a pride parade, which made her feel she belonged. Melanie signed up for a pottery class, which she called therapy. Caroline was building a children's library for her future kids and looked forward to a transgender conference that month. On 12 July, she said an LGBTQ conference two days earlier had been special, and that support had helped her through her own mental health struggles. On 15 July, Melanie said she and her kids had made pots at a pottery workshop. Caroline had attended an adoption council meeting, which made her more determined to adopt. She said the best part of pride was being herself without fear.

On 17 July, Caroline said she had joined a mentorship program for LGBTQ youth and was mentoring a transgender teen, helping them build confidence. She said she would hold an LGBTQ art show with her paintings the following month. Her painting of a tree with a bright sun was inspired by a visit to an LGBTQ center and meant to capture unity and strength. Melanie said she and her kids had finished another painting.

On 20 July, Caroline said she had joined a new LGBTQ activist group, "Connected LGBTQ Activists," which holds regular meetings, plans events, and runs campaigns. Melanie described a beach trip with the kids and said family camping was the highlight of their summer.

On 14 August 2023, Melanie said the family had celebrated her daughter's birthday with a concert by Matt Patterson the night before. Caroline said she had attended a pride parade the previous Friday and felt pushed to keep fighting for LGBTQ rights. She shared her paintings, including "Embracing Identity," about comfort, love, and self-acceptance. She said art had helped her work through her transition and her changing body, and had taught her to accept imperfection.

On 17 August, Caroline said a recent hike had gone badly when she met religious conservatives who upset her, and that supportive friends were helping her cope. Melanie said she had finished another pottery project. Melanie then suggested a family outing this summer. Caroline offered either a family outing or a trip just the two of them to explore nature. Both agreed to plan something special, but no date or format had been set.

Across the sessions, Caroline's life moved from exploring careers to adoption research, then to active mentoring, activism, and art about her trans experience. Melanie's life stayed centered on her family, her charity and self-care efforts, and creative outlets such as painting, pottery, and music.
