He was rehearsing new dance routines for an upcoming show and shared a photo of a woman in a gray dress doing a trick. He said he was getting ready for a dance competition near him "next month," which would be March 2023, and hoped to earn respect from the dance community. Gina encouraged him throughout, saying setbacks are just opportunities for comebacks, and he said he would not give up.

Deborah and Jolene are two women who have each lost their mothers. They have been chatting since 23 January 2023, when they first met. Deborah is a yoga teacher whose goal is to keep teaching and supporting her community. She is passionate about helping people find peace and joy through yoga, which helped her through a rough time and inspired her to share it with others. Jolene is an electrical engineer. Her mother passed away in 2022. She finished a demanding electrical engineering project in the week before their first chat.

In the first session, on 23 January 2023 at 4:06 pm, Deborah said she had visited her late mother's old house, which holds many memories for her. Her mother passed away a few years earlier. Deborah shared a photo of what she called their last photo together, showing her mother hugging her, with both of them in wheelchairs. Her mother had a special bench near the window where she liked to sit every morning and take in the view. Deborah sometimes sits on that bench herself because it helps her stay connected to her mother. She also has a pendant that reminds her of her mother. Deborah ended that session early, saying she had to run. Jolene shared a photo of her room in her mother's house, which has a bench and a window, and said she has many memories of that room. She wears a heart-shaped pendant with a bird on it, which her mother gave her in 2010 in Paris, and it reminds her of her mother. Her jewelry also has a symbol that represents freedom for her, a reminder to pursue her goals and not be held back. Jolene was enthusiastic about Deborah's yoga work and said she was looking forward to the next chat. Both women keep a physical connection to their mothers: Deborah through her mother's bench and pendant, and Jolene through her mother's room and pendant. Both have described a mother-linked bench and a pendant as meaningful keepsakes.

In the second session, on the morning of 27 January 2023 at 9:49 am, Deborah told Jolene that her father had passed away two days earlier, around 25 January. His sudden death left the whole family shell-shocked. Deborah said she was channeling her grief by spending more time with family and cherishing memories, which remind her to live life fully. She shared a photo of a woman hugging another woman seated on a couch. Jolene offered condolences and asked how the family was coping. Deborah said looking back on good memories is comforting, and that the family had been going through the family album. Photos give her peace in hard times. She shared a photo of her parents' wedding in 1993, a bride and groom posing together, and said she and her husband are trying to be as good a family as her parents were. When Jolene asked what she valued in her relationship, Deborah said love and openness have kept her and her husband close over the years, and that being there for each other has made them both happy. Deborah then shared a photo of a handwritten note she had received the day before from her group members, thanking her for the positive influence she had on them. She said moments like that remind her why she is so passionate about yoga.

Asked where she most often practices yoga, Deborah shared a photo of a living room with a television and a window. She said it is one of the places she practices, and that it is her old home, which she visits now and then for her mother, who has passed. Sitting in the spot by the window gives her peace, and she feels her mother's presence there, which comforts her. She then shared a photo of a window seat in a room with a window. Deborah said her mother would sit there every night with a book and a smile, since reading was one of her hobbies, and it was one of her favorite places in the house. The first session had described her mother sitting on the bench every morning to take in the view, so the bench was used both in the morning and at night. Deborah also said travel was her mother's great passion, and she shared a photo of a view of the sky from an airplane window to illustrate it.

Jolene then introduced her pets, which calm her down and make her happy. She shared a photo of a bed with a snake's head poking out, of her snake named Susie. Deborah said having a pet brightens life and asked for a fun moment with Jolene's pet. Jolene described how her second snake, Seraphim, slinked out of its cage and coiled up next to her while she was playing video games, which she found very funny. She shared a photo of Seraphim peeking out of a blanket with its sly eyes, and said she bought Seraphim a year earlier in Paris. Deborah said pets bring so much happiness, and Jolene called snakes very unusual pets. Jolene then shared a photo of herself and her partner gaming the previous week, with a dog watching TV beside them. She said they are both crazy about playing the game "Detroit" on a console. Deborah asked whether her boyfriend had taught her to play. Jolene said that even as a child she learned to play on her own. When Deborah asked whether she played only old games or tried new ones, Jolene said she and her partner planned to play "The Walking Dead" next Saturday. Deborah closed by telling Jolene to take care and keep spreading good vibes, and Jolene said goodbye.

In the third session, on 1 February 2023 at 7:03 pm, Jolene said she had been busy because her engineering professor had given her class a huge robotics project. She called it tough but fun, and said it was making her get creative and problem-solve. She shared a photo of a table with a robot on it and a laptop. When she first received the project she felt a mix of excitement and nervousness, but she now really enjoys it. She described it as like solving a puzzle, figuring out the best design and programming, and said seeing the robot come together is awesome. Deborah said she met her new neighbor Anna the previous day, 31 January, and shared a photo of a yellow sign with a picture of a family. They met at yoga in the park. Deborah said they talked about how yoga has improved their lives and the sense of community it gives. Jolene said it is great to connect with people who share similar interests. She then shared a photo of a purse with a plant on a table. Deborah asked whether Jolene had ever thought about resuming yoga. Jolene replied that she and her partner had planned to play the console together. Deborah said it is good that Jolene has something to do with her partner, and Jolene thanked her for the kind words. Deborah then said she had to run, and Jolene said she would see her soon. Like the first session, Deborah ended this one abruptly.

In the fourth session, on 4 February 2023 at 9:48 am, Jolene said she had been on an emotional rollercoaster lately but was coping. She said she had a major milestone the previous week that went really well, leaving her relieved and proud, and it was a huge accomplishment for her as an engineer. She had planned, researched, and designed a sustainable water purifier for a rural community in need, and building it was tough but she loved the experience. Seeing it work and provide clean water to the community was a surreal and deeply satisfying moment. It reminded her that engineering can make a difference in people's lives, and it made her feel she had a purpose and had done something good. Her career aspiration is to keep working in engineering and make a positive impact on communities in need through sustainable solutions, contributing to a better world. She said Deborah's encouragement motivates her to pursue her passions and that she is determined to keep going. Deborah told Jolene to take a deep breath and remember why she does this, and said she spends a lot of her time teaching yoga, which is a great way to find balance and reconnect with ourselves. Deborah said she bonded with Anna during the previous day's yoga class, which was 3 February, and shared a photo of two women in a dance studio doing a dance pose. She said they were trying different dance poses, including Warrior II, which builds strength and boosts focus, and shared a photo of a woman doing a yoga pose on a chair. Jolene asked whether it was difficult, and Deborah said yes, but it brought them closer and they supported each other. Deborah then described a modified pose: sit on the edge of a chair with feet planted, twist the torso to one side with a hand on the knee for support, hold for a few breaths, then switch sides, which stretches the back and shoulders and relaxes tense muscles. Jolene said it sounded hard and shared a photo of her bookshelf full of books. She said she is really into "Sapiens," a fascinating look at human history and how technology has affected us. Two weeks before this session she read "Avalanche" by Neal Stephenson in one sitting. She also mentioned a recent story about someone who became successful despite many challenges, which showed her that anything is possible with belief and hard work. Deborah said that story reminded her of someone special and their grace and strength through hardships. Deborah then shared a photo of a bouquet of flowers in a vase on a table. She said a friend gave her the bouquet when she was struggling, and it gives her hope and courage and fills her with warmth and appreciation. Jolene said such a small thing can make a real difference. Asked about her favorite nature spots, Deborah named a park with a forest trail, where getting lost in nature is calming, and a nearby beach where the sound of waves and sand underfoot make her feel peaceful and happy. Jolene shared a photo of a person walking on a beach with a surfboard, from a vacation in Bogota last summer, where watching the sunset over the water was beautiful and calming. Deborah said she likes to come to a spot by the water near her mom's old house to reflect on her mother's life and find peace, and she shared a photo of a small island with a lone boat in the water. Jolene asked about her traditions there. Deborah said she brings an amulet that belonged to her mother whenever she visits, because holding it lets her feel her mother's love and stay close to her, and she shared a photo of herself wearing a white shirt and a gold chain necklace. Jolene remarked how something so small can have such a big impact, and Deborah said such things remind us of the love and strength we carry inside and connect us to people we have lost. Jolene said they keep those people close in our hearts every day. Deborah added that Anna also wears a pendant in memory of her mother, which also brought them closer. Jolene said such reminders are a source of strength when needed. Deborah closed by telling Jolene that life is tough but to hang in there, look to her sources of strength, stay in touch, take care of herself, and know Deborah is always there to cheer her on. Jolene said she would stay in touch and said goodbye, and Deborah replied "Stay safe!" and said goodbye.

Gina and Jon are friends who have talked in person and online since January 2023. The record now runs through fourteen sessions, the most recent on 16 June 2023. They discuss their careers, their love of dance, and the businesses each is building. Both lost their jobs in January 2023: Jon was a banker, and Gina worked at DoorDash. Since then, each has built a business while staying close to dance and supporting the other. Jon is building a dance studio, and Gina is building a clothing business. Their talks are warm and encouraging, and they usually close with a promise to keep pushing forward together.

The first conversation took place in person on 20 January 2023, at about 4:04 pm. Jon said he had lost his banking job the day before, on 19 January, and planned to start a dance studio. He has loved dancing since childhood and sees it as both his passion and his escape. He wants to open the studio to teach others the joy dance brings him. He loves all dance styles but names contemporary as his favorite. His dance crew took first place at a local competition in 2022. He described his ideal studio as one by the water with an ocean view and yoga mats. He rehearses after work with a small group of dancers who perform everything from contemporary to hip-hop, and he was finishing choreography for a February 2023 festival performance.

Gina also lost her job at DoorDash in January 2023. Dance is her main stress relief, and she loves contemporary dance for being expressive and graceful. She has competed in several dance competitions and shows. Her favorite memory is her team winning first place at a regional competition when she was fifteen, performing a contemporary piece called "Finding Freedom."

During that conversation, Jon invited Gina to see his moves at a dance session "next Friday," and she agreed. They also talked about taking a dance class together. The date of that Friday was never specified. The most likely date is 27 January 2023, but the record does not confirm that the session happened, nor whether the dance class was ever taken.

On 29 January 2023, at about 2:32 pm, they chatted online. Gina said things had been hectic because she had launched an ad campaign to grow her clothing store. Jon said he was still searching for a studio space but had found one with great natural light. He said he had been to Paris "yesterday," which would be 28 January. Gina said she had never visited Paris and had only been to Rome once. Jon said the space he was considering is downtown and that he still needed to check its size and floor quality. He prefers Marley flooring, which is grippy but still lets dancers move and is easy to clean. Gina agreed that Marley sounded perfect. Jon described the search as a mix of exciting and nerve-wracking.

On 1 February 2023, at about 12:48 am, they chatted again. Jon said his dance journey had been bumpy, but he was determined to make it work. Gina said a wholesaler she had emailed had agreed that same day to work with her, which meant she could expand her store. She shared a photo of a shopping mall with a glass entrance, which she presented as the store's new spot. She also shared a photo of a clothing store she had designed, which she described as cozy and inviting, with a chandelier for a glam feel. Jon said he believed she could create the space she imagined.

On 4 February 2023, at about 10:43 am, they chatted again. Gina said her store was doing great and called running it a wild ride. Jon said some days did not go his way, but he was sure that if he kept pushing he would reach his dreams. Gina told him setbacks are opportunities for comebacks. Jon said searching for a studio location had been tricky, and he was rehearsing hard for a dance competition in March 2023, which he saw as a chance to earn respect from the dance community. He shared a photo of a woman in a gray dress doing a trick, and the record does not say who she is.

On 8 February 2023, at about 9:32 am, they chatted again. Gina shared a photo of women posing with a giant balloon, saying she had teamed up with a local artist for designs for her store. Jon said he had already performed at the festival and that many people had complimented his moves. Asked his favorite part of running his own studio, he answered as though it were already running. He loves the freedom to create a space and help dancers of all ages express themselves. Jon said taking risks had gotten him out of his secure 9-to-5 as a banker, and Gina said taking risks is scary but is the only way to grow. Gina showed a photo of a tattoo inspired by a quote about fear, which stands for dancing without worrying what people think. Jon also shared a photo of a trophy with a glass globe on top during this exchange. That trophy matters for a later session.

On 16 March 2023, at about 2:35 pm, they chatted again in a new session. Jon said he had started going to the gym the previous week to stay on track. Gina said she had been having tough times since losing her DoorDash job, but her online clothing store was now open, and she wanted to blend her love of dance and fashion. Jon congratulated her and said losing his job had been hard, but he was living his dreams now. Jon said it helps that they both face the same challenges, and he raised a toast to new heights.

On 23 March 2023, at about 7:28 pm, in what the record labels Session 7, Gina said her online store had been a roller coaster but rewarding, and she asked for tips. Jon advised her that brand identity is key, that she should build relationships with customers, and that her positive energy would be contagious. Asked what keeps him motivated with his studio, Jon said seeing his students succeed does. He shared a photo of a group of women doing a dance routine, which he described as a photo of the two of them from one of the dance classes, though the image shows only the women dancing. This session speaks of dance classes and students as current, but the record does not confirm that a studio location was ever secured.

He was also hosting a dance competition the following month to showcase local talent, and he asked whether Gina would come. She said she was definitely in.

Jon has returned that support with thanks and his own determination. Jon and Gina are friends who catch up in person and by message, and both love dance. Both lost their jobs in January 2023 and turned to building their own businesses. Across eleven sessions from January to 11 May 2023, their conversations have stayed warm and encouraging, and each has been a steady source of support for the other.

Jon lost his job as a banker on 19 January 2023 and decided to start a dance studio. He has loved dance since childhood and sees it as both his passion and his escape. His favorite style is contemporary, though he enjoys all styles. His ideal studio is a space by the water with an ocean view and yoga mats, but he has not found it. On 8 February he said leaving his secure job had pushed him to grow, though the path "ain't been a walk in the park." On 3 April he said shutting his bank account was tough but necessary. On 11 May he described the studio as a dream he is finally pursuing, said he is "stepping into the unknown and hoping for the best," and said dance is his stress-buster and where he feels most alive.

Jon's location search has been a major thread. On 29 January he found a downtown place with great natural light, but he still needed to check its size and floor quality. He wants a bouncy Marley floor for safe movement, and Gina agreed good floors help prevent injuries. On 4 February he said the right spot would come. No location has been confirmed in any session, including the most recent on 11 May. On 8 February, 9 April, and 11 May he used present-tense or hopeful language about the studio without naming a venue, so it is still unclear whether the studio is open or whether he was describing his hopes.

Jon dances with a small crew he rehearses with after work, performing everything from contemporary to hip-hop. The crew won first place in a local competition in 2022. In February 2023 he prepared choreography for dancers at a nearby festival, which went well. On 4 February he mentioned a March 2023 competition near him, but nothing confirms he entered. On 3 April he said he was hosting his own competition the following month to showcase local talent, with his studio and other schools taking part, and he invited Gina, who said she was definitely coming. No venue was named, and the 11 May session did not mention it, so whether it is still going ahead is unknown. On 11 May Jon said he had been practicing routines because they keep his mind focused, and he offered to send Gina a video. Gina agreed to watch it.

Gina also lost her job at DoorDash in January 2023. She used to compete in dance competitions and shows, and her favorite memory is her team's first place at a regional competition when she was fifteen, performing a contemporary piece called "Finding Freedom." Dance is her main stress reliever, and on 11 May she said it is "like air" to her. Her freedom tattoo means dancing without worrying what people think.

Gina chose to start her own clothing business rather than look for another job. On 29 January she launched an ad campaign and called the venture scary and rewarding. On 1 February a wholesaler agreed to work with her, which is confirmed, and she proposed a glass-entrance shopping mall as a new location, though expansion timing is unknown. On 8 February she teamed up with a local artist for new designs. By 16 March her online store was open, though whether a physical store has expanded is not stated. On 3 April she launched new offers and promotions that were bringing more sales, and on 25 April she shared a sale ad from her online store. On 11 May she mentioned a design internship interview the day before, calling it "so cool" and saying it went great. It is not stated whether she got the role or whether the clothing business continues alongside it.

The two have encouraged each other throughout. On 8 February Gina urged Jon not to stop dreaming. On 16 March Jon said he had started going to the gym to stay on track and that Gina's success inspired him. Gina said she wanted to blend her love of dance and fashion. On 23 March Jon said he was "gonna make it happen," and when Gina asked for business advice, he suggested a strong brand identity, customer relationships, and staying positive. On 9 April he said his students were "killing it" and that he had learned his own happiness matters most.

On 25 April Jon said he had gone to a fair to show off his studio. It was stressful and great, and he got some possible leads, though whether they became deals was never stated. He felt low on confidence at times, and Gina advised him to keep his big goal in mind, lean on supporters, and dance out stress. On 11 May Gina again expressed confidence in his determination and said his studio would give people a place to express themselves through dance, which Jon said was a long-held dream.

Both have been working toward their goals while leaning on each other. Gina's love of contemporary dance remains central to her identity, and her online store is her main active venture, now alongside a design internship interview. Jon's dance life remains active, with classes, workshops, a hosted competition, and regular practice, though his studio still has no confirmed location. Open questions include whether Jon's studio has a physical home and when it will open, whether the fair leads became business, whether he entered the March 2023 competition, whether his May competition is happening, whether the dance session planned for 27 January 2023 took place, whether the video routine has been sent, whether Gina got the internship, and whether her physical store has expanded.

The memory covers nine conversations between Calvin and Dave, from their first meeting on 23 March 2023 through a ninth session on 21 June 2023.

In the first session, at 11:53 am on 23 March 2023, Calvin and Dave met for the first time. Dave said things had been going well and that he had recently attended a car event full of classic cars, where he spoke with owners and heard their stories. Calvin said he had just gone through a big life change and shared a photo of his new mansion, a building with a sign on its front. He framed the change around learning about Japanese culture and getting a chance to expand. Calvin has never been to Japan and is fascinated by its traditions. He planned to leave for Japan in April 2023. His agent found him a place to stay there, and he shared a photo of its cozy living room with a couch, table, and television. In Japan he planned to explore the city, try local cuisines, and perhaps collaborate with local musicians. He would stay a few months and then travel to Boston. Dave had been spending a lot of time at a beautiful, calming park with a lake and a few boats, and he shared a photo of it. Calvin had never been there but said he would check it out when he returned. Dave offered more recommendations if Calvin needed them, and they ended by wishing each other well for the trip.

The second session took place at 4:45 pm on 26 March 2023. Calvin said it had been a few days since they last talked and announced that he had just bought a new car, a luxury car he described as a long-held dream come true. He called it smooth and powerful, said driving it made him feel like a rockstar, and said it was what he deserved after all his hard work. He shared a photo of a red sports car parked on the side of the road, taken on 25 March when he first took it for a ride. He did not name the car's make or model when Dave asked. Calvin also said he was on cloud nine. Dave reported that he was doing well and that the previous weekend (around 18 to 19 March) he had gone to a music festival in Boston, which he loved and which reminded him why he loves music. He shared a photo of a large crowd at a concert. Dave said his favorite band there was Aerosmith, whose performance he found incredible. He shared two photos: one of a concert stage with a large eagle, and one of two people on stage with guitars and a microphone. He said he had finally seen them live and that the singer was jamming to one of their hits. Dave said he did not get to hang out with the band after the show. When Dave asked about news in Calvin's life, Calvin said he had got a new ride, had written some new tunes, and had had several studio sessions the previous week. He said he was excited to collaborate and would share the music with everyone once it was ready. He promised to keep Dave updated on how the collaborations went, and the two signed off by wishing each other well and staying safe.

The third session took place at 4:15 pm on 20 April 2023. Calvin said it had been a long time since they had seen each other and reported that he had just been to a music festival in Tokyo, which he called awesome. He did not see any bands there, but he met many talented artists and industry people, and he found the experience enriching. He said he learned a lot and got valuable advice from professionals in the music industry. A producer told him to stay true to himself and sound unique, which got him thinking about where he wants his music to go. His long-term dream is to tour the world, performing for different people and connecting with them, and he hopes his music can reach a global audience and make an impact. He said he was looking forward to an upcoming trip to Boston after he finishes the Frank Ocean tour, and he had heard the music scene there is awesome. Dave responded enthusiastically and offered to show Calvin around Boston and its cool spots. He recommended Paradise Rock, House of Blues, and Fenway Park as places with a great music scene, and said he would be in the front row whenever Calvin performed onstage. Dave shared a photo of a city skyline with a boat in the water, which Calvin admired. Dave also said that the previous weekend (around 15 to 16 April) he had gone to a car show, where he found classic cars charming and admired the dedication people put into restoring them. This is why he is so into auto engineering. He shared a photo of a green Mustang parked in a field of grass. Calvin replied that the car looked great and shared a photo of a red sports car on display at a show, saying he had put a lot of work into it and could not wait to see more cars in Boston. This red car appears to be the same sports car Calvin bought in March, now shown at an event. When Dave asked whether Calvin had seen anything in Boston beyond the gigs, Calvin said not yet, because he had been busy with rehearsals and traveling, but he was looking forward to exploring the city, trying delicious food, and visiting popular attractions. He suggested they grab a bite together when he arrives, and Dave agreed to share his favorite spots in the city. The conversation ended with both expressing excitement about meeting in Boston and seeing each other soon.

The fourth session took place at 6:24 pm on 1 May 2023, and it was a longer, more upbeat exchange in which Dave shared big news about his career. He said it had been a long time since they last talked and announced that he had finally opened his own car maintenance shop, which he described as a dream come true and a spot to work on cars that he finds deeply satisfying. He shared a photo of a car dealership with cars parked in front of it. Calvin congratulated him and shared a photo of a man standing under a car in a garage. Dave thanked him, said the shop had been his dream and that it took a lot of hard work, but that it was worth it. Calvin praised his guts and ambition and shared a photo of a book with a space theme on its cover. Dave said the shop is a step toward his other dream of working on classic cars, which he loves for their design and engineering. Calvin shared a photo of a red car parked in a parking lot and said that going for classic cars was cool. Dave said he is obsessed with classic cars because of their unique charm, and that last year he had been thrilled to restore one, which he called a labor of love that was challenging but worth it. He shared a photo of the restored car's engine, which has a small air filter. Calvin said it looked awesome, and the two exchanged a series of messages about how satisfying it is to see something you worked on come back to life and to see hard work pay off. Dave then shared a photo of his shop, a group of people standing in front of a car, and invited Calvin to come by if he could. Calvin said he would love to visit and asked what cars Dave works on. Dave said he works on all kinds of cars, from regular maintenance to full restorations of classic cars, and that he finds it rewarding to see transformations and to know he is helping people keep their cars in good condition. Calvin encouraged him to keep up the great work. Calvin then shared a photo of a gold necklace with a diamond pendant and called it stunning. When Dave asked where he got it, Calvin said it was a gift from another artist and a reminder of why he keeps hustling as a musician. The two closed by encouraging each other to keep pushing, with Calvin saying that they should keep each other motivated.

The fifth session took place at 1:16 pm on 3 May 2023. Dave opened by saying it had been a long time since they talked and announced that he was teaming up with a local garage, sharing a photo of a car being worked on in a garage. Calvin congratulated him, called the news inspiring, and shared a photo of a green car in a garage with a sign in the background. Dave said he was loving the job, getting to work with skilled mechanics and share his knowledge about cars. He shared a photo of a man working on a car engine in a garage, describing it as a cool project that was a bit challenging. Calvin said the car looked awesome and encouraged him to keep up the good work. Dave said he planned to keep learning about auto engineering and hoped to build a custom car from scratch someday, which is his dream. For now he would keep working on the current project and assisting customers. Calvin called him inspiring and told him to relax and enjoy the process. Dave said he needed to take time to chill and asked whether Calvin had hobbies that helped him relax. Calvin said long drives in his red sports car, the one he shared a photo of, really helped him relax, because the wind and open road were freeing and cleared his head. Dave said driving with the wind in your hair was calming and that walking and exploring, taking in the sights and sounds, was a peaceful way for him to destress. Calvin agreed that embracing nature had been calming for him as well, and said he had been loving getting to know Japanese culture. He then admitted that he was stuck with his music, that his creativity felt frozen, and asked for tips. Dave suggested immersing himself in something he loves, such as concerts or favorite albums, which usually jumpstarts his inspiration, and recommended taking a break from music to explore other things and have some fun. Calvin said taking a break was great for getting his mojo back and that he would take the advice and explore. Dave encouraged him to keep pursuing music and never give up. The two agreed to stay in touch, said goodbye, and Calvin signed off with a thank-you.

The sixth session took place at 11:50 am on 16 May 2023, and it was a more mixed exchange. Calvin opened by saying it had been a long time since they chatted and that a lot had happened. He reported that things had not been going smoothly: about a week earlier (around 9 May, "last week") his place had been flooded. He managed to save his music gear and his favorite microphone, and he said it had been tough but he was staying positive and looking forward to getting everything fixed. Dave sympathized, said he was glad the important gear was saved, and offered help. Calvin said he was waiting on insurance to kick in before starting repairs and hoped it would not take long. He shared a photo of his music studio, a room with a keyboard, a synthesizer, and other musical equipment, which he called his creative haven where he pours his heart into music. Dave said the studio looked awesome and hoped it would be fixed soon. Calvin asked Dave about exciting work, and Dave said he had opened his car shop "last week," invited friends over to celebrate, and found it amazing; he said he was stoked to share his passion and help folks with their rides. (This is a little inconsistent with the 1 May session, where Dave first announced the shop's opening.) Calvin congratulated him. Calvin then said he had an upcoming performance in Tokyo "this month" (May 2023) and hoped to show his music to a new crowd and expand his following. Dave wished him luck and asked to hear how it went, and Calvin promised to keep him posted. Calvin then shared a photo of a city at night full of lights, saying he took it in Tokyo "last night" (15 May) and that the skyline was stunning. Dave said the skyline looked great and that he hoped to visit Tokyo soon, and Calvin encouraged him to visit. Dave said he was adding it to his list.

The seventh session took place at 6:06 pm on 31 May 2023. Calvin opened by saying it had been ages since they chatted and that so much had happened. Deborah and Jolene are two women who have each lost their mothers. They have been chatting since 23 January 2023, when they first met. Deborah is a yoga teacher whose goal is to keep teaching and supporting her community. She is passionate about helping people find peace and joy through yoga, which helped her through a rough time and inspired her to share it with others. Jolene is an electrical engineer. Her mother passed away in 2022. She finished a demanding electrical engineering project in the week before their first chat.

In the first session, on 23 January 2023 at 4:06 pm, Deborah said she had visited her late mother's old house, which holds many memories for her. Her mother passed away a few years earlier. Deborah shared a photo of what she called their last photo together, showing her mother hugging her, with both of them in wheelchairs. Her mother had a special bench near the window where she liked to sit every morning and take in the view. Deborah sometimes sits on that bench herself because it helps her stay connected to her mother. She also has a pendant that reminds her of her mother. Deborah ended that session early, saying she had to run. Jolene shared a photo of her room in her mother's house, which has a bench and a window, and said she has many memories of that room. She wears a heart-shaped pendant with a bird on it, which her mother gave her in 2010 in Paris, and it reminds her of her mother. Her jewelry also has a symbol that represents freedom for her, a reminder to pursue her goals and not be held back. Jolene was enthusiastic about Deborah's yoga work and said she was looking forward to the next chat. Both women keep a physical connection to their mothers: Deborah through her mother's bench and pendant, and Jolene through her mother's room and pendant. Both have described a mother-linked bench and a pendant as meaningful keepsakes.

In the second session, on the morning of 27 January 2023 at 9:49 am, Deborah told Jolene that her father had passed away two days earlier, around 25 January. His sudden death left the whole family shell-shocked. Deborah said she was channeling her grief by spending more time with family and cherishing memories, which remind her to live life fully. She shared a photo of a woman hugging another woman seated on a couch. Jolene offered condolences and asked how the family was coping. Deborah said looking back on good memories is comforting, and that the family had been going through the family album. Photos give her peace in hard times. She shared a photo of her parents' wedding in 1993, a bride and groom posing together, and said she and her husband are trying to be as good a family as her parents were. When Jolene asked what she valued in her relationship, Deborah said love and openness have kept her and her husband close over the years, and that being there for each other has made them both happy. Deborah then shared a photo of a handwritten note she had received the day before from her group members, thanking her for the positive influence she had on them. She said moments like that remind her why she is so passionate about yoga.

Asked where she most often practices yoga, Deborah shared a photo of a living room with a television and a window. She said it is one of the places she practices, and that it is her old home, which she visits now and then for her mother, who has passed. Sitting in the spot by the window gives her peace, and she feels her mother's presence there, which comforts her. She then shared a photo of a window seat in a room with a window. Deborah said her mother would sit there every night with a book and a smile, since reading was one of her hobbies, and it was one of her favorite places in the house. The first session had described her mother sitting on the bench every morning to take in the view, so the bench was used both in the morning and at night. Deborah also said travel was her mother's great passion, and she shared a photo of a view of the sky from an airplane window to illustrate it.

Jolene then introduced her pets, which calm her down and make her happy. She shared a photo of a bed with a snake's head poking out, of her snake named Susie. Deborah said having a pet brightens life and asked for a fun moment with Jolene's pet. Jolene described how her second snake, Seraphim, slinked out of its cage and coiled up next to her while she was playing video games, which she found very funny. She shared a photo of Seraphim peeking out of a blanket with its sly eyes, and said she bought Seraphim a year earlier in Paris. Deborah said pets bring so much happiness, and Jolene called snakes very unusual pets. Jolene then shared a photo of herself and her partner gaming the previous week, with a dog watching TV beside them. She said they are both crazy about playing the game "Detroit" on a console. Deborah asked whether her boyfriend had taught her to play. Jolene said that even as a child she learned to play on her own. When Deborah asked whether she played only old games or tried new ones, Jolene said she and her partner planned to play "The Walking Dead" next Saturday. Deborah closed by telling Jolene to take care and keep spreading good vibes, and Jolene said goodbye.

In the third session, on 1 February 2023 at 7:03 pm, Jolene said she had been busy because her engineering professor had given her class a huge robotics project. She called it tough but fun, and said it was making her get creative and problem-solve. She shared a photo of a table with a robot on it and a laptop. When she first received the project she felt a mix of excitement and nervousness, but she now really enjoys it. She described it as like solving a puzzle, figuring out the best design and programming, and said seeing the robot come together is awesome. Deborah said she met her new neighbor Anna the previous day, 31 January, and shared a photo of a yellow sign with a picture of a family. They met at yoga in the park. Deborah said they talked about how yoga has improved their lives and the sense of community it gives. Jolene said it is great to connect with people who share similar interests. She then shared a photo of a purse with a plant on a table. Deborah asked whether Jolene had ever thought about resuming yoga. Jolene replied that she and her partner had planned to play the console together. Deborah said it is good that Jolene has something to do with her partner, and Jolene thanked her for the kind words. Deborah then said she had to run, and Jolene said she would see her soon. Like the first session, Deborah ended this one abruptly.

In the fourth session, on 4 February 2023 at 9:48 am, Jolene said she had been on an emotional rollercoaster lately but was coping. She said she had a major milestone the previous week that went really well, leaving her relieved and proud, and it was a huge accomplishment for her as an engineer. She had planned, researched, and designed a sustainable water purifier for a rural community in need, and building it was tough but she loved the experience. Seeing it work and provide clean water to the community was a surreal and deeply satisfying moment. It reminded her that engineering can make a difference in people's lives, and it made her feel she had a purpose and had done something good. Her career aspiration is to keep working in engineering and make a positive impact on communities in need through sustainable solutions, contributing to a better world. She said Deborah's encouragement motivates her to pursue her passions and that she is determined to keep going. Deborah told Jolene to take a deep breath and remember why she does this, and said she spends a lot of her time teaching yoga, which is a great way to find balance and reconnect with ourselves. Deborah said she bonded with Anna during the previous day's yoga class, which was 3 February, and shared a photo of two women in a dance studio doing a dance pose. She said they were trying different dance poses, including Warrior II, which builds strength and boosts focus, and shared a photo of a woman doing a yoga pose on a chair. Jolene asked whether it was difficult, and Deborah said yes, but it brought them closer and they supported each other. Deborah then described a modified pose: sit on the edge of a chair with feet planted, twist the torso to one side with a hand on the knee for support, hold for a few breaths, then switch sides, which stretches the back and shoulders and relaxes tense muscles. Jolene said it sounded hard and shared a photo of her bookshelf full of books. She said she is really into "Sapiens," a fascinating look at human history and how technology has affected us. Two weeks before this session she read "Avalanche" by Neal Stephenson in one sitting. She also mentioned a recent story about someone who became successful despite many challenges, which showed her that anything is possible with belief and hard work. Deborah said that story reminded her of someone special and their grace and strength through hardships. Deborah then shared a photo of a bouquet of flowers in a vase on a table. She said a friend gave her the bouquet when she was struggling, and it gives her hope and courage and fills her with warmth and appreciation. Jolene said such a small thing can make a real difference. Asked about her favorite nature spots, Deborah named a park with a forest trail, where getting lost in nature is calming, and a nearby beach where the sound of waves and sand underfoot make her feel peaceful and happy. Jolene shared a photo of a person walking on a beach with a surfboard, from a vacation in Bogota last summer, where watching the sunset over the water was beautiful and calming. Deborah said she likes to come to a spot by the water near her mom's old house to reflect on her mother's life and find peace, and she shared a photo of a small island with a lone boat in the water. Jolene asked about her traditions there. Deborah said she brings an amulet that belonged to her mother whenever she visits, because holding it lets her feel her mother's love and stay close to her, and she shared a photo of herself wearing a white shirt and a gold chain necklace. Jolene remarked how something so small can have such a big impact, and Deborah said such things remind us of the love and strength we carry inside and connect us to people we have lost. Jolene said they keep those people close in our hearts every day. Deborah added that Anna also wears a pendant in memory of her mother, which also brought them closer. Jolene said such reminders are a source of strength when needed. Deborah closed by telling Jolene that life is tough but to hang in there, look to her sources of strength, stay in touch, take care of herself, and know Deborah is always there to cheer her on. Jolene said she would stay in touch and said goodbye, and Deborah replied "Stay safe!" and said goodbye.

In the fifth session, on 9 February 2023 at 9:03 pm, Jolene opened by saying it had been a few days since they last talked, and she wanted to share news about a mini retreat she had done the previous Wednesday, most likely 8 February, to assess where she was in life. The retreat gave her a new outlook and a real confidence boost, and she said she achieved far more than she had imagined. Deborah praised her for stepping outside her comfort zone and believing in herself. Jolene said she accomplished something with her engineering project, coming up with some neat solutions that she is excited about, and she said she wanted to look into green tech, which could make a real difference in disadvantaged areas, and see how she could contribute. She then proposed an idea for a volunteer program in which engineers teach STEM to underprivileged kids, and asked Deborah's opinion. Deborah called it a great way to help and inspire others and said the kids would benefit from Jolene's knowledge. Jolene said she had not finished planning, but was considering teaming up with local schools and community centers to run workshops, and possibly inviting engineers as guest speakers to show the kids their career options. Deborah said guest speakers would give the kids a real-world view. Jolene said she had not yet reached out to any schools or centers, because she wanted to solidify the plan first, but she could not wait to start. Deborah said she was excited to hear how it went and asked to be kept informed. Jolene shared a photo of her planner sketches, a notebook with a pen and a page of notes, and thanked Deborah for her support. Deborah offered further tips or information if needed, and Jolene said she would let Deborah know if she needed anything else and called her awesome. Deborah said goodbye with "Take care!" and Jolene replied "Stay safe!"

Audrey and Andrew are friends who chat periodically about their love of animals, nature, and the outdoors. Across the sessions, Audrey's life centers on her dogs and their adventures, while Andrew's search for a dog and a pet-friendly home is a running storyline. Andrew also takes up new outdoor and indoor hobbies over time, and Audrey shares her dog-related activities, recipes, and home life.

On 27 March 2023 at about 1:10 pm, Andrew said he had started a new job as a Financial Analyst the previous week, a big change from his former job. Audrey said she had recently bought new collars and tags for her dogs and sent a photo of them in the grass with their mouths open. The photo showed two dogs, though she named three: Pepper, Precious, and Panda. She had had them for 3 years and said she could not live without them. Audrey lives in the city and described her dogs as city dogs who often explore parks and trails and go on adventures with her very frequently. Andrew said he was a bit jealous of those outings. He had no pets at that time but said he loves animals. His favorite animal is the bird, because he is awed by their ability to soar and explore new places, and his favorite bird is the eagle, which he finds strong and graceful. He shared a photo of two eagles flying against a sun. He had not gone bird-watching on purpose but sees birds when he hikes. He recommended Fox Hollow, a trail he likes for weekend hikes because of its great views. Audrey said she would try Fox Hollow and promised to let Andrew know how she liked it. The conversation ended with both wishing each other well.

On 2 April 2023 at about 2:42 pm, Audrey announced that she and her household had adopted another puppy named Pixie, a small white dog, and shared a photo of herself sitting on a carpet. Andrew asked whether she had checked out Fox Hollow, and Audrey said she had not yet, because Pixie had been keeping them busy. Pixie took a few days to get used to the other dogs but then became good friends with them; they love playing and exploring the house. Audrey shared a photo of Pixie playing with a group of other dogs. She said Pepper took a bit of time to get used to Pixie, but the two are now always together, and she shared a photo of two dogs standing in grass near a fence. Andrew said he was considering getting a dog of his own but found it challenging to find a dog-friendly place in the city, so he asked Audrey for tips. Audrey said she and her family had used websites with filters that helped them find a place that allowed dogs, and that they found a perfect spot through them. She shared a photo of a dog sitting in a field of flowers. Andrew said he would try those websites and hoped to find an apartment and a furry friend soon. He shared a photo of his family's dog on a couch and said he misses exploring nature trails with that dog, recalling hiking photos of the two of them. Audrey shared a photo of one of her dogs lying on a couch with a pillow and said taking dogs on hikes must be awesome and made her want to hike with hers. Andrew shared a photo of a man sitting on a rock with a dog and said hiking with a dog is a great way to bond and make memories. He said he needed to find a dog-friendly spot soon and would keep looking until he found it. Audrey wished him the best, and Andrew said he would keep her posted before saying goodbye.

On 16 April 2023 at 4:19 pm, Andrew said he had missed chatting and that he and his girlfriend (whom he called "my girl") had tried a new cafe in the city the previous weekend. He said it was super fun but that being out of nature is sad for him, because nature is where he feels he really thrives. He misses the peacefulness of hiking and feels connected and restored outdoors, describing nature as a home for his soul. Audrey agreed that nature's beauty and peace are unbeatable compared with concrete jungles, and said that walking her dogs in the park helps her find her center and recharges her. Andrew said he cannot do that in the city, and that he misses the connection and companionship, sometimes feeling like he is missing out. Audrey asked what he likes to do in the city, and he said he and his girlfriend love discovering new places to eat around town, which helps them try new things and unwind after a long week. They had found a cafe with amazing pastries, and he shared a photo of a bakery display with pastries and coffee. They had eaten croissants, muffins, and tarts. Audrey said she had made some of her favorite treats the week before and proposed a pastry party sometime, sharing a photo of a muffin pan filled with blueberries and muffins. Andrew said he would count himself in. Audrey said her dogs would tag along and would love it, and Andrew said he was excited to see all of them together. Audrey shared a photo of a dog running with three other dogs in the background and said she cannot imagine life without her dogs. Andrew said their happy faces must mean a lot to her. Audrey said she had gotten a tattoo of her dogs on her arm a while ago, which also includes sunflowers and represents her love for her pups and nature's beauty. She shared a photo of the tattoo on a woman's arm and a photo of a woman walking with her dogs in the woods. Andrew said the tattoo looked great and asked why she got it. Audrey said she has always had a strong bond with her dogs, that they make her very happy, and that she wants to see their happy faces even when they are not with her. Andrew said he was glad they bring so much joy into her life. Audrey did not mention Fox Hollow in this session, and Andrew's goal of finding a dog-friendly apartment and a furry friend was still unresolved.

On 3 May 2023 at 5:41 pm, Audrey said it had been a long time since they talked and that the previous week she had finally gone on a hike, where she had a memorable encounter with a hummingbird darting around on its wings. She shared a photo of a hummingbird sitting on a branch with its wings spread. Deborah and Jolene are two women who have each lost their mothers. They have been chatting since 23 January 2023, when they first met. Deborah is a yoga teacher whose goal is to keep teaching and supporting her community. She is passionate about helping people find peace and joy through yoga, which helped her through a rough time and inspired her to share it with others. Jolene is an electrical engineer whose mother passed away in 2022. She finished a demanding electrical engineering project in the week before their first chat.

In the first session, on 23 January 2023 at 4:06 pm, Deborah said she had visited her late mother's old house, which holds many memories for her. Her mother passed away a few years earlier. Deborah shared a photo of what she called their last photo together, showing her mother hugging her, with both of them in wheelchairs. Her mother had a special bench near the window where she liked to sit every morning and take in the view. Deborah sometimes sits on that bench herself because it helps her stay connected to her mother. She also has a pendant that reminds her of her mother. Deborah ended that session early, saying she had to run. Jolene shared a photo of her room in her mother's house, which has a bench and a window, and said she has many memories of that room. She wears a heart-shaped pendant with a bird on it, which her mother gave her in 2010 in Paris, and it reminds her of her mother. Her jewelry also has a symbol that represents freedom for her, a reminder to pursue her goals and not be held back. Jolene was enthusiastic about Deborah's yoga work and said she was looking forward to the next chat. Both women keep a physical connection to their mothers: Deborah through her mother's bench and pendant, and Jolene through her mother's room and pendant. Both have described a mother-linked bench and a pendant as meaningful keepsakes.

In the second session, on the morning of 27 January 2023 at 9:49 am, Deborah told Jolene that her father had passed away two days earlier, around 25 January. His sudden death left the whole family shell-shocked. Deborah said she was channeling her grief by spending more time with family and cherishing memories, which remind her to live life fully. She shared a photo of a woman hugging another woman seated on a couch. Jolene offered condolences and asked how the family was coping. Deborah said looking back on good memories is comforting, and that the family had been going through the family album. Photos give her peace in hard times. She shared a photo of her parents' wedding in 1993, a bride and groom posing together, and said she and her husband are trying to be as good a family as her parents were. When Jolene asked what she valued in her relationship, Deborah said love and openness have kept her and her husband close over the years, and that being there for each other has made them both happy. Deborah then shared a photo of a handwritten note she had received the day before from her group members, thanking her for the positive influence she had on them. She said moments like that remind her why she is so passionate about yoga.

Asked where she most often practices yoga, Deborah shared a photo of a living room with a television and a window. She said it is one of the places she practices, and that it is her old home, which she visits now and then for her mother, who has passed. Sitting in the spot by the window gives her peace, and she feels her mother's presence there, which comforts her. She then shared a photo of a window seat in a room with a window. Deborah said her mother would sit there every night with a book and a smile, since reading was one of her hobbies, and it was one of her favorite places in the house. The first session had described her mother sitting on the bench every morning to take in the view, so the bench was used both in the morning and at night. Deborah also said travel was her mother's great passion, and she shared a photo of a view of the sky from an airplane window to illustrate it.

Jolene then introduced her pets, which calm her down and make her happy. She shared a photo of a bed with a snake's head poking out, of her snake named Susie. Deborah said having a pet brightens life and asked for a fun moment with Jolene's pet. Jolene described how her second snake, Seraphim, slinked out of its cage and coiled up next to her while she was playing video games, which she found very funny. She shared a photo of Seraphim peeking out of a blanket with its sly eyes, and said she bought Seraphim a year earlier in Paris. Deborah said pets bring so much happiness, and Jolene called snakes very unusual pets. Jolene then shared a photo of herself and her partner gaming the previous week, with a dog watching TV beside them. She said they are both crazy about playing the game "Detroit" on a console. Deborah asked whether her boyfriend had taught her to play. Jolene said that even as a child she learned to play on her own. When Deborah asked whether she played only old games or tried new ones, Jolene said she and her partner planned to play "The Walking Dead" next Saturday. Deborah closed by telling Jolene to take care and keep spreading good vibes, and Jolene said goodbye.

In the third session, on 1 February 2023 at 7:03 pm, Jolene said she had been busy because her engineering professor had given her class a huge robotics project. She called it tough but fun, and said it was making her get creative and problem-solve. She shared a photo of a table with a robot on it and a laptop. When she first received the project she felt a mix of excitement and nervousness, but she now really enjoys it. She described it as like solving a puzzle, figuring out the best design and programming, and said seeing the robot come together is awesome. Deborah said she met her new neighbor Anna the previous day, 31 January, and shared a photo of a yellow sign with a picture of a family. They met at yoga in the park. Deborah said they talked about how yoga has improved their lives and the sense of community it gives. Jolene said it is great to connect with people who share similar interests. She then shared a photo of a purse with a plant on a table. Deborah asked whether Jolene had ever thought about resuming yoga. Jolene replied that she and her partner had planned to play the console together. Deborah said it is good that Jolene has something to do with her partner, and Jolene thanked her for the kind words. Deborah then said she had to run, and Jolene said she would see her soon. Like the first session, Deborah ended this one abruptly.

In the fourth session, on 4 February 2023 at 9:48 am, Jolene said she had been on an emotional rollercoaster lately but was coping. She said she had a major milestone the previous week that went really well, leaving her relieved and proud, and it was a huge accomplishment for her as an engineer. She had planned, researched, and designed a sustainable water purifier for a rural community in need, and building it was tough but she loved the experience. Seeing it work and provide clean water to the community was a surreal and deeply satisfying moment. It reminded her that engineering can make a difference in people's lives, and it made her feel she had a purpose and had done something good. Her career aspiration is to keep working in engineering and make a positive impact on communities in need through sustainable solutions, contributing to a better world. She said Deborah's encouragement motivates her to pursue her passions and that she is determined to keep going. Deborah told Jolene to take a deep breath and remember why she does this, and said she spends a lot of her time teaching yoga, which is a great way to find balance and reconnect with ourselves. Deborah said she bonded with Anna during the previous day's yoga class, which was 3 February, and shared a photo of two women in a dance studio doing a dance pose. She said they were trying different dance poses, including Warrior II, which builds strength and boosts focus, and shared a photo of a woman doing a yoga pose on a chair. Jolene asked whether it was difficult, and Deborah said yes, but it brought them closer and they supported each other. Deborah then described a modified pose: sit on the edge of a chair with feet planted, twist the torso to one side with a hand on the knee for support, hold for a few breaths, then switch sides, which stretches the back and shoulders and relaxes tense muscles. Jolene said it sounded hard and shared a photo of her bookshelf full of books. She said she is really into "Sapiens," a fascinating look at human history and how technology has affected us. Two weeks before this session she read "Avalanche" by Neal Stephenson in one sitting. She also mentioned a recent story about someone who became successful despite many challenges, which showed her that anything is possible with belief and hard work. Deborah said that story reminded her of someone special and their grace and strength through hardships. Deborah then shared a photo of a bouquet of flowers in a vase on a table. She said a friend gave her the bouquet when she was struggling, and it gives her hope and courage and fills her with warmth and appreciation. Jolene said such a small thing can make a real difference. Asked about her favorite nature spots, Deborah named a park with a forest trail, where getting lost in nature is calming, and a nearby beach where the sound of waves and sand underfoot make her feel peaceful and happy. Jolene shared a photo of a person walking on a beach with a surfboard, from a vacation in Bogota last summer, where watching the sunset over the water was beautiful and calming. Deborah said she likes to come to a spot by the water near her mom's old house to reflect on her mother's life and find peace, and she shared a photo of a small island with a lone boat in the water. Jolene asked about her traditions there. Deborah said she brings an amulet that belonged to her mother whenever she visits, because holding it lets her feel her mother's love and stay close to her, and she shared a photo of herself wearing a white shirt and a gold chain necklace. Jolene remarked how something so small can have such a big impact, and Deborah said such things remind us of the love and strength we carry inside and connect us to people we have lost. Jolene said they keep those people close in our hearts every day. Deborah added that Anna also wears a pendant in memory of her mother, which also brought them closer. Jolene said such reminders are a source of strength when needed. Deborah closed by telling Jolene that life is tough but to hang in there, look to her sources of strength, stay in touch, take care of herself, and know Deborah is always there to cheer her on. Jolene said she would stay in touch and said goodbye, and Deborah replied "Stay safe!" and said goodbye.

In the fifth session, on 9 February 2023 at 9:03 pm, Jolene opened by saying it had been a few days since they last talked, and she wanted to share news about a mini retreat she had done the previous Wednesday, most likely 8 February, to assess where she was in life. The retreat gave her a new outlook and a real confidence boost, and she said she achieved far more than she had imagined. Deborah praised her for stepping outside her comfort zone and believing in herself. Jolene said she accomplished something with her engineering project, coming up with some neat solutions that she is excited about, and she said she wanted to look into green tech, which could make a real difference in disadvantaged areas, and see how she could contribute. She then proposed an idea for a volunteer program in which engineers teach STEM to underprivileged kids, and asked Deborah's opinion. Deborah called it a great way to help and inspire others and said the kids would benefit from Jolene's knowledge. Jolene said she had not finished planning, but was considering teaming up with local schools and community centers to run workshops, and possibly inviting engineers as guest speakers to show the kids their career options. Deborah said guest speakers would give the kids a real-world view. Jolene said she had not yet reached out to any schools or centers, because she wanted to solidify the plan first, but she could not wait to start. Deborah said she was excited to hear how it went and asked to be kept informed. Jolene shared a photo of her planner sketches, a notebook with a pen and a page of notes, and thanked Deborah for her support. Deborah offered further tips or information if needed, and Jolene said she would let Deborah know if she needed anything else and called her awesome. Deborah said goodbye with "Take care!" and Jolene replied "Stay safe!"

In the sixth session, on 22 February 2023 at 4:12 pm, Jolene opened by saying she was buzzing after a great night out the previous evening, 21 February, with dinner and drinks with friends, where she was glad to let her hair down. She shared a photo of a plate of food and a glass of wine. Deborah said she had just visited a calming and nostalgic place, and shared a photo of a garden with flowers in buckets. Jolene asked about the flowers, and Deborah said the roses and dahlias bring her peace. She said she had lost a friend the previous week, around 15 February, and had been spending time in the garden to find comfort. Jolene offered condolences and asked how she was holding up. Deborah said it had been tough, but she was comforted by remembering their time together, which reminds her how special life is. Jolene said memories can bring comfort and joy, and Deborah replied that memories keep loved ones close. Deborah then shared a photo of two women riding a motorcycle on a dirt road, and said it was the last photo with her friend Karlie, taken last summer when they hiked, and that it was their last one together. She said they had a great time and she cannot help smiling whenever she sees it. This friend Karlie is distinct from Deborah's mother, whose last photo with her was the wheelchair hug shared in the first session. Asked where else she had traveled, Deborah said she had been blessed to visit a few places, and that Bali last year was one of her favorites, a gorgeous island that gave her peace and was great for yoga. Jolene asked whether yoga on the beach was a thing, saying she had been wanting to try it, and Deborah said the sound of the waves and fresh air is wonderful.
