SUMMARY:
Andrew (a Financial Analyst at a new job since about March 2023) and Audrey have chatted periodically since late March 2023. Their topics are pets, nature, hiking, and Andrew's search for a dog. Session 8 (13 June 2023) is the most recent.

Audrey's dogs and life: She has had Pepper, Precious and Panda for 3 years as of March 2023. They are city dogs who explore often. In early April 2023 her family adopted a puppy, Pixie, who took a few days to fit in. Pepper took a while to warm up to her but now they are always together. By 11 May 2023 Audrey had four dogs. She calls them quick learners who love rewards, and says caring for them is fulfilling and keeps her busy. She takes them on road trips about once every couple of months. In early May she described a recent national park road trip. The dogs love hikes, new scents, fetch with a ball or frisbee, and doggie playdates at the park. She uses a safety item on them that looks funny but works, and they wear party hats for fun and treats. She has a tattoo of her dogs on her arm, representing her love for them and for nature. Walking them in the park recharges her, and she wants to see their happy faces even when they are apart. In early April she said she had not tried Fox Hollow yet because Pixie kept them busy. In early May she recommended a dog park beside the park they usually walk, with trees and benches. In April she made favorite treats and proposed a pastry party, which Andrew agreed to, with her dogs coming too. In May she signed up for a positive reinforcement training workshop on bonding with pets, held in June 2023. She saw the flyer at her local pet store, where she also met a friendly, playful dog. She says punishment is never the right way to train pets and that she could not bear to hurt them. In early June she took the dogs to the park, where they ran off-leash. She also described a national park peak hike with them, with a stunning sunset, and shared photos. Nature cheers her up and makes her grateful. On 2 June she offered to help Andrew find a dog-friendly spot if he emailed his criteria. In session 8 she said she recently found a small park with a tree-lined trail for the dogs' walks, and invited Andrew to join. Their walks usually last about an hour, with the dogs exploring at their own pace. She shared photos of the dogs running with a ball and playing with a frisbee in a meadow. She says being outdoors with the dogs puts her in her happy place, and that dogs and nature bring her joy and peace.

Andrew's life and interests: In March 2023 he said he had no pets but loves animals, and that eagles fascinate him. He recommended the Fox Hollow trail for weekend hikes. In early April he said his family has a dog, and he misses hiking with it. He was considering getting a dog but found it hard to find dog-friendly places in the city. In mid-April he and his girlfriend ("my girl") tried a new city cafe and enjoy finding new places to eat. They loved its croissants, muffins and tarts. He said city life makes it hard to get out into nature, where he feels most at home and connected. He agreed to the pastry party. In early May he had found a new open space to hike nearby and usually tries to escape the city at least once a weekend. He calls nature therapeutic. On 6 May he said he had been searching for a dog through websites, shelters and friends. As someone living in an apartment, he thinks a smaller dog would suit him, though an active dog would want to play and run. He is contacting landlords and checking neighborhoods for a pet-friendly place near a park or woods. He wishes he could road trip with a dog and added it to his bucket list. On 11 May he had a great hike with friends and his girlfriend at a spot they had recently found. He was almost convinced to take Audrey's training class and said he would look into classes. Session 8 (13 June 2023): Last Sunday (11 June) he and friends took a rock climbing class, and he reached the top. He is now "hooked" and wants to do outdoor activities every week. He has been encouraged to try kayaking and maybe bungee jumping. He shared a photo of the view from the top, and said the climb was tricky because he is still a newbie. He said friends supported him. He agreed to join Audrey and her dogs for a walk in the park.

Status as of 13 June 2023 (latest): Andrew has taken up rock climbing and is keen on more outdoor activities. He is still looking for a dog and a pet-friendly place in the city, a search that was discouraging as of 2 June, and he has not mentioned a dog since then. Audrey invited him on a walk with her dogs. He said he would like to join and meet them.

The memory covers ten conversations between Calvin and Dave, from their first meeting on 23 March 2023 through a tenth session on 7 July 2023.

In the first session, at 11:53 am on 23 March 2023, Calvin and Dave met for the first time. Dave said things had been going well and that he had recently attended a car event full of classic cars, where he spoke with owners and heard their stories. Calvin said he had just gone through a big life change and shared a photo of his new mansion, a building with a sign on its front. He framed the change around learning about Japanese culture and getting a chance to expand. Calvin has never been to Japan and is fascinated by its traditions. He planned to leave for Japan in April 2023. His agent found him a place to stay there, and he shared a photo of its cozy living room with a couch, table, and television. In Japan he planned to explore the city, try local cuisines, and perhaps collaborate with local musicians. He would stay a few months and then travel to Boston. Dave had been spending a lot of time at a beautiful, calming park with a lake and a few boats, and he shared a photo of it. Calvin had never been there but said he would check it out when he returned. Dave offered more recommendations if Calvin needed them, and they ended by wishing each other well for the trip.

The second session took place at 4:45 pm on 26 March 2023. Calvin said it had been a few days since they last talked and announced that he had just bought a new car, a luxury car he described as a long-held dream come true. He called it smooth and powerful, said driving it made him feel like a rockstar, and said it was what he deserved after all his hard work. He shared a photo of a red sports car parked on the side of the road, taken on 25 March when he first took it for a ride. He did not name the car's make or model when Dave asked. Calvin also said he was on cloud nine. Dave reported that he was doing well and that the previous weekend (around 18 to 19 March) he had gone to a music festival in Boston, which he loved and which reminded him why he loves music. He shared a photo of a large crowd at a concert. Dave said his favorite band there was Aerosmith, whose performance he found incredible. He shared two photos: one of a concert stage with a large eagle, and one of two people on stage with guitars and a microphone. He said he had finally seen them live and that the singer was jamming to one of their hits. Dave said he did not get to hang out with the band after the show. When Dave asked about news in Calvin's life, Calvin said he had got a new ride, had written some new tunes, and had had several studio sessions the previous week. He said he was excited to collaborate and would share the music with everyone once it was ready. He promised to keep Dave updated on how the collaborations went, and the two signed off by wishing each other well and staying safe.

The third session took place at 4:15 pm on 20 April 2023. Calvin said it had been a long time since they had seen each other and reported that he had just been to a music festival in Tokyo, which he called awesome. He did not see any bands there, but he met many talented artists and industry people, and he found the experience enriching. He said he learned a lot and got valuable advice from professionals in the music industry. A producer told him to stay true to himself and sound unique, which got him thinking about where he wants his music to go. His long-term dream is to tour the world, performing for different people and connecting with them, and he hopes his music can reach a global audience and make an impact. He said he was looking forward to an upcoming trip to Boston after he finishes the Frank Ocean tour, and he had heard the music scene there is awesome. Dave responded enthusiastically and offered to show Calvin around Boston and its cool spots. He recommended Paradise Rock, House of Blues, and Fenway Park as places with a great music scene, and said he would be in the front row whenever Calvin performed onstage. Dave shared a photo of a city skyline with a boat in the water, which Calvin admired. Dave also said that the previous weekend (around 15 to 16 April) he had gone to a car show, where he found classic cars charming and admired the dedication people put into restoring them. This is why he is so into auto engineering. He shared a photo of a green Mustang parked in a field of grass. Calvin replied that the car looked great and shared a photo of a red sports car on display at a show, saying he had put a lot of work into it and could not wait to see more cars in Boston. This red car appears to be the same sports car Calvin bought in March, now shown at an event. When Dave asked whether Calvin had seen anything in Boston beyond the gigs, Calvin said not yet, because he had been busy with rehearsals and traveling, but he was looking forward to exploring the city, trying delicious food, and visiting popular attractions. He suggested they grab a bite together when he arrives, and Dave agreed to share his favorite spots in the city. The conversation ended with both expressing excitement about meeting in Boston and seeing each other soon.

The fourth session took place at 6:24 pm on 1 May 2023, and it was a longer, more upbeat exchange in which Dave shared big news about his career. He said it had been a long time since they last talked and announced that he had finally opened his own car maintenance shop, which he described as a dream come true and a spot to work on cars that he finds deeply satisfying. He shared a photo of a car dealership with cars parked in front of it. Calvin congratulated him and shared a photo of a man standing under a car in a garage. Dave thanked him, said the shop had been his dream and that it took a lot of hard work, but that it was worth it. Calvin praised his guts and ambition and shared a photo of a book with a space theme on its cover. Dave said the shop is a step toward his other dream of working on classic cars, which he loves for their design and engineering. Calvin shared a photo of a red car parked in a parking lot and said that going for classic cars was cool. Dave said he is obsessed with classic cars because of their unique charm, and that last year he had been thrilled to restore one, which he called a labor of love that was challenging but worth it. He shared a photo of the restored car's engine, which has a small air filter. Calvin said it looked awesome, and the two exchanged a series of messages about how satisfying it is to see something you worked on come back to life and to see hard work pay off. Dave then shared a photo of his shop, a group of people standing in front of a car, and invited Calvin to come by if he could. Calvin said he would love to visit and asked what cars Dave works on. Dave said he works on all kinds of cars, from regular maintenance to full restorations of classic cars, and that he finds it rewarding to see transformations and to know he is helping people keep their cars in good condition. Calvin encouraged him to keep up the great work. Calvin then shared a photo of a gold necklace with a diamond pendant and called it stunning. When Dave asked where he got it, Calvin said it was a gift from another artist and a reminder of why he keeps hustling as a musician. The two closed by encouraging each other to keep pushing, with Calvin saying that they should keep each other motivated.

The fifth session took place at 1:16 pm on 3 May 2023. Dave opened by saying it had been a long time since they talked and announced that he was teaming up with a local garage, sharing a photo of a car being worked on in a garage. Calvin congratulated him, called the news inspiring, and shared a photo of a green car in a garage with a sign in the background. Dave said he was loving the job, getting to work with skilled mechanics and share his knowledge about cars. He shared a photo of a man working on a car engine in a garage, describing it as a cool project that was a bit challenging. Calvin said the car looked awesome and encouraged him to keep up the good work. Dave said he planned to keep learning about auto engineering and hoped to build a custom car from scratch someday, which is his dream. For now he would keep working on the current project and assisting customers. Calvin called him inspiring and told him to relax and enjoy the process. Dave said he needed to take time to chill and asked whether Calvin had hobbies that helped him relax. Calvin said long drives in his red sports car, the one he shared a photo of, really helped him relax, because the wind and open road were freeing and cleared his head. Dave said driving with the wind in your hair was calming and that walking and exploring, taking in the sights and sounds, was a peaceful way for him to destress. Calvin agreed that embracing nature had been calming for him as well, and said he had been loving getting to know Japanese culture. He then admitted that he was stuck with his music, that his creativity felt frozen, and asked for tips. Dave suggested immersing himself in something he loves, such as concerts or favorite albums, which usually jumpstarts his inspiration, and recommended taking a break from music to explore other things and have some fun. Calvin said taking a break was great for getting his mojo back and that he would take the advice and explore. Dave encouraged him to keep pursuing music and never give up. The two agreed to stay in touch, said goodbye, and Calvin signed off with a thank-you.

The sixth session took place at 11:50 am on 16 May 2023, and it was a more mixed exchange. Calvin opened by saying it had been a long time since they chatted and that a lot had happened. He reported that things had not been going smoothly: about a week earlier (around 9 May, "last week") his place had been flooded. He managed to save his music gear and his favorite microphone, and he said it had been tough but he was staying positive and looking forward to getting everything fixed. Dave sympathized, said he was glad the important gear was saved, and offered help. Calvin said he was waiting on insurance to kick in before starting repairs and hoped it would not take long. He shared a photo of his music studio, a room with a keyboard, a synthesizer, and other musical equipment, which he called his creative haven where he pours his heart into music. Dave said the studio looked awesome and hoped it would be fixed soon. Calvin asked Dave about exciting work, and Dave said he had opened his car shop "last week," invited friends over to celebrate, and found it amazing; he said he was stoked to share his passion and help folks with their rides. (This is a little inconsistent with the 1 May session, where Dave first announced the shop's opening.) Calvin congratulated him. Calvin then said he had an upcoming performance in Tokyo "this month" (May 2023) and hoped to show his music to a new crowd and expand his following. Dave wished him luck and asked to hear how it went, and Calvin promised to keep him posted. Calvin then shared a photo of a city at night full of lights, saying he took it in Tokyo "last night" (15 May) and that the skyline was stunning. Dave said the skyline looked great and that he hoped to visit Tokyo soon, and Calvin encouraged him to visit. Dave said he was adding it to his list.

The seventh session took place at 6:06 pm on 31 May 2023. Calvin opened by saying it had been ages since they chatted and that so much had happened. He said touring with Frank Ocean the previous week (around 24 May) had been wild, and that Tokyo, where he had performed, was unreal, with an insane crowd. He said he felt so alive when performing that he could not find the words to express it. Dave congratulated him and said he had been busy too, sharing a photo of a man working on a car engine in a garage. Dave described it as his neighbor's car, which had been having engine trouble, and said he had fixed it himself. Calvin said the fans' energy and love had been crazy. He asked whether the car was the one Dave had been fixing up for a friend, which slightly mixes up the detail, since Dave had said it belonged to a neighbor. Calvin said working on cars helped him chill and clear his head. Dave said helping neighbors with their cars was not difficult for him and that working on cars was therapeutic, and he asked whether it relaxed Calvin as much as it relaxed him. Calvin said fixing cars calmed him down and gave him a real sense of achievement, like meditating, and asked whether Dave had hobbies that gave him the same satisfaction. Dave said fixing things was more than a hobby for him, giving him a sense of achievement and purpose, and that he got a real buzz turning something broken into something that runs smoothly, like giving it a second chance. Calvin said Dave found purpose in transforming things, and that they were both making something great out of nothing. Dave agreed that making something look amazing was cool and said giving things new life made him feel powerful and happy. Calvin said the feeling of power and happiness was amazing and that it was great to see what they had created with their hard work and ideas. Dave said accomplishment kept him motivated, then asked Calvin whether he always enjoyed performing live. Calvin said performing live always fueled his soul, that he loved the rush and connection with the crowd, and called it an absolute high. Dave said the connection between artist and audience must be powerful and shared a photo of a large crowd of people taking pictures at a concert, calling the atmosphere off the charts. Calvin agreed that everyone was part of it, like one big harmony, and shared a photo of a crowd watching a concert under bright lights. Dave said music brought people together and was like therapy for everyone, then shared a photo of a band performing on stage and asked what was next for Calvin's music. Calvin said he could not wait for the tour with Frank and was buzzing to perform in Boston and see what it was like, and that it would be great playing for folks from home. He asked what Dave thought of the Boston music scene. Dave said it was awesome, with plenty of talented musicians and cool places to play, and said he would be there to cheer Calvin on. Calvin thanked him and said Dave's support meant a lot. Dave said he hoped Calvin had a great time in Boston and wanted to hear all about it when he got back. Calvin promised to fill him in on all the details when he returned and signed off with "See you soon!"

The eighth session took place at 2:31 pm on 9 June 2023. Calvin opened by saying he had met with the creative team for his album the previous day (8 June), a long session that was awesome to see coming together. Dave replied warmly and shared a photo of a pond with a boat in it, surrounded by trees. Calvin said he was feeling stoked about the album, described the team as making some magic in the studio, and shared a photo of a recording studio with a large window and a desk. He asked Dave for news since they last talked. Dave said he had been doing well and had been exploring parks on weekends to relax, finding nature very peaceful. He asked whether Calvin knew any chill spots in Boston. Calvin said he had never been to Boston before, had heard the parks were amazing, and could not wait to visit next month (July 2023). He asked Dave for anything he remembered about Boston parks and shared a photo of a tree with pink flowers in the foreground. Dave said the Boston parks are awesome, especially in spring, and are very serene for walking. He said he had gone for a stroll the previous Friday (around 2 June) and it was amazing, and that he loves weekend walks because they recharge him for the whole coming week. Calvin said he was excited to experience that serenity and to take walks in the parks himself, then asked whether Dave had been hiking lately and shared a photo of a path climbing a hill with mountains in view. Dave said he had not gone hiking recently but found it awesome for being in nature and pushing yourself to new heights, and that it clears the mind and brings calm. He asked whether Calvin had been to the mountains, which he had heard were super chill. Calvin said he had not been to the mountains but was keen to go, looking for a way to escape it all and de-stress, and that he wanted to hike somewhere like the place in the photo. He shared a photo of a plane flying over a snowy mountain range and asked what was new and exciting for Dave. Dave said he had booked a trip to a mountainous region for next month (July 2023), finally going to see those majestic peaks, and expected it to be an amazing experience. Calvin wished him a great time and asked him to take lots of pictures and show him when he got back. Dave agreed to take many photos and to show Calvin on his return. The two signed off with Calvin wishing Dave safe travels and saying they would see each other soon, and Dave thanking him and saying the same.

The ninth session took place at 3:15 pm on 21 June 2023. Calvin opened by saying hello and that some things had happened since they last chatted. He said he had been in a small car accident the previous Friday (around 16 June), which was upsetting but left no one hurt. He said he had been dealing with insurance and repairs, which took a lot of time and energy, and he shared a photo of a red car with a black rim parked on a sidewalk. Dave sympathized, said he was glad nobody was hurt, and asked whether Calvin had run into problems with the insurance process. Calvin said the process was a hassle, took forever, and involved a ton of paperwork, but that it was now sorted and the car was being fixed. He shared a photo of a tow truck parked in a parking lot and said he could not wait to drive the car again. Dave asked how long everything had taken. Calvin said it took only about a week to sort out, and that although he had worried about the cost, it was not too bad. He shared a photo from the auto repair shop of a man working on a car in a garage. Dave asked who the man was, and Calvin said he was the mechanic, someone who knows his stuff and is doing his best to get the car running again. Dave said it was great to have skilled, knowledgeable people working on the car. Calvin said he was feeling much more confident and excited to show off the car, and that he trusted their expertise. Dave said it was awesome to trust the people fixing it and that the car would be back to normal soon. Calvin thanked him and said he appreciated his help. He then shared a photo of a view from his living room, a small town with a mountain in the background, and said it was from a small town in Japan and that the mountain view was unbelievably stunning. Dave asked whether Calvin had visited the place yet. Calvin said he had not been there before and that it was on his to-do list for after his Frank Ocean tour ends, and he said he could not wait to see them in person. He then shared a photo of a person on skis on a snowy mountain and said it looked like a snowy peak. Dave asked whether he had ever tried skiing. Calvin said he had not but that it looked like a lot of fun and he might give it a try once. He then asked Dave what was new in his daily routine. Dave said he had recently joined a rock band and had been practicing guitar, and he shared a photo of the band members, a group of men playing instruments in a room. Calvin said playing guitar in a rock band was awesome and would bring Dave a lot of emotions. Dave said good company and great music lift the mood and bring a lot of positive emotions, and then said he had to go and would see Calvin soon. Calvin said he hoped to keep in touch and wished Dave well.

The tenth session took place at 7:56 pm on 7 July 2023. Dave opened by asking how Calvin's car was doing after the crash and whether he was stoked to be back on the road. Calvin replied that the car was fixed and going strong, that cruising around was the best, and he shared a photo of a red sports car parked on the side of the road. He asked Dave how he had been and whether anything was new. Dave said he had been good and had been hanging out with friends at parks lately, and that he had arranged regular walks together in the park with friends. Calvin said this sounded like a great plan and that fresh air and friends could do wonders, then asked whether Dave had a favorite spot for hanging out. Dave said they were going to that spot that day and shared a photo of a city skyline with a river and boats in the water. Calvin admired the view, said the sunset over the river was gorgeous and the place must be tranquil, and said it reminded him of living in his Japanese mansion with its epic cityscape, which he called a dream come true. He shared a photo he had taken from his backyard of the mansion, showing a boat docked in a canal at sunset. Dave said the peace by the river was nice and that living in a Japanese mansion surrounded by a city skyline must be stunning. Calvin said that whenever he looked out the windows and saw the city lights it was awe-inspiring, described it as luxury and beauty on a whole new level, and shared a photo of the front of the mansion, a large house with many windows and lights. Dave said the mansion looked great, guessed the view from inside was stunning, and asked whether Calvin was looking forward to anything else in Japan. Calvin said he could not wait to try the food and check out the culture, and asked whether Dave had ever been to Japan. Dave said he had never been but was keen to go one day, had heard it was full of vibes, good eats and awesome tech, and that he was hooked on Japanese music. Calvin said Japan had it all and was like stepping into another world, and that he had been working on cool music collaborations with Japanese artists and was excited to hear how they turned out. Dave said working with them was a great chance and he could not wait for the tunes. Calvin promised to share some clips when everything was ready and said collaborating with various artists was always exciting and a chance to create something unique. Dave praised the collaboration and said he could not wait to see or hear the end product. Calvin thanked him, said it was going to be awesome, said he had to get back to work, and signed off. Dave told him to take care, not to overwork himself, to talk soon, and to stay safe.

This memory covers two friends, Deborah and Jolene, who spoke in 30 sessions between 23 January 2023 and 20 September 2023. Deborah is a yoga teacher with a close family history, and Jolene is an electrical engineering student who also works as an intern. Their conversations moved from first introductions, through grief and loss, to shared interests in yoga, nature, pets, and time management. The sections below group what each person shared, then give a dated timeline so that changes over time can be traced.

Deborah's mother died several years before January 2023. Deborah showed a photo of herself and her mother, both in wheelchairs and embracing, and described it as their last photo together. Her mother's old house is central to her memories. In the first session she described a special bench near the window where her mother sat every morning to take in the view. Deborah sometimes sits there herself, and she says it helps her stay connected to her mother. In the second session, on 27 January, she showed a window seat in the house where her mother sat every night with a book and a smile, since reading was one of her hobbies. Her mother's other great passion was travel. Her mother also loved flowers, art, cooking, and singing. Deborah recalled that her mother baked pineapple birthday cakes for her as a child, that the smell of her mother's special dish filled the house and brought everyone together, and that her mother sang lullabies to her. In a April session, Deborah described her mother as someone who believed art could carry strong emotions and connect people, and said that attending art shows made her feel they were still experiencing things together even though her mother was gone.

Deborah wears a pendant that reminds her of her mother. In the fourth session, on 4 February, she described an amulet from her mother, which she carries on a gold chain whenever she goes to the sea near her mother's old house. She says holding it lets her feel her mother's love and stay close. She also mentioned that her new friend Anna wears a pendant in memory of Anna's own mother, and that this shared symbol brought them closer. Deborah has two cats. Max is eight years old and was her mother's cat, and Deborah took him in when her mother died. Her other cat, Luna, is five years old and came from a shelter. Deborah does not like dogs and prefers cats. In late August she shared a photo of Luna and Max sitting on a window sill and said both bring a lot of joy and peace to the home.

Deborah's father died suddenly about two days before her second session on 27 January 2023. She said his death left the family shell-shocked, and she was trying to channel her grief into spending more time with family and cherishing memories. She shared a photo of her parents' wedding in 1993 and said she and her husband were trying to be as good a family as her parents had been. She named love and openness as the things that have kept her marriage close over the years, and said being there for each other has made both of them happy. Her husband is not named in the conversations. In late August she shared a photo of him standing in front of her mother's house and said the house still holds her mother's strength and the love she shared with Deborah, even though her mother had both good and bad times there. Deborah also mentioned that she and her husband used to play detective games together and that they enjoyed spending time outdoors and exploring nature. In a June session she said she had visited her mother's house the week before and felt her mother's presence there.

In late February 2023, Deborah lost a friend named Karlie. She had been spending time in her garden, which holds roses and dahlias that bring her peace, and she found comfort in remembering their time together. She showed a photo of the last time she saw Karlie, taken the summer before when the two hiked together. She described it as their last photo together, and said that every time she looks at it she cannot help but smile. In August 2023, Deborah also mentioned a friend who had written her a note saying "Let go of what no longer serves you." She said that friend would never be able to support her again, and that she misses him.

Deborah's yoga teaching is the main thread of her life in these conversations. In the first session she said one of her goals was to keep teaching yoga and supporting her community, and that yoga had helped her find peace during a rough time. In late January she showed a photo of a group letter from members of her class, who thanked her for the positive influence she had on them. Her teaching grew over the year. In early February she was preparing to welcome a new neighbor, and in March she said she had started a yoga class in her neighborhood for her neighbors and hosted it on a Friday. In June she was preparing for a yoga retreat with friends, and in August she described a retreat near her mother's old place as life-changing. She said she got to spend time with nature and really get to know herself. In July she organized a yoga event with food stalls and live music, reaching out to nearby businesses to make it happen. In August she also led a meditation yoga session for elderly people at a local care home during sunset, and at the end of the month she wrote a meditation guide for her retreat. In September she and a neighbor ran a free gardening class for the community, which she described as a way of sharing her love of plants and helping people look after the world. Deborah's morning routine is to meditate, do yoga, and teach classes, and she spends her evenings with loved ones. In a July session she mentioned that she had begun jogging for the first time in a nearby park and planned to make it part of her daily routine. She also takes her cats out for a run in the park every morning and evening, since she values exercise and nature.

Deborah met her new neighbor Anna at yoga in the park, and the two talked about how yoga had improved their lives and the sense of community it gives. In early February, Deborah and Anna bonded during a dance studio class, when they tried Warrior II and other poses together and supported each other. Warrior II builds strength and boosts focus. Deborah later explained a modified chair twist to Jolene, describing how to sit on the edge of a chair, twist the torso to one side, use a hand on the knee for support, hold for a few breaths, and switch sides, and she said it is good for relaxing tense muscles. In July, Deborah said she had started a running group with Anna, and that they push each other to stay motivated. In late March, Deborah and Anna sat by the sea watching a sunset and realized they inspire each other. In August, Deborah shared that she had told Anna the story of her life and that Anna was very kind about it. Anna also made Deborah a vegan stir-fry of tofu and vegetables with ginger and soy sauce in early March.

Deborah has traveled to several places. She visited Bali the year before the February conversation and described it as a gorgeous island that gave her peace and was great for yoga. She has also traveled to Rio de Janeiro, where she was three years before August 2023 and took a photo of a large stone structure with a mountain in the background. She shared a photo of an old temple visit in Rio and said she likes exploring historical places and learning their stories. In September she had a planned yoga getaway that was cancelled because of a storm, and she said she found comfort in her work and in spending time at home. In the same session she invited Jolene to a coffee date at a cafe, and later rescheduled because she already had plans. Deborah is also interested in music and relaxation. In late August she was listening to an album called "Sleep," which she finds great for meditation and deep relaxation. Earlier, she had told Jolene that instrumental tracks with mellow melodies and rhythms create a peaceful vibe, and that her favorite was a track called "Savana." In September she wrote that she had attended a music festival with pals, and that the music reminded her of her mother's soothing voice when she sang lullabies.

Deborah also described her own practices of mindfulness and gratitude. In mid-August she said she started with workshops and books, and that mindfulness is now a huge part of her life. She uses visual reminders and photos of nature to stay motivated. She also enjoys candles and essential oils, and in late March she said she had bought new props for her yoga class and a candle to improve her practice. In early September she spoke about a gorgeous blossom tree near her home that bloomed every spring, and how watching it filled her with awe and a sense of hope for growth in tough times. She also keeps a close connection to nature more generally, and has said that birds chirping and a gentle breeze remind her of what really matters.

Deborah was also interested in games. She said she used to play video games and that it is a good way to relax after a busy day, though it has been a while. In late August she mentioned that she and her husband prefer detective games. In September she described a card game about cats, in which players take cards one by one from a deck and then attack an opponent with them. She said she would definitely play it with Jolene at some point.

Jolene's world is centered on engineering school and an internship. In late January 2023 she said she had just finished an electrical engineering project after a lot of work. In early February she described a major milestone: she had planned, researched, and built a sustainable water purifier for a rural community in need, and seeing it provide clean water made her feel she had a purpose. Her career goal is to keep working on engineering solutions that make a positive impact on communities. In early February she also mentioned a robotics project from her engineering professor, which she found tough but fun, and she described enjoying the puzzle of design and programming. In early February she also shared that she had been reading a book called "Sapiens," which looks at human history and how technology has affected us, and that she had read "Avalanche" by Neal Stephenson in one sitting two weeks earlier. In late February she said that balancing engineering school with gaming and meditation was a feat.

In early February Jolene also described a volunteer idea that came out of a mini retreat she took the Wednesday before 9 February. The retreat helped her assess where she was in life and gave her a new outlook and a confidence boost. The idea was a volunteer program in which engineers teach STEM to underprivileged kids, with workshops run with local schools and centers and engineers invited as guest speakers. She also said green technology could make a real difference in disadvantaged areas and that she wanted to look into how she could contribute. By the time of that conversation she had not yet reached out to any schools or centers, but she planned to do so once the plan was solid.

In early March, Jolene said she was struggling with exams and deadlines and felt overwhelmed. She said she needed to be more mindful of her stress levels and take care of her mental health. Later that month she described how she used the Pomodoro Technique, working for 25 minutes and then taking a five-minute break, to avoid burnout, though she still struggled to prioritize. Deborah then introduced her to the Eisenhower Matrix, which sorts tasks into four boxes by urgency and importance, and Jolene found the visual approach helpful. In mid-March, Jolene said she was having a hard time with engineering assignments and asked to talk about time management. On 28 March she said she had a breakthrough with her project the previous Friday and found a solution to a problem that had been bothering her. In June she said she had finished the difficult engineering project the previous month, and she shared a photo of a solar-powered vehicle with a solar panel on the back. She said she felt proud of sticking with it despite the problems.

In June she also began an internship at a well-known engineering firm. She described the best part so far as being able to apply what she learned in school to real projects, and said it is so fulfilling to see her ideas come to life. She said the internship stoked her love of engineering and encouraged her to keep striving for her dreams, and that hanging out with people who love what they do has inspired her to stay focused. She also mentioned that finding a good work-life balance has been tough, and that she has been slogging away and finding it hard to make time for hobbies and relaxation. In late June she said she had a big breakthrough with a project, though things had been intense and overwhelming at times, and she said she was determined to overcome obstacles. In early August she said her project had crashed and she had lost everything. In a session on 12 August she said she had lost her work files and felt overwhelmed, but meditation kept her calm and gave her clarity back. In mid-August she told Deborah she was working on a prototype that could revolutionize aerial surveillance. Her aim was to devise a more productive and affordable aerial surveillance system to help respond to emergencies and monitor the environment. She also shared notebooks she had designed with galaxies and circuitry, inspired by her love of space and engines, and said that seeing art and design in things gives her a unique perspective on problems. In late August she said she had presented at a virtual conference and received positive feedback, which confirmed she was on the right track. She said she is thinking about more internships to further her skills. In September she said she had been working on a project that is tough but taking shape, and that she was keen to see the final result.

Jolene's stress in 2023 was a recurring subject. In early March she said exams and deadlines made her feel overwhelmed, and in late March she said she was struggling to prioritize, with a to-do list that felt never-ending. In mid-August she started using a bullet journal to track tasks and stay organized, and she said crossing tasks off her list is very satisfying. In early September she said having a routine helps her stay on top of everything, with a schedule for classes, studying, and personal time, and that self-care such as yoga and meditation keeps her balanced. In late September she said she had signed up for a meditation course at a retreat near a lake, and that she hoped to share the experience with her partner.

Jolene's mother passed away in 2022. In January 2023 Jolene told Deborah that she also had many memories in her room in her mother's house, and she shared a photo of a room with a bench and a window. She shared a photo of a heart-shaped pendant with a bird on it that her mother gave her in Paris in 2010. Jolene said the pendant has a special symbol that represents freedom for her and reminds her to go for her goals and not get held back. In late August she mentioned that her mother always told her never to give up, and that her mother stressed the value of helping others. Jolene wants to carry both of those values into her engineering projects.

Jolene's partner is important to her, though he is not named in these conversations. They met in an engineering class in college and quickly became friends, and the friendship developed into a relationship. In late February, Jolene said they had been together for three years, were not married, and were taking it slow. She mentioned that a ring on his hand was only a decoration and not a wedding ring. They work on engineering projects together and both enjoy the process, since they understand each other's struggles. They play video games together, including "Detroit," "The Walking Dead," "It Takes Two," and "Battlefield 1," which they were given the week before the 21 August session. Jolene once won three large pizzas from her partner when they played "Overcooked 2" for bets. In August she bought him a console as a gift on the 17th, and he managed to play it. In early September, Jolene said that she and her partner were taking little trips to the beach to relax, and she said she was thankful for him as someone encouraging her goals. In late August they visited Rio de Janeiro and attended some yoga classes there, and in mid-September Jolene said they had been on a meditation retreat in Phuket for a few weeks. She said the retreat helped her find inner peace and reflect on what makes her happy. Her partner also began joining her for yoga, which has brought them closer. Her jewelry also has a symbol that represents freedom for her, a reminder to pursue her goals and not be held back. Jolene was enthusiastic about Deborah's yoga work and said she was looking forward to the next chat. Both women keep a physical connection to their mothers: Deborah through her mother's bench and pendant, and Jolene through her mother's room and pendant. Both have described a mother-linked bench and a pendant as meaningful keepsakes.

In the second session, on the morning of 27 January 2023 at 9:49 am, Deborah told Jolene that her father had passed away two days earlier, around 25 January. His sudden death left the whole family shell-shocked. Deborah said she was channeling her grief by spending more time with family and cherishing memories, which remind her to live life fully. She shared a photo of a woman hugging another woman seated on a couch. Jolene offered condolences and asked how the family was coping. Deborah said looking back on good memories is comforting, and that the family had been going through the family album. Photos give her peace in hard times. She shared a photo of her parents' wedding in 1993, a bride and groom posing together, and said she and her husband are trying to be as good a family as her parents were. When Jolene asked what she valued in her relationship, Deborah said love and openness have kept her and her husband close over the years, and that being there for each other has made them both happy. Deborah then shared a photo of a handwritten note she had received the day before from her group members, thanking her for the positive influence she had on them. She said moments like that remind her why she is so passionate about yoga.

Asked where she most often practices yoga, Deborah shared a photo of a living room with a television and a window. She said it is one of the places she practices, and that it is her old home, which she visits now and then for her mother, who has passed. Sitting in the spot by the window gives her peace, and she feels her mother's presence there, which comforts her. She then shared a photo of a window seat in a room with a window. Deborah said her mother would sit there every night with a book and a smile, since reading was one of her hobbies, and it was one of her favorite places in the house. The first session had described her mother sitting on the bench every morning to take in the view, so the bench was used both in the morning and at night. Deborah also said travel was her mother's great passion, and she shared a photo of a view of the sky from an airplane window to illustrate it.

Jolene then introduced her pets, which calm her down and make her happy. She shared a photo of a bed with a snake's head poking out, of her snake named Susie. Deborah said having a pet brightens life and asked for a fun moment with Jolene's pet. Jolene described how her second snake, Seraphim, slinked out of its cage and coiled up next to her while she was playing video games, which she found very funny. She shared a photo of Seraphim peeking out of a blanket with its sly eyes, and said she bought Seraphim a year earlier in Paris. Deborah said pets bring so much happiness, and Jolene called snakes very unusual pets. Jolene then shared a photo of herself and her partner gaming the previous week, with a dog watching TV beside them. She said they are both crazy about playing the game "Detroit" on a console. Deborah asked whether her boyfriend had taught her to play. Jolene said that even as a child she learned to play on her own. When Deborah asked whether she played only old games or tried new ones, Jolene said she and her partner planned to play "The Walking Dead" next Saturday. Deborah closed by telling Jolene to take care and keep spreading good vibes, and Jolene said goodbye.

In the third session, on 1 February 2023 at 7:03 pm, Jolene said she had been busy because her engineering professor had given her class a huge robotics project. She called it tough but fun, and said it was making her get creative and problem-solve. She shared a photo of a table with a robot on it and a laptop. When she first received the project she felt a mix of excitement and nervousness, but she now really enjoys it. She described it as like solving a puzzle, figuring out the best design and programming, and said seeing the robot come together is awesome. Deborah said she met her new neighbor Anna the previous day, 31 January, and shared a photo of a yellow sign with a picture of a family. They met at yoga in the park. Deborah said they talked about how yoga has improved their lives and the sense of community it gives. Jolene said it is great to connect with people who share similar interests. She then shared a photo of a purse with a plant on a table. Deborah asked whether Jolene had ever thought about resuming yoga. Jolene replied that she and her partner had planned to play the console together. Deborah said it is good that Jolene has something to do with her partner, and Jolene thanked her for the kind words. Deborah then said she had to run, and Jolene said she would see her soon. Like the first session, Deborah ended this one abruptly.

In the fourth session, on 4 February 2023 at 9:48 am, Jolene said she had been on an emotional rollercoaster lately but was coping. She said she had a major milestone the previous week that went really well, leaving her relieved and proud, and it was a huge accomplishment for her as an engineer. She had planned, researched, and designed a sustainable water purifier for a rural community in need, and building it was tough but she loved the experience. Seeing it work and provide clean water to the community was a surreal and deeply satisfying moment. It reminded her that engineering can make a difference in people's lives, and it made her feel she had a purpose and had done something good. Her career aspiration is to keep working in engineering and make a positive impact on communities in need through sustainable solutions, contributing to a better world. She said Deborah's encouragement motivates her to pursue her passions and that she is determined to keep going. Deborah told Jolene to take a deep breath and remember why she does this, and said she spends a lot of her time teaching yoga, which is a great way to find balance and reconnect with ourselves. Deborah said she bonded with Anna during the previous day's yoga class, which was 3 February, and shared a photo of two women in a dance studio doing a dance pose. She said they were trying different dance poses, including Warrior II, which builds strength and boosts focus, and shared a photo of a woman doing a yoga pose on a chair. Jolene asked whether it was difficult, and Deborah said yes, but it brought them closer and they supported each other. Deborah then described a modified pose: sit on the edge of a chair with feet planted, twist the torso to one side with a hand on the knee for support, hold for a few breaths, then switch sides, which stretches the back and shoulders and relaxes tense muscles. Jolene said it sounded hard and shared a photo of her bookshelf full of books. She said she is really into "Sapiens," a fascinating look at human history and how technology has affected us. Two weeks before this session she read "Avalanche" by Neal Stephenson in one sitting. She also mentioned a recent story about someone who became successful despite many challenges, which showed her that anything is possible with belief and hard work. Deborah said that story reminded her of someone special and their grace and strength through hardships. Deborah then shared a photo of a bouquet of flowers in a vase on a table. She said a friend gave her the bouquet when she was struggling, and it gives her hope and courage and fills her with warmth and appreciation. Jolene said such a small thing can make a real difference. Asked about her favorite nature spots, Deborah named a park with a forest trail, where getting lost in nature is calming, and a nearby beach where the sound of waves and sand underfoot make her feel peaceful and happy. Jolene shared a photo of a person walking on a beach with a surfboard, from a vacation in Bogota last summer, where watching the sunset over the water was beautiful and calming. Deborah said she likes to come to a spot by the water near her mom's old house to reflect on her mother's life and find peace, and she shared a photo of a small island with a lone boat in the water. Jolene asked about her traditions there. Deborah said she brings an amulet that belonged to her mother whenever she visits, because holding it lets her feel her mother's love and stay close to her, and she shared a photo of herself wearing a white shirt and a gold chain necklace. Jolene remarked how something so small can have such a big impact, and Deborah said such things remind us of the love and strength we carry inside and connect us to people we have lost. Jolene said they keep those people close in our hearts every day. Deborah added that Anna also wears a pendant in memory of her mother, which also brought them closer. Jolene said such reminders are a source of strength when needed. Deborah closed by telling Jolene that life is tough but to hang in there, look to her sources of strength, stay in touch, take care of herself, and know Deborah is always there to cheer her on. Jolene said she would stay in touch and said goodbye, and Deborah replied "Stay safe!" and said goodbye.

In the fifth session, on 9 February 2023 at 9:03 pm, Jolene opened by saying it had been a few days since they last talked, and she wanted to share news about a mini retreat she had done the previous Wednesday, most likely 8 February, to assess where she was in life. The retreat gave her a new outlook and a real confidence boost, and she said she achieved far more than she had imagined. Deborah praised her for stepping outside her comfort zone and believing in herself. Jolene said she accomplished something with her engineering project, coming up with some neat solutions that she is excited about, and she said she wanted to look into green tech, which could make a real difference in disadvantaged areas, and see how she could contribute. She then proposed an idea for a volunteer program in which engineers teach STEM to underprivileged kids, and asked Deborah's opinion. Deborah called it a great way to help and inspire others and said the kids would benefit from Jolene's knowledge. Jolene said she had not finished planning, but was considering teaming up with local schools and community centers to run workshops, and possibly inviting engineers as guest speakers to show the kids their career options. Deborah said guest speakers would give the kids a real-world view. Jolene said she had not yet reached out to any schools or centers, because she wanted to solidify the plan first, but she could not wait to start. Deborah said she was excited to hear how it went and asked to be kept informed. Jolene shared a photo of her planner sketches, a notebook with a pen and a page of notes, and thanked Deborah for her support. Deborah offered further tips or information if needed, and Jolene said she would let Deborah know if she needed anything else and called her awesome. Deborah said goodbye with "Take care!" and Jolene replied "Stay safe!"

In the sixth session, on 22 February 2023 at 4:12 pm, Jolene opened by saying she was buzzing after a great night out the previous evening, 21 February, with dinner and drinks with friends, where she was glad to let her hair down. She shared a photo of a plate of food and a glass of wine. Deborah said she had just visited a calming and nostalgic place, and shared a photo of a garden with flowers in buckets. Jolene asked about the flowers, and Deborah said the roses and dahlias bring her peace. She said she had lost a friend the previous week, around 15 February, and had been spending time in the garden to find comfort. Jolene offered condolences and asked how she was holding up. Deborah said it had been tough, but she was comforted by remembering their time together, which reminds her how special life is. Jolene said memories can bring comfort and joy, and Deborah replied that memories keep loved ones close. Deborah then shared a photo of two women riding a motorcycle on a dirt road, and said it was the last photo with her friend Karlie, taken last summer when they hiked, and that it was their last one together. She said they had a great time and she cannot help smiling whenever she sees it. This friend Karlie is distinct from Deborah's mother, whose last photo with her was the wheelchair hug shared in the first session. Asked where else she had traveled, Deborah said she had been blessed to visit a few places, and that Bali last year was one of her favorites, a gorgeous island that gave her peace and was great for yoga. She shared a photo of a swing on a beach under a blue sky. Jolene asked whether yoga on the beach was a thing, saying she had been wanting to try it, and Deborah said the sound of the waves and fresh air is wonderful. Jolene said she would definitely give it a go and would keep Deborah posted if she decided to go there. Deborah asked her to let her know how it goes, told her to enjoy it, and closed with "Take care!"

In the seventh session, on 25 February 2023 at 4:50 pm, Jolene said it had been a while since they last talked and that much had happened. She described balancing engineering school with her partner's video games, and said she now sets aside time for herself to do yoga and meditation, which gives her calm amid the chaos. Deborah welcomed the break and asked how these practices had been helping. Jolene said they had seriously saved her: yoga helps her chill out and gain perspective, and afterward she feels more alert and motivated. She shared a photo of a woman sitting on a yoga mat in a pose, calling it her most recent photo. Asked whether her partner does yoga with her, Jolene said he had started joining her sometimes, which is nice for bonding and relaxing and has brought them closer. She shared a photo of a man and a woman holding hands with rings on their fingers. Jolene said they are not married yet but have been together for three years, taking it slow and loving the ride, and that the ring on his hand is just a decoration, not a wedding ring. Deborah said enjoying the journey is the main thing and asked how they met. Jolene said they met in an engineering class in college, quickly became friends, and the friendship eventually blossomed into something more. She shared a photo of a book and a calculator on a table. Jolene said they still work on engineering projects together, which feels great because they understand each other's struggles and both love it. She shared a photo of a group of men standing in front of a building. Asked whether yoga or meditation had helped with stress, Jolene said that whenever she is overwhelmed she takes a break to breathe or meditate, which makes her calmer and clearer and better able to handle challenges. Deborah said it was great to see her progress, and Jolene thanked her, saying Deborah's support means a lot and that she will keep pushing forward and making time for herself. Deborah said she is always rooting for her, urged her to listen to her heart and take good care, and shared a photo she had taken while reflecting outdoors, a person sitting on a bench looking at the sunset, as a reminder to find peace even in chaos. Jolene asked about Deborah's daily routine. Deborah said that in the morning she meditates, does yoga, and teaches classes, and that the day before, 24 February, she had gone for her first morning jog in a nearby park and would now make jogging part of her routine. In the evenings she spends time with loved ones. Asked why she chose to exercise, Deborah said exercise is key for her because it makes her feel connected to her body. Jolene called it a great healthy habit. Deborah said "Can't pour from an empty cup," explaining that looking after ourselves gives us the energy to help others, and reminded Jolene that she is worth it too. Jolene thanked her, said Deborah's words really mean something to her, and promised to keep prioritizing self-care.
