Melanie asked whether Caroline had other treasured objects. Caroline shared a photo of a stack of bowls and described a hand-painted bowl that a friend made for her 18th birthday ten years earlier, about 2013. She said its pattern and colors remind her of art and self-expression. Melanie said she had just taken her family camping in the mountains the previous week, around 19 to 23 June 2023, and that it was a really nice time together. Caroline asked how it was. Melanie said they explored nature, roasted marshmallows around the campfire, and went on a hike, and that the view from the top was amazing. She said the two younger kids love nature and that the family moments were special and unforgettable. Caroline said it sounded great. Melanie asked what was new with Caroline. Caroline said she has been looking into counseling and mental health as a career because she wants to help people who have gone through the same things she has. She shared a photo of a bookshelf with many books. Melanie asked what kind of counseling and mental health services she wants to pursue. Caroline said she is still working out the details but is thinking about working with trans people, helping them accept themselves and supporting their mental health. Last Friday, around 23 June 2023, she attended an LGBTQ+ counseling workshop that she found enlightening. It covered different therapeutic methods and how best to work with trans people, and she was moved by how passionate the professionals were about creating a safe space for people like her. Melanie praised her dedication and asked what motivated her to pursue counseling. Caroline said her own journey and the support she received made a huge difference, and that counseling and support groups improved her life, which led her to care more about mental health and understanding herself. She now wants to create a safe, inviting place for people to grow. Melanie said Caroline has gained a great deal from her own experience and is making a big impact, and Caroline thanked her. Melanie congratulated Caroline for going after what she really cares about and shared a photo of a bookshelf filled with books in a room.

In Session 5, on 3 July 2023 at 1:36 pm, Caroline opened by saying that some big things had happened since they last spoke. The previous week, around late June 2023, she attended an LGBTQ+ pride parade, where everyone seemed so happy and she felt she belonged. She said it showed her how much the community has grown. Melanie congratulated her and asked whether the experience had influenced her goals. Caroline said it motivated her a lot: talking with the community made her want to use her own story to help others, and she is still sure counseling and mental health is the path she wants, and she is eager to give back. Melanie said she had signed up for a pottery class the day before, around 2 July 2023, which she described as like therapy because it lets her express herself and get creative. She asked whether Caroline had found any activities that give her the same feeling, and shared a photo that was described as a person holding a frisbee in their hand. Caroline said she is getting creative too, by learning the piano, and asked what had made Melanie try pottery. Melanie said she is a big fan of pottery because of the creativity and skill involved, and that making it is very calming. She shared a photo of a bowl with a black and white flower design, which she said she had made in her class. It took work, but she was proud of it. Caroline called the bowl gorgeous and asked whether Melanie had made it, and praised the effort and creativity. Melanie said pottery is a huge part of her life, not just a hobby, because it helps her express her emotions, and that clay brings her a lot of joy. Caroline said she was stoked that art is helping Melanie express herself. Melanie said she is excited to see where pottery takes her and asked whether anything was coming up that Caroline was looking forward to. Caroline said she is attending a transgender conference later in July 2023, and is excited to meet others in the community and learn more about advocacy. Melanie wished her a great time, to learn a lot, and to stay safe. Caroline said she would keep Melanie posted, and the two said goodbye, with Melanie saying she was eager to hear about the conference.

Deborah and Jolene are two women who have each lost their mothers. Across thirteen sessions they have kept in touch and grown from polite acquaintances sharing photographs into people who check in on each other's losses, goals, stress, and small pleasures. They first met in chat on 23 January 2023. Session twelve took place on 9 April 2023 at 4:30 pm, and session thirteen on 6 June 2023 at 3:56 pm, roughly eight weeks later, the longest gap in the record. Jolene opened the newest session by apologizing for having been out of touch because she had a lot going on.

Deborah is a yoga teacher whose central goal is to keep teaching and supporting her community. She finds yoga a source of peace and joy, a practice that helped her through a hard time and inspired her to share it with others. Jolene is an electrical engineering student whose mother died in 2022. Over time she has balanced school, exams, projects, work, her partner, her pets, and life outside class. Deborah has consistently offered encouragement and practical tools, while Jolene has increasingly brought her own problems into the conversation, moving from sharing achievements toward asking for help with stress and organization.

In the first session, on 23 January 2023 at 4:06 pm, Deborah said she had recently visited her late mother's old house, which holds many memories. Her mother had died a few years earlier. She shared a photo of their last photo together, her mother hugging her while both sat in wheelchairs. She described a special bench near the window where her mother liked to sit every morning to take in the view, and said she sometimes sits there herself to feel connected to her mother. She also mentioned a pendant that reminds her of her mother. Then she ended the session early, saying she had to run. Jolene responded with a photo of her own room in her mother's house, which has a bench and a window, and said she has many memories of that room. Jolene wears a heart-shaped pendant with a bird on it, given to her by her mother in Paris in 2010. Her jewelry also carries a symbol of freedom, a reminder to pursue her goals. She was enthusiastic about Deborah's yoga work and looked forward to their next chat. From the beginning, both women have kept a physical link to their mothers: Deborah through her mother's bench and pendant, and Jolene through her mother's room and pendant.

The second session took place on the morning of 27 January 2023, at 9:49 am. Deborah told Jolene that her father had passed away suddenly around 25 January, and that the family was shell-shocked. She said she was channeling her grief into spending more time with family and cherishing memories. She shared a photo of one woman hugging another seated on a couch. Jolene offered condolences. Deborah said looking back on good memories was comforting, and that the family had been going through the family album together. She shared a photo of her parents' wedding in 1993 and said she and her husband were trying to be as good a family as her parents had been. Asked what she valued most in her relationship, Deborah said love and openness had kept her and her husband close. She finished that thread with a photo of a handwritten note she had received the day before from her group members, thanking her for her positive influence. Moments like that, she said, remind her why she is so passionate about yoga.

The second session then moved to Deborah's memories and to pets. Asked where she most often practices yoga, Deborah shared a photo of a living room with a television and a window in her old home, which she visits now and then for her mother. Sitting by the window gives her a sense of her mother's presence. She next shared a window seat where her mother would sit every night with a book, since reading was one of her hobbies. The morning bench and the evening window seat both belong to her mother's daily rhythms. Deborah also said travel was her mother's great passion, and shared a photo of the sky seen from an airplane window. Jolene then introduced her pets, which calm her down and make her happy. She shared a photo of her snake Susie's head poking out from a bed. Jolene described how her second snake, Seraphim, had slipped out of its cage and coiled up beside her while she was gaming, which she found very funny. She had bought Seraphim a year earlier in Paris. Deborah said pets bring so much happiness.

Jolene then shared a photo of herself and her partner gaming the previous week. They are both crazy about the console game "Detroit." She had learned to play on her own as a child, and she and her partner planned to play "The Walking Dead" the following Saturday. Deborah closed by telling her to take care and keep spreading good vibes.

The third session took place on 1 February 2023 at 7:03 pm. Jolene said she had been busy because her engineering professor had given the class a huge robotics project. She called it tough but fun, and said it was pushing her to get creative and problem-solve. She shared a photo of a robot on a table beside a laptop. She now really enjoys the project, which she described as like solving a puzzle. Deborah then said she had met her new neighbor Anna the previous day, 31 January, and shared a photo of a yellow family sign. They had met at yoga in the park and talked about how yoga had improved their lives. Jolene shared a photo of a purse with a plant on a table, an image she would share again later. Deborah asked whether Jolene had ever thought about resuming yoga. Jolene replied that she and her partner had planned to play the console together. Deborah then said she had to run, and Jolene said she would see her soon. As in the first session, Deborah ended abruptly.

The fourth session took place on 4 February 2023 at 9:48 am. Jolene said she had been on an emotional rollercoaster but was coping. The previous week she had reached a major milestone: she had planned, researched, and designed a sustainable water purifier for a rural community. Seeing it deliver clean water was deeply satisfying, and it gave her a sense of purpose. Her career aspiration is to keep working in engineering and make a positive impact on communities in need. Deborah told her to take a deep breath and remember why she does this, and said teaching yoga is a great way to find balance.

Deborah then said she had bonded with Anna during the previous day's yoga class, on 3 February. She shared photos of two women in a dance studio and a woman doing a pose on a chair. They had been trying Warrior II, and they supported each other through the hard poses. Deborah described a modified seated twist: sit on a chair, twist the torso to one side with a hand on the knee, hold for a few breaths, then switch sides. Jolene shared a photo of her bookshelf. She was really into "Sapiens," and two weeks earlier she had read "Avalanche" by Neal Stephenson in one sitting. Deborah then shared a photo of a bouquet a friend had given her when she was struggling, which gives her hope, courage, and warmth.

The fourth session also touched on nature and places of meaning. Deborah named a park with a forest trail and a nearby beach where the waves make her feel peaceful. Jolene shared a photo of a person walking on a beach with a surfboard, from a vacation in Bogota last summer. Deborah said she likes to visit a spot by the water near her mother's old house, and she brings an amulet that belonged to her mother on every visit. She shared a photo of herself in a white shirt and gold chain necklace. Jolene remarked how something so small can have such a big impact. Deborah added that Anna also wears a pendant in memory of her mother, which had brought the two of them closer. Deborah closed by telling Jolene to hang in there and know Deborah is always there to cheer her on. Jolene said goodbye, and Deborah replied "Stay safe!"

The fifth session took place on 9 February 2023 at 9:03 pm. Jolene shared news about a mini retreat she had done the previous Wednesday, most likely 8 February, to assess where she stood in life. It gave her a real confidence boost. She had also made progress on her engineering project and wanted to look into green technology. She proposed a volunteer program in which engineers teach STEM to underprivileged kids, and asked for Deborah's opinion. Deborah called it a great way to help and inspire others. Jolene was considering partnering with local schools and inviting engineers as guest speakers, but admitted she had not yet contacted anyone because she wanted to solidify the plan first. Deborah asked to be kept informed. Jolene shared a photo of her planner sketches, and Deborah said "Take care!" Jolene replied "Stay safe!"

The sixth session took place on 22 February 2023 at 4:12 pm. Jolene said she was buzzing after a great night out with friends on 21 February, with dinner and drinks, and she shared a photo of a plate of food and a glass of wine. Deborah said she had just visited a calming and nostalgic place, a garden with roses and dahlias in buckets. She then said she had lost a friend around 15 February and had been spending time in the garden to find comfort. Jolene offered condolences. Deborah shared a photo of two women riding a motorcycle on a dirt road, the last photo she has with her friend Karlie, taken last summer when they went hiking. Karlie is separate from Deborah's mother. Asked where else she had traveled, Deborah said Bali last year was one of her favorites and was wonderful for yoga. Jolene said she had been wanting to try yoga on the beach and would keep Deborah posted. Deborah closed with "Take care!"

The seventh session took place on 25 February 2023 at 4:50 pm. Jolene said she now sets aside time for yoga and meditation, which gives her calm amid the chaos. Her partner had started joining her sometimes, which had brought them closer. She shared a photo of a couple holding hands with rings on their fingers. She explained that she and her partner are not married yet, have been together for three years, and are taking things slowly. They met in an engineering class in college, and they still work on projects together. Jolene also shared photos of a book and calculator on a table, and of a group of men in front of a building. Asked whether yoga or meditation had helped with stress, Jolene said that whenever she is overwhelmed she takes a break to breathe or meditate. Deborah said she was always rooting for her and urged her to listen to her heart, and shared a photo of a person watching the sunset from a bench, as a reminder to find peace even in chaos.

Jolene then asked about Deborah's daily routine. Deborah said that in the morning she meditates, does yoga, and teaches classes. On 24 February she had gone for her first morning jog in a nearby park, and she planned to make jogging a routine. Exercise makes her feel connected to her body. She said "Can't pour from an empty cup," explaining that looking after ourselves gives us the energy to help others, and reminded Jolene that she is worth it too. Jolene promised to keep prioritizing self-care.

The eighth session took place on 2 March 2023 at 7:18 pm. Deborah said Anna had recently brought her a vegan stir-fry. Jolene said her favorite comfort food is lasagna. Asked whether she had found time for herself, Jolene said that on Friday, 24 February, she had done yoga and meditation, and she shared a photo of a room with a wooden floor and a window. Jolene shared once more the purse-with-a-plant photo. She said she had taken Seraphim to the park on Sunday, 26 February, and Seraphim loved it. She shared a photo of a lizard among leaves, though Jolene describes the animal as her snake. Deborah said birds chirping and a gentle breeze remind her what really matters, and Jolene agreed it is a reminder to slow down.

Deborah then asked whether there was anything Jolene wanted to be more mindful of. Jolene said she needed to pay more attention to her stress and mental health, because exams and deadlines had left her feeling overwhelmed and her to-do list seemed never-ending. She shared a photo of a desk with a notebook and a monitor, and asked for tips on studying and time management. Deborah advised breaking work into smaller pieces, setting goals, and using a planner, and offered to help build a study plan. She wished her good luck with her exams and promised to send her a mug like the yellow coffee cup in her photo, with a handwritten encouraging message. Jolene said the mug would cheer her up.

The ninth session took place on 13 March 2023 at 11:22 am. Deborah said they had not corresponded in a long time. She had started a yoga class in her neighborhood, which she had hosted on Friday, 10 March, and shared a photo of a group of women posing together. She said it felt wonderful to watch the class transform her neighbors, and that teaching has brought her great friendships and community. Then Jolene said she was having a hard time with her engineering assignments and asked whether they could still talk about time management. Deborah agreed and suggested finding a time that worked for both of them. Jolene said she would check her schedule. As of this session, she had not yet confirmed a time.

The tenth session took place on 22 March 2023 at 5:35 pm. Deborah said she knew exams and deadlines were difficult right now. Jolene said trying to fit everything in felt like playing catch-up. She was using the Pomodoro Technique, 25 minutes of work followed by a 5-minute break, but still struggled to prioritize. Deborah said she builds a daily to-do list and shared a photo of hers. Jolene said lists felt overwhelming when the stack of tasks got big, and shared a photo of a notepad. Deborah then described the Eisenhower Matrix, which sorts tasks into four boxes by urgency and importance, and shared a photo of a pair of scissors on a sheet of paper as a visual breakdown. Jolene said she would give it a go. Deborah then shared that she and Anna had recently watched the sunset by the sea and realized they inspire each other. She shared a photo of a person walking on a beach with a surfboard and asked what it made Jolene think of. Jolene said it made her think of learning to surf, and that she had got a beginner's guide and just needed the right time and place for a lesson. Deborah praised her first steps and said the experience matters as much as the end result.

The eleventh session took place on 28 March 2023 at 4:03 pm, and it was lighter in tone and about small pleasures. Jolene opened with "long time no talk" and said that on Friday, 24 March, she had a breakthrough on her engineering project. She shared a photo of a hand holding a pair of scissors. Deborah congratulated her. Deborah then said she had bought new props for her yoga class and shared a photo of a group doing yoga. Jolene shared a photo of a cardboard mat with a cup of coffee on it, saying she had new details for "this case" and asking Deborah to rate it. Deborah said she had also bought a candle, and shared a photo of a candle with a sprig of rosemary. Jolene said she loved creating a serene space with soothing scents like lavender and rosemary. Deborah said certain smells can transport a person to a place of peace. Jolene asked for favorite music, and Deborah recommended instrumental music, naming a track called "Savana" and an album called 'Sleep,' which she was listening to. Jolene said she loves Nils Frahm and Olafur Arnalds during practice, and said she would check the recommendations out. Deborah asked her to share her thoughts. Jolene said "See you!" and Deborah closed with "Take care and keep up the good work!"

The twelfth session took place on 9 April 2023 at 4:30 pm, and it was the first in which Deborah led with news of her own leisure and reflection. She opened with "Great to see you!" and said she had had a blast biking nearby with her neighbor the previous week, which was freeing and beautiful. She had also visited an art show with a friend that day, which reminded her of her mother. She shared a photo of a large brown and white photo of a person. Deborah said her mother had been interested in art and believed it could convey strong emotions and connect people in unique ways. At an art show, she feels as though they are still experiencing it together, which is hard but comforting. Jolene said finding something that helps you cope is great. Deborah said simple things like artwork can bring back powerful emotions and remind us of those we have lost. Jolene said her snakes cannot chat, but their time together teaches her to slow down and be in tune with herself, and that playing video games with her partner after a long day helps her relax. Deborah asked how these activities had helped during tough times. Jolene said they bring her and her partner closer together. Jolene then said she had been working on a big project, which has been tough but cool to watch take shape. Deborah said she was waiting to hear how everything turned out. Jolene promised to keep her updated, and Deborah said she would always be there for her. The session ended with Deborah telling Jolene to make time for the things that bring her joy.

The thirteenth session took place on 6 June 2023 at 3:56 pm, and it is the most recent. Jolene opened with "Hey Deborah!" and apologized for the long silence. She said she had finally wrapped up the tough engineering project the previous month, in May, and shared a photo of a solar-powered vehicle with a solar panel on the back. Deborah congratulated her, and Jolene said finishing it was a big milestone. Jolene said she is now interning at a well-known engineering firm, which has given her a chance to test her skills and gain real-world experience. She shared a photo of a group of construction workers posing for a picture and called them her new colleagues. The best part, she said, has been applying what she learned in school to real projects, and seeing her ideas come to life. The internship has stoked her love of engineering and encouraged her to keep striving for her dreams. Hanging out with people who love what they do has inspired her to stay focused.

Deborah asked whether Jolene had found a good work-life balance. Jolene said that had been tough, that she had been slogging away and found it hard to make time for her hobbies and for chilling out. Deborah suggested that she consider taking breaks and finding activities like yoga to help her unwind. Jolene said she was trying, and shared a photo of a man standing on a rock with his arms outstretched. She described it as an example of how she had spent the previous morning: yoga on top of Mount Talkeetna. The photo shows a man rather than Jolene herself. Deborah asked how long she had been doing yoga and meditation. Jolene said she had been doing them sporadically for about three years, and that they had helped her with stress and kept her centered. She said she had no idea how she would have survived without them. Deborah then shared a photo of a room with a bench and a window, calling it her favorite studio and always so calming. The bench and window echo the ones that have run through both women's accounts since the first session. Jolene asked for advice on calming the mind and breathing during yoga. Deborah recommended a few minutes of mindful breathing each day: sitting with eyes closed, taking deep breaths, and focusing on how the air feels entering and leaving the body. Jolene said she would definitely try it. Deborah offered more tips whenever Jolene needed them and closed with "Take care!" Jolene replied "See you!" and the session ended there.

Taken together, the memory shows a steady arc. Deborah's grief over her mother and father, and her loss of her friend Karlie in February, sit alongside her yoga teaching, her neighborhood class, her friendship with Anna, her routines of meditation and jogging, and her recent outings biking and at an art show. She has a growing interest in the sensory side of practice, from candles and rosemary to instrumental music. Her practice spaces keep returning to a bench and a window, which tie her to her mother's home. Jolene's grief for her mother sits alongside her engineering work, from the robotics project and water purifier to her volunteer STEM plans, her spring breakthrough, the completed solar-powered vehicle, and her current internship. Her life also includes friendships, her partner, her snakes Susie and Seraphim, her reading and gaming, and her efforts to manage stress and time. Jolene moved from sharing achievements toward asking for help, and by June she was describing exhaustion from the internship and turning to yoga and meditation to recover. Deborah moved from openly grieving to offering practical tools, encouragement, and small pleasures.

Several threads remain open. Deborah still owes Jolene the mug with the encouraging message, promised in February. Jolene has yet to confirm the time-management conversation and has not reported back on the Eisenhower Matrix. She still intends to try beach yoga in Bali and to learn surfing, and has not said whether she has taken up either. She has not reported back on "Savana," 'Sleep,' or the Nils Frahm and Olafur Arnalds recommendations. Deborah has asked to hear how Jolene's volunteer STEM plans progress, and those plans have not been mentioned since February. The big project from April is answered by the June session, which reports that it is finished. Jolene has said she will try Deborah's mindful breathing, and Deborah has offered more help whenever it is needed. Jolene's internship, her exhaustion, and her effort to restore work-life balance are the newest concerns in the record, and they are the most likely subject of any future check-in.

This memory covers fifteen conversations between Maria and John, from 17 December 2022 through 20 May 2023. The most recent is the fifteenth session, held on 20 May 2023 at 7:38 pm. Maria and John reconnected on 17 December 2022 after a long gap; John had returned on 16 December 2022 from a family road trip. From the start they encourage each other, praise each other's work, and describe themselves as a team. Their friendship centres on family, community service, education, kindness, and personal growth. Maria volunteers at a homeless shelter. John has been involved in campaigning and community politics, later focusing on education and infrastructure policy and, most recently, on support for military veterans.

The second session took place on 22 December 2022 at 6:10 pm. Maria said it had been a few days since they last chatted. On 21 December 2022 she had donated her old car to the homeless shelter where she volunteers. John said the campaign had been interesting and that he had been networking to gather people's input. A conversation with someone who shared amazing stories had fired his passion for improving local education, and he stressed that investing in future generations is the foundation of progress. He said Maria's support motivates him. He shared photos of his family picnicking in the park, calling them the reason he never gives up and his rock in tough times, and of the family on a playground swing. Maria said her family is small, but she loves spending time with friends, usually watching movies, hiking, and hosting game nights, and that quality connections matter most to her. John shared photos of a family dinner and a homemade pizza night, saying shared meals keep them close. Maria said she had recently made peach cobbler. John ended by saying he was off to taekwondo, a new activity separate from his kickboxing. Both agreed to keep cherishing time with loved ones.

The third session took place on 1 January 2023 at 8:30 pm. John said he had joined a service-focused online group in late December 2022, whose members share inspiring stories, advice, and encouragement. The group had held events, including a visit to a homeless shelter to hand out food and supplies, where seeing people's smiles showed him they had made a real difference. He shared a photo of a poster with Santa Claus, which fits the toy drive the group organized for children in need. The group is brainstorming ways to help underserved communities access education, mentorship, job training, and resume building. Maria said empowering people through education is crucial. John then revealed he had recently failed a military aptitude test, which left him stressed, and said Maria's support means a lot. Maria reassured him she has his back. She shared a photo of a sunset over the ocean she had taken at the beach in December 2022, saying nature's beauty reminds her to slow down. John recalled the film camera he had as a child and said nature helps people remember small joys.

The fourth session took place on 9 January 2023 at 7:06 pm. Maria said she had become friends with a fellow volunteer, and that they both love helping others. John said he had been busy with work and family, but in roughly the first week of January 2023 he had an unexpected incident on his way home. He shared a photo of a car with a broken windshield, and Maria said she was glad he was alright. He also shared a photo of a tattoo with a quote reminding him to stay strong in tough times. He handled the incident by staying calm and asking for assistance, and Maria praised his resilience. Asked how he calms down, John said he likes to look at the sunset. Maria asked about his political goals. John had been learning about his neighborhood's needs by talking with community leaders, and he felt optimistic. Maria said she had been taking notes on local politics and shared a photo of her notebook, which gave John new ideas. He had a community meeting coming up in mid-January 2023, where education and infrastructure upgrades would be discussed. He said he would stand up for the community, and Maria called speaking out admirable. John shared photos of a team around a table and of two people shaking hands. Maria said teamwork and unity bring positive change, and they agreed they make a great team.

The fifth session took place on 28 January 2023 at 1:17 pm. John said he had attended the community meeting and found hearing everyone's worries very interesting. He saw how crucial the upgrades are, especially for kids, and said he is upset by the state of local education. He asked how they could make things better. Maria said they should fight for more money and resources for schools and raise awareness that education matters for everyone. John said it breaks his heart that kids lack resources, and that his own kids have so much while others do not. Maria then said that around 21 January 2023 she had volunteered at a shelter event for kids, and she shared a photo of three women in green aprons. She said her aunt, who believed in volunteering, had helped her family when they struggled. The most impactful moment, she said, was a sad eight-year-old girl sitting alone, who had no other family. Maria sat with her, and they ended up laughing together. John shared a photo of a little girl kissing a doll, which reminded him of his own childhood doll and of the need to look out for others who feel down. Maria said spreading kindness makes a real difference, and they agreed they are on the same page.

The sixth session took place on 5 February 2023 at 2:33 pm. Maria said that around 3 February 2023 she had taken part in a heartwarming charity event that showed her the power of collective effort. Seeing gratitude on people's faces was rewarding. At the event she had talked with a man named David, whose story of hardship showed her that everyone deserves understanding. John asked whether she knew any organizations that could help him, and Maria said she had linked David with a nearby organization offering housing and support for homeless individuals, and she shared the flyer. Asked whether John had ever needed help, Maria said that when she was younger her family had money problems and relied on her aunt, which taught her the importance of helping others. John said we learn a lot from our own struggles and revealed that he had just started helping with a community food drive for people who had lost their jobs. He shared photos of himself at a food bank and of a Thanksgiving potluck and food drive flyer, saying the response had been overwhelming. Maria offered to help with networking or at future events, and John gratefully accepted. He said friendship means a lot and that they can work toward a shared goal. Earlier in this session, when Maria asked what had got him into politics, John said he feels a strong urge to serve his country and community, and that running for office was his chance to make an impact. He did not say at the time whether he was currently running.

The seventh session took place on 25 February 2023 at 8:55 pm. Maria said that on 24 February 2023 she had met Jean at the homeless shelter. Jean had gone through a divorce, lost her job, and become homeless, yet stayed optimistic and valued the little things. John found it inspiring, and both agreed that joy and hope can be found in any circumstance. Maria said she had recently taken a creative writing class that she found enlightening. John said his colleague Rob had invited him to a beginner's yoga class, which he had not yet scheduled. He then said he was running for office again. He called it a wild ride that has left him more excited than ever, and said that after his last run he had seen the impact he could make through politics.

The eighth session took place on 6 March 2023 at 6:03 pm. Maria said she had not talked to John in a while. Her grandmother had passed away the previous week, and it had been really hard. She was trying to stay positive but finding it tough. John offered his support. He said he had just had a picnic with his wife and kids, and he shared a photo of the family on the grass with a baby. Their one-year-old son is named Kyle. Asked about parenting, John said it has been a wild ride full of ups and downs, but love and happiness outweigh everything else. The family goes to the park a few times a week, and he finds activities by looking for things they will enjoy, such as a violin concert the whole family loved. Maria said she had loved similar activities with her siblings. She shared a photo of a castle in a shadow box she had made after a trip to England, and said she wanted to recreate some of London's charm at home. John then said he had retaken the aptitude test the week before, got great results, and felt drawn to serve his country in this way. Their tone is consistently friendly, upbeat and encouraging, and they usually end with a "see you soon" or similar goodbye. Calvin's life centers on music, touring, recording and travel, with frequent mentions of Japan, Tokyo and Boston. Dave's centers on cars, his shop and garage work, outdoor and park activities, and more recently playing guitar in a rock band. Earlier details are sometimes restated or shifted in time.

Session 1 (23 March 2023): Dave had recently attended an event he called a car lover's paradise and had been spending time at a calm park. Calvin had a big life change and shared a photo of his new "mansion." He was moving there the following month, where his agent had found him a place to stay. He planned a few months in Japan before going to Boston. He had never been to the park Dave mentioned and said he would check it out when he was back.

Session 2 (26 March 2023): Calvin had bought a new luxury car, which he said was what he deserved after hard work, and he had written new songs and had studio sessions the previous week. Dave had gone to a music festival in Boston the weekend before, which reminded him why he loves music. His favorite act was Aerosmith, whom he finally saw live.

A producer told him to stay true to himself and sound unique. He dreams of touring the world and hopes his music reaches a global audience. He planned to go to Boston after the Frank Ocean tour and suggested grabbing a bite together. Dave said Boston's music scene is awesome, named Paradise Rock, House of Blues and Fenway Park, and asked to have a front-row spot at Calvin's shows. He had gone to a car show and said classic car restorations are why he is into auto engineering.

Session 4 (1 May 2023): Dave announced he had opened his own car maintenance shop, which he called a dream come true. He works on everything from regular maintenance to full restorations of classic cars. He invited Calvin to visit. Calvin said he would like to visit and asked what cars Dave works on.

Session 5 (3 May 2023): Dave is teaming up with a local garage and loves the job. He called his current project cool but challenging and hopes to build a custom car from scratch someday. When Calvin said his creativity was frozen, Dave suggested immersing himself in things he loves, such as concerts or favorite albums, and taking a break from music. He encouraged Calvin never to give up. Calvin said long drives help him relax and clear his head, and both said they would stay in touch.

Session 6 (16 May 2023): Calvin's place was flooded the week before, but he saved his music gear and favorite microphone. He was waiting for insurance before repairs, and he stayed positive. He had an upcoming Tokyo performance "this month" (May 2023), which he hoped would grow his following. Dave said he opened his car shop "last week" and invited friends to celebrate. This conflicts with Session 4, so the opening date is unclear.

Session 7 (31 May 2023): Calvin had toured with Frank Ocean "last week," and his Tokyo show was "unreal," with an insane crowd. He said performing live "always fuels my soul" and that working on cars helps him chill. He was excited to perform in Boston for people from home. He said: "I booked a trip to a mountainous region for next month!" Calvin asked him to take lots of pictures and show them when he returned, and Dave agreed.

He trusts the mechanic, who is "doing his best to get my car running again." He shared a photo of a small Japanese town with a mountain in the background, seen from his living room. He said he had recently joined a rock band, has been practicing guitar, and shared a photo of the band.

They often encourage each other through setbacks, share photos freely, and return to a small set of recurring subjects: gaming, programming, their pets, travel, food, and future plans. Over the spring the talk moved toward real-world activity, including a charity tournament, volunteer software work, and outings with friends. The most recent session, on 23 May, covers an amusement park visit, a local tournament, and a personal milestone. Earlier threads remain open and are described below in roughly chronological order, followed by open commitments and notes on dates.

In their first conversation, on Thursday, 17 March 2022 at 3:47 pm, John said he was glad to finally talk with James. James said video games keep him motivated because they bring him joy and excitement, and John said games help him relax after a long day. James was absorbed in The Witcher 3 and praised its story and atmosphere. John had not played it yet but planned to. He had just signed up for a programming class, having done some HTML and CSS a few years earlier, and he wanted to refresh those skills. James said he first tried programming in college and that it is now central to his life. He has worked with Python and C++, has built a website, and has created game mods, and he shared a photo of a scene from one of them. At that point he had not used other languages but hoped to. John suggested they might someday develop mobile applications together, and James liked the idea.

In the same conversation James described his two dogs, Max and Daisy, and shared a photo of them tied to a fence. He proposed an app for dog walking and pet care that would connect owners with reliable dog walkers and offer helpful pet-care information. Its distinguishing feature would be a personal touch: users enter their pet's preferences and needs so the app feels customized. He shared a photo of a handwritten note about the idea. James finds deep satisfaction in creating something and seeing it come to life. He writes his goals in a notebook and enjoys checking them off, and he shared a photo of himself holding it. He is also building a computer game based on characters he sketched as a child, when he drew comics. He wants to combine his two favorite passions, gaming and storytelling, and finds the challenge enjoyable. He promised to keep John updated and said he might later invite John to help with the game's HTML, which John agreed to and said he looked forward to. John also shared a photo of a medical chart with procedure instructions. Nobody explained it, and the conversations never return to it.

The same session covered the previous day, 16 March 2022. James had gone bowling and gotten two strikes, and he said he loves bowling. John said he does not enjoy bowling and cannot bowl well because his fingers are too big, and he mentioned he might start running in the mornings. James was sorry they could not bowl together, so John suggested slot machines and arcades. James said he once got so absorbed in slot machines that someone pickpocketed his wallet, and John joked that he would watch James's pockets. John then suggested VR gaming, which he had tried a few times and found very immersive. James said it feels remarkably real. They agreed to try VR together "next Saturday," which could mean Saturday 19 or Saturday 26 March. No later conversation says whether they did it.

In a second conversation, on Sunday, 20 March 2022 at 9:26 pm, James said that since they last talked he had made a game avatar and joined a new online platform. Chatting with other gamers there feels like a new adventure each time, and he described gaming as their shared language and passion. He said games have been a refuge for him in tough times. When he feels overwhelmed, games work like therapy, letting him relax, forget his troubles, and get lost in another world. John said gaming also helps him escape stress. When John asked about new interests, James said he had been trying different styles of games to test himself in new ways. John said his new hobby is metal detecting on beaches with a detector he recently bought. So far he has found mostly bottle caps, a couple of coins, and once a gold ring. James wished him good luck. James then shared photos of his dogs, whom he calls his best buddies: one shows them running in a field with balls in their mouths, another shows Daisy waiting for a treat, and a third shows a dog on a bed with a name tag. He said he has trained them to sit, stay, paw, and rollover, that they learn quickly, and that they are like family. John said he wants a pet very much but is not there yet. James offered to help him find the perfect one, and John said he would keep the offer in mind.

In a third conversation, on Sunday, 27 March 2022 at 12:40 am, John said he had recently had a big win in his game the previous week, advancing to the next level, which boosted his confidence. James said he was learning a musical instrument, which he called quite the journey. He shared a photo of a drum kit with a white drum and a black drum, without naming the instrument in words. John said he also plays drums and shared a photo of his own drum set on a table. He had been playing for a month and found it tough but fun. James had started only a few days earlier, was practicing daily, and was already seeing improvements, which he called tough but rewarding. John also said that since they last spoke he had attended a gaming convention, where he tried many games, met developers, and competed in a tournament. He shared a photo of the crowded convention hall. He said he played an intense CS:GO tournament, and watching skilled players inspired him to improve. James said he had recently got a new high-end gaming system, had been playing all kinds of games to relax after work, and enjoyed connecting with friends who share his passion. He stays motivated by setting small goals and tracking progress, and he was getting into RPGs and strategy games. John asked him to update him on the new genres, and James agreed.

In a fourth conversation, on Monday, 4 April 2022 at 2:13 pm, James said that on 3 April he had joined an online gaming tournament, which he found very intense and fun, and he shared a group photo from it. He made it to the semifinals and won some rounds, and he shared a screenshot of his character. The final rounds were tough and he did not advance, but he said it was close and that he had a blast competing with talented players. He met his whole team and regretted not getting a photo with them. One member gave him a couple of gaming tips, and the team gave him autographs, which made him very happy. The most important lesson he remembered was that you always need to communicate correctly with the team and never put your ego above team success. John agreed that communication and teamwork are essential in gaming. James usually talks with his team by voice chat, which he finds fast and effective. Their favorite game together is Apex Legends, which he described as intense, with awesome graphics and super fast-paced gameplay. He shared a screenshot of the team playing it. He was thinking of trying RPGs or MOBAs and shared a photo of a game cover. John said RPGs offer engaging stories and MOBAs epic multiplayer fights, and he asked James to report back. James agreed to share his thoughts once he tries them. They said goodbye, and John told James to stay safe.

In a fifth conversation, on Tuesday, 12 April 2022 at 9:52 am, James said he had adopted a pup from a shelter in Stamford the previous week, and that his days had been much happier with him in the family. He named the pup Ned and shared a photo of a dog and a cat sitting on a dog bed. John said he had not made much progress lately because work and other things had been busy, but gaming is a good way to forget life's stresses. He was playing a new RPG with a very cool story and a futuristic, dystopian world, and he shared a photo of a city at night. He said it had a fun story, an awesome world, and tough gameplay. He warned that it was laggy and sometimes produced errors, and he shared a photo of a computer screen showing one error from the day before. James said the game must still be raw and that he would rather wait for the bugs to be fixed. John offered to send him a link, and James agreed to wait for it and try the game.

In a sixth conversation, on Wednesday, 20 April 2022 at 9:32 pm, John said he had great news: on Tuesday, 19 April, he met three cool new friends in his programming course who share his passion. James said that on Thursday, 14 April he had worked with one of his gaming pals on a project that combined programming and gaming. Together they created a virtual world inspired by The Witcher 3. James did not have a screenshot of the full world, but he shared one of the character he created, a woman in armor kneeling on a rock, and called the work a lot but very rewarding. He said the character was inspired by a stranger he saw on a walk with his dogs around 6 April. The woman was someone he had never seen nearby before, and he felt he had fallen in love at first sight. He regretted not approaching her but remembered her appearance and put it into the game. John said real-life experiences can be inspiring and that the virtual world is connected to the real one. He then said that on 18 April he had wanted to be alone with nature, and he shared a photo of a river running through a canyon surrounded by mountains. When James asked what motivates him, John said he follows the principle that only those who rest well work well, so chilling with friends and traveling always motivate him.

Travel came up in the same session. James said he loves to travel and visited Italy in 2021, which he described as very beautiful with delicious food. He has also been to Turkey and Mexico. John said he has always dreamed of visiting Italy, and that the last country he visited was Japan. He was impressed by its technologically advanced megacities, with huge screens on buildings, and enjoyed the very tasty street food. He shared a photo of a busy city street at night. James suggested they go somewhere together in 2023. John said he hoped it would work out, and James said he would start looking for a country they could visit together.

In a seventh conversation, on Saturday, 23 April 2022 at 11:04 am, James said things had been crazy, and that the previous Thursday he had taken his dogs on a hike through nice trails with fresh air. This "last Thursday" most likely refers to 21 April, though the conversation does not state the date. He shared a photo of a man walking two dogs on a woodland path. He said there is nothing like being surrounded by lush greenery and clean air, and that he loves the crunch of leaves underfoot and the peacefulness, which help him clear his head. John said he wished he could spend more time in nature and that he needed some chill vibes too, because things had been crazy for him. James asked what was going on. John said he had been super busy at work with deadlines everywhere, and that a difficult coding assignment had him stuck. He was trying to make a new algorithm work better, and he found it frustrating because he hates not making progress. James was not sure about John's algorithm specifically, but he suggested breaking the problem into smaller steps, researching similar algorithms, asking other programmers for advice, and not being afraid to seek help, adding that every problem has a solution. John said James's words had really helped and that he would not quit. He ended by sharing a photo of a notebook with a quote written on it.

In an eighth conversation, on Friday, 29 April 2022 at 2:36 pm, John said he was taking on freelance programming to hone his skills. He was building a website for a local small business, his first professional project outside of class. Progress was slow and there had been hiccups. His main challenge was figuring out how to add payments to the site. He had used some resources and some help to understand the process, and he said he was getting closer to a solution. James encouraged him to use setbacks to learn and grow. James said that about three days earlier, around 26 April, he had bought an adventure book with fantasy novels and cool art, and he shared a photo of a male character in it. John said the art reminded him of reading fantasy as a child and recommended "The Name of the Wind." James had not heard of it but said he would check it out, and he shared a photo of a set of three books on a wooden table. John said he was sure James would love the trilogy. James then shared a photo of Daisy lying on a bed beside a computer while he was gaming, and said his dogs often watch him play and hug him. John said he was currently playing Assassin's Creed Valhalla. James said he was trying strategy games like it and shared a photo of a world map on a TV screen. John guessed Civilization VI, and James described it as a high-quality turn-based strategy game about managing resources, leading armies, and conquering territories. It requires planning and good decisions, works his problem-solving, and feels satisfying when his plans pay off. He had been playing it for about a month. John said he enjoys games that make him think. He said that on 27 April he had played an exciting strategy board game with friends and shared a photo of it. He also described a card game, which he could not name, in which players must match the color or number of the card on the table, with occasional trading, drawing, or skipping. James did not recognize it. John also described a social deduction game about finding the impostors, which he found super fun, and advised James to play it with a large group.

In a ninth conversation, on Wednesday, 4 May 2022 at 7:01 pm, James said it had been a wild week. On what he called "last Friday," meaning 29 April, a bug in the code of a project he had worked on for weeks broke the game mechanics. He had nearly finished the project, but he debugged it for hours without success and found it very disappointing. A group of friends teamed up with him, and they got it fixed. He said it is awesome to have people who share the same passions, help each other, and bring their own ideas. This project is probably the computer game he has been building, though the conversation does not name it. John said he had the day off that day and had some new friends over to watch movies. He is trying to socialize more and said balancing work and enjoyment is important. He invited James to the next gathering, and James said he was definitely in. James said he had spent the day with his beloved pets and shared a photo of two dogs playing in a fenced area. Daisy is a Labrador who loves her toys but most of all loves to eat, and the other two are shepherds, which James said are very loyal. James said his pets, computer games, travel, and pizza bring him happiness. John said he loves pizza too and that his favorite is Hawaiian, because the sweet and salty combination delights him. He shared a photo of a pineapple and ham pizza on a wooden board. James likes pepperoni, which he called an amazing combination of spicy salami and cheese, and also likes cheese pizza and prosciutto. John had not tried prosciutto yet but had heard it was great. James urged him to try it, promised he would not regret it, and asked him to share his impressions. They wished each other well, with James adding "Bon Appetit."

In a tenth conversation, on Sunday, 8 May 2022 at 12:45 am, James opened by apologizing for not getting back sooner and asked how John was and whether he had any new games he was into. John said he knew James was busy at work. He said he had been organizing something with friends "yesterday," meaning Saturday, 7 May. He shared a photo of a wooden table with a game controller and asked James to guess. James guessed a new game's icon, but John said it was not a new game. They had put together a tournament for CS:GO, their favorite game, which drew many people and raised a good amount of money for charity. James said it must have taken a lot of effort but was worth it. John said seeing everyone come together for a good cause was very rewarding, and that he wants to organize more events because they combine his interests and help the community. James said combining gaming and volunteering is a great idea. The main goal had been to raise money for a dog shelter not far from John's street, and they reached it. Leftover money went to buy groceries and cook food for homeless people, who were very happy about it. James praised him for helping those in need, told him to keep up the good work, and said he was really proud of him. John said he would not stop.

In an eleventh conversation, on Wednesday, 11 May 2022 at 5:00 pm, John said something cool had happened: he had volunteered his programming skills for a social cause. He built a software tool for a charitable foundation that helps kids, streamlining its operations. The foundation had recorded all of its inventory manually on paper, and John built an application that structures its work so that everything it needs for inventory is in one smartphone application. The system tracks inventory, resources, and donations and can generate reports for analysis. He shared a photo that he described as a screenshot of the system, but the image actually shows a computer monitor displaying a computer's CPU performance, so the application itself has never been shown. John said seeing his skills make a real difference was very rewarding. He said coding also lets him challenge himself and expand his skills, and that the work gave him a real sense of purpose. He is now considering volunteer roles and potentially a career in the nonprofit sector. He had not yet found a particular organization that matches his values, but James said he was sure John would find the perfect one. John said he hoped to make a positive impact there, and thanked James for his encouragement.

In a twelfth and most recent conversation, on Monday, 23 May 2022 at 7:33 pm, James said that last weekend, meaning 21 and 22 May, he had an awesome time at an amusement park with friends, a great break from the virtual world. He rode some roller coasters, which reminded him of being a kid, and said everything felt so real and exciting that it was like being in a video game. He also rode the Ferris wheel, electric cars, and buggies. John said he entered a local tournament last Friday, meaning 20 May, and took second place. He called it a wild experience with insane competitive energy. James congratulated him and asked about rewards. John said he had not won the tournament but still received prize money for second place, and that seeing his effort pay off was awesome. James said growth and progress matter more than always winning. John said he also got a trophy, which was very satisfying and reminds him to always put in his best effort. He asked James for any recent success stories and shared a photo of a graduation cap on a book with a rope. James said that last month, meaning April 2022, he had reached a personal milestone. He had finished a big project he had worked on for months. It was challenging because he had to learn a new language and handle many details, and he learned a lot about problem-solving, patience, and perseverance. He said he now feels more confident about taking on bigger projects. The conversation does not name the language or confirm whether this project is the computer game. John praised his skills and said determination and confidence make any project a success. James thanked him and said he would keep that in mind. John told him to keep going and reach his goals. The session ended there, with no goodbye and no further plans discussed.

Deborah and Jolene are two women who have each lost their mothers. Across fourteen sessions they have kept in touch and grown from polite acquaintances sharing photographs into people who check in on each other's losses, goals, stress, and small pleasures. They first met in chat on 23 January 2023. Session twelve took place on 9 April 2023 at 4:30 pm, and session thirteen on 6 June 2023 at 3:56 pm, roughly eight weeks later, the longest gap in the record up to that point. Jolene opened session thirteen by apologizing for the long silence, explaining that she had a lot going on. Session fourteen took place on 26 June 2023 at 9:17 am, twenty days after session thirteen.

Deborah is a yoga teacher whose central goal is to keep teaching and supporting her community. She finds yoga a source of peace and joy, a practice that helped her through a hard time and inspired her to share it with others. Jolene is an electrical engineering student whose mother died in 2022. Over time she has balanced school, exams, projects, work, her partner, her pets, and life outside class. Deborah has consistently offered encouragement and practical tools, while Jolene has increasingly brought her own problems into the conversation, moving from sharing achievements toward asking for help with stress and organization.

In the first session, on 23 January 2023 at 4:06 pm, Deborah said she had recently visited her late mother's old house, which holds many memories. Her mother had died a few years earlier. She shared a photo of their last photo together, her mother hugging her while both sat in wheelchairs. She described a special bench near the window where her mother liked to sit every morning to take in the view, and said she sometimes sits there herself to feel connected to her mother. She also mentioned a pendant that reminds her of her mother. Then she ended the session early, saying she had to run. Jolene responded with a photo of her own room in her mother's house, which has a bench and a window, and said she has many memories of that room. Jolene wears a heart-shaped pendant with a bird on it, given to her by her mother in Paris in 2010. Her jewelry also carries a symbol of freedom, a reminder to pursue her goals. She was enthusiastic about Deborah's yoga work and looked forward to their next chat. From the beginning, both women have kept a physical link to their mothers: Deborah through her mother's bench and pendant, and Jolene through her mother's room and pendant.

The second session took place on the morning of 27 January 2023, at 9:49 am. Deborah told Jolene that her father had passed away suddenly around 25 January, and that the family was shell-shocked. She said she was channeling her grief into spending more time with family and cherishing memories. She shared a photo of one woman hugging another seated on a couch. Jolene offered condolences. Deborah said looking back on good memories was comforting, and that the family had been going through the family album together. She shared a photo of her parents' wedding in 1993 and said she and her husband were trying to be as good a family as her parents had been. Asked what she valued most in her relationship, Deborah said love and openness had kept her and her husband close. She finished that thread with a photo of a handwritten note she had received the day before from her group members, thanking her for her positive influence. Moments like that, she said, remind her why she is so passionate about yoga.

The second session then moved to Deborah's memories and to pets. Asked where she most often practices yoga, Deborah shared a photo of a living room with a television and a window in her old home, which she visits now and then for her mother. Sitting by the window gives her a sense of her mother's presence. She next shared a window seat where her mother would sit every night with a book, since reading was one of her hobbies. The morning bench and the evening window seat both belong to her mother's daily rhythms. Deborah also said travel was her mother's great passion, and shared a photo of the sky seen from an airplane window. Jolene then introduced her pets, which calm her down and make her happy. She shared a photo of her snake Susie's head poking out from a bed. Jolene described how her second snake, Seraphim, had slipped out of its cage and coiled up beside her while she was gaming, which she found very funny. She had bought Seraphim a year earlier in Paris. Deborah said pets bring so much happiness.

Jolene then shared a photo of herself and her partner gaming the previous week. They are both crazy about the console game "Detroit." She had learned to play on her own as a child, and she and her partner planned to play "The Walking Dead" the following Saturday. Deborah closed by telling her to take care and keep spreading good vibes.

The third session took place on 1 February 2023 at 7:03 pm. Jolene said she had been busy because her engineering professor had given the class a huge robotics project. She called it tough but fun, and said it was pushing her to get creative and problem-solve. She shared a photo of a robot on a table beside a laptop. She now really enjoys the project, which she described as like solving a puzzle. Deborah then said she had met her new neighbor Anna the previous day, 31 January, and shared a photo of a yellow family sign. They had met at yoga in the park and talked about how yoga had improved their lives. Jolene shared a photo of a purse with a plant on a table, an image she would share again later. Deborah asked whether Jolene had ever thought about resuming yoga. Jolene replied that she and her partner had planned to play the console together. Deborah then said she had to run, and Jolene said she would see her soon. As in the first session, Deborah ended abruptly.

The fourth session took place on 4 February 2023 at 9:48 am. Jolene said she had been on an emotional rollercoaster but was coping. The previous week she had reached a major milestone: she had planned, researched, and designed a sustainable water purifier for a rural community. Seeing it deliver clean water was deeply satisfying, and it gave her a sense of purpose. Her career aspiration is to keep working in engineering and make a positive impact on communities in need. Deborah told her to take a deep breath and remember why she does this, and said teaching yoga is a great way to find balance.

Deborah then said she had bonded with Anna during the previous day's yoga class, on 3 February. She shared photos of two women in a dance studio and a woman doing a pose on a chair. They had been trying Warrior II, and they supported each other through the hard poses. Deborah described a modified seated twist: sit on a chair, twist the torso to one side with a hand on the knee, hold for a few breaths, then switch sides. Jolene shared a photo of her bookshelf. She was really into "Sapiens," and two weeks earlier she had read "Avalanche" by Neal Stephenson in one sitting. Deborah then shared a photo of a bouquet a friend had given her when she was struggling, which gives her hope, courage, and warmth.

The fourth session also touched on nature and places of meaning. Deborah named a park with a forest trail and a nearby beach where the waves make her feel peaceful. Jolene shared a photo of a person walking on a beach with a surfboard, from a vacation in Bogota last summer. Deborah said she likes to visit a spot by the water near her mother's old house, and she brings an amulet that belonged to her mother on every visit. She shared a photo of herself in a white shirt and gold chain necklace. Jolene remarked how something so small can have such a big impact. Deborah added that Anna also wears a pendant in memory of her mother, which had brought the two of them closer. Deborah closed by telling Jolene to hang in there and know Deborah is always there to cheer her on. Jolene said goodbye, and Deborah replied "Stay safe!"

The fifth session took place on 9 February 2023 at 9:03 pm. Jolene shared news about a mini retreat she had done the previous Wednesday, most likely 8 February, to assess where she stood in life. It gave her a real confidence boost. She had also made progress on her engineering project and wanted to look into green technology. She proposed a volunteer program in which engineers teach STEM to underprivileged kids, and asked for Deborah's opinion. Deborah called it a great way to help and inspire others. Jolene was considering partnering with local schools and inviting engineers as guest speakers, but admitted she had not yet contacted anyone because she wanted to solidify the plan first. Deborah asked to be kept informed. Jolene shared a photo of her planner sketches, and Deborah said "Take care!" Jolene replied "Stay safe!"

The sixth session took place on 22 February 2023 at 4:12 pm. Jolene said she was buzzing after a great night out with friends on 21 February, with dinner and drinks, and she shared a photo of a plate of food and a glass of wine. Deborah said she had just visited a calming and nostalgic place, a garden with roses and dahlias in buckets. She then said she had lost a friend around 15 February and had been spending time in the garden to find comfort. Jolene offered condolences. Deborah shared a photo of two women riding a motorcycle on a dirt road, the last photo she has with her friend Karlie, taken last summer when they went hiking. Karlie is separate from Deborah's mother. Asked where else she had traveled, Deborah said Bali last year was one of her favorites and was wonderful for yoga. Jolene said she had been wanting to try yoga on the beach and would keep Deborah posted. Deborah closed with "Take care!"

The seventh session took place on 25 February 2023 at 4:50 pm. Jolene said she now sets aside time for yoga and meditation, which gives her calm amid the chaos. Her partner had started joining her sometimes, which had brought them closer. She shared a photo of a couple holding hands with rings on their fingers. She explained that she and her partner are not married yet, have been together for three years, and are taking things slowly. They met in an engineering class in college, and they still work on projects together. Jolene also shared photos of a book and calculator on a table, and of a group of men in front of a building. Asked whether yoga or meditation had helped with stress, Jolene said that whenever she is overwhelmed she takes a break to breathe or meditate. Deborah said she was always rooting for her and urged her to listen to her heart, and shared a photo of a person watching the sunset from a bench, as a reminder to find peace even in chaos.

Jolene then asked about Deborah's daily routine. Deborah said that in the morning she meditates, does yoga, and teaches classes. On 24 February she had gone for her first morning jog in a nearby park, and she planned to make jogging a routine. Exercise makes her feel connected to her body. She said "Can't pour from an empty cup," explaining that looking after ourselves gives us the energy to help others, and reminded Jolene that she is worth it too. Jolene promised to keep prioritizing self-care.

The eighth session took place on 2 March 2023 at 7:18 pm. Deborah said Anna had recently brought her a vegan stir-fry. Jolene said her favorite comfort food is lasagna. Asked whether she had found time for herself, Jolene said that on Friday, 24 February, she had done yoga and meditation, and she shared a photo of a room with a wooden floor and a window. Jolene shared once more the purse-with-a-plant photo. She said she had taken Seraphim to the park on Sunday, 26 February, and Seraphim loved it. She shared a photo of a lizard among leaves, though Jolene describes the animal as her snake. Deborah said birds chirping and a gentle breeze remind her what really matters, and Jolene agreed it is a reminder to slow down.

Deborah then asked whether there was anything Jolene wanted to be more mindful of. Jolene said she needed to pay more attention to her stress and mental health, because exams and deadlines had left her feeling overwhelmed and her to-do list seemed never-ending. She shared a photo of a desk with a notebook and a monitor, and asked for tips on studying and time management. Deborah advised breaking work into smaller pieces, setting goals, and using a planner, and offered to help build a study plan. She wished her good luck with her exams and promised to send her a mug like the yellow coffee cup in her photo, with a handwritten encouraging message. Jolene said the mug would cheer her up.

She had started a yoga class in her neighborhood, which she had hosted on Friday, 10 March, and shared a photo of a group of women posing together. She said it felt wonderful to watch the class transform her neighbors, and that teaching has brought her great friendships and community. Deborah agreed and suggested finding a time that worked for both of them. Jolene said she would check her schedule. As of this session, she had not yet confirmed a time.

The tenth session took place on 22 March 2023 at 5:35 pm. Deborah said she knew exams and deadlines were difficult right now. Jolene said trying to fit everything in felt like playing catch-up. Joanna invited Nate to hike with her, and he accepted, but no date has been set.

Session 1 (21 January 2022): Nate said he won his first video game tournament the week before, a Counter-Strike: Global Offensive event played with his team. Joanna said she had been working on a project but did not describe it. She recommended a romantic drama about memory and relationships, which she first watched about three years earlier and owns on physical media. Nate did not say whether he watched it.

Session 2 (23 January 2022): Joanna said she finished her first full screenplay and printed it the Friday before. It is a mix of drama and romance. She planned to submit it to film festivals. Nate said he has had his pets for three years and they bring him tons of joy. Joanna said she is allergic to most reptiles and animals with fur, but finds other ways to be happy. Nate said he just plays for fun and does not expect to win big.

Session 3 (7 February 2022): Joanna said the screenplay she sent to a film festival is always on her mind, and she hopes a producer or director falls for it. No result was reported. Nate said he made coconut milk ice cream and was proud of it. Joanna said she had just watched "Little Women," which she called amazing and a must-see.

Session 4 (25 February 2022): Joanna said she cannot have dairy and asked for a dairy-free recipe. Nate offered a coconut milk recipe. Joanna said she had started a second screenplay while she waits to hear back about the first. It is about a thirty-year-old woman on a journey of self-discovery after a loss, who takes a road trip to heal and grow. Joanna said it is her own story.

Session 5 (18 March 2022): Joanna said she wrapped up her second script and felt both relief and anxiety. Nate said he is drawn to turtles because they are unique, slow-paced, low-maintenance, and calming. Joanna said she wishes she were not allergic and would get two turtles if she could. Nate said it is probably the greatest trilogy of all time. He said gaming is his focus and that he won his second tournament the week before, a local Street Fighter event. He usually plays CS:GO but was surprised to find he was really good at Street Fighter. Joanna shared a photo of a dairy-free vanilla cake with strawberry filling and coconut cream frosting, and said cooking and baking are her creative outlets.

Session 11 (12 May 2022): Joanna said she went hiking again, found more trails in her town, and called herself an expert hiker now. Nate suggested they go hiking together sometime, and said he might write a drama and publish his own screenplay. Joanna invited him to join her on the trails, and Nate accepted. No date was set.

Nate told her to keep going and said she has tons of talent and potential.

Session 13 (25 May 2022): Nate said he took Max for a walk and met a super nice couple with a dog who live close by. They agreed to do doggy playdates. He said the couple shared little with him besides loving animals, but that was enough to make them good friends. Nate shared a photo of a stuffed animal on a bed and gave it to Joanna as a reminder of good vibes, which he called joy in your pocket. Joanna said finishing her screenplay taught her that tough moments make the journey worth it. She said she wants to show Nate the screenplay and values his opinion. Nate said he cannot wait to see it and offered his support.

Session 14 (3 June 2022): Joanna said that after finishing her screenplay she received a generic rejection letter from a major company, with little feedback, which bummed her out. It is not stated which screenplay it was. Nate said rejection does not mean she lacks talent and encouraged her to keep going. Joanna said she would not let it bring her down. Nate and Joanna are friends who reconnected after a long gap. They share interests in movies, stories, and creative hobbies, and they often trade recommendations, recipes, photos, and small personal updates. Their conversations move between creative work, food, pets, nature, and daily life. They have been warm and encouraging with each other, and they usually end sessions with friendly goodbyes and offers of support. Joanna tends to open with news about her projects or her week, and Nate often responds with his own updates, photos, or questions. Several threads have stayed open across many sessions, including movie recommendations, a book recommendation, a recipe, turtle photos, and a hiking invitation. Where the record conflicts with itself, this memory notes the conflict rather than resolving it.

Nate's main hobbies are playing video games and watching movies. He especially loves action and sci-fi films, likes how their effects look, and enjoys classics. He said he loves fantasy and sci-fi movies because they are a great escape and get his imagination going, and he describes playing video games as his creative outlet. Nate also enjoys cooking and experimenting in the kitchen, especially making ice cream and dairy-free desserts. He keeps pet turtles, which he says bring him joy and calm him when he is nervous. He described them as having big personalities and said caring for them is not hard, since they need a clean area, proper feeding, and enough light, and that it is actually kind of fun. He has described himself as not really into hiking, though he likes nature and has been curious about trails.

Joanna's hobbies are writing, reading, watching movies, exploring nature, and baking and cooking, which she calls her creative outlets. Her favorite genres are drama and romantic comedy, and she enjoys being immersed in a story's feelings and plots. She is not really into games, and they agree they share similar interests with different emphasis. Joanna has a serious allergy to animals. She is allergic to most reptiles and to animals with fur, and around them her face gets puffy and itchy, so she has always stayed away from pets. In Session 5 she also said she recently found out she is allergic to cockroaches, which makes her unsure whether she will ever have a pet. She has described her dietary restriction in two ways. In Session 4 she said she cannot have dairy, and in Session 8 she said she is lactose intolerant and needs the dairy-free version. Both point the same direction: she needs dairy-free desserts. Joanna has a background in acting. She said acting was her first passion, that she once forgot her lines during a first play, and that she now shines more in writing, though she might return to acting someday. Her main sources of joy are writing and time with friends, and she says writing lets her express her feelings and create wild worlds with awesome characters. She cannot imagine life without writing and plans to keep pursuing it.

Nate has not confirmed whether he watched it, so this recommendation remains open.

The screenplay mixes drama and romance and is probably the project from Session 1, though she did not say so directly. Joanna said she would think about getting pets of her own if she can find ones she is not allergic to, and that her allergy can be a drag but she finds other ways to be happy.
