Deborah and Jolene are two women who have each lost their mothers. Across seventeen sessions they have moved from polite acquaintances sharing photographs to people who check in on each other's losses, goals, stress, and small pleasures. They first met in chat on 23 January 2023. Session twelve took place on 9 April 2023 at 4:30 pm, and session thirteen on 6 June 2023 at 3:56 pm, roughly eight weeks later, the longest gap in the record up to that point. Jolene opened session thirteen by apologizing for the long silence. Session fourteen took place on 26 June 2023 at 9:17 am, twenty days after session thirteen. Session fifteen took place on 9 July 2023 at 7:37 pm, thirteen days after session fourteen, and was the first in which both women talked at length about everyday routines, friendships, and pets. Session sixteen took place on 1 August 2023 at 9:26 am, twenty-three days after session fifteen. Session seventeen took place on 12 August 2023 at 8:50 pm, eleven days after session sixteen.

Deborah is a yoga teacher whose central goal is to keep teaching and supporting her community. She finds yoga a source of peace and joy, a practice that helped her through a hard time and inspired her to share it with others. Jolene is an electrical engineering student whose mother died in 2022. She balances school, exams, projects, work, her partner, her pets, and life outside class. Deborah has consistently offered encouragement and practical tools, while Jolene has increasingly moved from sharing achievements toward asking for help with stress, setbacks, and organization.

In the first session, on 23 January 2023 at 4:06 pm, Deborah said she had recently visited her late mother's old house, which holds many memories. Her mother had died a few years earlier. She shared a photo of their last photo together, her mother hugging her while both sat in wheelchairs. She described a special bench near the window where her mother liked to sit every morning, and said she sometimes sits there herself to feel connected to her mother. She also mentioned a pendant that reminds her of her mother, then ended the session early, saying she had to run. Jolene responded with a photo of her own room in her mother's house, which has a bench and a window. Jolene wears a heart-shaped pendant with a bird on it, given to her by her mother in Paris in 2010, and her jewelry also carries a symbol of freedom, a reminder to pursue her goals. From the beginning, both women have kept a physical link to their mothers: Deborah through her mother's bench and pendant, and Jolene through her mother's room and pendant.

The second session took place on the morning of 27 January 2023, at 9:49 am. Deborah told Jolene that her father had passed away suddenly around 25 January, and that the family was shell-shocked. She said she was channeling her grief into spending more time with family and cherishing memories, and the family had been going through the family album together. She shared a photo of her parents' wedding in 1993 and said she and her husband were trying to be as good a family as her parents had been. Asked what she valued most in her relationship, Deborah said love and openness had kept them close. She finished with a photo of a handwritten note from her group members thanking her for her positive influence, which reminds her why she is so passionate about yoga.

The same session moved to Deborah's memories and to pets. Asked where she most often practices yoga, Deborah shared a photo of a living room with a window in her old home, which she visits now and then for her mother. Sitting by the window gives her a sense of her mother's presence. She also shared a window seat where her mother would sit every night with a book, since reading was one of her hobbies, and said travel was her mother's great passion. Jolene then introduced her pets, which calm her down and make her happy. She shared a photo of her snake Susie's head poking out from a bed, and described how her second snake, Seraphim, which she had bought a year earlier in Paris, had slipped out of its cage and coiled up beside her while she was gaming. Jolene then shared a photo of herself and her partner gaming the previous week. They are both crazy about the console game "Detroit," and planned to play "The Walking Dead" the following Saturday.

The third session took place on 1 February 2023 at 7:03 pm. Jolene said her engineering professor had given the class a huge robotics project, which she called tough but fun and said was pushing her to get creative and problem-solve. Deborah said she had met her new neighbor Anna on 31 January at yoga in the park. Jolene shared a photo of a purse with a plant on a table, an image she would share again later. When Deborah asked whether Jolene had ever thought about resuming yoga, Jolene said she and her partner had planned to play the console together. Deborah then said she had to run, ending abruptly as she had in the first session.

The fourth session took place on 4 February 2023 at 9:48 am. Jolene said she had been on an emotional rollercoaster but was coping. The previous week she had designed a sustainable water purifier for a rural community, and seeing it deliver clean water gave her a sense of purpose. Her career aspiration is to keep working in engineering and make a positive impact on communities in need. Deborah told her to take a deep breath and remember why she does this. John and James have now chatted across fifteen sessions, from Thursday, 17 March 2022 through Sunday, 19 June 2022. Their conversations have stayed friendly and supportive. Calvin and Dave have had eighteen recorded conversations, beginning with their first meeting on 23 March 2023 and most recently on 13 September 2023 at 10:56 am. They are friends who often ask about each other's lives and usually close with good wishes, safe travels, and promises to talk soon. Dave talks most often about cars, car maintenance, classic cars, restoration, and the outdoors. Calvin talks most often about music, his tours, his studio, his albums, and his collaborations. Each session below records what was said and when, followed by the places where later details changed or conflicted with earlier ones.

In the first session, at 11:53 am on 23 March 2023, the two met for the first time. Dave said things had been going well and that he had recently attended a car event full of classic cars, where he spoke with owners and heard their stories. Calvin said he had just gone through a big life change and shared a photo of his new mansion, a building with a sign on its front. He framed the change around learning about Japanese culture and getting a chance to expand. He had never been to Japan, planned to leave in April 2023, and had a place to stay that his agent found, which he showed in a photo of its cozy living room. He planned to explore the city, try local cuisines, perhaps collaborate with local musicians, and stay a few months before traveling to Boston. Dave shared a photo of a calm park with a lake and a few boats, and Calvin said he would check it out when he returned. They ended by wishing each other well for the trip.

The second session took place at 4:45 pm on 26 March 2023. Calvin said he had just bought a new luxury car, a long-held dream come true, and that it was smooth and powerful and what he deserved after his hard work. He said driving it made him feel like a rockstar and that he was on cloud nine. He shared a photo of a red sports car parked on the side of the road, taken on 25 March, but did not name the make or model when Dave asked. Dave reported that around 18 to 19 March he had gone to a music festival in Boston, where he finally saw his favorite band, Aerosmith, live and found the performance incredible. He did not get to hang out with the band afterward. He shared photos of a large concert crowd and a stage with a large eagle. Calvin said he had written new tunes and held studio sessions the previous week, and he promised to share the music once it was ready.

The third session took place at 4:15 pm on 20 April 2023. Calvin said he had just been to a music festival in Tokyo. He saw no bands there but met talented artists and industry people, and a producer told him to stay true to himself and sound unique. His long-term dream is to tour the world. He was looking forward to Boston after finishing the Frank Ocean tour, having heard the music scene there was awesome. Dave offered to show him around, recommended Paradise Rock, House of Blues, and Fenway Park, and said he would be in the front row whenever Calvin performed. Dave also said that around 15 to 16 April he had gone to a car show, where he admired the dedication people put into restoring classic cars, and he shared a photo of a green Mustang parked in a field of grass. Calvin replied with a photo of a red sports car on display at a show, saying he had put a lot of work into it. This appears to be the same car he bought in March. Calvin said he had not yet seen anything in Boston beyond the gigs but looked forward to its food and city, and Dave agreed to share his favorite spots.

The fourth session took place at 6:24 pm on 1 May 2023. Dave shared big career news: he had finally opened his own car maintenance shop, a dream come true, and he shared a photo of a car dealership with cars parked in front of it. Calvin congratulated him and shared a photo of a man standing under a car in a garage. Dave said the shop was a step toward his other dream of working on classic cars, which he loves for their design and engineering. The previous year he had been thrilled to restore one, a challenging labor of love. He shared a photo of the restored engine, and the two exchanged messages about how satisfying it is to see something you worked on come back to life. Dave shared a photo of his shop and invited Calvin to visit. He said he worked on everything from regular maintenance to full classic restorations. Calvin then shared a photo of a gold necklace with a diamond pendant, calling it stunning, a gift from another artist and a reminder of why he keeps hustling as a musician. They closed by encouraging each other to keep pushing.

The fifth session took place at 1:16 pm on 3 May 2023. Dave said he was teaming up with a local garage and shared a photo of a car being worked on there. Calvin called the news inspiring. Dave said he was loving the job, working with skilled mechanics, and that he hoped to build a custom car from scratch someday. Dave asked whether Calvin had hobbies that helped him relax. Calvin said long drives in his red sports car cleared his head, and that he had been loving getting to know Japanese culture. He then admitted he was stuck with his music, that his creativity felt frozen, and asked for tips. Dave suggested immersing himself in something he loves, such as concerts or favorite albums, and recommended taking a break from music to have some fun. Calvin said a break was great for getting his mojo back, and Dave encouraged him to never give up. They agreed to stay in touch.

The sixth session took place at 11:50 am on 16 May 2023, and it was a more mixed exchange. Calvin said that around 9 May, "last week," his place had been flooded. He saved his music gear and his favorite microphone and said he was staying positive. Dave sympathized and offered help. Calvin was waiting on insurance before starting repairs. He shared a photo of his music studio, with a keyboard, a synthesizer, and other equipment, which he called his creative haven. Dave said he had opened his car shop "last week," invited friends over to celebrate, and found it amazing. This is a little inconsistent with the 1 May session, where Dave first announced the shop's opening. Calvin said he had an upcoming performance in Tokyo "this month," meaning May 2023, and hoped to expand his following. He then shared a photo of a city at night full of lights, taken in Tokyo "last night," meaning 15 May. Dave said he hoped to visit Tokyo soon, and Calvin encouraged him to come.

The seventh session took place at 6:06 pm on 31 May 2023. Calvin said touring with Frank Ocean the previous week, around 24 May, had been wild, and that Tokyo, where he had performed, was unreal, with an insane crowd. He felt so alive when performing that he could not find the words for it. Dave shared a photo of a man working on a car engine in a garage. He described it as his neighbor's car, which had been having engine trouble, and said he had fixed it himself. Calvin asked whether it was the car Dave had been fixing up for a friend, which slightly mixes up the detail, since Dave had said it belonged to a neighbor. Dave said working on cars was therapeutic and gave him a sense of purpose. Calvin said fixing cars gave him a real sense of achievement, like meditating. Calvin said performing live fueled his soul, and that the crowd was part of it, like one big harmony. Dave said music was like therapy for everyone, then asked what was next. Calvin said he could not wait for the tour with Frank and was buzzing to perform in Boston. Dave said he would be there to cheer him on, and Calvin signed off with "See you soon!"

The eighth session took place at 2:31 pm on 9 June 2023. Calvin said he had met with the creative team for his album the previous day, 8 June, in a long session that was awesome to see coming together. He shared a photo of a recording studio with a large window and a desk. Dave said he had been exploring parks on weekends to relax and asked whether Calvin knew any chill spots in Boston. Calvin said he had never been to Boston and could not wait to visit next month, meaning July 2023. Dave said the Boston parks are awesome, especially in spring, and that he had gone for a stroll around 2 June. Calvin asked whether Dave had been hiking and shared a photo of a path climbing a hill with mountains in view. Calvin said he had not been to the mountains but was keen to go and escape it all. Dave said he had booked a trip to a mountainous region for July 2023. Calvin asked him to take lots of pictures, and they signed off with safe travels and promises to see each other soon.

The ninth session took place at 3:15 pm on 21 June 2023. Calvin said he had been in a small car accident around Friday, 16 June, which was upsetting but left no one hurt. He had been dealing with insurance and repairs and shared a photo of a red car with a black rim parked on a sidewalk. He said it took only about a week to sort out and that the cost was not too bad. He shared a photo from the auto repair shop and said he trusted the mechanic's expertise. He then shared a photo of the view from his living room, a small town with a mountain in the background, from a small town in Japan, which he put on his to-do list for after the Frank Ocean tour. He also shared a photo of a person skiing on a snowy mountain and said he might give skiing a try. Dave said he had recently joined a rock band and had been practicing guitar, and he shared a photo of the band playing in a room. Calvin said playing in a band would bring Dave a lot of emotions. Dave said good company and great music lift the mood, and then he had to go.

The tenth session took place at 7:56 pm on 7 July 2023. Dave asked how Calvin's car was doing after the crash, and Calvin said it was fixed and going strong. Dave said he had been hanging out with friends at parks and had arranged regular park walks with them. He shared a photo of a city skyline with a river and boats. Calvin said it reminded him of living in his Japanese mansion with its epic cityscape. He shared a photo he had taken from the mansion's backyard, showing a boat docked in a canal at sunset, and a photo of the mansion's front. He said seeing the city lights from the windows was awe-inspiring. Calvin asked whether Dave had ever been to Japan. Dave said he had never been but was keen to go one day, and that he was hooked on Japanese music. Calvin said he had been working on collaborations with Japanese artists and promised to share clips. He then signed off to get back to work, and Dave told him to take care and not overwork himself.

The eleventh session took place at 6:38 pm on 21 July 2023. Dave said he had just returned from a road trip with friends through stunning countryside, a lovely break from "the corporate mayhem." Driving winding roads had reminded him why he loves cars and why he is passionate about his work. Calvin said he was transforming a Japanese mansion into a recording studio, a long-held dream and his sanctuary. He shared a photo of a room with a ladder in it, showing his progress. He said he had been experimenting with new genres and adding electronic elements to his songs. Dave told him to keep going and said, "I'm your biggest fan." Calvin said that meant a lot, and they agreed to chat again soon.

The twelfth session took place at 1:12 pm on 3 August 2023. Calvin opened with "long time no see" and said he had just taken his Ferrari in for a service, which had been stressful, since he was attached to it. This is the first time Calvin names the make of his car. Earlier sessions described only an unnamed red sports car bought in late March 2023 and photographed at a show in April. The Ferrari is very likely the same car, though the memory has never confirmed that directly. Calvin asked what hobbies made Dave feel restored. Dave said fixing cars was like therapy for him, and that growing up he had worked on cars with his dad. This is the first mention of Dave's father and of Dave working on cars as a child. He described one summer when he and his dad restored an old car together, and shared a photo of a man and a child posing together. Calvin shared a photo of the red car raised on a lift in a garage. He said his current goal was to expand his brand worldwide, grow his fanbase, and work with artists from around the globe. He shared a photo of a band playing on stage under lights, saying it showed how he had performed with "the boys" the previous night, 2 August. This is the first mention of a band Calvin performs with, separate from the Frank Ocean tour and the Tokyo performances. Dave told him to stay focused, because he had this.

The thirteenth session took place at 5:22 pm on 11 August 2023. Dave opened by saying it had been ages since they talked, though only about eight days had passed. He announced that he had been picked for a car mod workshop, which he said was a dream come true, since he had always wanted to learn auto engineering and build a custom car. He said he had been doing engine swaps and suspension modifications and was now learning body modifications. He shared a photo of a silver Corvette in front of a building. This is the first time Dave names a make for a car he is working on, and it differs from the green Mustang photographed in April. The current project modifies an existing classic muscle car rather than the custom build from scratch he has long hoped for. Calvin praised the silver finish. Dave then offered help with Calvin's music and shared a photo of his own desk with a keyboard, a monitor, and a keyboard pad, calling it an awesome music studio setup. This is the first time Dave has shown a music setup of his own. Calvin thanked him but said he was super busy with his music and would keep the offer in mind. Dave told him to stay awesome.

The fourteenth session took place at 12:35 am on 14 August 2023, about three days after the thirteenth. Dave said he had gone to a car workshop in San Francisco, the first time the memory places him in that city. He said it was great to see different restoration techniques and found the people there passionate and dedicated. Calvin described his recent life as an amazing experience touring with "a well-known artist," which fits the Frank Ocean tour but is not named in this session. He said the tour ended with a show in Japan, after which he got to explore his new place. Dave asked how Tokyo had reacted to his music. Calvin said the crowd sang along to one of his songs, a magical moment, and shared a photo of a crowd with their hands up. Dave said he was restoring a car with a broken engine, shared a photo of it in the woods, and expected to finish by the end of next month, September 2023. Calvin said he was excited to see the result and called Dave talented. The session ended with "See ya!"

The fifteenth session took place at 11:06 am on 22 August 2023, about eight days after the fourteenth. Dave opened by saying they had not talked in a while, though the gap was about a week. He said that last Friday, around 18 August, he had hosted a card night with friends and shared a photo of a group of men at a table with playing cards. Calvin replied warmly and announced his biggest news so far: he had landed a deal to continue his collaboration with Frank Ocean. Calvin said he had met Frank Ocean at a music festival in Tokyo, that the two clicked, and that they had been sharing ideas. They arranged a meeting and recorded a song in the studio at Calvin's mansion. Calvin described Tokyo as buzzing with energy and shared a photo of a crowd sitting on the grass at night. Dave asked whether other collaborations had come out of the performance. Calvin said someone at the festival had noticed his performance and that he was now working with them. He said his tour would end soon, that he was heading to Boston afterward, and suggested they meet there. Calvin also said that on 21 August he and his friends had recorded a podcast about the rapidly evolving rap industry, to be uploaded later. The two said goodbye with "See ya then!"

The sixteenth session took place at 2:55 pm on 31 August 2023, about nine days after the fifteenth. Dave opened with "long time no chat," asked how the end of Calvin's tour had gone, and shared a photo of a concert crowd with hands in the air. Calvin said the tour had been amazing and that the audience's energy had left him pumped. Dave asked what it was like performing on such a big stage. Calvin said it was a dream come true, that he had felt on top of the world, and that it was seriously surreal. He then said that last weekend, around 26 and 27 August, he had started shooting a video for his new album and shared a photo of a camera on a beach. The shoot was in Miami, at a beach he picked for its epic visuals. Dave offered help with props or anything else, and Calvin said he would ask if he needed it. Dave then recalled a photo Calvin had sent him once and shared a photo of a guitar with an octopus on it, saying it showed their different artistic styles. This is the first record of this guitar. Calvin said he had it custom made by a Japanese artist friend, with the octopus representing his love for art and the sea. Calvin then shared a photo of a guitar with a purple glow and a shiny custom finish that suited his style. Dave praised its unique look, and Calvin said staying true to himself and being unique in his music mattered to him. Dave closed by telling him to keep it real, then shared a photo of a man working on a car engine in a garage, with no remark.

The seventeenth session took place at 9:19 am on 2 September 2023, only two days after the sixteenth. Dave opened with "Been a while," which again overstates the gap. He said he had been tied up with car work and that the day before, 1 September, he had come back from San Francisco with insights and knowledge on car modification that he wanted to share. He said he was changing things around and giving an old car a new life. This is the first session that places Dave's San Francisco trip in late August or early September, and the memory does not know whether it was the same workshop visit described in the fourteenth session. Calvin replied that he understood the satisfaction of fixing cars. Dave said fixing things gives him a sense of purpose, and that he feels he makes a difference when he fixes someone's car. Calvin responded with praise, calling him a superhero, and Dave said seeing a customer's relief made him proud. Calvin then announced that he had booked a flight ticket to Boston "last week," meaning around 25 August, and said he was excited for the upcoming trip. He shared a photo described as a book with a boarding pass. This is the first record of a confirmed Boston trip, though no travel date is given and the memory does not know whether he has arrived. Dave asked him to let him know when he was free so they could catch up in Boston. Calvin said he would contact Dave when he arrived, and Dave wished him a safe trip.

The eighteenth session took place at 10:56 am on 13 September 2023, eleven days after the seventeenth. Calvin opened by apologizing for his slow reply and said things had been crazy. His album had been released on 11 September, and he said everyone was loving it and that the response was both awesome and a little overwhelming. He said it motivated him to make even better music and reminded him why he got into music: making a difference and sharing his own story. He said a tour was coming up and that afterward he planned to explore and grow his brand. When Dave asked which cities or venues, Calvin answered only that they were hitting awesome spots, without naming any place. Dave invited him to visit his garage and see some cool cars. Calvin said he would take him up on it and would let Dave know when he was in Boston. Dave shared a photo of a car in a garage with a Coca-Cola sign and said it looked stunning. The memory does not establish whether this is his car shop, the partner garage, or another space, and the car's make is not named. Dave also thanked Calvin for "your help," though Calvin had offered no specific help in this session. They said goodbye with wishes for a great day.

Taken together, the sessions show how Calvin's life moved over these months. He began in March 2023 about to leave for Japan, moved into a Japanese mansion, performed at a Tokyo festival in April and again in Tokyo in May, toured with Frank Ocean in late May, and by July was building a recording studio in the mansion and collaborating with Japanese artists. By August he was performing with a band he called "the boys," and he described a tour with a well-known artist that he had said ended in Japan. By 22 August he had landed a deal to continue working with Frank Ocean, recorded a song at his mansion studio, and started a rap podcast with friends. By 31 August he described the tour as over and a music video shoot on a Miami beach. By 2 September he had booked a flight to Boston. By 13 September his album had been released on 11 September and a new tour was about to begin, with Boston still ahead. His car went from a newly bought red sports car in March to one in a crash in June, repaired in about a week, and by August he was calling it a Ferrari. His music moved from creative block in May to album meetings in June, genre experiments in July, video production in late August, and a finished release in September.

Dave began in March talking about classic cars and a calming park. In April he described a car show and a plan to meet in Boston, and in May he announced his car maintenance shop and a partnership with a local garage. In June and July he talked about weekend parks, a mountain trip, joining a rock band, and a road trip with friends. In August he described childhood work on cars with his father, being picked for a car mod workshop, a San Francisco workshop, and a restoration he expected to finish by September 2023. He hosted a card night in late August. By 31 August his messages were mostly about supporting Calvin's projects. On 2 September he returned to car talk after a fresh San Francisco trip, and in the most recent session he celebrated Calvin's album and invited him to his garage. He has not reported on the restoration he expected to finish in September, so that thread is still open.

Several details are inconsistent or uncertain. Calvin's 3 May session described a red car, but its make was not named until August, and the memory has never directly confirmed that the Ferrari is the same red sports car he bought in March. Calvin said in April that he would visit Boston after the Frank Ocean tour, and in June he said he planned to go in July, so the timing moved. In August he said he was heading to Boston once his tour ended, and in September he said he had booked a flight there and would let Dave know when he arrived. No session confirms that any Boston visit has happened or when it will. Dave said in May that he had fixed a neighbor's car, and Calvin later asked whether it belonged to a friend. Calvin hoped in June to visit the mountain town in his living-room photo after his tour, but no session confirms that trip. Dave's account of the shop's opening conflicts slightly, since the 1 May session presents it as news and the 16 May session says he opened "last week." Calvin placed himself in a small Japanese town in June and at a mansion with a city skyline in July, so the mansion's location has not been clearly placed, and the memory should not assume a specific city. Calvin described performing "with the boys" in August, and Dave described being in a rock band, but the memory does not confirm whether these are the same group. Dave's use of "ages" and "long time" is often an exaggeration: he said it had been ages after eight days, a week, nine days, and two days. The memory does not establish whether Dave's green Mustang and silver Corvette are the same car, or whether his current project is the restoration he described in May. In the fourteenth session Dave's project, a car with a broken engine expected to finish in September, conflicts with the thirteenth session, where his current work was modifying a silver Corvette. The memory does not establish whether these are two separate projects or one car described differently. James finds deep satisfaction in creating something, writes his goals in a notebook, and enjoys checking them off. He is also building a computer game based on characters he sketched as a child, aiming to combine his passions for gaming and storytelling. He said he might later invite John to help with the game's HTML, and John agreed. John also shared a photo of a medical chart with procedure instructions. Deborah and Jolene are two women who have each lost their mothers. Across eighteen sessions they have moved from polite acquaintances sharing photographs to people who check in on each other's losses, goals, stress, and small pleasures. They first met in chat on 23 January 2023. Session twelve took place on 9 April 2023 at 4:30 pm, and session thirteen on 6 June 2023 at 3:56 pm, about eight weeks later, the longest gap in the record up to that point. Jolene opened session thirteen by apologizing for the long silence. Session fourteen took place on 26 June 2023 at 9:17 am, twenty days after session thirteen. Session fifteen took place on 9 July 2023 at 7:37 pm, thirteen days after session fourteen, and was the first in which both women talked at length about everyday routines, friendships, and pets. Session sixteen took place on 1 August 2023 at 9:26 am, twenty-three days after session fifteen. Session seventeen took place on 12 August 2023 at 8:50 pm, eleven days after session sixteen. Session eighteen took place on 16 August 2023 at 2:58 pm, four days after session seventeen, the shortest gap since spring.

Deborah is a yoga teacher whose central goal is to keep teaching and supporting her community. She finds yoga a source of peace and joy, a practice that helped her through a hard time and inspired her to share it with others. Jolene is an electrical engineering student whose mother died in 2022. She balances school, exams, projects, work, her partner, her pets, and life outside class. Deborah has consistently offered encouragement and practical tools, while Jolene has increasingly moved from sharing achievements toward asking for help with stress, setbacks, and organization.

In the first session, on 23 January 2023 at 4:06 pm, Deborah said she had recently visited her late mother's old house, which holds many memories. Her mother had died a few years earlier. She shared a photo of their last photo together, her mother hugging her while both sat in wheelchairs. She described a bench near the window where her mother liked to sit every morning, and said she sometimes sits there herself to feel connected to her. She also mentioned a pendant that reminds her of her mother, then ended the session early, saying she had to run. Jolene responded with a photo of her own room in her mother's house, which has a bench and a window. Jolene wears a heart-shaped pendant with a bird on it, given to her by her mother in Paris in 2010, and her jewelry also carries a symbol of freedom, a reminder to pursue her goals. From the start, both women have kept a physical link to their mothers: Deborah through her mother's bench and pendant, and Jolene through her mother's room and pendant.

The second session took place on the morning of 27 January 2023, at 9:49 am. Deborah told Jolene that her father had passed away suddenly around 25 January, and that the family was shell-shocked. She was channeling her grief into spending more time with family, and the family had been going through the family album together. She shared a photo of her parents' wedding in 1993 and said she and her husband were trying to be as good a family as her parents had been. Asked what she valued most in her relationship, Deborah said love and openness had kept them close. She finished with a photo of a handwritten note from her group members thanking her for her positive influence, which reminds her why she is passionate about yoga.

The same session moved to Deborah's memories and to pets. Deborah shared a photo of a living room with a window in her old home, where she practices yoga now and then for her mother. Sitting by the window gives her a sense of her mother's presence. She also shared a window seat where her mother used to read every night, since reading was one of her hobbies, and said travel was her mother's great passion. Jolene introduced her pets, which calm her down and make her happy. She shared a photo of her snake Susie's head poking out from a bed, and described how her second snake, Seraphim, which she had bought a year earlier in Paris, slipped out of its cage and coiled up beside her while she was gaming. She also shared a photo of herself and her partner gaming the previous week. They are both crazy about the console game "Detroit," and planned to play "The Walking Dead" the following Saturday.

The third session took place on 1 February 2023 at 7:03 pm. Jolene said her engineering professor had given the class a huge robotics project, which she called tough but fun and said was pushing her to get creative. Deborah said she had met her new neighbor Anna on 31 January at yoga in the park. When Deborah asked whether Jolene had thought about resuming yoga, Jolene said she and her partner had planned to play the console together. Deborah then said she had to run, ending abruptly as she had in the first session.

The fourth session took place on 4 February 2023 at 9:48 am. Jolene said she had been on an emotional rollercoaster but was coping. The previous week she had designed a sustainable water purifier for a rural community, and seeing it deliver clean water gave her a sense of purpose. Her career aspiration is to keep working in engineering and make a positive impact on communities in need. Deborah told her to take a deep breath and remember why she does this. Deborah then said she had bonded with Anna during the 3 February yoga class, where they tried Warrior II and supported each other through the hard poses. She described a modified seated twist: sit on a chair, twist the torso to one side with a hand on the knee, hold for a few breaths, then switch sides. Jolene said she was into "Sapiens" and had read "Avalanche" by Neal Stephenson in one sitting. She likes to visit a spot by the water near her mother's old house, and brings an amulet that belonged to her mother on every visit. Anna also wears a pendant in memory of her mother, which had brought the two of them closer. Deborah closed by telling Jolene to hang in there, and said "Stay safe!" as Jolene said goodbye.

Deborah agreed and suggested finding a time that worked for both of them. Jolene said she would check her schedule, and had not yet confirmed a time.

The twelfth session took place on 9 April 2023 at 4:30 pm, and was the first in which Deborah led with news of her own leisure and reflection. The thirteenth session took place on 6 June 2023 at 3:56 pm. Jolene opened with "Hey Deborah!" and apologized for the long silence. The fourteenth session took place on 26 June 2023 at 9:17 am. Deborah opened with "Hey Jolene!" and said she had been busy preparing for a yoga retreat with friends, a chance to be among people who think like her. This memory covers nineteen conversations between Maria and John, from 17 December 2022 through 16 June 2023. The most recent is the nineteenth session, held on 16 June 2023 at 7:20 pm. Maria and John reconnected on 17 December 2022, shortly after John returned from a family road trip. From the start they have encouraged each other, praised each other's work, and described themselves as a team. Their friendship centres on family, community service, education, kindness, and personal growth. Maria volunteers at a homeless shelter. John has been involved in campaigning and community politics, later focusing on education and infrastructure policy and, most recently, on support for military veterans. In June 2023 he also reported a work promotion.

The first session, on 17 December 2022, was the reconnection. On 21 December 2022 Maria donated her old car to the homeless shelter.

The second session took place on 22 December 2022 at 6:10 pm. Maria said it had been a few days since they last chatted. John said the campaign had been interesting and that he had been networking to gather people's input. A conversation with someone who shared inspiring stories had fired his passion for improving local education, and he stressed that investing in future generations is the foundation of progress. He said Maria's support motivates him, and he shared photos of his family at a park picnic and on a playground swing, calling his family the reason he never gives up. Maria said she loves spending time with friends, watching movies, hiking, and hosting game nights, and that quality connections matter most to her. John shared photos of family dinners and a homemade pizza night, saying shared meals keep them close. He ended by saying he was off to taekwondo, a new activity separate from his kickboxing.

The third session took place on 1 January 2023 at 8:30 pm. John said he had joined a service-focused online group in late December 2022, whose members share stories, advice, and encouragement. The group had visited a homeless shelter to hand out food and supplies, and it organized a toy drive for children in need. It is brainstorming ways to help underserved communities access education, mentorship, job training, and resume building. Maria said empowering people through education is crucial. John then revealed he had recently failed a military aptitude test, which left him stressed, and said Maria's support means a lot. She reassured him she has his back. She said nature's beauty reminds her to slow down, and John said nature helps people remember small joys.

The fourth session took place on 9 January 2023 at 7:06 pm. John said that in roughly the first week of January 2023 he had an unexpected incident on his way home, in which his car windshield was broken. He handled it by staying calm and asking for assistance, and Maria praised his resilience. He said he calms down by looking at the sunset. Caroline and Melanie are friends whose conversations, held between 8 May 2023 and 20 July 2023, grow warmer and more personal over time. Caroline is a trans woman who moved from Sweden about four years before July 2023 and has been transitioning for about three years, since roughly 2020. Melanie is a mother of young children, married to her husband for about five years as of June 2023. Their chats mostly show Caroline's growing focus on counseling, mental health work, and advocacy, and Melanie's search for balance as a busy parent who works and raises her kids. Each encourages the other, and by the later sessions they speak as close friends who share family photos, hobbies, and personal milestones.

On 8 May 2023, at 1:56 pm, the two caught up in person. Melanie said she was swamped with her kids and work. Caroline reported that the day before, on 7 May 2023, she had attended an LGBTQ support group and found it very powerful. The stories shared by transgender speakers were especially inspiring, and she left feeling happy and thankful. She shared a photo of a dog walking past a wall with a painting of a woman. The group made her feel accepted and gave her the courage to embrace herself, and Melanie praised her courage. Caroline plans to continue her education and is drawn to counseling or mental health work because she wants to support people facing similar issues. Melanie said Caroline would make a great counselor because of her empathy and understanding. Melanie then shared a photo of a sunset over a lake, a painting she made in 2022 of a lake sunrise. She explained that painting is her creative outlet and helps her relax after long days, and Caroline agreed that relaxation and self-expression are key. Caroline then left to do some research, and Melanie said she was going swimming with her kids.

On 25 May 2023, at 1:14 pm, they chatted again. Melanie said she had a lot going on. On the previous Saturday, around 20 May 2023, she ran a charity race for mental health. She found it rewarding and it made her think about taking care of our minds. Caroline praised her for taking part and raising awareness. Melanie said the event was thought-provoking and that self-care is really important. She described it as a journey: when she looks after herself, she can better look after her family. Caroline agreed that taking care of ourselves matters even when it is not easy. Melanie said she is now carving out daily me-time, including running, reading, or playing her violin, which helps her stay present for her family. She called it a work in progress. Her kids were excited for summer break, and her family was thinking about camping in June 2023. Melanie asked about Caroline's summer plans.

Caroline replied that she is researching adoption agencies, since giving a loving home to kids who need one has been a long-held dream. Melanie called her kind and said her future family would be lucky to have her. Caroline said she is grateful for the support of her friends and mentors, and that the hard work now is turning her dream into reality. She shared a photo of a sign for a new arrival at an adoption agency she was considering. She had chosen that agency because it helps LGBTQ+ people adopt, and its inclusivity spoke to her. She knows it will be tough as a single parent, but she is up for the challenge. Melanie said she will be an awesome mom, and Caroline said she will do her best to make sure the kids have a safe and loving home. Melanie replied that she has a caring heart and that the kids would get all the love and stability they need.

On 9 June 2023, at 7:55 pm, in the third session, Caroline told Melanie about a school event where she had spoken the previous week, around late May or early June 2023. She called it awesome. She talked about her transgender journey, encouraged students to get involved in the LGBTQ community, and enjoyed seeing their reactions. The event made her reflect on how far she has come since she started transitioning. Melanie praised her for spreading awareness. Caroline said she felt powerful giving the talk, and she was glad the audience related and wanted to be better allies. She said conversations about gender identity and inclusion are necessary, and she wants to build a strong, supportive community of hope. Melanie said vulnerable moments are where people bond, and that sharing stories shows people they are not alone. Caroline plans to keep using her voice to make a change and named Melanie as part of that effort. Melanie said she was proud to be part of the difference Caroline is making, and both agreed to keep motivating each other.

Melanie then asked what motivates Caroline. Caroline said her friends, family, and mentors are her rocks. She shared a photo of a family posing in a yard, taken when they met up the previous week. She has known these friends for four years, since she moved from Sweden, and they have been there through everything, including a tough breakup. Caroline asked Melanie who supports her. Melanie said her husband and kids keep her motivated, and she shared a photo of a man and a little girl standing in front of a waterfall. Caroline asked how long Melanie has been married. Melanie said it has been five years, and she shared a wedding photo, saying it feels like only yesterday she put on that dress. Caroline congratulated her and wished her many happy years. Melanie shared a photo of a man and a woman sitting on a blanket eating food, and said family moments make it all worth it. Both agreed that cherishing time with loved ones is what makes them feel alive, and Caroline said family is everything.

On 27 June 2023, at 10:37 am, in the fourth session, Caroline said it had been a long time since they talked and that a lot had been happening in her life. She shared a photo of a necklace with a cross and a heart, a gift from her grandmother in Sweden. It stands for love, faith, and strength, and reminds her of her roots. Melanie asked whether Caroline had other treasured objects. Caroline shared a photo of a stack of bowls and described a hand-painted bowl that a friend made for her 18th birthday about ten years earlier. Melanie said she had just taken her family camping in the mountains the previous week, around 19 to 23 June 2023. They explored nature, roasted marshmallows, and went on a hike, and the view from the top was amazing. The two younger kids love nature, and the family moments were unforgettable.

Melanie asked what was new with Caroline. Caroline said she has been looking into counseling and mental health as a career because she wants to help people who have gone through the same things she has. She shared a photo of a bookshelf. She is thinking about working with trans people, helping them accept themselves and supporting their mental health. The previous Friday, around 23 June 2023, she attended an LGBTQ+ counseling workshop that she found enlightening, and she was moved by how passionate the professionals were about creating a safe space. Melanie asked what motivated her. Caroline said her own journey and the support she received had made a huge difference, and she now wants to create a safe, inviting place for people to grow. Melanie congratulated her for going after what she really cares about.

On 3 July 2023, at 1:36 pm, in the fifth session, Caroline said some big things had happened since they last spoke. The previous week, around late June 2023, she attended an LGBTQ+ pride parade, where everyone seemed so happy and she felt she belonged. Melanie asked whether the experience had influenced her goals. Caroline said it motivated her a lot, and she is still sure counseling and mental health is the path she wants. Melanie said she had signed up for a pottery class the day before, around 2 July 2023, which she described as being like therapy because it lets her express herself. Caroline said she is getting creative too, by learning the piano. Melanie shared a photo of a bowl with a black and white flower design that she made in her class, and said she was proud of the work it took. Caroline called the bowl gorgeous. Caroline then said she is attending a transgender conference later in July 2023, where she hopes to learn more about advocacy. Melanie wished her a great time and safety, and they said goodbye.

On 6 July 2023, at 8:18 pm, in the sixth session, Caroline said a lot had been going on. She has been looking into counseling or mental health work more, and she described the work as tough but really rewarding. Melanie congratulated her on following her dreams. Melanie said that on 5 July 2023 she had taken the kids to a museum, where they were excited about the dinosaur exhibit, and the outing reminded her why she loves being a mom. Caroline said she is building a library for when she has kids of her own, with classics, stories from different cultures, and educational books. She asked Melanie about a favorite childhood book, and Melanie said she loved "Charlotte's Web," because it showed how friendship and compassion can make a difference. Caroline said she feels lucky to have friends and family helping with her transition, and she shared a photo of a group of friends at a picnic held the previous week. Melanie asked how they have been helping. Caroline said the support network has given her love, guidance, and acceptance every step of the way. Melanie said unconditional love is so important, and she shared a photo of her family around a campfire on the beach, saying camping brings them closer.

On 12 July 2023, at 4:33 pm, in the seventh session, Caroline said so much had happened since they last spoke. She had attended an LGBTQ conference two days earlier, around 10 July 2023, which was very special. She met people who had been through similar journeys and felt totally accepted. The community had shown her how important it is to fight for trans rights, and she wants to help make a difference. Melanie asked what Caroline's plan was for pitching in. Caroline said she is still looking into counseling and mental health jobs, because it matters to her that people have someone to talk to. She said she had struggled with her own mental health, and that the support she received had shown her how important a support system is. Melanie then shared a photo of a book cover with a gold coin on it, saying a book she read last year reminds her to always pursue her dreams. Caroline's favorite guide was "Becoming Nicole" by Amy Ellis Nutt, a true story about a trans girl and her family, which gave her hope. She recommended it, saying it showed her that tough times don't last. Caroline asked about Melanie's pets. Melanie said they have a dog named Luna and a cat named Oliver. Melanie also mentioned new purple running shoes, and said she has been running farther to de-stress, which has been great for her mental health. Caroline encouraged her to keep it up, noting that running can boost mood, and Melanie said she plans to continue.

On 15 July 2023, at 1:51 pm, in the eighth session, Caroline said it had been a busy week. Melanie said it had been super busy for her too. The previous Friday, around 7 July 2023, she had taken her kids to a pottery workshop, where they all made their own pots. She called it fun and therapeutic, and shared a photo of children making clay sculptures. Melanie said the kids loved it, and she shared a photo of a cup with a dog face on it that one of the children made. Caroline said kids show their personalities through art. Melanie said they have also been painting together, especially nature-inspired pieces, and she shared a photo of their latest work, a painting of a sunset with a palm tree. Caroline praised the bold colors. Melanie shared a photo of a field of purple flowers and said she appreciates the small things in life. Caroline then said that on the previous Friday, around 7 July 2023, she had attended a council meeting for adoption. She found it inspiring and emotional, and it made her even more determined to adopt. Melanie then shared a photo of a blue vase holding sunflowers and roses. Caroline said blue is her favorite color because it makes her feel relaxed. Melanie said the flowers were an important part of her wedding decor and always remind her of that day. She described the wedding as full of love and joy, and shared a photo of a wedding ceremony in a greenhouse. Caroline asked what her favorite part had been, and Melanie said marrying her partner and promising to be together forever was the best part. She shared a photo of herself and her partner standing on a beach.

Caroline then brought up a pride parade she had attended a few weeks earlier, and shared a photo of people walking down the street. She said it was amazing, and that she felt so accepted and happy being around people who celebrated her. It is a top memory for her. The best part, she said, was realizing she can be herself without fear, and having the courage to transition. Melanie said that finding the courage to be oneself is important for mental health and finding peace. Caroline said it had been a long road but she is proud of how far she has come, and asked how Melanie was doing with finding peace. Melanie said creativity and family keep her at peace. Caroline then asked how Melanie's family had been supportive during her move. Melanie said they had been awesome, helping out and showing lots of love. Melanie added that the family had gone on another camping trip in the forest, and she shared a photo of a man and two children sitting around a campfire. She said they enjoy hiking in the mountains and exploring forests, which are some of her favorite memories. Caroline said she was really glad to have Melanie as a friend to share her journey with, and Melanie said she appreciated the friendship.

On 17 July 2023, at 2:31 pm, in the ninth session, Melanie said she had a quiet weekend after the family camping trip two weekends earlier, and that it was great to unplug and spend time with the kids. Caroline said that last weekend, around 15 to 16 July 2023, she had joined a mentorship program for LGBTQ youth, which she finds very rewarding. She has met some amazing young people, and she mentors a transgender teen who is just like her. They have been working on building confidence and finding positive strategies, which has been paying off. Caroline also described an LGBT pride event the two had attended together in June 2023, which was awesome and very encouraging. She shared a photo of a woman holding a rainbow umbrella in the air. The best moment for her was seeing her mentee's face light up when they saw the support around them. Melanie said it is awesome to see the difference people can make in each other's lives. Caroline then said that in August 2023 she is having an LGBTQ art show featuring her own paintings, and she cannot wait. Melanie asked for previews and shared a photo of a painting with a blue and yellow design. Caroline shared a photo of her painting of a tree with a bright sun, made after visiting an LGBTQ center, which she meant to capture everyone's unity and strength. Melanie praised the vivid colors. At the end of the session Melanie said that she and her kids had just finished another painting like their last one.

On 20 July 2023, at 8:56 pm, in the tenth session, Caroline said a lot had happened since they last chatted. She had joined a new LGBTQ activist group the previous Tuesday, around 18 July 2023, and was meeting many people as passionate as she is about rights and community support. She said the work was fulfilling and that she felt she was making a real difference. She named the group "Connected LGBTQ Activists," which holds regular meetings and plans events and campaigns so members can support one another. Caroline then said that the previous weekend, around 15 to 16 July 2023, her city held a pride parade. She said she missed it herself, but it was a powerful reminder that they are not alone in the fight for equality.

Melanie then said that the family had recently been to the beach, where the kids had a great time, and she shared a photo of three children playing with a kite. She said they go to the beach only once or twice a year, though those visits are always special. She described the family camping trip, where they roast marshmallows and tell stories by the campfire, calling it the highlight of their summer. Caroline asked for her best camping memory. Melanie described a camping trip the previous year, around summer 2022, when the family watched the Perseid meteor shower, with streaks of light across a clear, star-filled sky. They all made wishes and felt part of something huge. Melanie said it made her feel tiny and in awe of the universe, and she shared photos of a plane in a starry sky and a beach with footprints in the sand.

Caroline then asked for other memories that make Melanie feel thankful. Melanie said she would never forget the day her youngest took her first steps, watching her wobble and realizing how fleeting life is. Caroline called the milestones reminders of how special their bonds are, and shared a photo of a baby in a white crib. Melanie said these moments make her appreciate her family's love, and she shared a photo of a family standing on the beach at sunset. Caroline said Melanie is lucky to have such an awesome family. Melanie replied that she is really lucky, because her family brings so much joy and love. This was the final exchange in the session.

A few details may be inconsistent across sessions. In the tenth session Caroline said she "missed" the pride parade held the weekend of 15 to 16 July 2023, although in the eighth session she described attending a pride parade a few weeks before 15 July 2023, and in the fifth session she attended one in late June 2023. Melanie's Perseid meteor shower memory is described as occurring "last year," which would place it in summer 2022. The beach trip in the tenth session is described as "recent" without a specific date. Caroline's group, Connected LGBTQ Activists, is new as of 18 July 2023. Her art show is planned for August 2023. Where these timings conflict, the speakers' own accounts should be relied on, and their exact dates treated with caution.

Deborah and Jolene are two women who have each lost their mothers. Across nineteen sessions they have moved from polite acquaintances trading photographs to people who check in on each other's losses, goals, stress, and small pleasures. They first met in chat on 23 January 2023. Session twelve took place on 9 April 2023 at 4:30 pm, and session thirteen on 6 June 2023 at 3:56 pm, about eight weeks later, the longest gap up to that point. Session fourteen followed on 26 June 2023 at 9:17 am, twenty days later. Session fifteen took place on 9 July 2023 at 7:37 pm, thirteen days after that. Session sixteen took place on 1 August 2023 at 9:26 am, twenty-three days after session fifteen. Session seventeen took place on 12 August 2023 at 8:50 pm, eleven days later. Session eighteen took place on 16 August 2023 at 2:58 pm, four days later. Session nineteen took place on 19 August 2023 at 12:52 am, three days later, the shortest gap in the record.

Deborah is a yoga teacher whose central goal is to keep teaching and supporting her community. She finds yoga a source of peace and joy, a practice that helped her through a hard time and inspired her to share it with others. Jolene is an electrical engineering student whose mother died in 2022. She balances school, exams, projects, work, her partner, her pets, and life outside class. Deborah has consistently offered encouragement and practical tools, while Jolene has increasingly moved from sharing achievements toward asking for help with stress, setbacks, and organization.

In the first session, on 23 January 2023 at 4:06 pm, Deborah said she had recently visited her late mother's old house, which holds many memories. Her mother had died a few years earlier. She shared a photo of their last photo together, her mother hugging her while both sat in wheelchairs. She described a bench near the window where her mother liked to sit every morning, which she sometimes sits on herself to feel connected to her. She also mentioned a pendant that reminds her of her mother, then ended the session early, saying she had to run. Jolene responded with a photo of her own room in her mother's house, which has a bench and a window. Jolene wears a heart-shaped pendant with a bird on it, given to her by her mother in Paris in 2010, and her jewelry also carries a symbol of freedom, a reminder to pursue her goals. From the start, both women have kept a physical link to their mothers.

The second session took place on the morning of 27 January 2023, at 9:49 am. Deborah told Jolene that her father had passed away suddenly around 25 January, and that the family was shell-shocked. She was channeling her grief into spending more time with family, who had been going through the family album together. She shared a photo of her parents' wedding in 1993 and said she and her husband were trying to be as good a family as her parents had been. Asked what she valued most in her relationship, Deborah said love and openness had kept them close. She finished with a photo of a handwritten note from her group members thanking her for her positive influence, which reminds her why she is passionate about yoga.

The same session moved to memories and pets. Deborah shared a photo of a living room with a window in her old home, where she practices yoga now and then for her mother. She also shared a window seat where her mother used to read every night, and said travel was her mother's great passion. Jolene introduced her pets, which calm her and make her happy. She shared a photo of her snake Susie's head poking out from a bed, and described how her second snake, Seraphim, which she had bought a year earlier in Paris, slipped out of its cage and coiled up beside her while she was gaming. She and her partner were both crazy about the console game "Detroit," and planned to play "The Walking Dead" the following Saturday.

The third session took place on 1 February 2023 at 7:03 pm. Jolene said her engineering professor had given the class a huge robotics project, which she called tough but fun. Deborah said she had met her new neighbor Anna on 31 January at yoga in the park. When Deborah asked whether Jolene had thought about resuming yoga, Jolene said she and her partner had planned to play the console together. Deborah then said she had to run, ending abruptly as she had in the first session.

The fourth session took place on 4 February 2023 at 9:48 am. Jolene said she had been on an emotional rollercoaster but was coping. The previous week she had designed a sustainable water purifier for a rural community, and seeing it deliver clean water gave her a sense of purpose.
