Nate and Joanna are friends who reconnected after a long gap and have kept in touch across fifteen sessions, from 21 January 2022 through 5 June 2022. They share a love of movies, stories, and creative hobbies, and their conversations move among creative work, food, pets, nature, games, and daily life. They trade recommendations, recipes, photos, and small personal updates. Both have been warm and encouraging throughout, usually closing with friendly goodbyes and offers of support. Joanna tends to open with news about her writing or her week, and Nate usually answers with his own updates, photos, or questions. Several threads have stayed open for many sessions, including a romantic drama and "Little Women" recommended to Nate, a book series recommended to Joanna, a coconut milk recipe, turtle photos, a hiking invitation, Nate's dog Max, and Joanna's screenplays. Where the record contradicts itself, this memory notes the contradiction rather than resolving it.

Nate's main hobbies are playing video games and watching movies. He especially loves action and sci-fi films, likes how their effects look, and enjoys classics. He says fantasy and sci-fi movies are a great escape that get his imagination going, and he describes playing video games as his creative outlet. He also enjoys cooking and experimenting in the kitchen, especially ice cream and dairy-free desserts. In Session 3 he said he had just discovered he could make coconut milk ice cream, which he called rich and creamy, and he likes chocolate and mixed berry flavors. He has described himself as not really into hiking, though he likes nature and has been curious about trails. In Session 8 he said he was curious to see Joanna's trail and mentioned a nice one just north of where he lives. He has accepted the idea of hiking together, but he has not committed to a date.

In Session 15 Nate named Iron Man as his favorite superhero, because he loves the tech and sarcastic humor and said seeing figures like that makes him feel invincible. He shared a photo of a toy Iron Man figure, which he said reminds him of something he loves and keeps him working toward his goals. In Session 9 he named a trilogy he loves for its world building, battles, and storytelling, which Joanna later identified as "The Lord of the Rings." He also called a book series with adventures, magic, and great characters a must-read, but he did not name it.

Nate keeps pet turtles, which bring him joy and calm him when he is nervous. He described them as having big personalities and said they are not hard to care for, since they need a clean area, proper feeding, and enough light. He called turtles unique and low-maintenance, and said their slow pace is a nice change from the rush of life. His turtle count is not consistent. In Session 2 he described a turtle and a baby turtle on a rock and said he had had them for three years. In Session 5 he shared a photo of two tortoises on the ground in a jungle and then a photo of three turtles on rocks in a pond, and the record does not clarify how many he has. In Session 8 he said he sometimes brings the turtles into the kitchen while he cooks. In Session 12 he announced that he had adopted a dog named Max and shared a photo of Max on a couch. He described Max as full of energy and said Max keeps his other pets active. In Session 13 he said he takes Max on walks and had met a very nice couple with a dog who live close by. The three of them agreed to arrange doggy playdates, and Nate said Max really likes the other dog. He said the couple shared little beyond a love of animals, but that was enough to make them good friends, and that seeing his dog so happy is a dream come true. The record does not show that any playdate has happened yet.

Joanna's hobbies are writing, reading, watching movies, exploring nature, and baking and cooking, which she calls her creative outlets. Her favorite genres are drama and romantic comedy, and she enjoys being immersed in a story's feelings and plots. She is not really into games, and she and Nate agree they share similar interests with different emphasis. She has a background in acting. She said acting was her first passion, that she once forgot her lines during a first play because she was so nervous, and that she now shines more in writing, though she might return to acting someday. Her main sources of joy are writing and time with friends. She says writing lets her express her feelings and create wild worlds with awesome characters, and she cannot imagine life without it. In Session 6 she advised Nate to read widely, try different genres, write and share with friends, and gather feedback. Her go-to place for inspiration is a bookshelf full of books and magazines.

Joanna has a serious allergy to animals. She is allergic to most reptiles and to animals with fur, and around them her face gets puffy and itchy, so she has always stayed away from pets. In Session 5 she also said she recently found out she is allergic to cockroaches. Her dietary restriction has been described in two ways. In Session 4 she said she cannot have dairy, and in Session 8 she said she is lactose intolerant and needs the dairy-free version. Both point the same direction: she needs dairy-free desserts. In Session 10 she said she had been testing dairy-free dessert recipes for friends and family, and she shared a photo of a dairy-free vanilla cake with strawberry filling and coconut cream frosting.

Joanna's attitude toward pets has shifted over time. In Session 2 she said she would think about getting pets if she could find ones she is not allergic to. In Session 5 she wished she were not allergic and said she would get two turtles that day if she could. Nate offered to send her turtle pictures so she could watch them grow without getting close, and she liked the idea. In Session 12 she said her allergies make her not really want a pet, and that she is too lazy to research alternatives. In Session 13 Nate sent her a photo of a stuffed animal and called it a new pup for her, meant to remind her of good vibes. She said she would cherish "that little guy." The stuffed animal is a toy, so it does not conflict with her allergies, and the record does not show that Joanna has a real pet.

Session 1 took place on 21 January 2022 at 7:31 pm. Joanna said she had been working on a project that was pretty cool, without naming it. Nate said he had won his first video game tournament the previous week, a team shooter called Counter-Strike: Global Offensive. Joanna congratulated him but said she is not really into games. She then recommended a romantic drama about memory and relationships and sent a photo of its poster, which shows a man and a woman sitting on a bench. She did not name the film. She first watched it around 2019, bought a physical DVD, and considers it one of her favorites. Nate said he would check it out soon, and he has not confirmed whether he watched it.

Session 2 took place on 23 January 2022 at 2:01 pm. Joanna announced that she had finished her first full screenplay and printed it around 21 January. She felt relieved, but also excited and somewhat anxious. The screenplay mixes drama and romance and is probably the project from Session 1, though she did not say so directly. Her plan was to submit it to film festivals. In the same session, Nate said small pets keep him calm when he is nervous, shared the turtle photo, and said he would cheer for others at tournaments even if he lost, since he plays for fun. He then asked how bad her allergies were, which led to the details above.

Session 3 took place on 7 February 2022 at 9:27 am. Joanna said the screenplay she had sent to a film festival had been on her mind all day, so by this date she had submitted it. She hoped a producer or director would fall in love with it. Nate offered support, then shared a photo of a bowl of coconut milk ice cream. Joanna shared a photo of a cake with berries and said she was tempted to try dairy-free flavors. Nate said he had made a dairy-free chocolate cake with berries on top, and Joanna said she should try making one or come over to try one herself. Later, Joanna recommended "Little Women," which she called amazing and a must-see. Nate said he would add it to his list and promised she would be the first to know what he thinks. He has not yet confirmed whether he watched it.

Session 4 took place on 25 February 2022 at 1:07 pm. Nate said he had made chocolate and vanilla swirl ice cream for a friend, who loved it. Joanna said she cannot have dairy and asked for a dairy-free recipe, a restriction not mentioned in earlier sessions. Nate offered a coconut milk recipe and said he would send it, but the record does not show that he did, so the request stayed pending until Session 8. Joanna said she cannot stop thinking about the screenplay and had started a second one while she waited to hear back about the first. This means the first screenplay had not yet received a result by late February. Session twelve took place on 9 April 2023 at 4:30 pm, and session thirteen on 6 June 2023 at 3:56 pm, about eight weeks later, the longest gap up to that point. Session fourteen followed on 26 June 2023 at 9:17 am, twenty days later. Session fifteen took place on 9 July 2023 at 7:37 pm, thirteen days after that. Session sixteen took place on 1 August 2023 at 9:26 am, twenty-three days after session fifteen. Session seventeen took place on 12 August 2023 at 8:50 pm, eleven days later. Session eighteen took place on 16 August 2023 at 2:58 pm, four days later. Session nineteen took place on 19 August 2023 at 12:52 am, three days later. Jolene is an electrical engineering student whose mother died in 2022. She balances school, exams, projects, work, her partner, her pets, and life outside class. Deborah has consistently offered encouragement and practical tools, while Jolene has increasingly moved from sharing achievements toward asking for help with stress, setbacks, and organization.

Jolene responded with a photo of her own room in her mother's house, which has a bench and a window. She wears a heart-shaped pendant with a bird on it, given to her by her mother in Paris in 2010. Each consistently encourages the other. Photo descriptions are often loose and sometimes do not match the text beside them, so the written accounts should be relied on wherever they differ.

Caroline is a trans woman who moved from Sweden about four years before July 2023 and has been transitioning since roughly 2020. Her recurring interests are counseling and mental health work, LGBTQ advocacy, a long-held dream of adopting children, and her own painting. Her grandmother in Sweden gave her a necklace with a cross and a heart, which stands for love, faith, and strength and reminds her of her roots. Her closest local friends have known her for about four years and supported her through a tough breakup, which showed her how important a support system is. A friend once made her a hand-painted bowl for her 18th birthday, about ten years before June 2023, and she still treasures it. Caroline also draws and has taken up piano.

Melanie said she would be an awesome mom.

Caroline described a school event she had spoken at the previous week, where she shared her transgender journey and encouraged students to get involved in the LGBTQ community. The event made her reflect on how far she has come, and she was glad the audience related and wanted to be better allies. She said conversations about gender identity and inclusion are necessary and that she wants to build a strong, supportive community of hope. Melanie said sharing stories shows people they are not alone. Caroline plans to keep using her voice and named Melanie as part of that effort. Asked what motivates her, Caroline said her friends, family, and mentors are her rocks. Melanie said her husband and kids keep her motivated and shared a wedding photo, saying it feels like only yesterday she put on that dress.

The fourth session took place on 27 June 2023 at 10:37 am. Caroline said a lot had been happening in her life. She shared a photo of her grandmother's necklace and described the hand-painted bowl from her 18th birthday. Melanie said she had just taken her family camping in the mountains around 19 to 23 June, where they roasted marshmallows and hiked to a view from the top. Caroline said she has been looking into counseling and mental health as a career, particularly to help trans people accept themselves. On about 23 June she attended an LGBTQ+ counseling workshop that moved her with how passionate the professionals were about creating a safe space. Melanie congratulated her for going after what she cares about.

The fifth session took place on 3 July 2023 at 1:36 pm. Caroline said that in late June she attended an LGBTQ+ pride parade, where she felt she belonged, and it strengthened her conviction that counseling is the path she wants. Melanie said she had signed up for a pottery class around 2 July, which feels like therapy. Caroline said she is learning the piano. Melanie shared a photo of a black and white flower bowl from her class, and Caroline called it gorgeous. Caroline then said she would attend a transgender conference later in July to learn more about advocacy. Melanie wished her a great time and safety.

The sixth session took place on 6 July 2023 at 8:18 pm. Caroline said counseling work is tough but really rewarding. Melanie said that on 5 July she took the kids to a museum, where they loved the dinosaur exhibit. Caroline is building a library for her future children, with classics, stories from different cultures, and educational books. Melanie said she loved "Charlotte's Web" because it showed how friendship and compassion can make a difference. Caroline said she feels lucky to have friends and family helping with her transition. Melanie said unconditional love is so important and shared a photo of her family around a campfire on the beach, saying camping brings them closer.

The seventh session took place on 12 July 2023 at 4:33 pm. Around 10 July Caroline attended an LGBTQ conference, which was very special. She met people who had been through similar journeys and felt totally accepted. She said she is still looking into counseling and mental health jobs, because it matters to her that people have someone to talk to. Caroline's favorite guide is "Becoming Nicole" by Amy Ellis Nutt, a true story about a trans girl and her family, which gave her hope. Melanie mentioned a book she read last year that reminds her to always pursue her dreams. She also said she has been running farther to de-stress, including in new purple running shoes, and Caroline encouraged her to keep it up.

The eighth session took place on 15 July 2023 at 1:51 pm. Both said it had been a busy week. Around Friday 7 July, Melanie took her kids to a pottery workshop, where they made their own pots, and she shared photos of their clay sculptures and a cup with a dog face on it. Melanie said they have also been painting together, especially nature-inspired pieces, and Caroline praised the bold colors of their sunset with a palm tree. Caroline said that on the same Friday she had attended a council meeting for adoption, which she found inspiring and emotional and which made her even more determined to adopt. Caroline said blue is her favorite color because it makes her feel relaxed. Melanie described her wedding as full of love and joy, and said the best part was promising to be together forever. Caroline then brought up a pride parade she had attended a few weeks earlier, where she felt she could be herself without fear. Melanie said her family had been awesome during her move and had gone on another camping trip in the forest.

The ninth session took place on 17 July 2023 at 2:31 pm. Melanie said she had a quiet weekend after the family camping trip two weekends earlier. Caroline said that around 15 to 16 July she had joined a mentorship program for LGBTQ youth. She mentors a transgender teen who is just like her, and they have been working on building confidence, which has been paying off. Caroline also described an LGBT pride event the two had attended together in June 2023, which was awesome and encouraging. Caroline said that in August 2023 she is having an LGBTQ art show featuring her own paintings and cannot wait. Melanie asked for previews and shared a painting with a blue and yellow design. Caroline shared a painting of a tree with a bright sun, made after visiting an LGBTQ center. At the end of the session Melanie said that she and her kids had just finished another painting.

The tenth session took place on 20 July 2023 at 8:56 pm. Around Tuesday 18 July Caroline joined a new LGBTQ activist group called "Connected LGBTQ Activists," which holds regular meetings and plans events and campaigns. She said she felt she was making a real difference. She then said that the weekend of 15 to 16 July her city held a pride parade. She said she missed it herself, but it was a powerful reminder that they are not alone in the fight for equality. Melanie said the family had recently been to the beach, where the kids had a great time. She said beach visits happen only once or twice a year, and described camping trips with marshmallows and campfire stories as the highlight of their summer. Melanie described a trip around summer 2022, when the family watched the Perseid meteor shower and all made wishes. She also said she would never forget the day her youngest took her first steps, realizing how fleeting life is. Caroline said those milestones remind her how special their bonds are.

The eleventh session took place on 14 August 2023 at 2:24 pm. Melanie said that on 13 August the family celebrated her daughter's birthday with a concert by Matt Patterson, whose songs she found amazing. Caroline mentioned an advocacy event full of love and support. She then said that around Friday 11 August she had attended a pride parade, which reminded her how important it is to keep standing up for equality. Melanie asked how Caroline stays inclusive in her work as an artist. Caroline said her art expresses her trans experience, which is her way of showing her story and helping people understand the trans community. She shared "Embracing Identity," a painting about finding comfort and love in being yourself, in which the woman depicted stands for the journey of acceptance. Melanie called it gorgeous. Caroline said art has helped her accept the beauty of imperfections, and Melanie said art can be healing. Melanie closed by telling Caroline to reach out any time.

The twelfth session took place on 17 August 2023 at 1:50 pm. Caroline said she had recently had a not-so-great experience on a hike, when she ran into a group of religious conservatives who said something that really upset her. It made her think about how much work remains for LGBTQ rights, and she said it had been helpful to have people who accept and support her. Melanie said strong support really helps. She then shared a photo of a colorful pottery bowl she had finished and said she was proud of it. Melanie said painting helps her express her feelings, and that art is both a sanctuary and a source of comfort. Both agreed that surrounding themselves with things that bring joy matters. Caroline thanked Melanie for being in her corner, and Melanie said Caroline has always been there for her. Late in the session Caroline recalled a Pride festival the two had attended together, which she described as a blast, and described it as "last year," which would place it in 2022, although that date is uncertain. Melanie asked whether they should do a family outing this summer. Caroline offered two options: a family outing, or something special just for the two of them to catch up and explore nature. Melanie said they should plan something special and that she would start thinking about it. No date, destination, or final choice has been settled.

The thirteenth session took place on 23 August 2023 at 3:31 pm. Caroline said that during the week before she had taken the first step toward becoming a mom by applying to adoption agencies. She said she felt ready to give her love to a child, and she had received lots of help from an adoption advice and assistance group she attended that week. Melanie congratulated her. Caroline said it was exciting but a little nerve-wracking, since parenting is such a big responsibility, and Melanie said feeling both is normal. Caroline has a guinea pig named Oscar, and she sent a photo of him eating parsley. Melanie said Oliver once hid his bone in her slipper, and she shared a photo of a horse being fed a carrot. Caroline said she used to go horseback riding with her dad as a child and has always loved horses. Melanie shared a horse she had recently painted on a wooden wall, and Caroline praised its grace and strength. Caroline shared a self-portrait from the previous week, a painting of a woman with a blue face. Melanie said the blue is powerful. Caroline said painting it made her feel liberated and empowered, and that art helps her explore her identity and is definitely therapeutic. She said she wants to live authentically and help others do the same. Melanie wished her the best on her adoption journey.

The fourteenth session took place on 25 August 2023 at 1:33 pm and is the most recent conversation on record. Caroline said she had gone hiking the week before and had got into a bad spot with some people there, which bothered her enough that she tried to apologize to them. Melanie praised the apology as a sign of courage and maturity. Melanie then shared a photo of a flower-decorated plate she had made in pottery class the day before, on 24 August, and said pottery is relaxing and creative. Caroline said she had not yet tried pottery, since she had been busy painting. She shared a sunset painting on a small easel, which she had painted after visiting the beach the week before, when watching the sun dip below the horizon felt calming. She shared a second sunset painting over the ocean. Melanie said the art made her feel the serenity of the moment. Melanie then said she had spent the day before volunteering with her family at a homeless shelter, which was hard to see but made her feel they could make a difference. Caroline called her an inspiration.

Melanie asked what had led Caroline to transition and join the transgender community. Caroline said that finding a community where she was accepted, loved, and supported had meant a great deal. She described a rainbow flag mural as reflecting the courage and strength of the trans community, and an eagle painted on a building as symbolizing freedom, pride, and resilience. Melanie said she was in awe of Caroline's courage. Caroline then described her stained glass work. One window was made to remind people that the key to their true potential lies within them. Another, made for a local church, shows time changing our lives and expresses her own journey as a transgender woman. Caroline also described stained glass as a symbol of togetherness that celebrates differences, and said she would love to make something like it next. She mentioned a rainbow sidewalk for Pride Month that she found while walking in her neighborhood, which reminds people that love and acceptance can appear where they least expect it. Caroline said she had recently seen someone drawing on the ground, which made her happy, and that creativity can lighten someone's day.

Caroline said art gives her joy and helps her express feelings and capture moments, such as a bouquet of flowers. She shared a drawing of flowers on a table, which Melanie found so realistic that she asked whether Caroline had made it. Caroline said drawing flowers is one of her favorites. Caroline asked what kind of art Melanie loves most. Melanie said she loves painting landscapes and still life, and shared a sunflower painting on canvas. She said she is feeling inspired by autumn and is planning several more paintings. Caroline said she is putting together an LGBTQ art show next month, in September 2023, where she will show her paintings, and that she is very excited. Melanie said she can't wait to see it and that the LGBTQ community needs more platforms like this. Caroline said the show will feature LGBTQ artists and is meant to spread understanding and acceptance. The session ended on that note of shared excitement.

Several details across the sessions may be inconsistent, and the speakers' own accounts should be relied on where timings conflict. In the tenth session Caroline said she missed the pride parade held the weekend of 15 to 16 July, although in the eighth session she described attending a pride parade a few weeks before 15 July, and in the fifth session she attended one in late June. Melanie's Perseid meteor shower memory is described as "last year," placing it in summer 2022. The beach trip in the tenth session is described only as recent. Connected LGBTQ Activists is new as of 18 July 2023. Caroline's art show was first described in the ninth session as taking place in August 2023, but in the fourteenth session she said it is next month, which would be September 2023. No show has been confirmed as having taken place. The Pride festival in the twelfth session is described as "last year," which conflicts with the 2023 Pride events discussed elsewhere. Photos do not always match their text, including the guinea pig sign and black dog image in the thirteenth session and the stained glass and concert poster images in the fourteenth session, so the written descriptions are the more reliable record. Oliver is consistently described as a cat, even though one photo was described as showing a dog. The hike in the twelfth session and the one in the fourteenth may be the same outing, since both involve trouble with other people on a trail, though the sessions do not say so directly.

As of the latest session on 25 August 2023, Caroline continues her interest in counseling and mental health work and her mentoring of a transgender teen. She applied to adoption agencies in the week before 23 August and describes herself as excited but nervous about parenthood. She remains active in advocacy and in Connected LGBTQ Activists, and she recently apologized to people she had a falling-out with on a hike. She keeps a guinea pig named Oscar and describes her painting, drawing, and stained glass as expressions of her trans experience and sources of freedom and joy. Her most recent painting is a beach sunset, and she plans an LGBTQ art show for September 2023 that has not yet happened. She has not tried pottery yet. Melanie continues to balance her job and parenting with pottery, painting, running, violin, and family camping. She keeps a dog named Luna, a cat named Oliver, and a newer cat named Bailey, and she recently painted a horse on a wooden wall and a sunflower on canvas, with more autumn paintings planned. She volunteered with her family at a homeless shelter around 24 August. The two are close friends who regularly encourage each other, and they have tentatively agreed to plan a summer outing, either with the whole family or just the two of them, though the details remain undecided.

SUMMARY:

Overview: Nate and Joanna are friends who keep in touch about her screenwriting and books, his gaming, his pets, dairy-free food, hiking, films, and reading. The record covers 21 January 2022 to 22 August 2022 across nineteen sessions. Joanna moved from finishing her first screenplay, to a second and third script, a writers group, a book, a blog, and a reader's letter. Nate moved from casual gaming to a run of tournament wins, including an international win on 21 August 2022, and then to teaching dairy-free dessert making and caring for a growing set of pets. Nate's Spider-Man pin remark suggests they have met in person before. Joanna invited Nate to hike with her, and he accepted, but no date has been set. They have not met up in any session on record.

- 21 Jan 2022: Nate said he won his first tournament the week before, a Counter-Strike: Global Offensive event with his team. Joanna said she first watched the game about three years earlier and owns a physical copy.

- 18 Mar 2022: Joanna wrapped up her second script and felt both relief and anxiety. She wishes she were not allergic and would get two turtles if she could. She recently learned she is allergic to cockroaches too.
- 24 Mar 2022: Joanna had an audition for a writing gig on 23 March. It went alright, with mixed excitement and anxiety. No result was reported. Nate said he was in the video game tournament again and it was intense.
- 15 Apr 2022: Nate said he dyed his hair the week before. Joanna said her writing is consuming her and she hopes for good news soon.
- 17 Apr 2022: Joanna found a hiking trail in her hometown and asked for hiking spots. Nate said he is not really into hiking but would like to see the trail, which is just north of where he lives. He shared his dairy-free ice cream recipe: coconut milk, vanilla extract, sugar, and a pinch of salt, chilled, churned, then frozen until scoopable.
- 21 Apr 2022: Joanna joined a writers group and said it feels like she finally belongs. The group is working on "Finding Home," a script about a girl on a journey to find her true home. Nate said his next tournament would be his fourth. Joanna said acting was her first passion and she may return to it.
- 2 May 2022: Joanna watched "The Lord of the Rings" trilogy on Nate's recommendation and said it was awesome. Nate said he won his second tournament the week before, a local Street Fighter event, though he usually plays CS:GO.

Audrey and Andrew are friendly acquaintances who live in the same city and have been chatting intermittently since 27 March 2023. Their conversations are casual and warm. Neither has described the other as a close friend, but both are consistently encouraging and eager to hear how each other's plans turn out. They often sign off with lighthearted phrases such as "Talk later!" or, most recently, "Talk later k?" Twelve sessions are on record, the most recent on 11 July 2023 at 10:05 am. Early sessions centered on animals, nature, hiking, and everyday life. Cooking became a shared topic in July, and by the latest session dogs and a planned outdoor outing were the main subjects.

Andrew is a financial analyst who started a new job in the week before 27 March 2023, a major change from his previous position. He rents an apartment in the city. He loves animals, names the eagle as his favorite bird, and notices birds on hikes without ever having gone bird-watching on purpose. He usually hikes on weekends and tries to leave the city at least once a weekend. He calls nature therapeutic, a reset button, and the place where he feels most like himself. He refers to his girlfriend as "my girl," and the two like to explore new restaurants and cafes together. She was not mentioned again until 8 July, when he described a picnic with her the previous Friday (7 July) and shared a photo of a picnic table covered in snacks and drinks.

Andrew's dog search ran from early April. He wanted a smaller, active dog and a pet-friendly apartment near a park or woods. On 6 May he described browsing websites, visiting shelters, and asking friends with dogs, finding the process annoying but meeting the dogs awesome. On 2 June he said he felt discouraged but determined, and Audrey offered to help if he emailed his criteria. There is no record that he sent them. On 8 July he said he wished he could get a dog but that finding a place and the right dog was tough. In the 11 July session he introduced Toby, a puppy he had just taken home, describing him as a bundle of joy and saying he "couldn't resist" despite "city living and all." He shared a photo of a dog sitting on a leash in a room. How he got Toby, whether his apartment allows dogs, and Toby's breed, age, and size are all unknown.

Andrew's outdoor life expanded in June. On Sunday, 11 June, he and his friends took a rock climbing class and made it to the top. He called it a fantastic experience that left him hooked, said he was still a newbie, and wanted to try outdoor activities like this every week. The class also got him thinking about kayaking and perhaps bungee jumping. On Friday, 23 June, he hiked with friends and took photos he had not yet gone through, offering to share them later. By the 3 July session his tone had shifted. He said life had thrown him a few curveballs, that he could not find dog-friendly rentals, and that he could not hike right now, though he did not say why. He described his outings as "urban adventures" and has taken up cooking as a new hobby, calling himself a rookie and saying it helps him de-stress. In the latest session he said work had been piling up and he had been stuck inside, missing the peace and freedom of hiking. He then proposed a hike next month and invited Audrey and her dogs. The reason he could not hike in early July remains unexplained.

Audrey lives in the city, and her dogs are central to her happiness. Pepper, Precious, and Panda have been with her for about three years. Pixie, a small white puppy, was adopted by her family in early April 2023 and quickly became friends with the others, especially Pepper. On 3 July Audrey said all four are three-year-old mutts, two Jack Russell mixes and two Chihuahua mixes, which conflicts with Pixie's puppy status in April. On 8 July she said she "got lucky finding a breeder nearby that has the dogs I wanted," which is also hard to square with the April adoption. She walks her dogs regularly in a nearby park with many trees and benches, where she finds her center, and the dogs play fetch and attend playdates at a dog park beside it. Her family takes national park road trips roughly once every couple of months. In mid-April she got a tattoo of her dogs with sunflowers. On 26 June she announced a move into a new home with a bigger backyard and an agility play area, though she said she was still unpacking.

The first session, on 27 March, opened with Andrew mentioning his new job and Audrey sharing a photo of new collars and tags. Andrew recommended Fox Hollow, a trail with great views, and Audrey said she would try it. On 2 April Audrey announced Pixie's adoption and said she had not yet visited Fox Hollow. Andrew said he was considering a dog but found dog-friendly places hard to find, and Audrey suggested websites with pet-friendly filters. On 16 April Andrew said he missed talking to her and felt sad not being out in nature. Audrey proposed a pastry party, and Andrew agreed to come with her dogs. That party has never been scheduled. On 3 May Audrey said she had hiked the previous week and photographed a hummingbird, but did not name the trail. Andrew said he had found a new open space nearby, and he asked for tips on keeping dogs safe outdoors. On 11 May Andrew described a great hike with friends and his girlfriend at a recently discovered spot. Audrey said caring for her four dogs takes up most of her free time, and she announced a positive reinforcement workshop about bonding with pets, set for June 2023. She said punishment is never the proper way to train. On 2 June Audrey described taking her dogs to the park off-leash, and Andrew shared a sunset photo with a grazing horse. On 13 June Andrew described the climbing class, and Audrey invited him on a walk to a small tree-lined park her dogs love. He readily agreed. On 26 June Andrew shared a photo of a doggy daycare near him, and Audrey said she might take the dogs soon. Andrew offered to help her find more dog-friendly places. On 3 July, at 8:32 pm, Audrey said she was taking a challenging but rewarding dog training course and that her dogs were already improving. It may be the May workshop, but this is not confirmed. She also mentioned a playdate "last Friday," which would have been 30 June. Much of that session centered on cooking. Audrey said her favorite recipe is Chicken Pot Pie, a family recipe that reminds her of her grandmother's kitchen, and she promised to send it "in a bit." Her favorite garlic dish is Roasted Chicken, which combines chicken, garlic, lemon, and herbs, and she promised that recipe too. Andrew said he was always looking for healthier meal ideas and would report back.

On 8 July, at 9:48 am, Andrew said his picnic with his girlfriend was amazing. Audrey mentioned a great walk with her dogs "the other day." Andrew said parks where dogs can be leashed are not the same as open areas where they can run, and he promised to tell her if he found one. The main development was a proposed hike. Audrey said she should join Andrew and bring her dogs so they could run freely. Andrew suggested going next month, when the weather is more pleasant. He shared a photo of a steep trail with an ocean view as an example of a suitable trail, then a map of a tree-filled park. Both agreed that safety is the top priority. Audrey also shared photos of three dogs with leashes, saying they were "all set for their next outdoor adventure," plus photos of dogs running with a ball and a sunset from a hike last year, a three-hour drive away, whose trail she did not name.

The most recent session, on 11 July at 10:05 am, opened with Andrew saying "so much has changed since last time," although only three days had passed. He introduced Toby and then said he had plans for a hike next month and wanted Audrey and her pups to join. Audrey said she was in and that her dogs could come too. She then shared a photo of wooden keychains with engraved names, which she said she had made herself to fit each dog's personality, because she wanted her pets to feel seen and loved. Andrew said these small acts showed how much they cared, and both agreed they make a big difference. They ended by counting down to the hike and sending each other off with "Talk later k?"

As of this session, Andrew has a puppy, which is a major change from earlier sessions when he had no pets and was still searching. His 8 July remark that he wished he could get a dog came just three days before the announcement. The August hike is tentatively planned, with no date or trail confirmed. Audrey's household is described as four dogs, though the 8 July photos show three dogs with leashes, and the dogs' age and origin remain inconsistent. Pixie is described both as an April puppy and as a three-year-old mutt, and Audrey's breeder remark is still unclear. She has not confirmed visiting the doggy daycare, Fox Hollow, or any new trails since spring, and the pastry party has never been scheduled.

Several open threads remain. It is unknown whether the August hike will happen, which trail they will choose, and whether the dogs and Toby will meet there. It is also unknown whether Andrew will try kayaking or bungee jumping, whether he will share his 23 June hike photos, and why he could not hike in early July. Audrey promised the Chicken Pot Pie and Roasted Chicken recipes, but there is no confirmation they were sent, and Andrew said he would report back on the roasted chicken. Whether the training course is the June workshop remains unconfirmed. Andrew's relationship with his girlfriend is a casual, positive detail in his life, and the 7 July picnic is the only time she has been described. Overall, the friendship remains warm and encouraging, focused on dogs, nature, and plans they hope to carry out together.

Audrey and Andrew are friendly acquaintances who live in the same city and have chatted intermittently since 27 March 2023. Their conversations are casual and warm. Neither has called the other a close friend, but both are encouraging and eager to hear how each other's plans turn out. They often sign off with lighthearted phrases such as "Talk later!" or, most recently, "Talk later k?" Thirteen sessions are on record, the most recent on 27 July 2023 at 3:52 pm. Early sessions centered on animals, nature, hiking, and everyday life. Cooking became a shared topic in July, and later sessions focused on dogs, pets, and planned outdoor outings.

Andrew is a financial analyst who started a new job in the week before 27 March 2023, a major change from his previous position. He rents an apartment in the city. He loves animals, names the eagle as his favorite bird, and notices birds on hikes without having gone bird-watching on purpose. He usually hikes on weekends and tries to leave the city at least once a weekend. He calls nature therapeutic, a reset button, and the place where he feels most like himself. He refers to his girlfriend as "my girl," and they like exploring new restaurants and cafes together. She was not mentioned again until 8 July, when he described a picnic with her on 7 July. On 27 July he said they had volunteered together at a pet shelter on Monday, 24 July, and that it reminded him how much he loves animals.

Andrew's dog search began in early April. He wanted a smaller, active dog and a pet-friendly apartment near a park or woods. On 6 May he found browsing and shelter visits annoying but enjoyed meeting the dogs. On 2 June he said he felt discouraged but determined, and Audrey offered to help if he emailed his criteria. There is no record that he did. On 8 July he said he wished he could get a dog but that finding a place and the right dog was tough. On 11 July he introduced Toby, a puppy he had just taken home, saying he "couldn't resist" despite "city living and all." How he got Toby, whether his apartment allows dogs, and Toby's breed, age, and size are unknown.

Andrew's outdoor life expanded in June. On Sunday, 11 June, he and friends took a rock climbing class and reached the top. He called it fantastic, said he was still a newbie, and wanted to try outdoor activities like this every week. The class also got him thinking about kayaking and perhaps bungee jumping. On Friday, 23 June, he hiked with friends and took photos he had not yet gone through, offering to share them later. By 3 July his tone had shifted. He said life had thrown him curveballs, that he could not find dog-friendly rentals, and that he could not hike right now, without saying why. He described his outings as "urban adventures" and has taken up cooking as a rookie hobby that helps him de-stress.

Audrey lives in the city, and her dogs are central to her happiness. She calls her four dogs her "fur babies" and says they matter more to her than anything. Pepper, Precious, and Panda have been with her for about three years. Pixie, a small white puppy, was adopted by her family in early April 2023 and quickly befriended the others. On 3 July Audrey said all four are three-year-old mutts, two Jack Russell mixes and two Chihuahua mixes, which conflicts with Pixie's puppy status in April. On 8 July she said she "got lucky finding a breeder nearby," which is also hard to square with the April adoption. On 27 July she described their personalities: the oldest is a relaxed wise old sage, the second is always ready for a game, the third is naughty but loves cuddles, and the youngest is full of life and always up for adventure. She walks the dogs in a nearby park with many trees and benches, where she finds her center, and they attend playdates at a dog park beside it. Her family takes national park road trips about once every couple of months. In mid-April she got a tattoo of her dogs with sunflowers. On 26 June she announced a move to a new home with a bigger backyard and an agility play area, though she was still unpacking.

The first session, on 27 March, opened with Andrew mentioning his new job and Audrey sharing a photo of new collars and tags. Andrew recommended Fox Hollow, a trail with great views, and Audrey said she would try it. On 2 April she announced Pixie's adoption and said she had not yet visited Fox Hollow. Andrew said he was considering a dog but found dog-friendly places hard to find. On 16 April he said he missed talking to her. Audrey proposed a pastry party with her dogs, which has never been scheduled. On 3 May she said she had hiked the previous week and photographed a hummingbird, without naming the trail. Andrew said he had found a new open space nearby and asked for tips on keeping dogs safe outdoors. On 6 May Andrew added road-tripping with a furry companion to his bucket list.

On 11 May Andrew described a great hike with friends and his girlfriend. Audrey said caring for her four dogs takes most of her free time and announced a positive reinforcement workshop about bonding with pets, set for June 2023. She said punishment is never the proper way to train. On 2 June she described taking her dogs to the park off-leash. On 13 June Audrey invited Andrew on a walk to a small tree-lined park her dogs love, and he readily agreed. On 26 June Andrew shared a photo of a doggy daycare near him, and Audrey said she might take the dogs soon. On 3 July, at 8:32 pm, Audrey said she was taking a challenging but rewarding dog training course and that her dogs were already improving. It may be the May workshop, but this is unconfirmed. She also mentioned a playdate "last Friday," which would have been 30 June. Much of that session centered on cooking. Audrey named Chicken Pot Pie, a family recipe that reminds her of her grandmother's kitchen, as her favorite, and promised to send it "in a bit." She also promised her Roasted Chicken recipe, which combines chicken, garlic, lemon, and herbs. Andrew said he was always looking for healthier meal ideas and would report back.

On 8 July, at 9:48 am, Andrew said his picnic with his girlfriend was amazing. Audrey mentioned a great walk with her dogs "the other day." Andrew said leashed parks are not the same as open areas where dogs can run, and promised to tell her if he found one. The main development was a proposed hike. Audrey said she should join and bring her dogs so they could run freely. Andrew suggested going next month, when the weather is nicer, and shared photos of a steep trail with an ocean view and a tree-filled park as examples. Both agreed safety is the top priority. Audrey also shared photos of three dogs on leashes, saying they were "all set for their next outdoor adventure," plus a sunset from a hike last year, a three-hour drive away, whose trail she did not name.

The session on 11 July at 10:05 am opened with Andrew saying "so much has changed since last time," though only three days had passed. He introduced Toby, then said he had plans for a hike next month and wanted Audrey and her pups to join. Audrey said she was in and that her dogs could come too. She then shared a photo of wooden keychains with engraved names that she had made herself to fit each dog's personality, because she wanted her pets to feel seen and loved. Both agreed such small acts make a big difference, and they ended with "Talk later k?"

The 27 July session was warm and reflective, with little about plans. Andrew described the shelter volunteering with his girlfriend. Audrey said she had never volunteered at a shelter but would like to someday. She shared a photo of a woman kissing a dog in a park, and when Andrew asked about her dogs, she gave the personality descriptions above. Andrew then shared a photo of a dog on the floor with a tennis ball, and Audrey explained it was Max, her childhood dog, who loved fetch. She recalled long neighborhood walks with Max, exploring new paths and sharing her worries and hopes with him, since he was a great listener. Both agreed pets become friends and confidants who offer unconditional love. Andrew described volunteering as a way of giving back, and Audrey closed by saying his kindness would make the shelter animals happier. The August hike did not come up.

As of 27 July, Andrew has a puppy, Toby, a major change from earlier sessions when he had no pets and was still searching. His 8 July remark that he wished he could get a dog came just three days before the Toby announcement. He has also become a volunteer at a pet shelter with his girlfriend. The August hike is tentatively planned, with no date or trail confirmed. Audrey's household is described as four dogs, though the 8 July photos show three dogs on leashes, and the dogs' age and origin remain inconsistent. Pixie is described both as an April puppy and as a three-year-old mutt. Max is a separate, earlier dog now remembered fondly. Audrey has not confirmed visiting the doggy daycare, Fox Hollow, or any new trails since spring, and the pastry party has never been scheduled.

Several open threads remain. It is unknown whether the August hike will happen, which trail they will choose, and whether the dogs and Toby will meet. It is also unknown whether Andrew will try kayaking or bungee jumping, whether he will share his 23 June hike photos, and why he could not hike in early July. Audrey promised the Chicken Pot Pie and Roasted Chicken recipes, but there is no confirmation they were sent. Whether the training course is the June workshop remains unconfirmed. The woman in Audrey's 27 July photo was not explicitly identified as her. Andrew's girlfriend appears only on 8 July and 27 July, as a casual, positive part of his life. Overall, the friendship remains warm and encouraging, focused on dogs, nature, giving back, and plans they hope to carry out together.

The conversations between Caroline and Melanie run from 8 May 2023 through 28 August 2023 across fifteen sessions. They begin as friendly catch-ups and grow warmer and more personal, moving into shared stories about identity, advocacy, adoption, mental health, and creative life. Each woman consistently encourages the other. Photo descriptions are often loose and sometimes do not match the text beside them, so the written accounts should be relied on wherever they differ.

Caroline is a trans woman who moved from Sweden about four years before July 2023 and has been transitioning since roughly 2020. Her recurring interests are counseling and mental health work, LGBTQ advocacy, her long-held dream of adopting children, and her own art. Her grandmother in Sweden gave her a necklace with a cross and a heart, which stands for love, faith, and strength and reminds her of her roots. Her closest local friends have known her for about four years and supported her through a difficult breakup, which showed her how important a support system is. A friend once made her a hand-painted bowl for her 18th birthday, about ten years before June 2023, and she still treasures it. She draws and paints, works in stained glass, has taken up piano, and, according to the fifteenth session, plays acoustic guitar. She keeps a guinea pig named Oscar.

Melanie is a mother of young children who works while raising them. She has been married for about five years as of June 2023, and she describes her wedding, including a ceremony in a greenhouse, as full of love and joy. Her recurring themes are balancing work and parenting, self-care, and creative outlets such as painting, pottery, and music. She runs to de-stress and enjoys family camping and hiking. Her household includes a dog named Luna, a cat named Oliver, and, as of the thirteenth session, another cat named Bailey. Her youngest child recently took first steps, and her daughter's birthday was celebrated on 13 August 2023, though no age is given.

The first session took place on 8 May 2023 at 1:56 pm and was an in-person catch-up. Melanie said she was swamped with her kids and work. Caroline reported that on 7 May she had attended an LGBTQ support group whose transgender speakers moved her, leaving her happy, accepted, and courageous enough to embrace herself. Melanie praised that courage. Caroline plans to continue her education toward counseling or mental health work, and Melanie said she would make a great counselor because of her empathy. Melanie shared a photo of a lake sunset and mentioned a 2022 painting of a lake sunrise, describing painting as her way to relax after long days.

The second session took place on 25 May 2023 at 1:14 pm. Melanie said she had a lot going on. Around 20 May she ran a charity race for mental health, which made her think about taking care of our minds. She described self-care as a journey, since looking after herself helps her look after her family, and she is carving out daily me-time for running, reading, or violin. Her family was thinking about camping in June. Caroline said she is researching adoption agencies, since giving a loving home to children who need one has long been her dream. She shared a photo of an agency sign, chosen because it helps LGBTQ+ people adopt, and said she knows it will be tough as a single parent but is up for the challenge. Melanie said she would be an awesome mom.

The third session took place on 9 June 2023 at 7:55 pm. Caroline described a school event she had spoken at the previous week, where she shared her transgender journey and encouraged students to get involved in the LGBTQ community. The event made her reflect on how far she has come, and she was glad the audience related and wanted to be better allies. She said conversations about gender identity and inclusion are necessary and that she wants to build a strong, supportive community of hope. Melanie said sharing stories shows people they are not alone. Caroline plans to keep using her voice and named Melanie as part of that effort. This memory covers sixteen sessions between Nate and Joanna, from 21 January 2022 through 24 June 2022. They are friends who reconnected after a long gap and have stayed in touch since. They share a love of movies, stories, and creative hobbies, and their conversations move among creative work, food, pets, nature, games, and daily life. They trade recommendations, recipes, photos, and small personal updates. Both have been warm and encouraging throughout, usually closing with friendly goodbyes and offers of support. Joanna tends to open with news about her writing or her week, and Nate usually answers with his own updates, photos, or questions. Where the record contradicts itself, this memory notes the contradiction rather than resolving it.

Nate's main hobbies are playing video games and watching movies. He especially loves action and sci-fi films, likes how their effects look, and enjoys classics. He says fantasy and sci-fi movies are a great escape that get his imagination going, and he describes playing video games as his creative outlet. In Session 16 he mentioned playing Chess with friends after a gaming party, the first board game in the record. Joanna is not really into games, and the two agree they share similar interests with different emphasis.

Nate also enjoys cooking and experimenting in the kitchen, especially ice cream and dairy-free desserts. In Session 3 he said he had just discovered he could make coconut milk ice cream, which he called rich and creamy, and he likes chocolate and mixed berry flavors. In Session 8 he gave the coconut milk recipe in the chat: coconut milk, vanilla extract, sugar, and a pinch of salt, chilled, churned in an ice cream maker, then frozen until scoopable. In Session 16 he described making vegan ice cream around 17 June and sharing it with people in his vegan diet group, the first mention of such a group. He promised to send that recipe on 25 June.

Nate has described himself as not really into hiking, though he likes nature and has been curious about trails. In Session 8 he said he was curious to see Joanna's trail and mentioned a nice one just north of where he lives. He has accepted the idea of hiking together but has not committed to a date.

In Session 15 Nate named Iron Man as his favorite superhero, because he loves the tech and sarcastic humor and said such figures make him feel invincible. He shared a photo of a toy Iron Man figure, which he said reminds him of something he loves and keeps him working toward his goals. In Session 9 he named a trilogy he loves for its world building, battles, and storytelling, which Joanna later identified as "The Lord of the Rings." He also called a book series with adventures, magic, and great characters a must-read, but he did not name it.

Nate keeps pet turtles, which bring him joy and calm him when he is nervous. He described them as big personalities that are low-maintenance, and said their slow pace is a nice change from the rush of life. His turtle count is not consistent. In Session 2 he described a turtle and a baby turtle and said he had had them for three years. In Session 5 he shared a photo of two tortoises in a jungle and then of three turtles on rocks in a pond, and the record does not clarify how many he has. In Session 8 he said he sometimes brings the turtles into the kitchen while he cooks.

In Session 12 Nate announced that he had adopted a dog named Max and shared a photo of Max on a couch. He described Max as full of energy and said Max keeps his other pets active. In Session 13 he said he takes Max on walks and had met a very nice couple with a dog who live close by. The three agreed to arrange doggy playdates, and Nate said Max really likes the other dog. He said the couple shared little beyond a love of animals, but that was enough to make them good friends. The record does not show that any playdate has happened yet.

Joanna's hobbies are writing, reading, watching movies, exploring nature, and baking and cooking, which she calls her creative outlets. Her favorite genres are drama and romantic comedy. She has a background in acting. She said acting was her first passion, that she once forgot her lines during a first play because she was so nervous, and that she now shines more in writing, though she might return to acting someday. Her main sources of joy are writing and time with friends. In Session 6 she advised Nate to read widely, try different genres, write and share with friends, and gather feedback. Her go-to place for inspiration is a bookshelf full of books and magazines.

Joanna has a serious allergy to animals. She is allergic to most reptiles and to animals with fur, and around them her face gets puffy and itchy, so she has always stayed away from pets. In Session 5 she also said she recently found out she is allergic to cockroaches. Her dietary restriction has been described in two ways. In Session 4 she said she cannot have dairy, and in Session 8 she said she is lactose intolerant and needs the dairy-free version. Both point the same direction: she needs dairy-free desserts. In Session 10 she said she had been testing dairy-free dessert recipes for friends and family, and she shared a photo of a dairy-free vanilla cake with strawberry filling and coconut cream frosting. In Session 16 she plans to make Nate's vegan ice cream for her family.

Joanna's attitude toward pets has shifted over time. In Session 2 she said she would think about getting pets if she could find ones she is not allergic to. In Session 5 she wished she were not allergic and said she would get two turtles that day if she could. Nate offered to send her turtle pictures so she could watch them grow without getting close, and she liked the idea. In Session 12 she said her allergies make her not really want a pet. In Session 13 Nate sent her a photo of a stuffed animal and called it a new pup for her. She said she would cherish "that little guy." The stuffed animal is a toy, so it does not conflict with her allergies, and the record does not show that Joanna has a real pet.

Deborah and Jolene are two women who have each lost their mothers. Across twenty-two sessions, from their first chat on 23 January 2023 through 26 August 2023, they have moved from polite acquaintances trading photographs to people who check in on each other's losses, goals, stress, and small pleasures. Deborah usually offers routines, encouragement, and emotional support, while Jolene has increasingly moved from sharing achievements toward asking for help. Both keep a physical link to their mothers through objects, places, and rituals.

The first session took place on 23 January 2023 at 4:06 pm. Deborah said she had recently visited her late mother's old house. She shared a photo of their last picture together, her mother hugging her while both sat in wheelchairs, and described a bench near the window where her mother liked to sit every morning, which Deborah sometimes sits on herself to feel connected to her. She mentioned a pendant that reminds her of her mother, then ended the session early, saying she had to run. Jolene answered with a photo of her own room in her mother's house, which has a bench and a window. She wears a heart-shaped pendant with a bird on it, given to her by her mother in Paris in 2010.

The second session took place on 27 January 2023 at 9:49 am. Deborah said her father had passed away suddenly around 25 January, and the family was shell-shocked. She was channeling her grief into time with family, who had been going through the family album. She shared a photo of her parents' wedding in 1993 and said she and her husband were trying to be as good a family as her parents had been. Asked what she valued most in her relationship, she said love and openness had kept them close. She also shared a photo of a living room with a window in her old home, where she sometimes practices yoga for her mother. Jolene introduced her pets, which calm her. She shared a photo of her snake Susie and described how her second snake, Seraphim, which she had bought a year earlier in Paris, slipped out of its cage and coiled up beside her while she was gaming. She and her partner were both crazy about the console game "Detroit," and they also played "The Walking Dead."

The third session took place on 1 February 2023 at 7:03 pm. Jolene said her engineering professor had given the class a huge robotics project, which she called tough but fun. Deborah said she had met her new neighbor Anna on 31 January at yoga in the park. When Deborah asked whether Jolene had thought about resuming yoga, Jolene said she and her partner had planned to play the console together. Deborah then had to run, ending abruptly as she had before.

The fourth session took place on 4 February 2023 at 9:48 am. Jolene said she had been on an emotional rollercoaster but was coping. The previous week she had designed a sustainable water purifier for a rural community, and seeing it deliver clean water gave her a sense of purpose. Her career aspiration is to keep working in engineering and make a positive impact on communities in need. Deborah told her to take a deep breath and remember why she does this. Deborah named a park with a forest trail and a nearby beach where the waves make her feel peaceful, and said she visits a spot by the water near her mother's old house, bringing an amulet that belonged to her mother.

The fifth session took place on 9 February 2023 at 9:03 pm. Jolene said a mini retreat she had done on 8 February to assess where she stood in life had given her a real confidence boost. She had also made progress on her engineering project and proposed a volunteer program in which engineers teach STEM to underprivileged kids. She had not yet contacted any schools. Deborah asked to be kept informed.

The sixth session took place on 22 February 2023 at 4:12 pm. Jolene said she was buzzing after a night out with friends on 21 February. Deborah said she had been spending time in a garden to find comfort, because she had lost a friend around 15 February. She shared the last photo she has with her friend Karlie, two women riding a motorcycle on a dirt road. Karlie is separate from Deborah's mother. Deborah said Bali last year was one of her favorite trips and was wonderful for yoga, and Jolene said she had been wanting to try yoga on the beach.

The seventh session took place on 25 February 2023 at 4:50 pm. Jolene said she now sets aside time for yoga and meditation, which gives her calm amid the chaos, and that her partner sometimes joins her. She and her partner are not married, have been together for three years, and are taking things slowly. They met in an engineering class in college and still work on projects together. Deborah described her routine of meditating, doing yoga, and teaching each morning, and said that on 24 February she had gone for her first morning jog. She said "Can't pour from an empty cup," and reminded Jolene that she is worth it too.

The eighth session took place on 2 March 2023 at 7:18 pm. Deborah said Anna had recently brought her a vegan stir-fry, and Jolene said her favorite comfort food is lasagna. Jolene had done yoga and meditation on Friday, 24 February, and taken Seraphim to the park on Sunday, 26 February. She said exams and deadlines had left her overwhelmed and asked for tips on studying and time management. Deborah advised breaking work into smaller pieces, setting goals, and using a planner, and promised to send her a mug with a handwritten encouraging message. That mug is still owed.

The ninth session took place on 13 March 2023 at 11:22 am. Deborah said she had started a neighborhood yoga class, hosted on Friday, 10 March. Jolene said she was struggling with her engineering assignments and asked whether they could still talk about time management. Deborah suggested finding a time that worked for both of them, and Jolene said she would check her schedule.

The tenth session took place on 22 March 2023 at 5:35 pm. Jolene said fitting everything in felt like playing catch-up. She was using the Pomodoro Technique but still struggled to prioritize. Deborah described the Eisenhower Matrix, and Jolene said she would give it a go. Deborah shared that she and Anna had recently watched the sunset by the sea and realized they inspire each other. Asked what a photo of a person walking on a beach with a surfboard made her think of, Jolene said learning to surf, and that she had a beginner's guide and just needed the right time for a lesson.

The eleventh session took place on 28 March 2023 at 4:03 pm and was lighter in tone. Jolene said that on 24 March she had a breakthrough on her engineering project. Deborah had bought new props for her yoga class and a rosemary candle, and Jolene said she loves serene spaces with scents like lavender and rosemary. Deborah recommended instrumental music, naming a track called "Savana" and an album called 'Sleep.' Jolene said she loves Nils Frahm and Olafur Arnalds during practice and would check the recommendations out.

The twelfth session took place on 9 April 2023 at 4:30 pm. Deborah led with news of an art show she had visited with a friend, which reminded her of her mother, who believed art could connect people in unique ways. Jolene said her snakes cannot chat, but their time together teaches her to slow down, and that playing video games with her partner after a long day helps her relax. She said she had been working on a big project that was tough but cool to watch take shape.

The thirteenth session took place on 6 June 2023 at 3:56 pm, about eight weeks after the previous one, the longest gap up to that point. Jolene apologized for the silence. She had wrapped up the tough engineering project in May and shared a photo of a solar-powered vehicle. She is now interning at a well-known engineering firm and said it has been hard to find time for her hobbies. She shared a photo of a man standing on a rock with his arms outstretched, describing it as an example of her previous morning: yoga on top of Mount Talkeetna. The photo shows a man rather than Jolene herself. She said she had been doing yoga and meditation sporadically for about three years. Deborah shared a photo of a room with a bench and a window, calling it her favorite studio, and recommended a few minutes of mindful breathing each day.

The fourteenth session took place on 26 June 2023 at 9:17 am. Deborah said she had been busy preparing for a yoga retreat with friends. Jolene said her internship had been super busy and she could use a break. She shared photos of Seraphim in a new aquarium she had bought on 24 June. She said she was pushing herself hard, which sometimes felt overwhelming, though she was determined to reach her goals. She also claimed a big breakthrough with a project, though the photo of a house drawing does not make clear which project it is.

The fifteenth session took place on 9 July 2023 at 7:37 pm and was mostly about routines, friendships, and pets. Deborah said she had started a running group with Anna. Jolene was adding workouts to her studying schedule and said gaming had been tough lately, though she was grateful for a partner who helped her stay focused. She named "It Takes Two" as their favorite game to play together. Jolene described a snake that got out and was found hours later snuggling under the bed. The snake is not named, and the story differs from the Seraphim episode, so it is safest to treat it as separate. Deborah introduced her cats for the first time, sharing a photo of two cats on a couch. She does not like dogs, which is why she has cats, and she runs with them in the park every morning and evening, describing running as a reset button. Jolene shared a photo of a dock on a lake, calling it a hidden gem where she feels peaceful. Both said they would go there together sometime.

The sixteenth session took place on 1 August 2023 at 9:26 am. Deborah said she had just started a community cleanup project and was trying to raise funds for it. Jolene said life had been a rollercoaster. In the week before 1 August, a project she had worked on hard crashed, and she lost everything. She called it frustrating and depressing. Deborah apologized and offered to help. Jolene said Susie really helps when times get tough, and that video games have been a nice distraction. She shared a photo of a man holding a snake on his arm, not a photo of herself. Asked how she came to have Susie, Jolene said she adopted her two years ago, when she was feeling lonely. This is not reconciled with the record's earlier silence on Susie's origin or with the Paris purchase of Seraphim. Deborah promised a tutorial video, and Jolene promised to practice the routine and report back.

The seventeenth session took place on 12 August 2023 at 8:50 pm. Deborah said she had made a meditation guide for her yoga retreat. Jolene said she had been stressed since she lost her work files and that meditation had helped her recover her clarity. This is the first explicit account of the August setback. The lost files and the crashed project are likely related given the timing, but the record does not confirm they are the same. Deborah told her that if she ever needs support she should say so, because they are in this together. Jolene then shared a photo of two blue-covered notebooks she had designed herself and described a prototype for aerial surveillance, a more affordable system for responding to emergencies and monitoring the environment. This is the first mention of aerial surveillance.

The eighteenth session took place on 16 August 2023 at 2:58 pm. Jolene said she had been thinking a lot about her plans, especially after checking in with her boyfriend, whom she calls her bf. She did not know how to juggle her engineering work, her relationship, and her growth, and asked Deborah how she manages when things become too much. Jolene said she had recently started a bullet journal, the first time the record names one. Deborah said she had led a meditation yoga session for elderly residents of a local care home the week before, held during sunset. She asked whether Jolene had tried mindfulness, and Jolene said she had not tried it yet but was keen to. Deborah offered to help her get started.

One detail from this session does not fit the earlier record. Jolene said she had "not tried" mindfulness, yet in sessions seven, eight, thirteen, sixteen, and seventeen she described regular yoga and meditation. She may have meant formal mindfulness training, but the wording is unreconciled, and a future assistant should not assume either reading without asking.

The nineteenth session took place on 19 August 2023 at 12:52 am, the first held after midnight. Deborah said that last Friday she had told Anna the story of her life, and Anna had been very kind. The record does not settle whether "last Friday" meant 18 or 11 August. Deborah asked how Jolene's mindfulness workshops and reading were going. Jolene did not answer directly. The session then turned to games. Jolene asked whether Deborah played video games, and Deborah said she used to, but it had been a while. This is the first time Deborah has mentioned games. Jolene recommended "Zelda: Breath of the Wild," "Animal Crossing: New Horizons," and "Overcooked 2," a co-op game she and her partner often play for bets. A future assistant should not assume the husband is no longer part of her life unless Deborah says so. Deborah then described a park near her house with a forest trail and a beach, which matches the park she named in session four, and a special bench there that holds memories of her and her mother, who would come there to talk about dreams and life. Jolene shared a photo of a park bench with a tree behind it. The record does not say whether this is the same bench as the one by the window in session one. The session ended without a formal goodbye.

The twentieth session took place on 21 August 2023 at 9:11 am and was the first in which Jolene opened the conversation. She wrote "Long time no talk!" and said the team had been given a new console game, Battlefield 1, the week before. The record does not say who gave it to them. Deborah said she had gone to a place that held many memories and had sat on a bench where, in her words, "we used to chat." She had brought flowers and shared a photo of a vase set on the ground in a street. Deborah said her mother loved flowers and appreciated simple things, then shared a photo of a woman holding a bouquet of red roses, though the record does not say who is pictured. Deborah said her mother had taught her to take things slow, see beauty in them, and find joy. Jolene said she was trying to do more yoga and meditation to relax and stay focused, that she loves savasana because it helps her let go, and that she had been practicing for three years.

The twenty-first session took place on 24 August 2023 at 9:34 am and was the first in which Deborah greeted Jolene warmly with "Good to hear from you!" The week before, Deborah had gone to a yoga retreat near her mother's place, which she called very cool, a time to be with nature and get to know herself, and life-changing. This is not clearly the same as the June retreat she had been preparing for or the August meditation guide, so the record treats it as a separate, recent retreat unless Deborah says otherwise. Jolene said she was glad Deborah had connected with nature, which is also how Jolene relaxes. She said life had been hectic but she was making strides toward her goals. She had been studying, attending workshops, and networking, and had recently presented at a virtual conference and received positive feedback. This is the first mention of a conference presentation, and its subject is not named. Jolene said she was considering more internships, and Deborah said she was super proud and asked to be told if Jolene needed help. Deborah closed with "Always by your side!"

The twenty-second session took place on 26 August 2023 at 5:33 pm, two days after session twenty-one. Deborah said she had been thinking about her mother's influence and that remembering those we love is important. Jolene replied that last Friday she and her partner had talked about how their loved ones had shaped them and what those people's values meant. The date is not stated. Jolene said yoga gives her balance and strength, and asked for tips on staying relaxed while studying. Deborah suggested breaks, stretching, walks, enough sleep, and self-care. Jolene said yoga and meditation help her recharge and calm her mind, and that she had already shared her love of yoga with her partner. They are planning a meditation retreat together, with no date yet. Jolene shared a photo of a woman in a pink shirt doing a yoga pose, but the record does not say who is pictured. Asked whether her snakes enjoy yoga, Jolene said her snakes like watching her chill, and that one of them, not named, is great company.

Deborah then named her cats for the first time. Luna is the cat on the left in a photo of two cats on a window sill. The second cat is Max. The most likely subjects of a future check-in are the lake trip, the planned meditation retreat with Jolene's partner, the aerial surveillance prototype, the conference, the cleanup fundraising and running group, whether Jolene has begun mindfulness, whether she will pursue the internships she mentioned, the renewable energy and clean water projects, and whether Max, Luna, Susie, and Seraphim come up again.

Taken together, the memory shows a steady arc. Deborah's grief over her mother and father, and her loss of Karlie in February, sit alongside her yoga teaching, her neighborhood class, her friendship with Anna, her running group, her retreats, her cats, her cleanup project, and her community events. Jolene's grief for her mother sits alongside her engineering work, from the robotics project and water purifier to her internship, her August setback, her aerial surveillance prototype, and her conference presentation.
