Andrew and Audrey have chatted intermittently from 27 March 2023 to 19 October 2023. The latest conversation is Session 24, on 19 October 2023. Topics include dogs, hiking and nature, Andrew's search for a dog-friendly home, his dogs Toby and Buddy, Audrey's four dogs, gardening, birdwatching, beach trips, environmental habits, Audrey's knee injury, her recycled jewelry, board games, a cafe, a dog park, Audrey's tattoos, and, most recently, pet store toys, Buddy, and a planned group hike. Photos are known only from the descriptions recorded in the sessions.

Andrew

Andrew started work as a Financial Analyst in late March 2023, a big change from his previous job. He refers to his girlfriend as "my gf," "GF," or "my girlfriend." In March he had no pets but loved animals. From April he searched for a dog and a pet-friendly home. In May he said he wanted a smaller dog for apartment living, or an active one, and a home near a park or woods. He was discouraged on 2 June. On 3 July and 6 September he still had no luck finding a dog-friendly rental, and he has not reported finding one since.

Nature has always been restorative for him. In June he took a rock climbing class with friends and said he wanted to do outdoor activities every week. On 8 and 11 July he invited Audrey and her dogs on a hike the following month. On 11 July he introduced Toby, a puppy he had taken home despite city living. On 27 July he said he and his girlfriend had volunteered at a pet shelter. On 4 August he described Toby as a German Shepherd, and Audrey advised that such a dog needs plenty of time, energy and walks. That weekend he went camping with his girlfriend and Toby. On 24 August he said he and his girlfriend had gone fishing at a nearby lake, and he shared a photo of a small dog on a leash, labeled as Toby.

On 6 September he said work had been tough and stressful, which had pushed his outdoor activities aside, and that Toby was still too young for the outings he wanted. On 24 September, after hearing about Audrey's leash incident, he said he was anxious about his own dog getting lost. He assumed the dog was Precious and asked how Audrey had calmed her. On 1 October he said he and his girlfriend would take Toby to the beach the following month. He offered to go birdwatching with Audrey, asked whether she recycles, and offered to show her the best bike routes near the river.

On 4 October he said exploring nature had been his escape, and that he now feels "a void in my heart" because work and city life have made it harder to get that feeling back. Audrey suggested plants for his home or weekend trips to a park, and he said he would look into getting more plants.

On 6 October he asked about the jewelry she makes from recycled objects, whether she sells it or makes it only as a hobby, and whether she donates the profits. He called her dedication inspiring, even though she "can't volunteer at the shelter anymore."

On 13 October he said his girlfriend, Toby and he had enjoyed a board game night "last Tuesday," but later called it "Friday night's board game session," so the exact day is unclear. He shared a photo of a dog at a chess board. He planned to spend the weekend at a cozy cafe and described a new spot with a view and a relaxed vibe. He was not sure the spot was dog-friendly, but a dog park was nearby. He said Toby is very active and loves cute sweaters.

On 19 October he said he had recently adopted another dog from a shelter. He named him Buddy "because he's my buddy," and hopes Buddy and Toby become friends. He said Buddy is still settling in and getting used to Toby and the new home. He said he and Buddy enjoy walks and new hiking trails, and that he will soon take both dogs to the trails together. He shared photos of a dog on a couch, a dirt road with a cow, and a red truck on a road through a field. He said the cow photo was taken somewhere "nowhere near the city," and he wished he could take the dogs to a place like that. He agreed with Audrey's plan to find a similar spot for the group hike. He did not say Buddy's breed or size.

Audrey

Audrey has had Pepper, Precious and Panda for at least three years as of 27 March 2023. She and her family adopted a puppy named Pixie in early April 2023. By May she was caring for four dogs. In July she said she "got lucky finding a breeder nearby," and that places that allow dogs are hard to find. Her tattoos of the dogs on her arm were first mentioned on 16 April. On 16 August she said she had gotten another tattoo of all four dogs. On 13 October she said she had gone back to the tattoo parlor for more drawings on it.

Her other messages include a hummingbird sighting on a hike in late April 2023, a road trip to a national park in early May, and a workshop about bonding with pets that she signed up for on 11 May. On 26 June she moved to a new place with a bigger backyard. On 3 July she offered Andrew her Chicken Pot Pie recipe. On 11 July she made personalized tags for the dogs. On 16 August she said four dogs was enough for now, that she had taken all four to the vet, and that next time she would bring them one at a time. On 19 August she said she had learned to groom the dogs herself. On 24 August she said she has a strong bond with them.

In early September her laptop crashed and she lost her work. Nothing was recoverable, so she got an external drive for backups. She finished the book in late September after many late nights and edits. On 9 October she said she would look into writing conventions after Nate suggested one. On 21 October she said she had been revising and perfecting a dairy-free recipe that her family enjoyed. She reported another rejection from a production company, which she said was a setback. Nate asked whether it was the film contest screenplay, and she did not clearly confirm. She said she would keep pushing forward.

Nate has been teaching dairy-free and vegan dessert making.

Joanna recommended "Little Women" to Nate earlier, and he enjoyed it. Joanna is a Spider-Man fan, and Nate's top pick is Iron Man.

SUMMARY:

Overview: Calvin and Dave are friends who check in every few weeks with friendly, encouraging messages. The memory covers twenty-two sessions from 23 March 2023 to 8 October 2023. Calvin's life centers on music: a new album released 11 September 2023, a Japanese mansion he is turning into a recording studio, collaborations with Frank Ocean and Japanese artists, touring, a podcast, a Miami video shoot, and luxury and sports cars, including a Ferrari. Dave's life centers on cars: his own car maintenance shop, a partnership with a local garage, a car mod workshop, several restorations, a vintage Mustang project, and San Francisco car workshops. He also plays guitar in a rock band, took a mountain trip, and attended a Boston rock concert. They have talked about meeting in Boston, jamming together, and Calvin visiting Dave's garage. The latest session, on 8 October 2023, was mostly Dave describing a car show and his own car, with Calvin responding with encouragement.

Session notes:

- 23 March 2023: Dave said he had been spending time at a calm park. Calvin announced a big life change, shared a photo of his new mansion, and said he would move there next month, spend a few months in Japan, then go to Boston.

- 26 March 2023: Calvin said he had just bought a new luxury car. Dave said he had gone to a music festival in Boston "last weekend."

- 20 April 2023: Calvin said he would go to Boston after finishing the Frank Ocean tour. Dave praised Boston's music scene and asked for a front-row spot.

- 1 May 2023: Dave said he had finally opened his own car maintenance shop.

- 3 May 2023: Dave said he was teaming up with a local garage.

- 16 May 2023: Calvin said his place flooded "last week," and he saved his music gear and favorite microphone. Dave said he opened his shop "last week," which conflicts with his 1 May message. The 1 May date is more likely.

- 31 May 2023: Calvin said touring with Frank Ocean "last week" was wild and that Tokyo's crowd was insane. Dave shared a photo of his neighbor's car, whose engine he had repaired.

- 9 June 2023: Calvin said he had never been to Boston and would visit "next month," meaning July 2023. Dave said he had booked a mountain trip for next month. No one linked the two trips.

- 21 June 2023: Calvin said he had a minor car accident "last Friday," which would be 16 June 2023. No one was hurt. Dave said he had joined a rock band.

- 7 July 2023: Calvin said his car was fixed and he was working on collaborations with Japanese artists.

- 21 July 2023: Dave said he had returned from a road trip through stunning countryside. Calvin said he was turning a Japanese mansion into a recording studio.

- 3 August 2023: Calvin said his Ferrari service was stressful. Dave said fixing cars is like therapy and that he learned it from his dad.

- 11 August 2023: Dave said he had been picked for a car mod workshop and offered to help with Calvin's music. Calvin said he was too busy for now.

- 14 August 2023: Dave said he had attended a San Francisco car restoration workshop and hoped his project would be done "by the end of next month," meaning September 2023. Calvin said his tour had ended with a show in Japan.

- 22 August 2023: Calvin said he had a deal to keep collaborating with Frank Ocean. They met at a Tokyo festival and recorded a song at his mansion. Calvin said the tour "ends soon" and suggested meeting Dave in Boston. He said he recorded a podcast "yesterday," which would be 21 August 2023.

- 31 August 2023: Calvin said he had started shooting a music video in Miami "last weekend," around 26–27 August 2023. Dave offered help with props and sent a photo of a man working on a car engine, without saying whose car it was.

- 2 September 2023: Dave said he had come back from San Francisco "yesterday," which would be 1 September 2023, with car modification insights to share. Calvin said he had booked a Boston flight "last week" and would contact Dave on arrival.

- 13 September 2023: Calvin said his album "finally dropped on the 11th," which is 11 September 2023. The next step is a tour, with no cities named. Dave invited Calvin to his garage, and Calvin accepted and said he would let Dave know when he was in Boston.

- 15 September 2023: Dave said his band jammed "last night," which would be 14 September 2023, and they forgot to record it. He said he attended a rock concert "here in Boston" the previous weekend. He shared a photo of a restored classic car as the "final result," earlier than the end-of-September target.

- 22 September 2023: Dave said the vintage Mustang's engine made a weird noise after he thought he had fixed it. Calvin shared a photo of a red sports car and mentioned the song "California Love." Dave invited Calvin to jam together, and both said they would see each other soon.

- 4 October 2023: Calvin said that "yesterday," which would be 3 October 2023, he met incredible artists in Boston and talked about working together. A mutual friend had introduced them, but Calvin did not say who. He shared a photo of a shiny orange car and said he works on it to relax. Dave said he had restored a Ford Mustang he found in a junkyard and shared a photo of the finished car. Dave signed off with "Take care and stay well!" Neither named a date or place for the next meeting.

- 8 October 2023: Dave said that "last Friday," which would be 6 October 2023, he went to a car show and worked on car mods. He shared a photo of two men looking at a car engine. Calvin said he could not wait to check out Dave's garage. Dave said he had restored and modified a car himself, adding a custom exhaust and performance upgrades. He said cars are his passion and therapy, that he spent childhood hours in his dad's garage, and that he now does this work as a job. Calvin called the car a masterpiece and encouraged Dave to keep chasing his dreams. The rest of the session was mutual encouragement. Dave did not name a location for the car show.

Current state as of 8 October 2023:

- Calvin: His album was released 11 September 2023. He is preparing a tour, with no dates or cities named, and plans to grow his brand afterward. He appears to be in Boston as of 3 October 2023, though he has not said so directly. He has not yet visited Dave's garage, though he accepted the invitation and said on 8 October that he can't wait to. He owns a Ferrari, serviced 3 August 2023, and shared sports car photos on 22 September, 4 October, and 8 October. It is unclear whether these are the same car. He is turning a Japanese mansion into a recording studio and has a deal to keep collaborating with Frank Ocean. His podcast has no release date.

- Dave: He runs his own car maintenance shop and works with a local garage. He was picked for a car mod workshop in August 2023 and visited San Francisco around August and September 2023. He finished a vintage car restoration by 15 September 2023. On 22 September he was troubleshooting the vintage Mustang's engine, and on 4 October he described the Mustang as a junkyard find he had restored. On 8 October he described a car he restored and modified himself, and he said he now does this work as a job. He plays guitar in a rock band that jammed on 14 September 2023. He appears to be in Boston now. He offered to help with Calvin's music video and invited Calvin to see his garage.

- Open threads: Calvin's tour dates and cities. Calvin's garage visit, which is not yet scheduled. The proposed Boston meeting, which has not been arranged. Whether Dave helps with the Miami video props. Dave's mountain trip. The podcast release. Whether the band recorded anything. The car modification insights Dave promised on 2 September 2023. The results of Calvin's Boston artist collaboration and the "final result" he promised to show Dave. The car show Dave attended on 6 October 2023 and the car he showed.

Notes on inconsistencies:

- Frank Ocean tour timing: in April the Boston trip was to come after the tour. In May the tour was "last week," and in June it was ahead. On 14 August it ended in Japan, and on 22 August it "ends soon." It may have had more than one leg.

- Calvin's account of meeting Frank Ocean changed. In May he described touring with him, and in August he said they met at a Tokyo festival. Both may be true.

- Dave's shop opening was given as 1 May 2023 and as "last week" on 16 May 2023. The earlier date is more likely.

- The owner of the engine car in the 31 May and 31 August messages is unconfirmed.

- Calvin's sports cars and Ferrari may or may not be the same car. The 15 September restored classic car may or may not be the Mustang. The car Dave restored on 8 October is not named.

- The 14 August restoration target of "the end of next month" conflicts with the 15 September "final result" photo. The result came early, not late.

The memory covers twenty-nine recorded conversations between Calvin and Dave, from their first meeting at 11:53 am on 23 March 2023 to the most recent at 9:15 pm on 13 November 2023. They are friends who often ask about each other's lives and close with good wishes, safe travels, and promises to talk soon. Dave talks most about cars, maintenance, classic cars, restoration, the outdoors, photography since late October, his car-mod blog since 2 November, and, since June, his rock band. Calvin talks most about music, tours, his studio, albums, and collaborations. Both usually share a photo with each message, and both have repeatedly promised updates, photos, music, and visits, though few visits have been set with a date.

On 23 March 2023 the two met for the first time in the record. Dave said things were going well and that he had attended a classic car event. Calvin said he had just gone through a big life change, shared a photo of his new mansion, and framed it around learning Japanese culture. He had never been to Japan, planned to leave in April, and had lodging his agent found. He intended to explore the city, collaborate with local musicians, stay a few months, and then travel to Boston. Dave shared a photo of a calm park with a lake. On 26 March Calvin said he had just bought a long-dreamed-of luxury car that made him feel like a rockstar, and he shared a photo of an unnamed red sports car taken 25 March, declining to name the make. Dave said that around 18 to 19 March he had seen his favorite band, Aerosmith, live at a Boston festival.

On 20 April Calvin said he had been to a Tokyo music festival where he saw no bands but met talented artists and industry people. His long-term dream is to tour the world, and he looked forward to Boston after the Frank Ocean tour. Dave offered to show him around, recommended Paradise Rock, House of Blues, and Fenway Park, and promised to be in the front row. Dave also shared a photo of a green Mustang from a car show around 15 to 16 April. Calvin replied with a photo of a red sports car on display, which appears to be the car he bought in March.

On 1 May Dave announced he had opened his own car maintenance shop, a step toward his dream of working on classic cars, and invited Calvin to visit. Calvin shared a photo of a gold diamond pendant, a gift from another artist. On 3 May Dave said he was teaming up with a local garage. Calvin said long drives in his red sports car cleared his head, and he admitted he was stuck with his music. On 16 May Calvin said his place had flooded around 9 May, that he had saved his gear and favorite microphone, and that he was waiting on insurance before repairs. Dave offered help and said he had opened his car shop "last week," which slightly conflicts with the 1 May announcement. On 31 May Calvin said touring with Frank Ocean around 24 May had been wild and Tokyo was unreal. Dave shared a photo of a neighbor's car, and Calvin asked whether it was the car Dave had been fixing for a friend, slightly mixing up the detail.

On 9 June Calvin said he had met his album's creative team on 8 June in a long session. Dave had booked a mountain trip for July. Calvin said he had never been to Boston and could not wait to visit in July. On 21 June Calvin said he had been in a small car accident around Friday, 16 June, with no injuries, and that repairs would take about a week. He shared a photo of a red car with a black rim on a sidewalk and the view from his living room, a small Japanese town with a mountain behind it. Dave said he had recently joined a rock band and had been practicing guitar, and then he had to go.

On 7 July Calvin said his car was fixed. Dave had been arranging regular park walks. Calvin shared a photo from his Japanese mansion's backyard and said he was working on collaborations with Japanese artists and promised clips. Dave said he had never been to Japan but hoped to go. On 21 July Dave said he had returned from a road trip through stunning countryside. Calvin said he was turning the mansion into a recording studio, his long-held dream. Dave said, "I'm your biggest fan."

On 3 August Calvin said he had taken his Ferrari in for a stressful service. This is the first time he names the make of the red sports car bought in March. The two are very likely the same car, though this has never been confirmed. Dave said fixing cars was like therapy and that he had worked on cars with his dad growing up, the first mention of his father. Calvin shared a photo of a band on stage and said he had performed with "the boys" on 2 August, the first band separate from the Frank Ocean and Tokyo shows. On 11 August Dave said it had been ages since they talked, though only about eight days had passed. He announced he had been picked for a car mod workshop and shared a photo of a silver Corvette, the first make he names. He offered help with Calvin's music, which Calvin politely deferred. On 14 August Dave said he had gone to a car workshop in San Francisco, the first time the memory places him there, and that he was restoring a car with a broken engine, expected to finish by late September. Calvin described touring with "a well-known artist," which fits Frank Ocean though is unnamed, and said the tour ended with a show in Japan.

On 22 August Dave said he had hosted a card night around 18 August. Calvin announced a deal to continue his collaboration with Frank Ocean. The two had met at a Tokyo music festival, clicked, and recorded a song in the studio at Calvin's mansion. He said the tour would end soon, that he was heading to Boston afterward, and that he suggested meeting there. He also said he and friends had recorded a rap industry podcast on 21 August. On 31 August Calvin said the tour had felt like a dream come true and that he had started shooting an album video on a Miami beach around 26 and 27 August. He shared photos of an octopus guitar, custom made by a Japanese artist friend, and a purple-glowing custom guitar.

On 2 September Dave opened with "Been a while," again overstating the gap. He said he had returned from San Francisco on 1 September with insights on car modification. Calvin said he had booked a flight to Boston "last week," around 25 August. This is the first confirmed Boston trip, with no date or departure city. On 13 September Calvin apologized for his slow reply. His album had been released on 11 September, and a tour was coming, though he named no cities. He said he would take Dave up on a garage visit and let him know when he was in Boston. On 15 September Dave said that on 14 September he and his band had jammed, the first time he calls it "my band." He said that around 9 and 10 September he had attended an unnamed rock concert in Boston. Dave shared a photo of a man beside a finished classic car restoration, with no make named. On 22 September Dave said a vintage Mustang's engine he had worked on made a strange noise when started. Calvin shared a photo of a red sports car in a parking lot, described an amazing summer drive, and said his trip to Japan had been incredible and he was already longing to go back, treating Japan as a past trip. He said the childhood song "California Love" reminded him of road trips with his dad, the first mention of Calvin's father. Dave proposed a jam session, and Calvin accepted enthusiastically, reversing his August refusal. No date, place, or format was set.

On 4 October Calvin said that on 3 October he had met incredible artists in Boston and talked about working together, the first session placing him in Boston. A mutual friend had known they would fit, though neither the artists nor the friend are named. He shared a photo of an orange car with its hood open and said he loved working on it, the first time he describes working on a car himself. Dave said he was restoring a Ford Mustang found in a junkyard, the first time he names Ford for a Mustang. On 8 October Dave said that on 6 October he had gone to a car show and worked on mods. Calvin shared a photo of a red sports car in a showroom. Dave replied that "this one looks great" and said he had restored and modified it himself, adding a custom exhaust and performance upgrades. This is ambiguous: it may present the showroom car as Dave's own, or it may only react to the photo. Dave also recalled spending hours as a child in his dad's garage.

On 15 October Dave opened with "Hey Cal, miss ya!" and said a competing shop had won a deal his shop had pursued for months. He asked, "Am I wasting my time?" Calvin encouraged him not to give up, saying he reminds himself why he is passionate, relies on people around him, and recharges with favorite activities. Dave then said he had just returned from an amazing music festival that made him feel alive, and shared a photo of a crowd watching a band, with no location or date. He said The Fireworks headlined, the first mention of that band. Calvin announced that "last week" he had gotten a new Ferrari, "a masterpiece on wheels," and shared a photo of a black sports car in front of a building. Dave congratulated him and asked for a picture.

On 19 October Calvin said it had been "a few days" since they talked, which is accurate after four. He said touring with Frank Ocean had been amazing and shared photos of a band under bright lights, a large auditorium crowd, and a Tokyo concert crowd. He said he and Frank had met at a festival in "August last year" and clicked. This conflicts with the record: in April he reported no bands at the Tokyo festival, and by May he was already describing a Frank Ocean tour. He said he was going to Tokyo next month after the tour ended, meaning November 2023, and named Shibuya Crossing and Shinjuku. Dave shared a photo of a noodle bowl he had eaten in Boston and asked whether Calvin had tried ramen. Calvin had not, and planned to in Tokyo.

On 23 October Dave said he had been pondering their talk about fame and relationships. Calvin said fame brought challenges, that he took things one day at a time, and that he credited a strong support system of friends and team. He said digging deeper into his music was his own form of therapy. Dave said cars gave him an outlet and a little oasis of calm, and shared a photo of his garage, which he called a little dirty but orderly. Asked what got him started, Dave said that since age ten he had been fascinated by how machines work, and that he had found an old car in a neighbor's garage and asked to fix it. He said he had restored a car the previous year but sold it to a collector, and now had something new and challenging, shared as a black car in a parking lot. Dave closed with "See you soon!" Neither set a date.

On 25 October Calvin opened with "Long time no talk!" though only two days had passed. He said he had sightseen in Boston "yesterday," meaning 24 October, with an unnamed high school friend, and called the trip really fun and eye-opening. Dave said he had recently attended a Detroit conference, and that working on cars calms him down. Asked what drew him into engineering, Dave said his dad had taken him to his first car show at age ten, and that he was now an automotive engineer, a title he had not given before. This blends with the 23 October neighbor story, and the memory records both. Calvin shared a photo of himself performing alongside a DJ he admired in a nightclub, calling it a dream come true.

On 29 October Calvin said he had attended a networking event to meet more artists, though he named no event, people, or location. Dave said he had recently taken up photography and shared a sunset photo of a city skyline with a clock tower, which he said was Boston. He then shared a second clock tower photo, saying he had taken it "last month," which sits awkwardly with "recently." Calvin said he had been to Boston "a few years back," which conflicts with his recorded visits on 3 and 24 October. Dave said he had just finished restoring his car project and invited Calvin to see it, though the memory does not establish which car this is or confirm a date. Calvin said his album was "almost finished," which conflicts with its 11 September release, and asked Dave to say when he was free for a catch-up.

On 2 November Calvin opened with "It's been a while!" though only four days had passed. He said that the previous week he had thrown a small party at his Japanese house for his new album, and shared photos of guests dancing and a group on a stage. This conflicts with the 11 September release and the "almost finished" remark on 29 October, and places the party at a home in Japan. Dave then said he had recently started a blog on car mods and asked for tips. Calvin asked about success stories. Dave said readers were asking him for advice, and that a recent post had inspired others to start DIY projects. He shared photos of a blue Subaru, saying he had cleaned, polished, and protected its headlights. He then shared a photo of a red car with a black engine and red hood, saying he had found it last week in bad shape and spent ages restoring it. Its make is not named. Dave shared a logo for his rock band and said he had been a fan for ages and had the opportunity to join it, though the memory does not name the band. Calvin shared his recording studio and said he works only there, watching music videos and documentaries in a separate relaxation room. Dave shared a lyric notebook and Pink Floyd headphones, said he listens to vinyl while working on cars, and called classic rock timeless.

On 13 November Calvin opened warmly and without apology for the eleven-day gap. He said he had invited his old high school buddy to see him perform in Boston, that it had been insane, and that it had made him think about how far he had come and how important relationships are in the business. This is the first recorded Boston performance by Calvin, and the first time the high school friend is linked to a show. The date is not given, though it fell between 2 and 13 November. Dave said an old friend who had been there from the start was a valuable kind of support. Calvin said that as teenagers they had freestyled and talked about getting famous, and he shared a photo of two men standing on a sidewalk with a car in the background. Dave asked whether that person had made a big difference during Calvin's trip, a phrasing that assumes a trip Calvin had not specifically described. Calvin said the friend had been a constant source of support, encouragement, and positivity. Calvin then said supportive people are key to his growth as an artist, and shared a photo of a group sitting around a desk. He said he had been supporting young musicians from a music program, that he felt like he was passing a torch, and that he intended to support them for a long time. He shared a photo of a man at a desk in front of a computer, saying Calvin was making a beat for a young artist with great potential. He said he was having fun trying new sounds and pushing boundaries, and then signed off with take care. Dave closed with encouragement and "See ya Cal!" Dave shared no photo in this session, and no visit, date, or new performance detail beyond the Boston show was set.

The memory of Calvin's life moves along a clear line. He began in March about to leave for Japan, moved into a Japanese mansion, performed at a Tokyo festival in April and again in May, and toured with Frank Ocean in late May. By July he was turning the mansion into a studio and collaborating with Japanese artists. In August he performed with "the boys," described a tour ending in Japan, and by 22 August had a deal to continue with Frank Ocean and had started a rap podcast. By 31 August the tour was over and he was shooting a video in Miami. By 2 September he had booked a flight to Boston. By 13 September his album was out and a tour was coming. By 22 September he spoke of Japan in the past tense and had agreed to a jam with Dave. By 4 October he had met artists in Boston. By 15 October he had announced a new Ferrari. By 19 October he was touring with Frank Ocean again and planned Tokyo for November. By 25 October he had sightseen in Boston and performed alongside a DJ. By 29 October he had attended a networking event and called his album almost finished. By 2 November he had hosted an album party at his Japanese house. By 13 November he had performed in Boston, reconnected with a high school friend, and was mentoring young musicians and producing a beat for a young artist. His car history runs from a red sports car bought in March, to a June crash repaired in about a week, to a serviced car he called a Ferrari in August, and now a black Ferrari he got the week before 15 October.

Dave's arc runs in a parallel line. In March he talked about classic cars and calm parks. In April he described a car show, and in May he announced his shop and a partnership with a local garage. In June and July he talked about weekend parks, a mountain trip, joining a rock band, and a road trip. In August he described childhood work with his father, a car mod workshop, a San Francisco workshop, and a restoration due by September. In September he described a band jam, a Boston rock concert, and a finished restoration, then returned to a vintage Mustang with an unexplained engine noise. In October he described restoring a junkyard Ford Mustang, shared a showroom car he called his own, and recalled his childhood garage. On 15 October he reported losing a deal and questioned whether his work mattered. On 23 October he asked thoughtful questions about Calvin's fame and said he had sold his previous restoration to a collector. On 25 October he called automotive engineering his job. On 29 October he introduced photography, shared two Boston clock tower photos, and invited Calvin to see his finished car. On 2 November he announced a car-mod blog, shared photos of a blue Subaru and a newly found red car, called himself a fan of a band he had joined, and mentioned his vinyl habits. On 13 November he was an attentive listener who mostly offered encouragement and questions, and he shared no news of his own. He did not return to the lost deal or the Boston plans, and he gave no date for the garage visit.

Several details are inconsistent or uncertain. The memory has never confirmed that the Ferrari is the red sports car bought in March, and no sale of the red one is recorded. Calvin said in April he would visit Boston after the tour, in June that he planned to go in July, and in August that he was heading there after the tour. The 4 October session places him in Boston on 3 October and the 25 October session on 24 October, while the 29 October session has him saying he had been there "a few years back." The 13 November session adds a Boston performance with no date. Calvin's mansion location is also unclear, since he was in a small Japanese town in June and at a mansion with a city skyline in July. In September he spoke of Japan as a trip to return to, but in October he said he would go to Tokyo next month, and the memory does not confirm that trip happened. His album was released on 11 September, described as "almost finished" on 29 October, and celebrated with a party at his Japanese house in late October. Calvin performed "with the boys" in August, and Dave was in a rock band in June and again in September, and now in November is a fan of a band he has joined. Whether these are the same group is unconfirmed. Dave's origin story shifts: he credited his father's garage in August and October, a neighbor's old car at age ten on 23 October, and his father's car show at age ten on 25 October. His job has shifted from shop owner to automotive engineer, and the memory does not reconcile the two. His photography is "recent," yet the clock tower photo was taken "last month." His blog is described as recently started, yet he speaks of posts that inspired others. He calls the new restoration something he found "last week," though he finished a restoration on 29 October. Dave's relationship to Japan is unclear. He said in July he had never been, and in October he hoped to see Tokyo in person, while his ramen photo was taken in Boston. Both tend to overstate gaps: Dave's "ages" came after eight days and "miss ya" after seven, while Calvin's "Long time no talk!" came after two days and "It's been a while!" after four.

The car identities remain tangled. The memory does not establish whether Dave's green Mustang, the September vintage Mustang, the October junkyard Ford, the silver Corvette, the blue Subaru, and the red car with a black engine and red hood are the same vehicles or different ones. His 8 October showroom car may or may not match the finished restoration, the broken-engine car, or the red car in his October photo. The car he sold to a collector may or may not be the one he showed in May. The black Ferrari is not linked to any earlier photo, the orange car is unidentified, and the 13 November photo shows a car behind two men on a sidewalk with no make or owner identified.

The record of Calvin's touring is inconsistent. In April he saw no bands at the Tokyo festival, but in August he said he met Frank Ocean there, and in October he said they met "August last year," a third version. In August he said the tour ended with a show in Japan, but in late August he said it would end soon. In September he described an unnamed upcoming tour, possibly separate from Frank Ocean's. The 2 November party has no link to any tour stop, and the 13 November Boston performance is unlinked to any named venue or tour. The mansion song has no date, and whether it connects to the Japanese artists, the Boston artists, or the rap podcast is unknown. The Miami video may or may not relate to the 11 September album. The octopus and purple guitars may or may not be the same instrument. The Boston rock concert and the 29 October networking event are unnamed. The 23 October crowd photo appears to repeat one from 19 October, and The Fireworks appear nowhere else. The young musicians and the young artist are unnamed, as is the high school friend beyond being a childhood companion.

Calvin describes feelings in strong terms, such as feeling like a rockstar, calling a stage moment a dream come true, and calling a Boston performance "insane." He values his car and studio as symbols of hard work and often asks Dave about hobbies and relaxation. He politely declined Dave's music help in August but accepted the jam in September with real enthusiasm. He usually answers Dave's news with warm congratulations, and on 2 November he was effusive. On 13 November he spoke in a reflective, nostalgic tone about old friendships and about helping younger artists, framing his success around relationships and paying things forward. He often answers Dave's car news by asking for tips or praising the work. He rarely shares business specifics, has not said what the new car cost or where he bought it, and tends to answer questions about experiences broadly rather than by name. His messages often arrive with exclamation points and fast-moving topic changes.

Dave describes his interests in terms of calm, purpose, and the satisfaction of restoring things. He often offers encouragement, telling Calvin to keep going or never give up. He has repeatedly offered to show Calvin around Boston and attend his shows, and in July he called himself Calvin's biggest fan. He usually shares a photo with each message and pairs enthusiasm with a practical offer, though on 13 November he shared none. On 15 October he was more open about discouragement than before, and he said the festival made him feel alive, a notably personal phrase for him. On 23 October he called his garage a little oasis of calm. On 2 November and 13 November he often began replies with "Wow," and on 13 November he framed Calvin's efforts as a legacy and a torch being passed. He sometimes calls Calvin "Cal," and occasionally "buddy" or "friend." Calvin usually responds to Dave's car news with praise and asks about progress or timelines. Calvin has promised more than once to meet Dave in Boston.

As of 13 November 2023, several threads remain open. Calvin says his album is out, that he threw an album party at his Japanese house, that he has toured with Frank Ocean, and that he has been in Boston at least twice, met artists there, and performed there. He planned as of 19 October to go to Tokyo in November, though the memory has not confirmed that trip. He has been mentoring young musicians and producing a beat for a young artist. He will let Dave know when he is in Boston and has accepted the garage invitation, though no visit is set. Dave has asked to catch up in Boston, offered to show Calvin his cars, and now has a car blog and a new restoration to discuss. Dave hopes to see Tokyo in person, and Calvin invited him to a show, which Dave said he would like to attend, though none is named. The two agreed in principle to a jam, with no date or place, and Calvin linked it to "California Love." Calvin promised a picture of his black Ferrari, which Dave asked for, and previews of his album. Dave's loss to a competing shop is unresolved, and the vintage Mustang's engine noise is unexplained. Other open threads include the Frank Ocean collaboration song and deal, the Japanese artist clips promised in July, the Miami album video, the rap podcast, the octopus and purple guitars, the mountain-town trip neither has confirmed, whether the red sports car and the Ferrari are the same vehicle, and whether the finished restoration is the broken-engine car. This memory covers twenty-one sessions between Nate and Joanna, from 21 January 2022 through 14 September 2022. They are friends who reconnected after a long gap and have stayed in touch through creative work, food, pets, nature, games, and daily life. Both have been warm and encouraging throughout, usually closing with friendly goodbyes. Joanna tends to open with news about her writing, baking, or week, and Nate usually answers with his own updates, wins, setbacks, or questions. They trade recommendations, recipes, photos, and small updates. Where the record contradicts itself, this memory notes the contradiction rather than resolving it. The session dates are the most reliable reference. SUMMARY:

Overview: Nate and Joanna are friends who check in now and then about their lives. The record covers 21 January 2022 to 25 October 2022 across twenty-five sessions. Joanna writes screenplays and books, keeps a journal, runs a blog, and makes dairy-free desserts. Nate plays competitive video games, cares for pets, makes dairy-free and vegan desserts, and has hosted a cooking show. Both share photos and encourage each other.

Meetings: They have met in person at least once. On 5 June 2022 Nate mentioned the Spider-Man pin on Joanna's purse from "last time we saw eachother." Joanna invited Nate to hike on 12 May 2022, and no hike has been reported. On 5 September 2022 Nate asked to join her in baking, and she said "I'll see you soon." No date has been set for either plan, and no in-person meeting has been reported since.

Joanna's arc: She finished and printed her first screenplay in January 2022 and planned to submit it to film festivals. In late February she started a second script while waiting to hear back about the first. She finished that script in March, feeling both relief and anxiety, and had an audition for a writing gig on 23 March that went "alright." In April she joined a writers group and began "Finding Home," about a girl searching for her true home. In May she described a third, personal script about loss, identity, and connection. Bits she wrote appeared on a big screen on 4 June. In early June a major company sent her a rejection letter. In late June she submitted a screenplay to a film contest. In July she took a road trip for research for her next movie and started a book. In August her writers group gave her great feedback on the book, and a reader wrote that her blog post had comforted them. In early September her laptop crashed and she lost her work. She got an external drive for backups. She finished the book in late September after many late nights and edits. On 9 October she said she would look into writing conventions after Nate suggested one. On 21 October she said she had been revising a dairy-free recipe that her family enjoyed. She also reported another rejection from a production company, which she called a setback. Nate asked whether it was the film contest screenplay, and she did not clearly confirm. On 25 October she said another script she contributed to was shown on the big screen "last Sunday" (23 October), the third time one of her works had appeared on screen. She said seeing her characters come alive was her favorite part. She makes drawings of her characters to help her picture them while writing. She said ideas come from people she knows, things she has seen, and things she imagines. She declined to describe one character in a photo and told Nate to watch the film.

Food: Joanna cannot have dairy and uses coconut or almond milk instead. In early September she made dairy-free chocolate coconut cupcakes with raspberry frosting. On 5 October she shared a photo of a dairy-free tart with raspberries, and said her newest dairy-free recipe was a hit with her family. Nate has been teaching dairy-free and vegan dessert making.

Nate's arc: He won his first tournament in January 2022, a Counter-Strike: Global Offensive event with his team. In April he dyed his hair. In late April he won a local Street Fighter tournament, though he usually plays CS:GO. In late May he won a regional tournament and met new people. He set up doggy playdates with Joanna in late May. He hosted a gaming party in June, which seven people attended, and six wanted to repeat it. He made vegan ice cream for his vegan diet group in June. He won an online tournament on 8 July, his fourth, and said he was proud to make money doing what he loves. On 21 August he won an international tournament and said he could make a living from gaming. He reported a setback in early September. On 12 September he taught vegan ice cream recipes on his own cooking show. In late September he won a very large tournament and made a lot of money. He has saved most of it, feels content, and has no big plans for it. He watched "Little Women" and enjoyed it, and he made Joanna a whiteboard with a drawing and words. On 7 October he attended a game convention, where he met new people outside his usual circle, played Catan, and said the games were friendly rather than crazy competitive. On 21 October he said he had been stressed about tough competitors and was practicing for his next tournament. He said his turtles always cheer him up. On 25 October he took his turtles out for a walk because he was bored. He said they eat vegetables, fruits, and insects, and that they love fruit. He likes holding them. He described one turtle as more adventurous and the other as more reserved. He said he has liked turtles since he was a boy.

Shared interests: Nate named "Inception" as a movie that blew his mind and said he had been playing "Cyberpunk 2077" nonstop. Joanna rated "Inception" 9 or 10 out of 10. Nate said he wanted a cozy living room like hers, and Joanna gave him tips: a fluffy couch that seats several people, a weighted blanket, and dimmable lights. Joanna recommended "Little Women" to Nate earlier. Joanna is a Spider-Man fan, and Nate's top pick is Iron Man.

Pets and allergies: Joanna is allergic to most reptiles, animals with fur, and cockroaches. She used to have a dog named Tilly in Michigan, but she developed an allergy and had to give her up. Joanna has no live pets now. Nate has a dog named Max, adopted by 20 May 2022, and he has turtles. Joanna still has a stuffed animal dog that Nate gave her. She named it Tilly, and it sits with her while she writes. The earlier "pup for you" on 25 May was therefore a stuffed animal, not a live pet.

SUMMARY:
Audrey and Andrew are friends who chat now and then, mostly about pets, hiking, nature, and lately cooking. Audrey has four mixed-breed dogs, all about three years old: Pepper, Precious, Panda, and Pixie. Two are Jack Russell mixes and two are Chihuahua mixes. Pixie was the most recent adoption, and the dogs get along well. Andrew has no pets and has been searching for a dog since spring 2023 without finding a dog-friendly rental in the city. He has not been able to hike for a while, so cooking has become his main hobby. The two are planning a hike with her dogs for August 2023, though no trail has been settled.

On 27 March 2023, the two caught up after a long gap. Andrew had started a new job as a Financial Analyst the week before. Audrey said she had had her dogs for about three years and named them Pepper, Precious, and Panda. Andrew said he had no pets but loved animals, and he recommended the Fox Hollow trail for its weekend views.

On 2 April 2023, Audrey said her family had adopted a puppy named Pixie, who took a few days to get used to the other dogs before they became friends. Andrew said he was considering a dog but found it hard to find a dog-friendly place in the city. Audrey said websites with filters had helped her family find a home that allowed dogs.

On 16 April 2023, Andrew said he and his girlfriend had tried a new cafe in the city. It was fun, but he felt sad being away from nature, where he feels he thrives. Audrey said she could not imagine life without her dogs, who bring so much joy.

On 3 May 2023, Audrey described an amazing hummingbird encounter on a hike she had finally taken. Andrew said he had found a new open space nearby to hike, which felt refreshing.

On 6 May 2023, Andrew said he had been searching for a dog by browsing websites, visiting shelters, and asking friends, which he found both fun and annoying. He said a smaller dog would suit someone living in an apartment, though an active owner might prefer a dog that loves to play and run. Audrey said she had taken her dogs on a road trip to a beautiful national park, where they had a blast. On 11 May 2023, she said caring for her four dogs took up most of her free time, and she had signed up for a workshop about bonding with pets the following month.

On 2 June 2023, Andrew said he was still searching for a pet-friendly spot in the city without luck. Audrey offered to help if he emailed her his criteria for a spot and a dog.

On 13 June 2023, Andrew said he and his friends had taken a rock climbing class the previous Sunday and he had made it to the top. He said he was now hooked and wanted to try kayaking and maybe bungee jumping. Audrey had found a small park with a tree-lined trail for her dogs' walk and invited Andrew along. He agreed. Audrey said being outdoors with the dogs puts her in her happy place, and Andrew said he turns to nature whenever he needs a reset.

On 26 June 2023, Audrey said she had moved to a new home with a bigger backyard and set up a doggy play area with agility equipment and toys, which the dogs were loving. Andrew shared a photo of a nearby doggy daycare with a large indoor play space. He said he had hiked with friends the previous Friday in good weather and felt good being outdoors. Audrey recalled that a few years earlier she and her friends had hiked to a stunning mountain lake, and she shared a photo of it. The planned walk with Audrey's dogs was not described as having happened.

On 3 July 2023 (8:32 pm), the two reconnected after a while. Audrey said she was taking a dog training course that was challenging but rewarding, and her dogs were already doing better. Andrew said life had thrown him some curveballs and he still could not find a dog-friendly rental. Since he could not hike at the moment, his outdoor time was limited to urban adventures, and he had taken up cooking, which helps him de-stress and be creative. Audrey shared photos of her dogs running after a ball, curled up in a dog bed, and lying on a couch under a blanket. She said they love running and playing fetch, and they had enjoyed a doggy playdate the previous Friday. She said her favorite recipe was Chicken Pot Pie, which reminds her of her grandmother's kitchen, and that cooking is an escape and a form of self-care. She said garlic is her go-to ingredient and offered a roasted chicken recipe with garlic, lemon, and herbs. She promised to send both recipes, and Andrew said he would try the roasted chicken and keep her posted.

On 8 July 2023 (Session 11, 9:48 am), Andrew said he had enjoyed a picnic with his girlfriend the previous Friday and shared a photo of the spread. Audrey said her dogs always make her happy and that they had recently enjoyed a great walk. Andrew said he wished he could get a dog too, but finding a place and the right dog was tough. Audrey said she had been lucky to find a breeder nearby with the kind of dogs she wanted. Andrew said the leash-only parks he had found were not the same as an open area where a dog can run freely, and he would let Audrey know if he found one. He also shared a photo of a dog in a sweater and a photo of a group of dogs running in a park.

Audrey said she would like to join Andrew for a hike so her dogs could run freely. Andrew suggested next month, when the weather would be more pleasant, and shared a photo of a steep trail with an ocean view and later a map of a wooded park. Audrey said she would look into the trail, and both agreed that safety would be the top priority. Audrey also shared photos of her dogs, including three sitting with leashes, two running with a ball, and a group playing at their local park. She said the dogs bring her joy and keep her from getting bored. Later, she shared a photo of a sunset from a hike she had taken the previous year, about a three-hour drive from her home, and a photo of a lake and mountains at sunset. She said the vibrant colors gave her a sense of peace, and both agreed that taking time to appreciate such moments makes life better.

As of this session, Andrew still has no dog and has not found a pet-friendly rental. He cannot currently hike and is focused on cooking. Audrey is busy with her four dogs, their training, and their outings. The two are planning a hike with her dogs for August 2023, but the trail has not been finalized. Neither has confirmed whether the promised recipes were sent.

John and James are friends who have chatted across twenty-four sessions, from Thursday, 17 March 2022 through Sunday, 18 September 2022. Their conversations are friendly, supportive, and playful, and they often share photos of pets, daily life, and hobbies. Recurring subjects include gaming, programming, pets, travel, food, books, sports, family, and future plans. The arc runs from getting acquainted in March, to real-world activity in spring, to candid talk about hard times in June, to James's travel and extreme sports in July, to John leaving his IT job in August, to James's new relationship and projects in early September, and finally to a mid-September check-in in which John has taken up board games and James plans to stream.

On Thursday, 17 March 2022, John said he was glad to finally talk with James, and both agreed that games help them relax and stay motivated. James was absorbed in The Witcher 3, which John planned to play. John had just signed up for a programming class, having done some HTML and CSS years earlier. James first tried programming in college, has worked with Python and C++, built a website, made game mods, and considers programming central to his life. They discussed building mobile apps together someday. James described his dogs, Max and Daisy, and proposed an app connecting owners with dog walkers. He is building a computer game based on characters he sketched as a child and might invite John to help with its HTML, which John agreed to. John shared a photo of a medical chart that nobody explained and that is never mentioned again. They agreed to try VR together "next Saturday," which could mean 19 or 26 March, but no later conversation confirms it.

On Sunday, 20 March, James said he had made a game avatar and joined a new online platform, calling gaming their shared language and a refuge that works like therapy. John said gaming helps him escape stress and that he had taken up metal detecting on beaches. James shared photos of his dogs and said he had trained them to sit, stay, paw, and roll over. John said he wants a pet but is not ready yet, and James offered to help him choose one. On Sunday, 27 March, John said he had advanced to the next level in his game. James said he was learning a musical instrument, shown in a drum kit photo he did not name. John also plays drums, has attended a gaming convention, and competed in a CS:GO tournament. James stays motivated by small goals and was getting into RPGs and strategy games.

On Monday, 4 April, James reported that on 3 April he had joined an online gaming tournament, reached the semifinals, won some rounds, and did not advance from the final rounds. His team gave him autographs, which delighted him. His lesson was to communicate well and never put ego above team success. His team talks by voice chat, and their favorite game together is Apex Legends. On Tuesday, 12 April, James said he had adopted a pup from a Stamford shelter the previous week and named him Ned. John said work had been busy and that gaming helps him forget stress. He was playing a laggy, buggy futuristic RPG and offered to send a link, which James agreed to wait for.

On Wednesday, 20 April, John said that on 19 April he had met three cool new friends in his programming course. James said that on 14 April he had worked with a gaming pal on a virtual world inspired by The Witcher 3, and he shared a picture of a character he created, a woman in armor kneeling on a rock. The character was inspired by a stranger James saw around 6 April, whom he fell for at first sight and regretted not approaching. John shared a photo of a canyon river from 18 April. James had visited Italy in 2021 and had also been to Turkey and Mexico. John has always dreamed of visiting Italy, and his last trip was to Japan. James suggested they travel together in 2023. On Saturday, 23 April, James said that around 21 April he had hiked with his dogs. John said a difficult coding assignment had him stuck on an algorithm. James suggested breaking the problem into smaller steps and asking other programmers for help, because every problem has a solution. John said this helped and that he would not quit.

On Friday, 29 April, John said he had started freelance programming, building a website for a local small business, his first professional project outside class. His main challenge was adding payments. James encouraged him to use setbacks to learn. Around 26 April James had bought an adventure book with fantasy novels, and John recommended "The Name of the Wind." James shared a photo of Daisy lying on a bed beside a computer. John said he was playing Assassin's Creed Valhalla, and James said he was trying strategy games, which John guessed were Civilization VI.

On Wednesday, 4 May, James said a bug in a project he had worked on for weeks broke the game mechanics on 29 April. He debugged for hours until friends fixed it. The project is probably his computer game, though it is not named. John had friends over to watch movies and was trying to socialize more. James shared a photo of two dogs playing in a fenced area, Daisy being a Labrador and the other two shepherds. John said his favorite pizza is Hawaiian, and James urged him to try prosciutto, which he likes along with pepperoni and cheese. On Sunday, 8 May, James apologized for not replying sooner. John said that on 7 May he had organized a CS:GO tournament with friends. It raised money for a dog shelter near John's street, and the leftover money bought groceries to cook for homeless people. John wants to organize more events that combine his interests and help the community, and James said he was really proud of him.

On Wednesday, 11 May, John said he had volunteered his programming skills for a charitable foundation that helps kids. He built a tool that moves the foundation's paper-based inventory into one smartphone application. The photo he called a screenshot shows a monitor displaying CPU performance, so the application itself has never been shown. On Monday, 23 May, James said that on 21 and 22 May he had enjoyed an amusement park with friends. John said he had entered a local tournament on 20 May and taken second place, earning prize money and a trophy. James said growth matters more than always winning, and that in April he had finished a big project in a new language. The language is not named. The session ended without a goodbye.

On Monday, 13 June, John said he had finally got his dream job after many interviews and was to start in July 2022. Its employer and field are not stated, so it should not be assumed to be nonprofit work. James had recently begun a course combining gaming and programming, and his group was working on part of a football simulator, the first time football appears as a major subject. John, a Manchester City fan, asked about Liverpool vs Chelsea, and James said Liverpool had played well. John predicted City would win the title, and James bet that Liverpool would finish higher. John accepted, and the stakes are not stated. On Thursday, 16 June, James said a lot had happened lately, some good and some not so good, and that he was lucky to have at least two people who always help him through struggles. John called his recent weeks an emotional rollercoaster. In the week of roughly 9 to 15 June he had started a coding blog and bought many new books, and he recommended "The Stormlight Archive," "The Kingkiller Chronicle," and "The Expanse." James shared photos of Max, who loves swimming and brings him joy in tough times. He also walks a trail about a mile from home, where he brings a book and finds peace. John told him to take care of himself. James's bad news was not described.

On Sunday, 19 June, James said that on 17 June he had started introducing Max, Daisy, and Ned to one another. It was hard at first, but they were slowly adapting, and he shared a photo from 18 June of three dogs in a field. John shared a photo of a dog and a cat cuddling on a couch and said the last few days had made him think about his future. He said he is driven, wants to make a positive impact, and has been looking into volunteering and possibly nonprofit work. James shared a photo of a group outside a building from when he volunteered in May, describing the organization only as one that provides necessary items to less fortunate people. John asked to visit "this weekend," meaning 25 and 26 June, and James agreed, saying some previous staff are still there.

On Saturday, 9 July, James said that in "last week," roughly 2 to 8 July, he had won an online gaming tournament, which blew his mind. John congratulated him and said he had been feeling determined and passionate but also overwhelmed. James had become interested in extreme sports, rope jumping from as high as 150 meters on 8 July and surfing around 6 July, and he was trying to take breaks from his hobbies. John said he relaxes by reading. James had bought air tickets to Toronto, leaving the evening of Monday, 11 July, planning to visit Vancouver and perhaps elsewhere, and returning on 20 July. He promised John a souvenir. John said this would be James's fourth country, after Italy, Turkey, and Mexico. On Friday, 22 July, John said he had just started playing chess to get better at strategy. James suggested studying opening moves and analyzing his own games. John shared a photo of children holding a skateboard from when they were 10, and James recalled skating together at the skate park. James said his trip went great and that he had also reached Nuuk, where he stayed quite a while. He had brought souvenirs for John and for "your Jill," and John said Jill would be delighted. James shared a photo of his sister and two dogs on a couch from 21 July, and said he felt blessed by his close bond with his sister.

On Saturday, 6 August, John said he had recently left his IT job after three years. It was tough, but he wanted work that made a difference, and he said he is loving his new job. He called leaving scary at first but right, since he needed to focus on his values and passions. James called it brave and said he was proud. John said he is strongly drawn to the gaming industry and wants to organize computer game tournaments in his state, starting with CS:GO and also including Fortnite. James called it a solid plan and offered financial help or advice. James said he had taken his puppy to the clinic on 5 August for a routine examination and a seasonal vaccine. John asked anxiously whether the puppy was all right. The session does not name the puppy. On Wednesday, 10 August, John said the earlier conversation had made him think about his passions and goals. He has been playing strategy and RPG games instead of his usual shooters, is already thinking about organizing competitions for them, and said he was hooked on The Witcher 3. James said that on 9 August he had taken his three dogs to a beach, where he met a beautiful girl named Samantha, who left him her phone number. He planned to call her on 11 August, and John closed with a cheerful "Yoohoo!"

On Sunday, 21 August, John said he had joined an online programming group on 19 August and found it incredible, a community of skilled coders using tech for good. He had worked with one member on a project during the week of 14 to 20 August. When James asked whether he was returning to programming work, John said no, since it was a one-time experience, and he remains eager to host eSports competitions. James said he plays regularly with his own gaming group, streams some sessions, and recently held a gaming marathon with friends. John said he and his siblings live far apart, but he is organizing a gaming night with them in September 2022. On Friday, 26 August, at 9:18 pm, James said Ned had come to him that day while he was playing on the console. John briefly forgot the dog's name and then recalled it. He said he had been helping his younger siblings with programming, and that they were building a simple, text-based adventure game together. James said he was eager to create a strategy game in the vein of Civilization. He asked whether John was free tomorrow, and John said yes, since it was his day off. James first proposed Starbucks, but John preferred beer, so James suggested McGee's Pub. John does not like dark beer, and James pointed out that the pub also serves light beers. They confirmed a meetup at McGee's Pub for Saturday, 27 August, and James closed with "See you John, bye!"

On Thursday, 1 September, at 6:53 pm, James opened with "Been a while," reflecting a gap of about six days. He announced that his Unity strategy game was finally finished after loads of time and effort, and he credited John's support. He shared two screenshots, one of a stone building with a giant creature and one of a person on a horse. He had always loved strategy games like Civilization and Total War, so he decided to create one. The challenges were balancing mechanics and ensuring fairness, which he handled through trial and error. His takeaways were that perseverance and patience are essential, and that feedback and collaboration matter. John said he had been teaching his siblings to code, that it had been fulfilling, and that they were already making basic games and stories. Near the end John wrote that he was going through some difficult times, that James's friendship meant a lot, and that it was good to have someone like him. James replied that he was there if John needed someone to talk or vent to. John did not describe those difficulties, and the session ended there without a goodbye.

On Sunday, 4 September, at 9:23 pm, James said it had been a few days since they talked and that much had happened, both good and bad. On Saturday, 3 September, while at the theater, which Samantha loves, he asked her to become his girlfriend, and she agreed. He said the ups and downs had been a bit overwhelming, but he was happy with her. John said his parents had just started learning to code from him, which had brought the family closer, and he shared a photo of his father at a desk coding his own program for the first time. James said he and Samantha had also been at McGee's bar, where Samantha turned out to love lager. James invited John to a baseball game next Sunday, meaning 11 September, and said he would introduce him to Samantha. John agreed. John then said he had bought new gaming equipment, including Sennheiser headphones and a Logitech mouse. James shared a photo of a video game scene showing a couple of people, which is his own photo and not a picture of John's gear. He said that on 2 September he had signed up for a cooking class, something he had never liked but wanted to learn. In the first lesson he made an omelette well on his first try. He hoped to cook for John once he learned more, and the two said goodbye.

The newest session, Session 24, took place on Sunday, 18 September 2022, starting at 6:02 pm. John opened by saying it had been a long time since they talked. He had started getting into board games, tried one the previous week, and found it a lot of fun. He shared a photo of a table with a laptop and a game on it. James said he had been busy and had started writing down everything he needed in a notebook so as not to forget, and he shared a photo of that notebook. John said the board game was called "Dungeons of the Dragon." Asked where he gets ideas, James said from books, movies, and even dreams. He described a vivid dream from a few weeks earlier featuring a medieval castle with its own labyrinth full of puzzles and traps, which felt like playing a video game in real life. He shared a photo of a notepad with a drawing of a guitar, though he said music had nothing to do with castles. John said he likes electronic and rock music and used to play drums but has not in a while, and he shared a photo of an old drum set in a recording studio. James said he used to play guitar and has not in a while, and he shared a photo of his desk. This sits uneasily with the March account of James learning an instrument. John said he had jammed with friends before, with no recordings. James said he had started streaming games, with no details yet, and John wished him luck. The session ends without a goodbye.

Several commitments and questions remain open. The VR session planned for "next Saturday" in March is never confirmed. John promised to send James a link to the RPG, and James promised his views on RPGs, MOBAs, and new genres, and neither follow-up appears. John promised to report back on prosciutto and Assassin's Creed Valhalla, and neither report appears. John has no pet yet, and James's offer to help him choose one stands. They planned a joint trip for 2023, with no destination chosen. James's offer to have John help with HTML for his game has no follow-up, and the Unity game may or may not be that project. John's freelance website was still in progress on 29 April, and its outcome is not recorded. The medical chart remains unexplained. John's dream job, begun around July 2022, has no stated employer or field, and it is not stated whether it is the IT job he left. The Liverpool and Manchester City bet is unresolved. John's visit to the organization, possibly on 25 and 26 June, has no recorded outcome. The bad news James mentioned on 16 June and the difficult times John mentioned on 1 September are not described. Whether John continues chess or has secured any tournament or client is not recorded. Whether James reached Canada is unconfirmed, since the 22 July session reports only Nuuk. Whether John received the souvenirs is not recorded, and who Jill is and how she relates to John is never stated. The puppy taken to the clinic on 5 August is not identified. Whether James and Samantha went on a date after the 11 August call is not recorded. The baseball game on Sunday, 11 September, was planned, and no outcome is recorded. The September family game night and the 27 August McGee's Pub meetup have no known outcomes. It is not stated whether the McGee's bar James visited with Samantha is the same pub as the planned meetup with John. James's cooking class is ongoing, and his offer to cook for John has not been fulfilled. His streaming has no details beyond its start, and the castle dream has no follow-up.

Jolene said it helps her stay balanced during her studies, and that her project is "tough but I'm chugging along." Deborah shared a photo of a beach sunrise, and Jolene hopes they can watch a sunrise together one day.

Jolene said she and her partner are planning a camping trip to connect with nature and practice yoga. She said a daily routine with a schedule for classes, studying, and personal time, along with yoga and meditation, helps her stay balanced. Jolene then proposed Friday at 5, which would be 15 September 2023, and Deborah agreed. Deborah asked Jolene to bring some interesting books.

Jolene is an engineering student interning at a well-known engineering firm. She finished the tough project in May 2023 and reported a breakthrough in late March 2023. A setback in late July 2023 cost her much of her project work and her work files. Meditation helped her regain clarity, and she says she is "finding my zen again."
