Caroline and Melanie are friends who check in every few weeks, sharing photos and talking about mental health, self-care, identity, family, creative work, and the futures they are building. They celebrate each other's progress and encourage each other's goals. Eighteen sessions are recorded, from 8 May 2023 to 20 October 2023. Session 18 came one week after session 17 on 13 October.

Caroline is a transgender woman who began transitioning about three years before June 2023. She moved from Sweden roughly four years earlier, around the time her current friendships began. After a painful breakup, her friends and mentors helped her through, and she calls them her "rocks." Family is everything to her. She keeps a necklace from her grandmother in Sweden with a cross and a heart, representing love, faith, and strength. Her favorite book is "Becoming Nicole" by Amy Ellis Nutt, and she loves horses, a love that began when she rode with her father as a child. Her favorite song is "Brave" by Sara Bareilles. She has played acoustic guitar for about five years and says playing helps her release her emotions. In the sixteenth session she said some close friends kept supporting her while a few could not handle her identity, and her relationships now feel more genuine.

Caroline has long wanted to become a mother. In the second session (25 May) she said she had chosen an adoption agency that supports LGBTQ+ adoptive parents, and that she felt ready, though single parenthood will be hard. In July she was building a children's library for her future kids, and an adoption council meeting on 14 July made her more determined. Between 21 and 23 August she applied to adoption agencies, her first concrete step toward motherhood. In the seventeenth session she said she had just contacted her mentor for adoption advice and wanted to provide a safe home for kids who need one. Whether any agency has accepted her application is not yet known.

Melanie has been married for about five years and has young kids. She works, looks after the family, and makes time for running, reading, music, and painting. In July she said her mental health had improved. She joined a pottery class on 2 July, which she says feels like therapy, and her favorite subjects are landscapes and still life. Her family life includes shared outings, such as camping in the mountains around 20 June. In the fourteenth session she recalled volunteering with her family at a homeless shelter.

In the seventeenth session Melanie raised adoption because a friend had adopted the previous year. She said the process was long but the family is now very happy, and it made her wonder whether she should adopt too. Caroline offered help and tips: research agencies or adoption lawyers, gather documents such as references, financial information, and medical checks, and prepare emotionally for the waiting. Melanie said she would do that. Whether she has taken any concrete steps is not known. In the same session Melanie said she had been hurt the month before and had to pause pottery, which she uses for self-expression and peace. She said she was doing okay, keeping busy with a book Caroline recommended and with painting. Whether she has returned to pottery is not known.

Art remains a strong thread for both of them. Melanie shared a pink-sky sunset painting that makes her feel calm, and an abstract blue painting with peaceful streaks meant to show tranquility. Caroline said abstract work feels freeing because she can put her feelings on canvas without much of a plan. In the eleventh session she shared "Embracing Identity," a painting of a woman in a red shirt, and said art teaches her to accept the beauty of imperfections. In the thirteenth session she shared a self-portrait of a woman with a blue face, which made her feel liberated. She has painted since about age 17. On 17 July she announced an LGBTQ art show of her paintings for August 2023, and on 25 August she said she was putting it together "next month," which would mean September. Whether it has happened is not known.

Caroline's community work has grown steadily. In early June she gave a school talk about her transgender journey. She attended pride parades in late June, on 14 July, and around 11 August, where she felt she could be herself without fear. Around 10 July she attended an LGBTQ conference where she felt totally accepted. In mid-July she joined a mentorship program for LGBTQ youth and began mentoring a transgender teen, and on 18 July she joined the activist group "Connected LGBTQ Activists." She volunteers at an LGBTQ+ youth center and is helping organize a youth talent show for September. In the seventeenth session she described a transgender poetry reading on Friday, 6 October, which inspired her to draw a woman in a dress, an image she said stands for freedom, being real, and staying true to herself.

Caroline still meets hostility at times. On 17 August she ran into religious conservatives on a hike, whose remarks upset her and reminded her how much work remains for LGBTQ rights. In the fourteenth session she said a bad encounter on a hike the week before had bothered her, and that she tried to apologize. The outcome is not recorded.

Some earlier exchanges remain open. In the thirteenth session Melanie shared a painting of a horse, which reminded Caroline of riding with her dad. In the twelfth session the two agreed in principle to a summer family outing or something special for just the two of them, but chose no date or format, and it has not been planned since. In the sixteenth session Melanie shared a photo of a café door sign saying someone was not able to leave. Caroline asked whether anything had happened, and Melanie said it was only a precaution. Caroline then said she was glad Melanie had a good time at the park, which seems to be a mix-up.

Session 18 opened with Melanie describing a family road trip over the weekend of 14 and 15 October, which she called "insane." Her son was in an accident during the trip. The family was frightened, but he was unhurt, and Melanie said the experience reminded her that life is precious and that she should cherish her family. Caroline apologized and said it must have been traumatizing. Melanie shared a photo of a car dashboard and steering wheel, which the session does not explain further. She later shared a photo of two children on a rocky cliff over the Grand Canyon, which she said the family enjoyed. The children were scared by the accident, but the family reassured them their brother would be okay. Caroline said children are amazingly resilient. Melanie said she wished she had that resilience herself, but her children give her strength to keep going. Caroline called Melanie's family her "rock," and Melanie agreed that having family around makes hard times easier.

Melanie then shared a photo of a woman and a child walking on a trail, taken the day before session 18, which she said was a nice way to relax after the drive. She also shared a photo of a sunset over water and described family camping trips as a chance to be present and together, with stories, campfires, birdsong, and fresh air that refresh her soul. Caroline said it was lucky Melanie gets such quality family time, and Melanie wrote that nature and quality time "can't be beaten." Caroline did not share her own news in this session, and the conversation stayed focused on Melanie's family.

Several threads remain open. Caroline plans to raise a child as a single parent, and her children's library may be tied to this, though she has not said so directly. Whether an agency has accepted her application is unknown. Melanie is considering adoption but has not said whether she has begun. The art show and the talent show were both planned for September, and neither outcome is known. Also unknown are how the apology after the hike turned out, whether Melanie has returned to pottery, whether the summer outing will be scheduled, and what happened to the car in the accident. Both women see self-care, community, and family as central to how they want to live. Melanie affirms Caroline's path toward counseling, adoption, mentoring, volunteering, and art, and Caroline cheers on Melanie's running, pottery, painting, music, and family life. In the seventeenth session they closed on a shared note: Caroline said being yourself is an ongoing adventure of learning and growing, and Melanie agreed that life is about learning and exploring and that she is glad they are on this trip together.

Nate and Joanna had not spoken for a long time before they reconnected in January 2022. Across ten sessions, from 21 January to 2 May 2022, they have talked about movies, Joanna's screenwriting, Nate's gaming, pets and allergies, baking, Nate's hair, nature, and books. The tone is friendly and supportive, and each often encourages the other's goals. Conversations usually open with casual greetings, close with warm send-offs, and often include photos that the two share as they talk.

Nate's main hobbies are gaming and movies. In the first session, on 21 January 2022, he said he had won his first video game tournament around 14 January. The game was Counter-Strike: Global Offensive, a team shooter, and he and his team had a blast right to the very end. Joanna congratulated him but said she is not really into games. On 23 January he said he mostly plays for fun and does not expect to win big. At the tournament he met people outside his usual circle, but competing against them felt awkward, so he tends to stick with the chiller players. He entered again in March, which he called INTENSE. On 21 April he said his fourth tournament was next month, in May, and that he felt good about it. In the session of 2 May 2022, he said gaming has been his focus, that he has been practicing a lot, and that he had won a few tournaments. Last week he won a local Street Fighter tournament. He usually plays CS:GO but had tried Street Fighter because he plays it often with friends. He said the last match was full of adrenaline and that the other finalist shook his hand. He sees gaming as a creative outlet. On 2 May he also shared a photo of his gaming room, which has a computer and a gaming chair.

Nate loves action, sci-fi, and fantasy films, especially their visual effects and world-building, and he likes classics. He calls these films a great escape that gets his imagination going. On 21 April he praised an unnamed fantasy trilogy for its world-building, battles, and storytelling, and he recommended a book series full of adventure, magic, and great characters. Joanna said the series had been on her list forever and promised to tell him what she thinks. On 2 May she said she had watched "The Lord of the Rings" trilogy on his recommendation and found it awesome. Nate replied that it is probably the greatest trilogy of all time. Joanna favors dramas, romcoms, and emotionally driven films, because she loves getting immersed in a story's feelings and plots. In the first session she recommended an unnamed romantic drama about memory and relationships. She shared a photo of its poster, which shows a man and a woman on a bench, and a photo of her DVD copy. She first watched it around 2019, bought the DVD afterward, and considers it one of her favorites, especially for its core idea and the acting. She asked whether Nate likes it, and he has never reported back. On 7 February she said she had just watched "Little Women" and called it amazing. She asked Nate to tell her what he thinks once he finishes it, and he has not reported on that either.

Joanna's screenwriting has moved through several stages. On 23 January she said she had finished her first full screenplay, a drama-romance, which she printed "last Friday," most likely 21 January. She planned to submit it to film festivals, and by 7 February she had sent it to one. On 25 February she said she could not stop thinking about it, so she had started a second screenplay while she waited. That script is a semi-autobiographical road-trip story about a thirty-year-old woman on a journey of self-discovery after a loss, inspired by Joanna's own experiences. Nate said it takes guts to tackle such a deep topic and said he was crossing his fingers for her. On 18 March she said she had finished the second script, feeling relieved but anxious about what comes next, and Nate encouraged her not to quit. On 24 March she said she had an audition on 23 March for a writing gig. It went alright, and she felt excited but anxious. She asked Nate to keep his fingers crossed, and the outcome has not been reported. On 21 April Joanna said she had just joined a writers group whose members really understand her writing, and that she felt motivated, supported, and as if she finally belonged somewhere. She said she wished she were not allergic and would get two turtles that day if she could. Nate offered to send pictures so she could still watch them grow, and she said she was already invested in "those little guys." For now, she has chosen writing and friends over pets.

Food and baking have been a recurring thread. Nate loves coconut milk and also enjoys chocolate and mixed berry flavors. Both agreed that small things make life worth savoring.

As of 2 May 2022, Joanna has finished two screenplays and joined a writers group working on "Finding Home." Her first screenplay was submitted to at least one film festival, and the second was finished by 18 March. Her audition result from 23 March has not been reported. She is allergic to most reptiles, furred animals, and cockroaches, and she is lactose intolerant. Nate has two turtles he has owned for three years. He plays in gaming tournaments, won a local Street Fighter tournament in late April, and will enter another in May. He became interested in writing in March and dyed his hair purple in April. Both have recommended major fantasy works to each other.

Several requests remain unresolved. Joanna asked what Nate thinks of the romantic drama she recommended in January, and he has never reported back. She asked what he thinks of "Little Women" once he finishes it, and he has not yet reported. Nate has promised to keep Joanna posted on the tournament, to send turtle photos, and to offer movie picks. Joanna has promised to update him on her audition, on how the ice cream turns out, on her screenwriting, and on the book series he recommended. She has also asked to hear about his progress as a writer, and he has said he will keep working on it. Joanna has invited Nate to go hiking with her, and he has not yet accepted.

Caroline and Melanie have recorded nineteen sessions, from 8 May to 22 October 2023. They check in every few weeks, share photos, and talk about mental health, self-care, identity, family, creative work, and the futures they are building. They celebrate each other's progress and encourage each other's goals.

Caroline is a transgender woman who began transitioning about three years before June 2023. She moved from Sweden roughly four years earlier, around the time her current friendships began. After a painful breakup, her friends and mentors helped her through, and she calls them her "rocks." Family is everything to her. She keeps a necklace from her grandmother in Sweden, with a cross and a heart representing love, faith, and strength. Her favorite book is "Becoming Nicole" by Amy Ellis Nutt, and her favorite song is "Brave" by Sara Bareilles. She loves horses, a passion that began when she rode with her father as a child. She has played acoustic guitar for about five years and says it helps her release her emotions. In the sixteenth session she said some close friends kept supporting her while a few could not accept her identity, and her relationships now feel more genuine.

Caroline has long wanted to become a mother. In the second session she said she had chosen an adoption agency that supports LGBTQ+ adoptive parents, and that she felt ready, though single parenthood will be hard. In July she was building a children's library for her future kids, and an adoption council meeting on 14 July made her more determined. Between 21 and 23 August she applied to adoption agencies, her first concrete step toward motherhood. In the seventeenth session she said she had contacted her mentor for adoption advice. In the nineteenth session, on 22 October, she announced that she had passed the adoption agency interviews the previous Friday, 20 October, calling it a big move toward her goal of having a family. Whether any agency has formally accepted her application is not yet known. She wants to give a home to kids who have never had one, believing that love and acceptance should be everyone's right.

Melanie has been married for about five years and has young kids. She works, looks after the family, and makes time for running, reading, music, and painting. In July she said her mental health had improved. She joined a pottery class on 2 July, which she says feels like therapy. In the fourteenth session she recalled volunteering with her family at a homeless shelter. In the seventeenth session she raised adoption because a friend had adopted the previous year, and wondered whether she should adopt too. Caroline offered tips on agencies, documents, and emotional preparation, and Melanie said she would follow them, though whether she has taken concrete steps is not known. In the same session she said she had been hurt the month before and had paused pottery, which she uses for self-expression and peace. Whether she has returned to it is not known.

Art remains a strong thread for both of them. Melanie has shared a pink-sky sunset painting that makes her feel calm, and an abstract blue painting meant to show tranquility. Caroline finds abstract work freeing because she can put her feelings on canvas without much of a plan. In the eleventh session she shared "Embracing Identity," a painting of a woman in a red shirt, and said art teaches her to accept the beauty of imperfections. In the thirteenth session she shared a self-portrait of a woman with a blue face, which made her feel liberated. She has painted since about age 17. On 17 July she announced an LGBTQ art show of her paintings for August 2023, and on 25 August she said she was putting it together "next month," which would mean September. Whether it has happened is not known.

Caroline's community work has grown steadily. In early June she gave a school talk about her transgender journey. She attended pride parades in late June, on 14 July, and around 11 August, where she felt she could be herself without fear. Around 10 July she attended an LGBTQ conference where she felt totally accepted. In mid-July she began mentoring a transgender teen through an LGBTQ youth program, and on 18 July she joined the activist group "Connected LGBTQ Activists." She volunteers at an LGBTQ+ youth center and is helping organize a youth talent show for September. In the seventeenth session she described a transgender poetry reading on 6 October, which inspired her to draw a woman in a dress, an image she said stands for freedom and staying true to herself.

Caroline still meets hostility at times. On 17 August she ran into religious conservatives on a hike, whose remarks upset her and reminded her how much work remains for LGBTQ rights. In the fourteenth session she said a bad encounter on a hike the week before had bothered her, and that she tried to apologize. The outcome is not recorded.

Some earlier exchanges remain open. In the twelfth session the two agreed in principle to a summer family outing or something special for just the two of them, but chose no date or format, and it has not been planned since. In the sixteenth session Melanie shared a photo of a café door sign saying someone was not able to leave. Caroline asked whether anything had happened, and Melanie said it was only a precaution. Caroline then said she was glad Melanie had a good time at the park, which seems to be a mix-up.

Session 18, recorded on 20 October, opened with Melanie describing a family road trip over the weekend of 14 and 15 October, which she called "insane." Her son was in an accident. He was unhurt, but the family was frightened, and Melanie said the experience reminded her that life is precious. Caroline apologized and said it must have been traumatizing. Caroline said children are amazingly resilient, and Melanie wished she had that resilience herself, though her children give her strength. Caroline called Melanie's family her "rock," and Melanie agreed that family makes hard times easier. Melanie then described family camping trips as a time to be present together, and wrote that nature and quality time "can't be beaten." Caroline did not share her own news in that session.

Session 19, recorded at 9:55 am on 22 October, was Caroline's turn to share. She announced that she had passed the adoption agency interviews. Melanie congratulated her and shared a photo of two wooden dolls, bought the day before as a reminder of family love. Caroline replied that the figurines showed how much love exists in both blood families and chosen ones, and she hopes to give a safe, loving home to children who have never had one. Melanie called adoption a loving way to build a family. Caroline reflected that finding self-acceptance had been a long process, and that the help of friends, family, and people she admired had been invaluable. She wants to pass that support on, and said helping others grow brings her joy. Caroline agreed that living honestly is freeing and that accepting who we are brings contentment. She ended by sharing a photo of a painting with the word "happiness" on it. She also slipped once, replying "Glad you agree, Caroline," which seems to be a mix-up, much like the one in session 16.

Several threads remain open. Caroline plans to raise a child as a single parent, and her children's library may be tied to this, though she has not said so directly. Whether the agency has accepted her application is unknown. Melanie is considering adoption but has not said whether she has begun. Neither the art show nor the youth talent show outcome is known. Also unknown are how the apology after the hike turned out, whether Melanie has returned to pottery, whether the summer outing will be scheduled, and what happened in the car accident. Both women see self-care, community, and family as central to how they want to live. Melanie affirms Caroline's path toward adoption, mentoring, volunteering, and art, and Caroline cheers on Melanie's running, pottery, painting, music, and family life. In the seventeenth session they closed on a shared note: being yourself is an ongoing adventure, and they are glad to be on this trip together.

Evan is usually the supportive, encouraging voice, and Sam usually comes looking for direction. On 27 August, Sam said he had started a new routine "last Monday," which sits oddly beside his 28 July gym start. Evan suggested a lake hike, and Sam promised a day trip that was never reported. On 11 September, Evan shared a sunset painting, Sam admitted sugar cravings, and they agreed to paint together "next Saturday," a session never mentioned again. Deborah and Jolene are two friends who have chatted in short, friendly sessions across twenty-one conversations from 23 January to 24 August 2023. Their talks moved from grief through community, self-care, time management, fitness, gaming, nature, and a painful setback, and more recently to engineering, retreat plans, games, flowers, calm, and Jolene's professional progress. Both have lost their mothers, both keep meaningful objects, and both value engineering, yoga, nature, gaming, and close relationships. Both sign off warmly and hope to keep supporting each other.

Deborah is the organized, encouraging member of the friendship. Her father died around 25 January 2023, and in February she lost a friend, Karlie. She has coped through family time, photographs, her mother's window seat, her rose and dahlia garden, art, and community work. She is raising money for a cleanup project she started in August. Her marriage matters greatly to her, and on 19 August she recalled playing detective games with her husband. Yoga is central to her life. She teaches it and follows a routine of morning meditation, yoga, teaching, and jogging. In July she organized a community yoga event with help from nearby businesses, and in August she led a meditation session for elderly care-home residents. She made a meditation guide for a yoga retreat she is preparing with some buddies. She tends to give advice quickly and broadly, and often shares yoga photos and small gifts. On 2 March she promised Jolene a yellow coffee mug with a handwritten message, which has never been mentioned as sent.

Deborah's favorite place is a park near her house with a forest trail and a beach. A bench there holds memories of talks with her mother about dreams and life, and the two once watched a sunset together in silence. This is a different bench from Jolene's, which sits by her mother's window. On 21 August Deborah said she had recently sat on a bench where the two of them used to chat, which stirred nostalgia, longing, and gratitude. The session does not name the place, but the description fits the park bench closely. She brought flowers there, recalling that her mother loved flowers and simple things.

Jolene lost her mother in 2022 and treasures the heart-shaped bird pendant her mother gave her in Paris in 2010. Engineering is at the heart of her life. Her work has included an electrical project finished in January, a robotics project for her professor, a water purifier for a rural community that gave her purpose in early February, a planned STEM volunteer program with local schools, a solar-powered vehicle finished in May, and an internship at a well-known engineering firm with no stated end date. She keeps pet snakes, Susie and Seraphim. She has been with her partner for three years. They are not married, and the ring in her photo is a decoration. They enjoy co-op games, often for bets, and on 17 August she bought him a black Xbox console. She reads widely, admires resilience, and wants to learn to surf. She has practiced yoga sporadically for about three years and has relied on yoga and meditation for calm since late February.

In January and February, Jolene shared a photo of the bench by her mother's window, and Deborah replied with a photo of herself hugging her mother in wheelchairs, their last photo together. On 9 February Jolene proposed the STEM program, though she had not yet contacted any schools. On 22 February she said she wanted to try beach yoga, possibly in Bali, and on 25 February she said yoga and meditation had "seriously saved" her. In March, Jolene said exams were piling up, and Deborah offered to help build a study plan, which has not been revisited. On 22 March Deborah introduced the Eisenhower Matrix, which Jolene agreed to try. On 28 March Jolene reported an engineering breakthrough, and the two swapped music recommendations. Deborah's question about those recommendations is still unanswered.

Jolene returned on 6 June after a long gap, sharing a photo of the finished solar vehicle and saying work-life balance had been hard. On 26 June she described determination to overcome obstacles and a big breakthrough, shown in a hand-drawn house photo, whose link to her earlier work was never stated. On 9 July she mentioned "my own journey" without elaborating, said gaming had been hard lately, and shared a lake dock photo for an unplanned visit.

On 1 August Jolene described a major setback the previous week that had wiped out a project she had worked hard on, leaving her frustrated and depressed. Deborah offered encouragement, a gentle breathing flow, and a promised tutorial video, and Jolene agreed to practice and report back. She has not yet done so. On 12 August Jolene said she had been stressed since losing her work files, probably the same setback, and described an aerial surveillance prototype for emergencies and environmental monitoring. On 16 August she said things had been up and down, especially after checking in with her boyfriend, and asked how Deborah manages when everything becomes too much. Deborah answered only in general terms. Jolene also said she had started a bullet journal and was keen to try mindfulness, which Deborah offered to help her start.

On 19 August Deborah asked about Jolene's mindfulness workshops and reading, but Jolene mentioned neither. She described a busy stretch and her engineering studies, and recommended Zelda: Breath of the Wild and Animal Crossing: New Horizons, noting that she and her partner often play Overcooked 2 for bets. Deborah gave scheduling advice, which Jolene said she would turn into a plan. No plans were made.

On 21 August Jolene said they had been given Battlefield 1 for the console. She said she was doing more yoga and meditation to relax and stay focused, named savasana as her favorite rest pose, and said yoga had been her escape from study and work stress for three years. She said she was "finding my zen again." Deborah named yoga, meditation, walks, and mindfulness as her calming habits, shared flower photos and bench memories, and called walks a reboot.

On 24 August, the first conversation in over a week, Deborah said she had attended a yoga retreat near her mom's place the previous week, which she called beautiful and life-changing for getting to know herself. She shared a mossy forest trail photo. Whether this was the retreat she had been preparing is not confirmed. Jolene said she was glad Deborah had reconnected with nature and called this "my own way to relax." Jolene said life had been hectic but she was making strides toward success in her field. She had been studying, attending workshops, and networking, and had recently presented at a virtual conference and received positive feedback that confirmed she was on the right track. The talk's topic and date are not given. She is considering more internships and hopes to share updates soon. Deborah said she was proud, offered help, and urged her to enjoy the journey. Deborah closed with "Always by your side!" No specific plans were made, and no earlier thread was revisited.

Several threads remain open. The yellow mug has not been mentioned as sent, and the study plan has not been revisited. It is unknown whether Jolene adopted the Eisenhower Matrix or a schedule. Beach yoga, possibly in Bali, and a surfing lesson remain ideas. The STEM proposal has not reached any schools. The late-June breakthrough has no stated connection to earlier work. Jolene has not reported on her breathing practice or the tutorial video, and has not said whether she will try mindfulness. The lake dock visit is unplanned. The lost work files and whether the setback project can be rebuilt have not been discussed. The internship has no end date, the June balance problem is unresolved, and "my own journey" is unexplained. The relationship strain from 16 August has no specifics, and the "workshops" and "reading" from 19 August are unexplained. The conference talk lacks details. Deborah's retreat location and its link to her mother's home are unclear. Deborah's cleanup fundraiser and Jolene's aerial surveillance prototype are active projects the other may want to hear more about. Deborah did not say whether she plans to return to the bench soon.

The exchanges have moved from grief toward practical stress help, shared memory, career strain, fitness and nature, vulnerability, renewed creative energy, and most recently light talk about games, flowers, and calm alongside an update on Jolene's achievements. Jolene often asks follow-up questions about Deborah's yoga, fitness, mother, and games, while Deborah offers warmth, practical advice, recommendations, and small gifts. Jolene tends to deflect personal attention, and since 16 August she has steered toward projects, purchases, yoga, and professional progress, avoiding the setback and her studies. Deborah's advice has been broad and quick, and Jolene's replies have usually been appreciative but brief. Deborah more often shares personal memories, while Jolene keeps her feelings lighter. The tone has stayed light and affectionate, and both have consistently hoped to keep supporting each other.

Nate and Joanna had not spoken for a long time before they reconnected in January 2022. Across twelve sessions, from 21 January to 20 May 2022, they have talked about movies, Joanna's screenwriting, Nate's gaming, pets and allergies, baking, Nate's hair, hiking, and books. The tone is friendly and supportive, and each often encourages the other's goals. Conversations usually open with casual greetings, close with warm send-offs, and often include photos.

Nate's main hobbies are gaming and movies. Around 14 January 2022 he won his first video game tournament, in Counter-Strike: Global Offensive, a team shooter. Joanna congratulated him but said she is not really into games. He said he mostly plays for fun, tends to stick with the chiller players, and does not expect to win big. He entered again in March, which he called INTENSE. On 21 April he said his fourth tournament was in May and that he felt good about it. On 2 May he said gaming had been his focus, that he had been practicing, and that he had won a few tournaments. In late April he won a local Street Fighter tournament, a game he plays often with friends. He sees gaming as a creative outlet. He shared a photo of his gaming room, which has a computer and a gaming chair. The May tournament has not yet been reported on.

Nate loves action, sci-fi, and fantasy films, especially their visual effects and world-building, and he likes classics. On 21 April he praised an unnamed fantasy trilogy and recommended a book series full of adventure and magic. Joanna said the series had been on her list forever and promised to tell him what she thinks. On 2 May she said she had watched "The Lord of the Rings" trilogy on his recommendation and found it awesome. Nate replied that it is probably the greatest trilogy of all time.

Joanna favors dramas, romcoms, and emotionally driven films. In the first session she recommended an unnamed romantic drama about memory and relationships, which she first watched around 2019 and considers one of her favorites. She asked whether Nate likes it, and he has never reported back. On 7 February she said she had just watched "Little Women" and called it amazing. She asked Nate to tell her what he thinks once he finishes it, and he has not reported on that either.

Joanna's screenwriting has moved through several stages. On 23 January she said she had finished her first full screenplay, a drama-romance, which she printed around 21 January. By 7 February she had sent it to one film festival. On 25 February she started a second screenplay, a semi-autobiographical road-trip story about a thirty-year-old woman on a journey of self-discovery after a loss, inspired by Joanna's own experiences. Nate said it takes guts and said he was crossing his fingers for her. On 18 March she finished the second script, feeling relieved but anxious about what comes next. On 24 March she said she had an audition on 23 March for a writing gig. It went alright, and she asked Nate to keep his fingers crossed. The outcome has not been reported. On 21 April she said she had joined a writers group whose members really understand her writing, and that she felt as if she finally belonged somewhere. She is working with the group on a script called "Finding Home," about a girl searching for her true home. On 20 May she said she had just finished something and called it a pretty wild journey. She shared a photo of a notepad with a dog drawn on it and confirmed that this is her third screenplay. It is a personal story about loss, identity, and connection, one she had carried for ages before finding the courage to write it. She said it was hard but that she is proud of it, and that she writes best when she is true to herself. Nate observed that she often writes about sadness and loss, and she agreed, saying meaningful stories come from personal experience.

Joanna's acting background came up on 21 April. In her first play she was so nervous that she forgot her lines, which taught her the value of preparation. She said acting was her first passion, though she now shines in writing, and that she might return to acting someday.

Nate has two turtles, which he has owned for three years. He said they keep him calm when he is nervous about important things. He has shared several photos of them and sometimes brings them into the kitchen while he cooks. He is drawn to turtles because they are unique, their slow pace is a nice change from life's rush, and they are low-maintenance. On 20 May he introduced a new family member, a dog named Max, whom he adopted. He shared a photo of Max lying on a couch. Nate described Max as full of energy and said he is filling Nate's life with joy and even keeping the other pets active. He asked Joanna whether she had thought more about getting a pet.

Joanna is allergic to most reptiles, furred animals, and cockroaches, which she learned in March. She said she wished she were not allergic and would get two turtles that day if she could. Nate offered to send pictures so she could still watch them grow, and she said she was already invested in "those little guys." On 20 May she said her allergies mean she does not really want a pet, and admitted she is too lazy to research alternatives. When Nate asked how she finds comfort without one, she said writing and creative projects get her through tough times, and that she is grateful for supportive friends who understand her work and give her feedback.

Food and baking have been a recurring thread. Nate loves coconut milk and also enjoys chocolate and mixed berry flavors. On 7 February he said he had made coconut milk ice cream and a dairy-free chocolate cake with berries. On 25 February he made a chocolate and vanilla swirl ice cream for a friend. Joanna revealed she cannot have dairy and asked for a dairy-free recipe. On 17 April Nate shared one: coconut milk, vanilla extract, sugar, and a pinch of salt, chilled, churned, and frozen until scoopable. Joanna said she is lactose intolerant and promised to report how it turns out. No report has come yet. On 2 May she said she had been testing dairy-free desserts for friends and family, and shared a photo of a dairy-free vanilla cake with strawberry filling and coconut cream frosting, crediting Nate's coconut recommendation. She said baking is her creative outlet. Nate called the cake amazing.

On 24 March Nate asked for advice on pursuing writing himself, which is new for him. Joanna told him to read widely, try different genres, and share his work. On 12 May he said he might start a drama himself.

On 15 April Nate talked about his hair, which he had dyed purple around 8 April. He shared a selfie in glasses and said he was stoked about it, choosing the bold color because it is bright, "like me." Joanna said his boldness inspired her. Nate said he was jealous and suggested they see each other soon. Joanna replied "Totally!"

On 17 April Joanna said she had been reading a lot, had rediscovered books she forgot she owned, and had found an awesome hiking trail in her hometown. She called nature her haven and asked whether Nate knew good hiking spots. He said he was not really into hiking but had heard of a nice trail north of where he lives. Joanna joked she might have to convince him to come along, and he said maybe. On 12 May she said she had gone hiking and found more amazing trails, and joked that she now considers herself an expert. She shared a photo of a waterfall under a dark sky at a spot she named Whispering Falls, which she described as peaceful and serene, saying only the present mattered there. Nate said nature is a break from the craziness, and that when he is out he gets deep in thought about his life or new recipes. Joanna said hiking has opened up a whole new world and that she always feels she could write a whole movie when she is out in cool places. Nate then suggested they go hiking together sometime. Joanna laughed and invited him to join her. Nate replied "Sounds like a plan!" This is the first time he has agreed, though no date or trail has been set.

As of 20 May 2022, Joanna has finished three screenplays. The first, a drama-romance, was submitted to at least one film festival. The second, a semi-autobiographical road-trip story, was finished by 18 March. The third, about loss, identity, and connection, was finished by 20 May. She also joined a writers group in April and is working with it on "Finding Home." Her audition result has not been reported. She is allergic to most reptiles, furred animals, and cockroaches, and she is lactose intolerant. She has become an active hiker and credits hiking with inspiring her writing. Nate has two turtles he has owned for three years and recently adopted a dog named Max. He plays in gaming tournaments, won a local Street Fighter tournament in late April, and planned to enter another in May. He became interested in writing in March, dyed his hair purple in April, and has said he might try writing a drama. Both have recommended major fantasy works to each other.

Several requests remain unresolved. Joanna asked what Nate thinks of the romantic drama she recommended in January, and he has never reported back. She asked what he thinks of "Little Women," and he has not yet reported. Nate has promised to keep Joanna posted on the tournament, to send turtle photos, and to offer movie picks. Joanna has promised to update him on her audition, on how the ice cream turns out, on her screenwriting, and on the book series he recommended. She has also asked to hear about his progress as a writer. A hiking trip is tentatively agreed but not yet scheduled. Max also raises an open question about whether Joanna will ever get a pet, which she currently says she does not want because of her allergies.

Nate and Joanna had not spoken for a long time before they reconnected in January 2022. Across thirteen sessions, from 21 January to 25 May 2022, they have talked about movies, Joanna's screenwriting, Nate's gaming, pets and allergies, baking, Nate's hair, and hiking. The tone is friendly and supportive, and each often encourages the other's goals. Conversations usually open with casual greetings, close with warm send-offs, and often include photos. Nate is playful and upbeat, while Joanna is warm and reflective.

Nate's main hobbies are gaming and movies. Around 14 January 2022 he won his first video game tournament, in Counter-Strike: Global Offensive. Joanna congratulated him but said she is not really into games. He said he mostly plays for fun and does not expect to win big. He entered again in March, which he called INTENSE. On 21 April he said his fourth tournament was in May. On 2 May he said he had been practicing and had won a few tournaments. In late April he won a local Street Fighter tournament. He sees gaming as a creative outlet and shared a photo of his gaming room. The May tournament has not yet been reported on.

Nate loves action, sci-fi, and fantasy films, especially their visual effects and world-building, and he likes classics. On 21 April he praised an unnamed fantasy trilogy and recommended a book series full of adventure and magic. Joanna said the series had been on her list forever. On 2 May she said she had watched "The Lord of the Rings" trilogy on his recommendation and found it awesome. Nate replied that it is probably the greatest trilogy of all time. Both have recommended major fantasy works to each other.

Joanna favors dramas, romcoms, and emotionally driven films. In the first session she recommended an unnamed romantic drama about memory and relationships, one of her favorites. She asked whether Nate likes it, and he has never reported back. On 7 February she said she had just watched "Little Women" and called it amazing. She asked Nate to tell her what he thinks once he finishes it, and he has not reported on that either.

Joanna's screenwriting has moved through several stages. On 23 January she said she had finished her first full screenplay, a drama-romance. By 7 February she had sent it to one film festival. On 25 February she started a second screenplay, a semi-autobiographical road-trip story about a thirty-year-old woman on a journey of self-discovery after a loss. Nate said it takes guts. On 18 March she finished it, feeling relieved but anxious. On 24 March she said she had an audition on 23 March for a writing gig. It went alright, and she asked Nate to keep his fingers crossed. The outcome has not been reported. On 21 April she said she had joined a writers group whose members really understand her writing, and that she finally felt she belonged somewhere. She is working with the group on a script called "Finding Home," about a girl searching for her true home.

On 20 May Joanna said she had just finished something and called it a pretty wild journey. She confirmed that it is her third screenplay, a personal story about loss, identity, and connection that she had carried for ages before finding the courage to write it. She said it was hard but that she is proud of it, and that she writes best when she is true to herself. Nate observed that she often writes about sadness and loss, and she agreed that meaningful stories come from personal experience. On 25 May she said that the joyful moments made the hard journey of finishing it worthwhile. She said she could not wait to show it to Nate and values his opinion. Nate said he is there to support her, and she promised to keep him updated.

Joanna's acting background came up on 21 April. She said acting was her first passion, though she now shines in writing, and that she might return to acting someday.

Nate has two turtles, which he has owned for three years. He said they keep him calm when he is nervous, and he is drawn to them because they are unique, slow-paced, and low-maintenance. On 20 May he introduced a new family member, a dog named Max, whom he adopted. He described Max as full of energy and filling his life with joy. He asked Joanna whether she had thought more about getting a pet. On 25 May Nate said he had met a friendly couple with a dog on a walk, and the two families decided to arrange doggy playdates. Max really likes the other dog, and Nate said seeing his dog so happy is a dream come true.

Joanna is allergic to most reptiles, furred animals, and cockroaches, which she learned in March. She said she wished she were not allergic and would get two turtles that day if she could. Nate offered to send pictures so she could still watch them grow. On 20 May she said her allergies mean she does not really want a pet, and admitted she is too lazy to research alternatives. She said writing and creative projects get her through tough times, and that she is grateful for supportive friends who give her feedback. On 25 May Nate sent a photo of a stuffed animal on a bed, calling it a "pup" for her and a reminder of good vibes. Joanna said she would cherish it. Nate said it is like having joy in your pocket.

Food and baking have been a recurring thread. Nate loves coconut milk and also enjoys chocolate and mixed berry flavors. On 7 February he said he had made coconut milk ice cream and a dairy-free chocolate cake with berries. Joanna revealed she cannot have dairy and asked for a dairy-free recipe. On 17 April Nate shared one: coconut milk, vanilla extract, sugar, and a pinch of salt, churned and frozen. Joanna said she is lactose intolerant and promised to report how it turns out. No report has come yet. On 2 May she shared a photo of a dairy-free vanilla cake with strawberry filling, crediting Nate's coconut recommendation, and said baking is her creative outlet. Nate called the cake amazing.

On 24 March Nate asked for advice on pursuing writing himself, which is new for him. Joanna told him to read widely and share his work. On 12 May he said he might start a drama himself. His progress has not been reported since.

On 15 April Nate shared a selfie showing his hair, which he had dyed purple around 8 April. He said he chose the bold color because it is bright, "like me." Joanna said his boldness inspired her. Nate suggested they see each other soon, and Joanna replied "Totally!"

On 17 April Joanna said she had been reading a lot and had found an awesome hiking trail in her hometown. She called nature her haven and asked whether Nate knew good hiking spots. He said he was not really into hiking but had heard of a nice trail north of where he lives. On 12 May she said she had gone hiking again and shared a photo of a waterfall she named Whispering Falls, which she described as peaceful. Nate said nature is a break from the craziness. Joanna said hiking has opened up a whole new world for her writing. Nate then suggested they go hiking together sometime, and Joanna invited him to join her. Nate replied "Sounds like a plan!" This is the first time he has agreed, though no date or trail has been set.

As of 25 May 2022, Joanna has finished three screenplays. The first, a drama-romance, was submitted to at least one film festival. The second, a semi-autobiographical road-trip story, was finished by 18 March. The third, about loss, identity, and connection, was finished by 20 May, and she wants Nate to read it. She joined a writers group in April and is working on "Finding Home." Her audition result has not been reported. She is allergic to most reptiles, furred animals, and cockroaches, and she is lactose intolerant. She has become an active hiker. Nate has two turtles, recently adopted a dog named Max, and has arranged doggy playdates with a neighboring family. He plays in gaming tournaments, won a local Street Fighter tournament in late April, and planned to enter another in May. He became interested in writing in March, dyed his hair purple in April, and has said he might try writing a drama.

Several requests remain unresolved. Joanna asked what Nate thinks of the romantic drama she recommended in January, and he has never reported back. She asked what he thinks of "Little Women," and he has not yet reported. Nate has promised to keep Joanna posted on the tournament, to send turtle photos, and to offer movie picks. Joanna has promised to update him on her audition, on how the ice cream turns out, on her screenwriting, and on the book series he recommended. She has also asked to hear about his progress as a writer. A hiking trip is tentatively agreed but not yet scheduled. The doggy playdates have no date yet. Max raises an open question about whether Joanna will ever get a pet, which she currently says she does not want because of her allergies.

Andrew admitted to being a little jealous. He has no pets but loves eagles, which he finds strong and graceful, and he hikes Fox Hollow on weekends. Audrey said she would try Fox Hollow and report back, but no visit has been reported since.

He was searching for both an apartment and a dog, had found neither, and missed hiking trails with a dog.

Andrew said he would look into classes.

Deborah and Jolene are two friends who have chatted in short, friendly sessions across twenty-two conversations from 23 January to 26 August 2023. Their talks have moved from grief through self-care, time management, fitness, gaming, nature, and a painful setback, and more recently to engineering, retreat plans, games, flowers, calm, pets, and shared values. Both have lost their mothers, both keep meaningful objects, and both value engineering, yoga, nature, gaming, and close relationships. Both sign off warmly and hope to keep supporting each other.

Deborah is the organized, encouraging member of the friendship. Her father died around 25 January 2023, and in February she lost a friend, Karlie. She has coped through family time, photographs, her mother's window seat, her rose and dahlia garden, art, and community work, and she is raising money for a cleanup project she started in August. Her marriage matters greatly to her. Yoga is central to her life. She teaches it and follows a routine of morning meditation, yoga, teaching, and jogging. She organized a community yoga event in July, led a meditation session for care-home residents in August, and made a meditation guide for a yoga retreat she is preparing with some buddies. She tends to give advice quickly and broadly, and often shares yoga photos and small gifts. On 2 March she promised Jolene a yellow coffee mug with a handwritten message, which has never been mentioned as sent. Her cats are Luna, a five-year-old she adopted from a shelter, and Max, an eight-year-old who was her mother's cat and whom she took in when her mother died.

Deborah's favorite place is a park near her house with a forest trail and a beach. A bench there holds memories of talks with her mother about dreams and life, and the two once watched a sunset together in silence. This is a different bench from Jolene's, which sits by her mother's window. On 21 August Deborah said she had recently sat on a bench where the two of them used to chat, stirring nostalgia and gratitude. The session does not name the place, but the description fits the park bench closely, and she brought flowers there, recalling that her mother loved simple things.

Jolene lost her mother in 2022 and treasures the heart-shaped bird pendant her mother gave her in Paris in 2010. Engineering is at the heart of her life. Her work has included an electrical project finished in January, a robotics project for her professor, a water purifier for a rural community that gave her purpose in early February, a planned STEM volunteer program with local schools, a solar-powered vehicle finished in May, and an internship at a well-known engineering firm with no stated end date. She keeps pet snakes, Susie and Seraphim. She has been with her partner for three years. They are not married, and the ring in her photo is a decoration. They enjoy co-op games for bets, and on 17 August she bought him a black Xbox console. She reads widely, admires resilience, and wants to learn to surf. She has practiced yoga sporadically for about three years and has relied on yoga and meditation for calm since late February.

In January and February, Jolene shared a photo of the bench by her mother's window, and Deborah replied with a photo of herself hugging her mother in wheelchairs, their last photo together. On 9 February Jolene proposed the STEM program, though she had not contacted any schools. On 22 February she said she wanted to try beach yoga, possibly in Bali, and on 25 February she said yoga and meditation had "seriously saved" her. In March Jolene said exams were piling up, and Deborah offered to help build a study plan, which has not been revisited. On 22 March Deborah introduced the Eisenhower Matrix, which Jolene agreed to try. On 28 March Jolene reported an engineering breakthrough, and the two swapped music recommendations. Deborah's question about those is still unanswered.

Jolene returned on 6 June after a long gap, sharing a photo of the finished solar vehicle and saying work-life balance had been hard. On 26 June she described determination and a big breakthrough, shown in a hand-drawn house photo, whose link to her earlier work was never stated. On 9 July she mentioned "my own journey" without elaborating, said gaming had been hard lately, and shared a lake dock photo for an unplanned visit.

On 1 August Jolene described a major setback the previous week that wiped out a project she had worked hard on, leaving her frustrated and depressed. Deborah offered encouragement, a gentle breathing flow, and a promised tutorial video, and Jolene agreed to practice and report back, which she has not yet done. On 12 August Jolene said she had been stressed since losing her work files, probably the same setback, and described an aerial surveillance prototype for emergencies and environmental monitoring. On 16 August she said things had been up and down, especially after checking in with her boyfriend, and asked how Deborah manages when everything becomes too much. Deborah answered only in general terms. Jolene also said she had started a bullet journal and was keen to try mindfulness, which Deborah offered to help her start.

On 19 August Deborah asked about Jolene's mindfulness workshops and reading, but Jolene mentioned neither. She described a busy stretch and her engineering studies, recommended Zelda: Breath of the Wild and Animal Crossing: New Horizons, and noted that she and her partner often play Overcooked 2 for bets. Deborah gave scheduling advice, which Jolene said she would turn into a plan, but no plans were made. On 21 August Jolene said they had been given Battlefield 1 for the console, and that she was doing more yoga and meditation, naming savasana as her favorite rest pose and saying she was "finding my zen again." Deborah named yoga, meditation, walks, and mindfulness as her calming habits and shared flower photos and bench memories.

On 24 August, the first conversation in over a week, Deborah said she had attended a yoga retreat near her mom's place the previous week, which she called beautiful and life-changing, and shared a mossy forest trail photo. Whether this was the retreat she had been preparing is not confirmed. Jolene said she was glad Deborah had reconnected with nature, and that life had been hectic but she was making strides in her field. She had studied, attended workshops, networked, and recently presented at a virtual conference with positive feedback. The talk's topic and date are not given. She is considering more internships and hopes to share updates soon. Deborah said she was proud, offered help, and closed with "Always by your side!"

In the most recent session, number 22 on 26 August, Deborah said she had been thinking about her mother's influence and how important it is to remember those we love. Jolene described a conversation with her partner the previous Friday about how their loved ones had shaped them. Jolene said her mother always told her never to give up and stressed helping others, while her partner's father taught determination. She is pursuing engineering and her partner creative work, and the two are working out how to build these values into their projects. Jolene named two directions she is keen on: renewable energy such as solar, and clean water for people with limited access. She also wants to work on sustainability and join social-cause organizations, though she said she still has much to figure out. Deborah called the plans inspiring and said small steps build strength. She shared a photo of a woman doing yoga on a beach. When Jolene asked for tips on staying relaxed while studying, Deborah suggested breaks, stretching, walks, sleep, and self-care. Jolene said yoga and meditation help her recharge, and that she and her partner plan to attend a meditation retreat together. She shared a photo of herself in a pink shirt doing a yoga pose and said one snake is a calming companion. Deborah then shared photos of Luna and Max and explained how she came to have both cats, saying she loves cats because they need homes, love, and care. Jolene said she was proud of Deborah for taking in these pets. No plans were made.

Several threads remain open. The yellow mug has not been mentioned as sent, and the study plan has not been revisited. It is unknown whether Jolene adopted the Eisenhower Matrix or a schedule. Beach yoga, possibly in Bali, a surfing lesson, and the shared meditation retreat remain ideas without dates, and the STEM proposal has not reached any schools. The renewable energy and clean water interests have no concrete steps. The late-June breakthrough has no stated connection to earlier work. Jolene has not reported on her breathing practice or the tutorial video, and has not said whether she will try mindfulness. The lost work files and whether the setback project can be rebuilt have not been discussed. The internship has no end date, the June balance problem is unresolved, and "my own journey" is unexplained. The relationship strain from 16 August has no specifics, and the "workshops" and "reading" from 19 August are unexplained. The conference talk lacks details. Deborah's retreat location and its link to her mother's home are unclear. Deborah's cleanup fundraiser and Jolene's aerial surveillance prototype are active projects the other may want to hear more about. Deborah has not said whether she plans to return to the bench soon.

The exchanges have moved from grief toward practical stress help, shared memory, career strain, fitness and nature, vulnerability, light talk about games, flowers, and calm, and most recently reflections on loved ones, values, and pets. Jolene tends to deflect personal attention, and since 16 August she has steered toward projects, purchases, yoga, professional progress, and shared values, avoiding the setback and her studies. Deborah's advice has been broad and quick, and Jolene's replies have usually been appreciative but brief. Deborah more often shares personal memories, especially of her mother, while Jolene keeps her feelings lighter, though the 26 August session was her most openly reflective talk so far. The tone has stayed light and affectionate, and both have consistently hoped to keep supporting each other.

Evan revealed he had lost his job "last month" in a company downsizing, which had not come up in October. They agreed to plan a beach trip "next month," with no date set.

Evan then shared a photo of a woman before a painting, describing a finished figurative work exhibited through an unnamed close friend. Sam praised them and shared a photo of a woman holding flowers, inspired by an exhibit he had seen a few days earlier. He said he sketches occasionally, and Evan offered to help him get started, which Sam has not yet taken up.

On 31 December Sam said he was getting into a healthier lifestyle and had taken friends on an epic hiking trip "last Friday," which would be 22 December. He shared a photo of a man on a rock over a valley. This is the first hike he has described since the August promise. Evan said he had taken the Prius on a long mountain drive "last weekend" and had a minor scrape on the way back. He also said the accident had dampened telling his work friends about his marriage and that those friends had been a great support, which sits uneasily with his November job loss. Evan then shared photos of a woman at a table with plates, which he called new healthy snacks, cookies he would send recipes for, and coconut energy balls with oats. On 27 March 2023, Andrew said he had recently started a new job as a Financial Analyst. Audrey said she had three dogs, Pepper, Precious and Panda, for about three years. Andrew had no pets but loves animals, especially eagles, and recommended the Fox Hollow trail for weekend hikes.

On 16 April 2023, Andrew said he and a companion had tried a new café in the city and enjoyed croissants, muffins and tarts. He said city living made it hard to get the connection and companionship he misses. Audrey had baked her favorite treats the week before and proposed a pastry party.

On 3 May 2023, Audrey said she had recently gone on a hike and seen a hummingbird. Andrew said he had found a new open space to hike nearby, and that he tries to escape the city at least once a weekend because nature is therapeutic for him. Audrey said her dogs love hikes and play fetch with a ball or frisbee, and that the park where they usually walk is right by a spot for doggie playdates. Andrew said he would check it out.

On 6 May 2023 (Session 5), Andrew said he had been searching for a dog to adopt, browsing websites, visiting shelters and asking friends for leads, which he found both fun and frustrating. He lives in an apartment, so he thinks a smaller dog would suit him best, though an active dog that loves to play and run would also work. He is looking for a pet-friendly home near a park or woods and is contacting landlords and checking neighborhoods. Audrey said she is lucky to have a park near her home for her dog's walks. She said her family took a road trip to a national park the previous Friday, and that she takes her dogs on road trips about once every couple of months. Andrew said he would like to take a road trip with his dog someday and added it to his bucket list. He is still searching for the right dog, and Audrey asked him to send a photo once he gets one.

Audrey and Andrew caught up on 27 March 2023 after a time apart. Andrew had just started work as a Financial Analyst. Audrey had three dogs, Pepper, Precious, and Panda, and she explored parks and trails with them. She said she could not live without them, and Andrew admitted to being a little jealous. He has no pets but loves eagles, and he hikes Fox Hollow on weekends. Audrey said she would try Fox Hollow and report back, but no visit has been reported since.

On 2 April, Audrey said her family had adopted a small white puppy named Pixie, who now gets along well with the other dogs. Andrew was considering getting a dog but found dog-friendly places hard to find in the city, so Audrey recommended websites with dog-friendly filters. On 16 April, Andrew said he felt sad away from nature, which he called a home for his soul. Audrey said walking her dogs helps her find her center. She proposed a pastry party and shared a photo of blueberry muffins she had made, and Andrew eagerly accepted. The party has not been mentioned again.

On 3 May, Audrey said she had recently hiked and watched a hummingbird. Andrew had found a new open space to hike nearby. Audrey said her dogs attend playdates at a dog park beside their usual park. Andrew asked for tips on keeping dogs safe outdoors and said he would check out the dog park and report back. On 6 May, he said he was searching for a dog by browsing websites, visiting shelters, and contacting landlords for a pet-friendly place near a park or woods. He advised that a smaller dog would suit an apartment best. Audrey's family takes road trips to national parks about once every couple of months, and Andrew added a road trip with a furry companion to his bucket list. Audrey asked to see a photo of his dog soon, and he said he had another shelter to check.

On 11 May, Andrew said he had enjoyed a great hike with friends and his girlfriend at the new open space. Audrey said she now had four dogs, which take up most of her free time. She had signed up for a June workshop on bonding with pets, which teaches positive reinforcement. She stressed that punishment is never the proper way to train pets. Andrew said he would look into classes.

On 2 June, in Session 7, Audrey said seeing her dogs run unleashed at the park filled her with joy, and she described a stunning sunset at a national park peak the week before. Andrew was still searching for a furry friend and a pet-friendly spot in the city. He had checked some places without luck and felt discouraged but determined. Audrey offered to help if he emailed his criteria, and they agreed to keep searching.

On 13 June, in Session 8, Andrew said that around 11 June he and his friends had taken a rock climbing class, and he had made it to the top. Later in that session, she found a small park with a trail surrounded by trees, a good spot for her dogs, and invited Andrew along. He happily agreed. No date or outcome for the trail walk is recorded. Andrew said he turns to nature whenever he needs a reset, but he still had not mentioned a dog of his own.

On 26 June, in Session 9, Audrey announced that she had moved into a new home with a bigger backyard for her dogs. She had set up a doggy play area there with agility equipment and toys. Andrew shared a photo of a doggy daycare near him with a large indoor play space, and Audrey said she would look into it and might take her dogs there soon. Andrew offered to help find more dog-friendly places. Both agreed that friends who understand their love for pets are special, and Audrey said she did not understand people who hurt animals. Andrew said that around 23 June he had hiked with friends in pleasant weather, though he had not yet gone through the photos. He said he had missed his connection with nature. Audrey said she was mostly unpacking boxes, and she shared photos of a lake she had visited with friends a few years earlier. The session ended with both agreeing to appreciate the small things in life.

Taken together, Andrew values nature, animals, and the peace he finds outdoors, and he has been escaping the city more regularly. He hiked a new open space by early May, took up rock climbing by June, and went on a hike with friends around 23 June. On 6 May and again on 2 June he was still searching for a dog and a pet-friendly home, and by 26 June he had not reported settling on either. It is unknown whether he sent Audrey his criteria. Audrey's household grew from three named dogs to four with Pixie, and her dogs shape her walks, playdates, road trips, and hikes. In late June she moved into a new home with a larger backyard. He has no dog or settled home so far, and both continue to share a strong love of nature and animals.

Sam and Evan are friends who have now had twenty-three conversations, the latest on 6 January 2024 at 1:32 pm. Their exchanges are friendly and enthusiastic. Evan usually plays the supportive, encouraging role, and Sam usually comes looking for direction. Evan increasingly shares his life through photos and announcements, and his details often do not line up with each other or with earlier sessions.

In May 2023, Evan described a family hiking trip to the Rockies. Sam loves hiking and was considering painting, while Evan's main hobby is watercolor. On 24 May a check-up put Sam outside a healthy weight range, and Evan suggested a fitness routine and smarter eating. On 6 June Sam admitted he still drank soda and ate candy. On 27 July friends mocking his weight pushed him to change, and he said he would start the gym on 28 July. In August Evan described a "rad vacay" in Canada with a new significant other and his son's soccer ankle injury. Sam called a doctor's appointment a wake-up call and said he was taking a cooking class.

On 19 August Sam reported a better diet, and Evan said he had started a painting class, which conflicts with his watercolor hobby. On 27 August Sam said he had started a new routine "last Monday," which sits oddly beside the 28 July gym start, and he promised a lake day trip that was never reported. On 11 September the two agreed to paint together "next Saturday," a session never mentioned again. On 6 October Sam said he was eating healthier. Evan reported a basketball knee setback and said he had missed family adventures "last year," which clashes with the May trips. On 8 October Sam said a check-up showed his weight was a serious health risk, and Evan advised finding a trainer. On 14 October Sam described a rough week of snacks and guilt and mentioned work stress for the first time. On 17 October he said he had been "missing our chats" after only three days, and he described an ER visit for gastritis as a wake-up call. Evan offered a workout buddy and proposed a hike, which Sam accepted. On 25 October Sam said his family was pushing him hard, the first mention of family pressure.

On 9 November Sam said he had become a Weight Watchers coach in his group, the first mention of any coaching role. Evan revealed he had lost his job "last month" in a company downsizing, which had not come up in October. They agreed to plan a beach trip "next month," with no date set. On 21 November Sam opened with "long time no chat" and described discomfort that limits his movement, his first mention of physical limits. Evan said a recent hospital visit after a suspicious check-up had been a misunderstanding, and he said he stayed in shape by "taking my car out for a spin," which does not fit as a fitness method. On 5 December Evan said his new Prius, which he had just bought, had broken down. Sam said he had attended a Weight Watchers meeting "yesterday," meaning 4 December, and shared a photo of fruit and yogurt bowls. Evan said he had been thinking about trying yoga, and Sam asked how it went. On 9 December Evan announced that his partner is pregnant, referring both to a toddler and to a first child, and said his family is planning a big reunion next summer.

On 17 December Evan said his son had fallen off his bike, a second injury in a few months that he did not connect to the earlier one. Sam said he was doing okay but had hit some bumps. He did not mention the Weight Watchers meeting, the yoga, or the coaching role, and he said his weight was hurting his confidence and that he kept lacking motivation, the first time he described his motivation as failing. Evan then shared a photo of a woman before a painting, describing a finished figurative work exhibited through an unnamed close friend. On 26 December Evan said he had married the previous week, sharing a photo of a bride and groom and identifying the bride as the woman from Canada, whom he had loved at first sight. Sam mentioned morning runs, his first mention of running. Evan then shared two paintings as his own work, neither matching his earlier accounts. Sam praised them and shared a photo of a woman holding flowers, inspired by an exhibit he had seen. He said he sketches occasionally, and Evan offered to help him get started, which Sam has not yet taken up.

On 31 December Sam said he was getting into a healthier lifestyle and had taken friends on an epic hiking trip "last Friday," which would be 22 December. He shared a photo of a man on a rock over a valley, the first hike he has described since the August promise. Evan said he had taken the Prius on a long mountain drive "last weekend" and had a minor scrape on the way back. He also said his work friends had been a great support, which sits uneasily with his November job loss. Evan then shared photos of what he called new healthy snacks, including coconut energy balls with oats, and promised recipes. Near the end, Sam reported another self-checkout struggle and offered to keep Evan company by phone at the store.

In the 6 January session, Evan said he and his partner had told their extended family about their marriage "yesterday," meaning 5 January, and shared a photo of a couple on a rocky beach. The two traded many messages about family support, and Sam said his family has been his rock. Evan shared a photo of a family get-together with homemade lasagna and said he had started a diet limiting himself to two ginger snaps a day. Sam shared his own light dinner and a photo of a pie with raspberries and limes, saying it came from his cousin's wedding. Evan announced that he and his partner leave for a honeymoon in Canada next month, which would be February, with plans to ski, try local food, and see the snowy landscapes. Sam shared a photo of caramel-covered fries, and Evan said he planned to try poutine there and would report back.

Evan's recent sessions are full of announcements that do not fit together: a pregnancy on 9 December, a late-December wedding, a marriage told to family only on 5 January, and an August Canada trip with a new partner, all set against a November job loss and a claimed "car out for a spin" fitness routine. The February honeymoon sits uneasily with the late-December wedding, and the ginger-snap diet conflicts with the healthy snacks he promoted on 31 December. Several of his photos do not show the foods he names. Sam's photos match his stated circumstances more closely, though his pie from a cousin's wedding and his "missing our chats" remark do not fit the timeline cleanly.

Sam's health journey has moved from curiosity about hobbies to a committed focus. He cut back on soda and candy, planned a gym routine, took a cooking class, and reported eating healthier. He treated his doctor's warning and gastritis as turning points, described family pressure in October, reported coaching in November, and described physical limits by 21 November. By 17 December his motivation and confidence were suffering. By 31 December he reported an epic group hike and a steadier focus on healthy snacks, without returning to his coaching or Weight Watchers details. His effort is sincere, but it has come with little measurable detail.

Several threads remain open. Whether Sam has started painting is unconfirmed, and Evan's offer to help him start has not been taken up. The August lake day trip was never reported, and the proposed hike with Evan has no date. The kayaking trip with "my mate" is unexplained. Sam's trainer search has not been mentioned since 8 October, and the family pressure from 25 October has not been explored. The gastritis follow-up and the discomfort from 21 November are unresolved. Sam's coaching role has unknown start and group details, and the December Weight Watchers meeting has not been reconciled with it. Evan's job search is ongoing, the beach trip is undated, the Prius repair is unresolved, and his yoga plans are unreported. The son's bike accident and recovery are still open. The pregnancy, the wedding, the family announcement, and the summer reunion remain unreconciled, with no reunion date set. Evan's promised recipes have not arrived, and Sam's question about how the yoga went has not been answered. Sam's self-checkout troubles remain unresolved. The February Canada honeymoon, the poutine report, and Evan's promised trip updates are all pending.
