Nate and Joanna lost touch for a long time before reconnecting in January 2022. Across twenty-seven sessions, from 21 January to 7 November 2022, they have talked about movies, Joanna's writing, Nate's gaming, pets, baking, hiking, and books. The tone is friendly and supportive, and each often encourages the other's goals. Nate is playful and upbeat, while Joanna is warm and reflective. Session 18 took place on 14 August, followed by a long gap until session 21 on 14 September. Sessions 22 through 27 fell on 6 October, 9 October (a Sunday), 21 October, 25 October, 4 November, and 7 November (a Monday), with a ten-day gap before session 26.

Gaming is Nate's main hobby, which he sees as a creative outlet and a way to escape life's struggles. He won his first tournament around 14 January, in Counter-Strike: Global Offensive, and Joanna said she is not really into games. He then won a local Street Fighter tournament in late April, a regional tournament reported on 3 June, an online tournament on 8 July, and an international tournament on 21 August, his biggest win so far. On 5 June he agreed to help tournament acquaintances with tips. Before 24 June he held a gaming party for seven guests, and six wanted a repeat in July, though none is confirmed. In session 22 he shared a trophy photo. In session 23 he attended a game convention on 7 October and planned a gaming session with Joanna; they have since played Catan. He suggested she might enjoy a writing convention, and she said she would look into it. In session 24 he said he feels stressed about tough competitors. In session 26 he said he had been helping friends reset their high scores at the international tournament. In session 27 he reported winning a big Valorant tournament, reaching the final the Saturday before the session, and said tournaments bring out strong emotions in him. He also showed his upgraded home setup, which he uses for practice, competition, and games with friends. He is now playing "Xenoblade Chronicles," a Japanese fantasy RPG his friends recommended.

Nate loves action, sci-fi, and fantasy films, especially their visual effects and world-building, and he likes classics. On 21 April he recommended a fantasy book series, and on 2 May Joanna said she had watched "The Lord of the Rings" trilogy on his recommendation and found it awesome. Joanna favors dramas, romcoms, and emotionally driven films. In January she asked his opinion of an unnamed romantic drama, and on 7 February she asked about "Little Women," which Nate said in session 22 he had loved. On 5 June Joanna said Spider-Man is her favorite, and Nate's top pick is Iron Man. On 22 August Nate recommended an unnamed series of his own, and he agreed to share his thoughts on the fantasy series she recommended. Neither has been followed up. In session 23 Nate said "Inception" blew his mind and that he has been playing "Cyberpunk 2077" nonstop. Joanna said she had recently watched an unnamed classic movie, rated it 9 or 10 out of 10, and shared a photo of a framed movie poster. In session 27 Nate said he likes the movies she recommends much more than random picks. He has promised movie picks.

Joanna's writing has become central to her life. She finished her first full screenplay, a drama-romance, on 23 January and sent it to a film festival by 7 February. On 18 March she finished a semi-autobiographical road-trip story. On 24 March she had an audition for a writing gig; the result has never been reported. On 21 April she joined a writers group where she finally felt she belonged, and they are working on a script called "Finding Home." On 20 May she finished a third screenplay about loss, identity, and connection, which she wants Nate to read. A major company rejected one screenplay on 3 June, and on 5 June she reported that bits of an unnamed screenplay appeared on the big screen on 4 June. On 24 June she submitted another screenplay to a film contest. On 10 July, on a road trip in Woodhaven, a small Midwestern town, she found a 1900s book of stories and sketches and started a book. Her writers group gave it great feedback on 22 August. On 14 September a laptop crash erased a week of her work, so she now keeps an external drive for backups. In session 24 she mentioned another rejection from a production company, and when Nate asked whether it was the contest entry, she replied only "Yeah.." In session 25 she said another script she contributed to was shown on the big screen "last Sunday," probably 23 October, which she called the third time her work has appeared on screen. She declined to describe one character from her drawing book, telling Nate to watch the movie. In session 26 she said she had just set up meetings with movie producers, which she found validating. In session 27 she said she finished the producer presentation the previous Friday, probably 4 November, and that it was tough but looking good. She is now writing a fourth script, a love story with many challenges that came from a dream. She also submitted several more scripts recently and expects replies soon, assuming some will be rejected. Nate said at least one will likely reach the screen as her third published movie, and Joanna said she will not give up. She shared a photo of a handwritten letter from her brother, which she is using at the start of her next script's introduction. She has started writing down favorite memories, and Nate promised to write down his own.

Nate has two turtles he has owned for three years, which keep him calm when he is nervous. In session 25 he shared a photo of them on a log in a pond, said they eat vegetables, fruits, and insects, and said they get excited about strawberries. One is more adventurous and the other more reserved. In session 27 he shared a photo of a turtle resting on rocks and gravel and said watching them is calming and fascinating. Joanna asked to be kept posted on them. He also adopted a dog named Max, introduced on 20 May, and on 25 May arranged doggy playdates with a neighboring family, though no dates are recorded. Joanna is allergic to most reptiles, furred animals, and cockroaches, so she does not really want a pet. On 25 May Nate sent a photo of a stuffed "pup," and in session 24 Joanna said she still has it, named Tilly after a real dog from her childhood in Michigan. Her photo that session showed a cat rather than a stuffed dog, a small inconsistency worth noting.

Food and baking recur throughout. Nate loves coconut milk and enjoys chocolate and mixed berry flavors. Joanna is lactose intolerant. On 17 April Nate shared a dairy-free ice cream recipe, and Joanna promised to report back, but no clear report has come. On 2 May she shared a dairy-free vanilla cake, crediting his coconut recommendation. In session 21 Nate said he teaches vegan ice cream recipes on his own cooking show, and his favorite is coconut milk ice cream; Joanna said she would try it and watch the show. Her favorite treat is a chocolate raspberry tart with an almond flour crust, and in session 22 she said her newest dairy-free recipe was a family hit. In session 26 Nate said he had just made lactose-free coconut milk ice cream and invited Joanna over. She accepted for 5 November and said she would bring recipes. Nate said he has long wanted to try her chocolate and raspberry cake. Session 27 did not mention whether that visit took place.

Friendship and shared plans have grown warmer over time. On 15 April Nate shared a selfie with purple hair and suggested seeing each other soon, and Joanna replied "Totally!" On 12 May she shared a photo of a waterfall, Whispering Falls, and Nate suggested hiking together; he replied "Sounds like a plan!" No date or trail has been set. In session 22 Nate made her a whiteboard drawing meant as a reminder to look back on when she needs encouragement. In session 23 Joanna said a movie on a comfy couch with a good blanket gives her deep peace. The 5 November visit is the first concrete in-person meeting they have arranged.

As of 7 November 2022, Joanna has written at least three screenplays, is writing a fourth, and has finished her book. One script went to a film festival, one to a contest, and one she wants Nate to read. Another reached the big screen on 23 October, and she is keeping its title private. Her audition result is still unreported. Nate has adopted Max, kept his turtles, won major tournaments including a recent Valorant final, and teaches dairy-free desserts on his cooking show. Open requests include Nate's thoughts on the romantic drama and the fantasy series, his movie picks, and his tournament updates. Joanna has promised updates on her audition, the dairy-free ice cream, her screenwriting, her book, and her family's reaction to the ice cream. She plans to try Nate's coconut milk ice cream and watch his show. Nate asked to hear how her bookmark gift lands. Both pledged to write down favorite memories. The gaming session, the hiking trip, and the doggy playdates have no set dates. The screenplays shown on 4 June and 23 October, the contest screenplay, the producer meeting outcomes, and the classic movie from session 23 remain unidentified. The 5 November visit was the next scheduled event, but session 27 does not confirm it happened.

On 8 December Tim said he had returned from a Harry Potter party in his Gryffindor scarf. John said his team beat a top team after a tough fight and called the camaraderie the season's best part. On 11 December John reported a career-high in assists against a rival the previous Friday, around 8 December, and recalled a buzzer-beater win after his team was down 10 in the fourth, with no date given. He said he practiced outside for hours as a kid to deal with doubts. Both ended that session by encouraging each other's dreams.

Audrey and Andrew are friends who keep in touch in sporadic bursts, bonded by a love of nature and animals. Their conversations center on Audrey's dogs, Andrew's search for a dog, and their outdoor adventures. Their most recent exchange was Session 21 on 4 October 2023.

On 27 March 2023, Andrew had just started work as a Financial Analyst after a period apart. He had no pets, loved eagles, and hiked Fox Hollow on weekends. Audrey had three dogs, Pepper, Precious, and Panda, and said she could not live without them, which made Andrew a little jealous. Her family adopted a small white puppy, Pixie, on 2 April. Andrew considered getting a dog but found dog-friendly city places scarce. Audrey's 16 April pastry party proposal was never mentioned again. On 11 May Andrew hiked a new open space with friends and his girlfriend, and Audrey said she had four dogs. On 13 June he finished a rock climbing class, and Audrey invited him on a trail walk, with no recorded outcome. Around 23 June Andrew said he missed nature, and on 26 June Audrey moved to a home with a bigger backyard.

On 3 July Audrey said a dog training course was taking much of her time, and Andrew said he had taken up cooking. On 11 July Andrew announced a German Shepherd puppy named Toby, taken home despite city living, and invited Audrey and her dogs on a hike, which she accepted. On 4 August he said he, his girlfriend, and Toby were going camping, and Audrey advised that German Shepherds need plenty of time, energy, and exercise. On 16 August she said she had a tattoo of her four dogs and that four was enough. On 19 August she said she had learned to groom her dogs herself. On 24 August Andrew shared a photo of Toby, a small dog on a leash, after a fishing trip. This conflicts with the German Shepherd description, and it has not been addressed. The hike and camping trip never came up again.

On 6 September Andrew said work was stressful and had pushed outdoor activities aside. He shared a sunset photo from a hike the previous weekend, his first recorded hike since July, and said Toby was still too young to hike and he was still searching for a dog-friendly home. On 24 September Audrey described calming a dog that pulled so hard the leash broke, by petting and hugging her, speaking calmly, and walking slowly. Andrew guessed the dog was Precious, which Audrey did not confirm. Audrey advised patience, regular training, time, love, and praise. Her dogs practice sit, stay, shake, and roll over, and they walk several times a day. All four are mutts: two Jack Russell mixes and two Chihuahua mixes. She keeps a garden with a vegetable patch and Peruvian Lilies, while Andrew has been caring for balcony flowers.

In Session 20 on 1 October, Andrew said he and his girlfriend are going to the beach next month with Toby. Audrey mentioned "our hike with the dogs next month," the first mention since August. Andrew said it had been a long time since they were all in nature together. Audrey said she wants to start birdwatching, is working through a guidebook, and showed a pair of binoculars. Andrew offered birdwatching advice and said he would bring binoculars and a notebook on a trip. Both agreed people must protect nature for future generations. Audrey said she usually takes public transport but would like to try biking, and Andrew offered to show her the best bike routes near the river.

In Session 21 on 4 October, Audrey said she had taken her dogs to the beach over the weekend, where they swam and played in the ocean. Andrew replied with a photo of a person walking on a beach with a surfboard, presented as his last beach trip, then said he had not been to the beach in a while. That is a discrepancy. He said he misses being outdoors, that open spaces are hard to find in the city, and that his work-life balance has made hiking harder. He called nature his escape and said he feels a void in his heart. Audrey suggested plants for his home or weekend park trips. Andrew said he would look into getting more plants, though nothing beats being outside. Audrey promised to say hi to her dogs for him. Toby, the dog hike, birdwatching, and biking were not mentioned.

Andrew's arc runs from having no pets and hiking regularly, through his dog search and Toby's arrival, to a stretch of work stress that pushed outdoor life aside. By autumn he was returning to nature through balcony gardening, birdwatching, and biking plans, but by early October he described a continuing void, with plants offered as a stopgap. Audrey's household grew from three named dogs to four with Pixie, though her July description of four adult dogs conflicts with Pixie being a puppy. She moved to a larger yard in June, started agility classes by early August, organized playdates in September, took up gardening and birdwatching by late September, and by early October had taken her dogs to the beach.

Open items include the pastry party, the Fox Hollow visit, the dog park report, the trail walk, the recipes, the August hike, the beach trip details, the birdwatching trip, the bike ride, and the dog hike. None has a set date. It is unknown whether Toby and Audrey's dogs will ever meet. Audrey still awaits a photo of Andrew's dog from May, and Andrew's nature reserve photos are pending. Unresolved are the Toby breed conflict, the unconfirmed Precious name, the beach photo discrepancy, and Andrew's dog-friendly home search, including whether his home is pet-friendly.

Joanna and Nate reconnected on 21 January 2022 after a long gap, and their conversations have stayed friendly, warm, and encouraging. Both enjoy movies, but their tastes differ. Joanna's hobbies are writing, reading, movies, and nature, and her main joys are writing and time with friends. She isn't into video games and prefers dramas, emotionally driven films, and romantic comedies. Acting was her first passion, though she now focuses mostly on writing. Nate's hobbies are video games and movies. He likes action and sci-fi for their visual effects, enjoys classics, and sees fantasy and sci-fi as an escape. He plays mainly for fun, prefers laid-back players, and has recently started playing with people outside his usual circle.

In January 2022, Nate said he had won his first Counter-Strike: Global Offensive tournament, and Joanna congratulated him. She recommended an unnamed romantic drama about memory and relationships. Nate said he would watch it but has never reported back. On 23 January, Joanna finished her first screenplay, a drama-romance, and planned to submit it to film festivals. No festival results have been reported.

On 7 February, Nate made coconut milk ice cream for the first time and shared a dairy-free chocolate berry cake. Joanna recommended "Little Women," about sisterhood, love, and reaching for your dreams. Nate said he would watch it but has not reported back. On 25 February he apologized for being out of touch. Joanna said she can no longer eat dairy, so Nate promised her a coconut milk recipe. That same day she started a second screenplay, a drama about a thirty-year-old woman on a road trip of self-discovery after a loss, drawn from her own experiences.

Joanna finished the second screenplay on 18 March, feeling relief, anxiety, and a tug-of-war between hope and doubt. Nate told her not to quit. That day she also revealed she is allergic to cockroaches, so she doubts she will ever have a pet. On 24 March she auditioned for a writing gig, which went alright but left mixed emotions. Nate said he had faith in her and was competing in a video game tournament again. When he asked for writing advice, she told him to read widely, write and share, gather feedback, and keep practicing.

Nate has two pet turtles and says they calm him when he is nervous. Joanna has always avoided reptiles and furred animals because she is allergic. Nate offered to send turtle pictures so she could watch them grow, and has since shared several.

On 15 April, Nate dyed his hair purple, saying the bold color helps him stand out. Joanna said his boldness inspired her, and she said her writing was consuming her, so no trips were lined up. Nate asked her to keep him posted and ended with "See you soon?" but no meetup has been arranged. On 17 April, Joanna said she had found an awesome hiking trail in her hometown. Nate isn't really into hiking but would like to see it. Nate also shared a bowl of dairy-free ice cream and gave Joanna the recipe, fulfilling his February promise: coconut milk, vanilla extract, sugar, and a pinch of salt, chilled, churned, then frozen until scoopable.

In Session 9 on 21 April 2022, Joanna said she had joined a writers group, where she feels motivated, supported, and finally like she belongs. She is working with the group on a script called "Finding Home," about a girl searching for her true home. Nate said he has a gaming tournament next month, his fourth, and feels good about it. Joanna recalled forgetting her lines at her first stage performance, which taught her to prepare and stay in the moment. Nate asked whether she would return to acting, and she said "never say never." Nate named a fantasy and sci-fi trilogy as a favorite and recommended a book series full of adventure, magic, and great characters. Joanna said she would check it out and report back.

As of 21 April 2022, Joanna has finished two screenplays. The first was submitted to film festivals with no reported result, and the second has no reported submission. She is still waiting on the writing gig, feeling hopeful but anxious, and values Nate's support. She is allergic to reptiles, furred animals, and cockroaches, has no pets, and avoids dairy. Nate has two turtles that calm him, competed in a March tournament, has a fourth tournament planned for May, dyed his hair purple, and has been experimenting with dairy-free desserts. He has not reported on the romantic drama or "Little Women." They remain friendly and in regular contact, but no in-person meetup is planned.

Nate and Joanna lost touch for a long time before reconnecting in January 2022. Across twenty-eight sessions, from 21 January to 9 November 2022, they have talked about movies, Joanna's writing, Nate's gaming, pets, baking, and hiking. The tone is friendly and supportive, and each often encourages the other's goals. Nate is playful and upbeat, and Joanna is warm and reflective. Session 18 took place on 14 August, followed by a long gap until session 21 on 14 September. Sessions 22 through 28 fell on 6 October, 9 October (a Sunday), 21 October, 25 October, 4 November, 7 November (a Monday), and 9 November (a Wednesday).

Gaming is Nate's main hobby, which he sees as a creative outlet and a way to escape life's struggles. He won his first tournament around 14 January, in Counter-Strike: Global Offensive, and Joanna said she is not really into games. He then won a local Street Fighter tournament in late April, a regional tournament reported on 3 June, an online tournament on 8 July, and an international tournament on 21 August, his biggest win so far. He suggested she might enjoy a writing convention, and she said she would look into it. In session 24 he said he feels stressed about tough competitors. He has had several offers from new gaming teams and plans to decide after his next tournament. He has also started making gaming content for YouTube, which he described as a way to entertain people between tournaments. He is playing "Xenoblade Chronicles," a Japanese fantasy RPG his friends recommended.

Nate loves action, sci-fi, and fantasy films, especially their visual effects and world-building, and he likes classics. On 21 April he recommended a fantasy book series, and on 2 May Joanna said she had watched "The Lord of the Rings" trilogy on his recommendation and found it awesome. Joanna favors dramas, romcoms, and emotionally driven films. In January she asked his opinion of an unnamed romantic drama, and on 7 February she asked about "Little Women," which Nate said in session 22 he had loved. Joanna said she had recently watched an unnamed classic movie, rated it 9 or 10 out of 10, and shared a photo of a framed movie poster. In session 27 Nate said he likes the movies she recommends much more than random picks, and he has promised movie picks.

Joanna's writing has become central to her life. She finished her first full screenplay, a drama-romance, on 23 January and sent it to a film festival by 7 February. On 18 March she finished a semi-autobiographical road-trip story. On 24 March she had an audition for a writing gig; the result has never been reported. On 21 April she joined a writers group where she finally felt she belonged, and they are working on a script called "Finding Home." On 20 May she finished a third screenplay about loss, identity, and connection, which she wants Nate to read. On 14 September a laptop crash erased a week of her work, so she now keeps an external drive for backups. She is writing a fourth script, a love story that came from a dream, and has submitted several more scripts. Nate predicted at least one will reach the screen as her third published movie, and she said she will not give up. In session 28 she said she pitched a script to producers on 8 November, and they liked it. She called the work satisfying and said it gave her a big confidence boost. She is now working on a suspenseful thriller set in a small Midwestern town, which she described as a great creative outlet.

Nate has owned two turtles for three years, which keep him calm when he is nervous. In session 25 he said they eat vegetables, fruits, and insects, and that they get excited about strawberries. In session 28 he announced a third turtle, bought at a pet store because the tank is now big enough, and Joanna said she had not expected him to add one this year. He also adopted a dog named Max, introduced on 20 May, and on 25 May arranged doggy playdates with a neighboring family, though no dates are recorded. On 25 May Nate sent a photo of a stuffed "pup," and in session 24 Joanna said she still has it, named Tilly after a real dog from her childhood in Michigan. Her photo that session showed a cat rather than a stuffed dog, a small inconsistency worth noting. In session 28 she asked to come over and watch the turtles from a distance, and he said he would bathe them before she arrives.

Food and baking recur throughout. Nate loves coconut milk and enjoys chocolate and mixed berry flavors. Joanna is lactose intolerant. On 17 April Nate shared a dairy-free ice cream recipe, and Joanna promised to report back, but no clear report has come. On 2 May she shared a dairy-free vanilla cake, crediting his coconut recommendation. In session 21 Nate said he teaches vegan ice cream recipes on his own cooking show; Joanna said she would try his coconut milk ice cream and watch the show. Her favorite treat is a chocolate raspberry tart with an almond flour crust. In session 26 Nate invited Joanna over to try his lactose-free coconut milk ice cream, and she accepted for 5 November. Session 27 did not confirm that visit took place. In session 28 Nate shared a photo of homemade coconut ice cream, and Joanna said she wished she could try it but could not right now.

Friendship and shared plans have grown warmer over time. On 15 April Nate suggested seeing each other soon, and Joanna replied "Totally!" On 12 May she shared a photo of a waterfall, Whispering Falls, and Nate suggested hiking together, though no date or trail has been set. In session 22 Nate made her a whiteboard drawing meant as a reminder to look back on when she needs encouragement. In session 23 Joanna said a movie on a comfy couch with a good blanket gives her deep peace. In session 28 she shared a sunset photo of a sunflower field from a hike near Fort Wayne the previous summer. The session ended with Joanna saying "see you tomorrow," which would be 10 November. This conflicts with her earlier request to come over "sometime," and it is unclear whether the 5 November visit happened.

As of 9 November 2022, Joanna has written at least three screenplays, is writing a fourth and a thriller, and has finished her book. One script went to a film festival, one to a contest, and one she wants Nate to read. Another reached the big screen on 23 October, and she is keeping its title private. Her audition result is still unreported. Nate has adopted Max, kept his turtles and added a third, won major tournaments including a recent Valorant final, lost a recent tournament, is weighing offers from gaming teams, has started a YouTube channel, and teaches dairy-free desserts on his cooking show. Open requests include Nate's thoughts on the romantic drama and the fantasy series, his movie picks, and his tournament updates. Joanna has promised updates on her audition, the dairy-free ice cream, her screenwriting, her book, and her family's reaction to the ice cream. Nate asked to hear how her bookmark gift lands. The screenplays shown on 4 June and 23 October, the contest screenplay, the producer meeting outcomes, and the classic movie from session 23 remain unidentified. John and James are two gamers who first spoke on 17 March 2022 at about 3:47 pm. Their conversations are friendly and personal, covering video games, programming, dogs, goals, travel, work, and more recently romance and hobbies outside gaming. James usually shares projects, achievements, outings, and photos. John usually shares new hobbies and experiences, and over time he has come to turn to James when stressed. There have been twenty-three sessions, dated 4, 8, 11, and 23 May; 13, 16, and 19 June; 9 and 22 July; 6 and 10 August; 21 and 26 August; 1 September; and 4 September 2022. Some sessions describe the friendship as reaching back to childhood, which does not fit their first conversation in March 2022, and this has never been explained. In Session 21 they arranged to meet at McGee's Pub on 27 August 2022, but whether that meeting happened is not recorded.

James has considered programming central to his life since college. He has worked with Python and C++, built a website, and made game mods. He writes goals in a notebook and says tracking progress keeps him motivated. In Session 13 he said he had started a course combining gaming and programming. He is developing a game based on a character he sketched as a child, and in the first session he offered to involve John in its HTML work, which has not come up since. He also proposed a dog-walking app that was never mentioned again. In Session 22, on 1 September 2022, he announced that his Unity strategy game was finally finished. He loves Civilization and Total War, struggled most with balancing and fairness, and credited John's encouragement. It is not stated whether this game is the childhood character game.

James has three dogs. Max is a shepherd, and Daisy is a Labrador. Ned is a pup James adopted in early April 2022 from a shelter in Stamford. In Session 15 James began introducing the three dogs to one another, which was hard at first but is slowly working. In Session 18 he took "his puppy" to the clinic on 5 August; the puppy is unnamed, and Ned is the likeliest candidate but unconfirmed. In Session 19 he took all three dogs to a beach outing on 9 August, where he met Samantha. He calls his pets "the source of my joy."

James has played many games. In the first session he praised The Witcher 3's story and atmosphere. In the fourth session his team reached the semifinals of an online tournament. His favorite game to play with his team is Apex Legends. In Session 8 he said he had played a turn-based strategy game for about a month, without naming it, and in Session 16 he announced an online tournament win, also without naming the game. He uses games to relax and compares them to therapy. He said he was considering RPGs or MOBAs and promised to share his thoughts, which have not come.

James's romantic life is now the most significant new thread. In the sixth session he shared a drawing of a woman in armor kneeling on a rock, based on a stranger he passed around 6 April. He fell for her at first sight, and she remains unidentified. He met Samantha at the beach outing on 9 August, and she gave him her phone number. He planned to call on 11 August, and John encouraged him, but the call was never described. In Session 23, on 4 September, James reported that on 3 September, at the theater, he asked Samantha to be his girlfriend, and she agreed. Samantha loves theater. He said the recent weeks had brought good and bad moments that were a bit overwhelming, but that he is happy with her. They had also been at McGee's bar, where she revealed she loves a good lager. He invited John to a baseball game next Sunday, which would fall on 11 September, and promised to show John what Samantha looks like. John agreed. This is James's first romantic relationship in the memory. Whether the McGee's visit was the planned 27 August meeting is not stated.

James also started a new hobby. Two days before 4 September he signed up for a cooking class, having never liked cooking. He made a good omelette on his first try, and the class also covered meringue and dough. The classes cost $10 each. He hoped to treat John to one of his creations and said John's encouragement gave him strength to pursue the hobby.

Travel and family are major threads. In the first session John suggested arcades over bowling because his fingers are too big for bowling balls, and James proposed trying VR gaming together "next Saturday," which no later session confirms. In Session 6 James said he had visited Italy, Turkey, and Mexico, and suggested a trip with John next year. In Session 16 he announced tickets to Toronto, with plans to visit Vancouver. In Session 17 he reported the trip went great and that he had reached Nuuk. Toronto and Vancouver were never mentioned again. He brought souvenirs for John and for someone named Jill, whose relationship to John is not stated. In Session 9 James named pepperoni as his favorite pizza, John named Hawaiian, and James urged John to try prosciutto. In Session 13 they had a football rivalry. James hopes Liverpool wins the title, while John, a Manchester City fan, predicted City would win. James bet Liverpool would finish higher, John accepted, and the stakes were never specified, so the bet will be settled at season's end.

John's life has been full of projects and changes. In the first session he suggested building mobile applications together someday, which has not been revisited. He is taking a programming class to refresh HTML and CSS. In Session 7 he was stuck on a difficult algorithm assignment. In Session 8 he started freelance programming, building a website for a local business, and getting payments working was the hardest part. Neither problem has a reported resolution. In Session 10 John organized a CS:GO tournament that raised money for a dog shelter near his street, and the leftover money bought groceries they cooked for homeless people. In Session 11 he volunteered his skills for a charitable foundation working with kids. In Session 12 he took second place in a local tournament. In Session 13 he got his dream job, starting in July 2022, though the employer and role were not named. In Session 17 he said he had just started playing chess, and James advised him to study opening moves. No update has come since.

In Session 18, John reported he had left his IT job after three years. He said it was frightening, but he wanted work that made a difference and matched his values, and he is now loving his new job. This may be the Session 13 dream job, but the sessions do not say so. He wants to organize computer game tournaments in his state, starting with CS:GO, and plans Fortnite competitions too. James offered financial help or advice if needed. John very much wants a pet but is not ready yet, and James's offer to help him find one still stands. In Session 14 he recommended "The Stormlight Archive," "Kingkiller Chronicle," and "The Expanse." In Session 15 he asked to visit James's volunteering organization, and the visit planned for late June was never confirmed. In Session 19 John said he had been playing strategy and RPG games instead of his usual shooters, and was hooked on The Witcher 3. In Session 20 he joined an online programming group of skilled coders who want to use technology for good. When James asked whether he was returning to programming work, John said no, it was a one-time experience. He still wants to host eSports competitions and sees gaming as an escape.

In Session 21, John said he had been helping his younger siblings with programming, and they are building a simple text-based adventure game together. James suggested meeting at McGee's Pub for its stout, and they agreed on 27 August, John's day off. In Session 22, John said teaching his siblings has been fulfilling. For the first time he said plainly that he is going through some difficult times, and that it is good to have someone like James. James replied that he is there to talk or vent to. The cause of John's stress has never been discussed. In Session 23 John said his parents have just started learning to code from him, which has drawn the family closer. He also bought new gaming equipment, Sennheiser headphones and a Logitech mouse. He still plans a family gaming night with his siblings for September 2022, and whether it happens is open.

Several items remain open as of Session 23. James has not shared thoughts on the RPG John recommended or on RPGs and MOBAs, and his turn-based and tournament games are unnamed. The VR outing and the trip with John next year are unconfirmed. The stranger behind James's character is unidentified. John's algorithm project, freelance payment problem, and chess study have no reported resolution, and his new job has no named employer or role. Whether John visited the volunteering organization is unknown. John owes James his prosciutto impressions, and the football bet is unresolved. The difficulties James mentioned in Session 14 were never explained, and the cause of John's current stress is not stated. The Toronto and Vancouver parts of the trip are unconfirmed beyond Nuuk. The identities of Jill, the cat, and the puppy are unknown. Whether John attends the 11 September baseball game is not yet recorded. The outcome of the planned 27 August McGee's meeting is not recorded. The dog-walking app, HTML collaboration, mobile app, and comic game have gone quiet. John's eSports competitions, online programming group, and teaching of his siblings and parents are active, and whether the September family gaming night happens is open.

Joanna and Nate reconnected on 21 January 2022 after a long gap and have stayed friendly, warm, and encouraging, in regular contact but with no in-person meetup planned. Both enjoy movies, but their tastes differ. Joanna enjoys writing, reading, movies, and nature, and her main joys are writing and time with friends. She isn't into video games and prefers dramas, emotionally driven films, and romantic comedies. Acting was her first passion, though she now focuses mostly on writing. Nate enjoys video games and movies, likes action and sci-fi for their visual effects, enjoys classics, and sees fantasy and sci-fi as an escape. He plays mainly for fun, prefers laid-back players, and has recently started playing with people outside his usual circle.

In January 2022, Nate said he had won his first Counter-Strike: Global Offensive tournament, and Joanna congratulated him. She recommended an unnamed romantic drama, which Nate said he would watch but has never discussed. On 23 January, Joanna finished her first screenplay, a drama-romance, and planned to submit it to film festivals. No results have been reported.

On 7 February, Nate made coconut milk ice cream for the first time and shared a dairy-free chocolate berry cake. Joanna recommended "Little Women," which Nate said he would watch but has not discussed. On 25 February, Joanna said she can no longer eat dairy, and Nate promised her a coconut milk recipe. That day she started a second screenplay, a drama about a thirty-year-old woman on a road trip of self-discovery after a loss, drawn from her own experiences. She finished it on 18 March, feeling relief, anxiety, and a tug-of-war between hope and doubt. Nate told her not to quit. That day she also revealed she is allergic to cockroaches. On 24 March she auditioned for a writing gig, which left her with mixed emotions. When Nate asked for writing advice, she told him to read widely, write and share, gather feedback, and keep practicing.

Nate has two pet turtles, which calm him when he is nervous. Joanna has always avoided reptiles and furred animals because of her allergies, and Nate has since shared several turtle pictures.

On 15 April, Nate dyed his hair purple to stand out. Joanna said his boldness inspired her and that her writing was consuming her, so no trips were lined up. On 17 April, she said she had found an awesome hiking trail in her hometown. Nate also shared a bowl of dairy-free ice cream and gave her the recipe, fulfilling his February promise: coconut milk, vanilla extract, sugar, and a pinch of salt, chilled, churned, then frozen until scoopable.

On 21 April, Joanna said she had joined a writers group, where she feels motivated, supported, and like she belongs. She is working with the group on a script called "Finding Home." Nate said he has a fourth gaming tournament next month. Joanna recalled forgetting her lines at her first stage performance, and when Nate asked whether she would return to acting, she said "never say never." Nate recommended a fantasy and sci-fi book series, and Joanna said she would check it out and report back.

On 2 May, Joanna said she had watched "The Lord of the Rings" trilogy at Nate's suggestion and found it awesome. Nate called it probably the greatest trilogy of all time. He said gaming has been his focus and that he won a local Street Fighter tournament, his second win, after usually playing Counter-Strike. Joanna shared a photo of a dairy-free vanilla cake with strawberry filling and coconut cream frosting, crediting Nate's coconut recommendation. She said cooking and baking are her creative outlets, and she has been testing dairy-free desserts for friends and family.

As of 2 May 2022, Joanna has finished two screenplays. The first was submitted to film festivals with no reported result, and the second has no reported submission. She is still waiting on the writing gig, feeling hopeful but anxious, and values Nate's support. She is allergic to reptiles, furred animals, and cockroaches, has no pets, and avoids dairy. Nate has two turtles, has dyed his hair purple, has been experimenting with dairy-free desserts, and has reported winning tournaments in January and late April. He has a fourth tournament planned for May. He has not reported on the romantic drama, "Little Women," or the fantasy book series.

John and James first met on 17 March 2022, when John said he was glad to finally talk with James and asked what motivates him. They both love video games but experience them differently: James finds them joyful and exciting, while John plays to relax after a long day. James praised The Witcher 3's story, and John planned to try it. They also discussed programming. John had just signed up for a class to refresh his HTML and CSS skills. James first tried programming in college, has worked with Python and C++, has built a website and created game mods, and hopes to learn other languages.

They talked about building a mobile app together someday. James proposed a dog walking and pet care app that connects owners with reliable walkers, with customization as its key feature, and John thought it would find many buyers. James has two dogs, Max and Daisy, and has long wanted to tell a story about a girl through a computer game, possibly inviting John to help with HTML. When John mentioned morning runs, James proposed VR gaming, and they agreed to try VR the following Saturday, most likely 19 March though possibly 26 March. This was never settled.

On 20 March 2022, James said he had made a game avatar and joined an online platform where gamers share tips, calling gaming their shared language and a refuge in hard times. John said gaming helps him escape stress. James shared photos of his dogs, whom he considers family. John said he wants a pet someday but is not ready yet, and James offered to help him find one. The record does not show whether the VR session happened.

On 27 March 2022, John said he had advanced to the next level in his game. James said he was learning drums, and John replied that he had played drums for about a month. John had attended a gaming convention and joined a CS:GO tournament. James had recently got a new gaming system and was exploring RPGs and strategy games.

On 4 April 2022, James said he had reached the semifinals of an online tournament, losing the close final rounds. He remembered the advice to communicate well and never put ego above team success.

On 12 April 2022, James said he had adopted a pup named Ned from a Stamford shelter the previous week. John said work left him little time for gaming, though it still helps him forget stress. He was playing a new RPG with a strong story and a futuristic dystopian world, but said it was laggy and buggy. James preferred to wait until the bugs were fixed, but John argued the graphics and gameplay were worth it now and offered to send a link. James agreed to wait for the link and to share his thoughts afterward. The game's title is never named, and the record does not confirm the link was sent.

On 20 April 2022, John said that last Tuesday, most likely 19 April, he met three new friends in his programming course who share his passion. James said that last Thursday, most likely 14 April, he worked with a gaming friend on a project combining programming and gaming, creating a virtual world inspired by The Witcher 3. He shared a photo of a character he made, a woman in armor kneeling on a rock, inspired by a stranger he saw on a walk with his dogs. John believes only those who rest well work well, so time with friends and travel motivate him most. James has been to Italy, Turkey, and Mexico, and John has always dreamed of visiting Italy. James suggested traveling together next year and said he would start looking for a country.

On 23 April 2022, James said he had taken his dogs on a hike "last Thursday," most likely 21 April though possibly 14 April, and that fresh air helps him clear his head. John said he wished he could spend more time in nature, because work had been hectic. He was stuck on a difficult coding assignment involving a new algorithm. James suggested breaking the problem into smaller steps, researching similar algorithms, and asking other programmers for help. John said he would keep going.

On 29 April 2022, John said he was taking on freelance programming to hone his skills. His current project is a website for a local small business, his first professional project outside of class. Progress has been slow, and the hardest part has been setting up payments, which he is getting closer to solving. James encouraged him to treat setbacks as learning experiences. James said about 26 April he had bought an adventure book of fantasy novels, and John recommended The Name of the Wind, which James said he would read. James also shared photos of a three-book set and of Daisy lying beside him while he played. John said he was playing Assassin's Creed Valhalla. James said he had been playing Civilization VI for about a month, and it had challenged his strategic thinking. John said he had played a strategy board game with friends about 27 April, and described a card game whose name James could not recall. John mentioned an impostor game with friends and advised James to play it with a large group, which James said he would try.

Open items: No record confirms whether the VR session took place. The medical chart John shared earlier was never explained. The RPG link has been promised but not confirmed as sent, and James has promised to report his impressions. The shared trip next year has no chosen destination, and James is responsible for finding one. John's algorithm problem was unresolved as of 23 April, and his payment feature is still in progress as of 29 April.

Deborah and Jolene have chatted regularly since they first met on 23 January 2023, supporting each other through grief, work stress, and self-care. Their conversations often return to their mothers, nature, yoga, and their work and hobbies. The most recent session, Session 17, took place on 12 August 2023.

Deborah is a yoga teacher who lost her mother years before they met, and her father died suddenly around 25 January 2023. She has turned her grief toward her relatives and the family album. She sits on the bench by the living-room window where her mother read each morning and night, to feel close to her. Deborah wants to help people find peace and joy through yoga, and her neighborhood class on 10 March left her deeply fulfilled. She met her neighbor Anna at a park yoga session on 31 January 2023, and in July she started a running group with Anna. After losing a friend, Karlie, in mid-February, she found comfort in a garden of roses and dahlias. She loves Bali, listens to the album "Sleep" for meditation, has cats, and walks or runs in the park every morning and evening. In late June she was preparing a yoga retreat with friends, and by 12 August she had made a meditation guide for it. On 1 August she began a community cleanup project and is raising funds for it.

Jolene is an electrical engineer who lost her mother in 2022. She has a similar bench and window at her mother's house and wears a heart-shaped bird pendant her mother gave her in Paris, which symbolizes freedom and her goals. She keeps two pet snakes, Susie and Seraphim, who help her tune in to herself. She and her partner, together three years and not married, enjoy console gaming, especially "It Takes Two," which relaxes her and brings them closer, though gaming had been hard lately as of July. Deborah has repeatedly suggested swapping some gaming for yoga. Jolene has practiced yoga and meditation sporadically for about three years and says it has "seriously saved" her. Her favorite memory is the "snake adventure," when Seraphim escaped and was found hours later snuggled under the bed. She loves a hidden lake dock surrounded by trees, and she and Deborah agreed to visit it together sometime.

Jolene's work has been a recurring theme. In February she proposed a STEM volunteer program for underprivileged kids that she never pursued, and said a water purifier she built for a rural community gave her real purpose. On 2 March, overwhelmed by exams, she got Deborah's advice to set smaller goals and use a planner, and Deborah promised a yellow coffee mug with an encouraging note; whether it arrived is not recorded. On 6 June she finished the tough project and shared a photo of the solar-powered vehicle she built. She was interning at a well-known engineering firm, where seeing her ideas come to life was the best part, but work-life balance was hard. Deborah recommended a few minutes of daily mindful breathing with eyes closed, which Jolene said she would try. In late June she said the internship was very busy and she needed a break. In July she added workouts to her studying schedule, which she found tough but fun.

On 1 August 2023 at 9:26 am, Jolene said her life had been a rollercoaster. Deborah encouraged her, and the session ended with "You got this!"

Maria and John are friends who check in periodically about volunteering, fitness, family, work, John's political ambitions, pets, and leisure. Twenty-seven sessions have taken place, from 17 December 2022 through 3 August 2023. Maria volunteers at a homeless shelter and a dog shelter, does aerial yoga, joined a nearby church in May, and started a new gym routine in June. John does kickboxing, has been a firefighting brigade member since late July, and has a growing involvement with veterans' causes. Maria keeps her own notes on local politics and asked to be kept posted on John's meetings with local leaders, which he agreed to.

John's main political goal remains local office focused on education and infrastructure, both lacking in the area where he grew up. On 1 January 2023 he said he had failed a military aptitude test, which left him stressed. On 25 February he announced he was running again, calling it a "last run." The office, election date, and launch have never been named. He later retook the aptitude test with strong results, and on 2 April said he had graduated and was considering policymaking. On 18 April he mentioned blogging and a convention, with no stated link to the office. On 6 May he said he had decided to run again, and Maria said she was fully behind him. That day he proposed a community infrastructure project after a power cut, aimed at West County, his old area, and Maria agreed to help win neighborhood backing. On 20 May he said he was busy with a petition supporting military veterans, again with no stated link to the office.

John's finances remain his main stress. His car broke down on 10 April, straining his budget. On 16 June he announced a promotion to assistant manager, a stepping stone to bigger things the memory does not name. On 22 July he said he was enjoying a new job with an encouraging team, though the memory does not confirm whether this is the June promotion. On 5 July he said his work often feels like an uphill battle and that he sometimes doubts he is making a difference, but Maria's support keeps him going.

Family matters have also come up. On 3 June the family said goodbye to Max, a dog they had owned for ten years, and they are considering adopting a rescue dog, which Maria encouraged. On 3 August John mentioned his children directly for the first time, saying a recent visit to a military memorial had moved them deeply.

John's public activity has grown more visible. On 3 July he said he had taken part in a veterans' rights march. On 7 July he said a severe flood the previous week had ruined many homes in his old area because of poor infrastructure. He was gathering people to discuss repairs, and Maria agreed to join. The meeting's date, place, and organizers were not given. On 17 July he said he had visited a veterans' hospital and met an elderly veteran named Samuel, whose resilience reminded him why he wanted to join the military. He described an organization he now works with as a family that supports each other, without naming it. Whether he has enlisted is not confirmed.

Public service has also widened into the fire brigade. On 31 July John said Maria's shelter work had made him think about how he could help too, so he had just joined a firefighting brigade, which he called intense but rewarding. Its first call-out, on 23 July, saved a family from a burning building. He said the team had become like family, a bond that reminded him of his military service. He has not linked the brigade to the office.

On 3 August John said he had asked family and friends to join a virtual support group and act as advocates for the military. It is not confirmed whether this group is the organization he described on 17 July. Maria said she volunteers at a homeless shelter and shared a photo of a group around a table. She had started a year earlier after seeing a family struggling on the streets, and the work has been fulfilling despite being tough at times. She also shared a handwritten note from a shelter resident named Cindy, expressing gratitude. John called her inspiring. In the same session John said his family had recently visited a military memorial, which deeply affected his kids. Maria said younger generations need to learn to remember those who served, and John agreed that teaching respect for veterans matters. Maria said more people like him were needed, and they agreed teamwork can accomplish a great deal.

Across these sessions, John's political activity has moved from the "last run" through talks with leaders, blogging, a convention, the veterans' petition, a march, and the flood meeting. Education and infrastructure remain central, with West County and veterans added as focuses. His public service has widened to include the fire brigade and the veterans' support group. The office, election date, launch, and whether he will enlist all remain unresolved, though he repeatedly says he feels called to serve.

Maria has consistently offered encouragement and practical help with networking, events, the infrastructure project, the petition, the flood meeting, and the possible rescue dog. Support runs both ways. John encouraged her when she opened up in session 20, and in session 23 he asked for her ideas. Her recent life has included the car accident on 2 July, helping her cousin find housing after the cousin left home in a hurry, church activities, a church hike that gave her peace, and baking for the shelter.

Several threads remain open. The memory does not establish whether the petition, march, project, convention, hospital visit, organization, support group, fire brigade, or flood meeting connects to the office. It does not say what the fundraiser raised, whether the new job is the June promotion, or whether John has enlisted. It does not say whether the family adopts a rescue dog, what Maria's struggle involves, or whether her cousin has found housing. The flood meeting's date, place, and link to the party invitation are also unknown.

Deborah and Jolene have chatted regularly since they first met on 23 January 2023, supporting each other through grief, work stress, and self-care. Their talks often return to their mothers, nature, yoga, and work. The most recent session, Session 18, took place on 16 August 2023.

Deborah is a yoga teacher who lost her mother years before they met, and her father died suddenly around 25 January 2023. She turns her grief toward relatives and the family album, and she sits on the bench by the living-room window where her mother read each morning and night. She wants to help people find peace and joy through yoga, and a neighborhood class on 10 March left her deeply fulfilled. She met her neighbor Anna at a park yoga session on 31 January 2023, and in July they started a running group together. After losing her friend Karlie in mid-February, she found comfort in a garden of roses and dahlias. She loves Bali, listens to the album "Sleep" for meditation, has cats, and runs or walks in the park. On 1 August she began a community cleanup project and is raising funds for it. She made a meditation guide for a yoga retreat by 12 August, and in mid-August she led a sunset meditation session for elderly residents at a care home.

Jolene is an electrical engineer who lost her mother in 2022. She has a similar bench and window at her mother's house, and she wears a heart-shaped bird pendant her mother gave her in Paris, which symbolizes freedom and her goals. She keeps two pet snakes, Susie and Seraphim. She and her partner, together three years and not married, enjoy console gaming, especially "It Takes Two," though gaming had been hard lately as of July. Deborah has repeatedly suggested swapping some gaming for yoga. Jolene has practiced yoga and meditation sporadically for about three years and says it has "seriously saved" her. Her favorite memory is the "snake adventure," when Seraphim escaped and was found hours later snuggled under the bed. She loves a hidden lake dock, and she and Deborah agreed to visit it together sometime.

Jolene's work is a recurring theme. In February she proposed a STEM volunteer program for underprivileged kids but never pursued it, and a water purifier she built for a rural community gave her real purpose. On 2 March, overwhelmed by exams, she received Deborah's advice to set smaller goals and use a planner. Deborah promised a yellow coffee mug with an encouraging note, but whether it arrived is not recorded. The Pomodoro Technique helped her avoid burnout later in March, and Deborah introduced the Eisenhower Matrix, which Jolene planned to try. She reported an engineering breakthrough on 28 March and mentioned a big unnamed project on 9 April. On 6 June she finished it and shared a photo of the solar-powered vehicle she built. She interned at a well-known engineering firm, where seeing her ideas come to life was the best part, but work-life balance was hard. Deborah recommended a few minutes of daily mindful breathing, which Jolene said she would try. In late June she said she needed a break, and in July she added workouts to her studying schedule.

On 1 August 2023, Jolene said her life had been a rollercoaster. A project she had poured enormous work into had crashed the previous week, and she lost everything, leaving her frustrated and depressed. Her pets and video games helped her cope, and she said yoga and meditation keep her grounded. Deborah offered support and described a gentle breathing-and-grounding flow, promising a tutorial video. Jolene said she would practice and report back.

On 12 August, Jolene said she was still stressed about losing her work files from the crashed project, but meditation had restored her clarity. Deborah said they were in this together. Jolene shared a photo of two blue notebooks she had designed with galaxies and circuitry, and she described her current project, a prototype for a more productive and affordable aerial surveillance system for emergencies and environmental monitoring. The session ended with "You got this!"

In Session 18 on 16 August 2023, Jolene said her plans and her relationship had been up and down, and that she struggled to juggle engineering, her relationship, and personal growth. Deborah said restoring balance and recognizing your needs makes a difference. Jolene had started a bullet journal, which she finds satisfying for tracking tasks, and she shared a photo of a new spread with a favorite quote that reminds her never to give up. Deborah then asked whether she had tried mindfulness. Jolene had not, but she was keen to try it to destress. Deborah said mindfulness had become a huge part of her own life after she began with workshops and books, and she offered to help Jolene get started. They closed with "We're in this together."

Open threads include Jolene starting mindfulness with Deborah's help, the yellow mug, the STEM volunteer program, the Eisenhower Matrix, the daily breathing practice, swapping gaming for yoga, the lake dock visit, Deborah's tutorial video, and Jolene's report on the new flow. Some photo captions do not match what the speakers said, so treat captions as approximate.

Joanna and Nate reconnected on 21 January 2022 after a long gap and have stayed friendly, warm, and encouraging. They keep in regular contact and support each other's projects, but no in-person meetup is confirmed. On 12 May 2022, Joanna invited Nate to hike the trails in her town, and he said it sounded like a plan, though no date was set. That hiking trip remains the main open plan between them.

Joanna enjoys writing, reading, movies, nature, cooking and baking, and time with friends. She isn't into video games and prefers dramas, emotionally driven films, and romantic comedies. Acting was her first passion, but she now focuses mostly on writing. She is allergic to reptiles, furred animals, and cockroaches, has no pets, and avoids dairy.

Nate enjoys video games and movies, especially action and sci-fi for their visual effects, and he enjoys classics. He sees fantasy and sci-fi as an escape, plays mainly for fun, prefers laid-back players, and has recently started playing with people outside his usual circle. He has two pet turtles, which calm him when he is nervous. On 15 April he dyed his hair purple to stand out.

Nate's gaming wins so far are a first Counter-Strike: Global Offensive tournament in January 2022 and a local Street Fighter tournament on 2 May, his second win. He mentioned a fourth tournament for May but has not reported on it.

Joanna's writing has moved steadily forward. On 23 January she finished her first screenplay, a drama-romance, and planned to submit it to film festivals; no results have been reported. On 25 February she started a second screenplay, a drama about a thirty-year-old woman on a road trip of self-discovery after a loss, drawn from her own experiences. She finished it on 18 March, feeling relief, anxiety, and a tug-of-war between hope and doubt. Nate told her not to quit, and no submission has been reported. On 24 March she auditioned for a writing gig, which left her with mixed emotions, and she is still waiting, feeling hopeful but anxious. When Nate asked for writing advice, she said to read widely, write and share, gather feedback, and keep practicing. On 21 April she said she had joined a writers group and was working with it on a script called "Finding Home." Asked whether she would return to acting, she said "never say never."

On 20 May 2022, Joanna said she had finished something after a "pretty wild journey" and shared a photo of a notepad. It was her third screenplay, deeply personal, about loss, identity, and connection, a story she had carried for ages before she felt ready to write it. She said writing it was hard but that she is proud of it, and that she writes best when she is true to herself. Nate noted that she seems drawn to sadness and loss, and she said meaningful stories come from personal experience. She said his support and that of her friends, especially friends who understand her work and give feedback, make the journey easier. It is unclear whether this is "Finding Home" or a separate project.

Food has been an ongoing thread. On 7 February Nate shared a dairy-free chocolate berry cake, and Joanna recommended "Little Women," which Nate has not discussed. On 25 February Joanna said she can no longer eat dairy, and Nate promised her a coconut milk recipe. He delivered it on 15 April as a dairy-free ice cream made from coconut milk, vanilla extract, sugar, and a pinch of salt. On 2 May Joanna shared a dairy-free vanilla cake, crediting his advice, and said she has been testing dairy-free desserts for friends and family.

Pets have also come up. Joanna has always avoided reptiles and furred animals because of her allergies, but Nate has since shared several turtle pictures. On 20 May he introduced Max, a dog he recently adopted, who is full of energy and keeping his other pets active. Joanna said allergies mean she doesn't want a pet and she is too lazy to research alternatives. She finds comfort in writing, creative projects, and supportive friends.

Nate recommended a fantasy and sci-fi book series on 21 April, and Joanna said she would check it out and report back, though she has not yet done so. On 2 May she said she had watched "The Lord of the Rings" trilogy at his suggestion and found it awesome, and Nate called it probably the greatest trilogy of all time.

On 12 May Joanna shared a photo of a waterfall at a spot called Whispering Falls. She said nature makes her feel calm and present, and that these trails made her want to write a drama. Nate said he tends to get lost in thought about his life or new recipes when he is out, suggested hiking together, and said he might write a drama himself.

Neither has reported on "Little Women," the unnamed romantic drama Joanna recommended in January, or the fantasy book series Nate suggested. Their relationship remains warm and supportive, with each cheering on the other's creative work.

SUMMARY:

Joanna and Nate are friends who chat regularly about their hobbies and lives. Joanna writes screenplays and enjoys movies, books, and nature. Nate plays competitive video games and enjoys cooking.

Joanna finished her first full screenplay in January 2022. She wrapped up a second script in March and then started "Finding Home" with her writing group, a story about a girl searching for her true home. She had an audition for a writing gig in late March but has not said how it went, and she has not said whether her first screenplay has been accepted anywhere. By 20 May 2022 she had finished a third script, which she described as personal and about loss, identity, and connection. It was a story she had carried for ages before she found the courage to write it. She called the process hard but said she is proud of it and writes best when she is true to herself. Writing and creative projects help her through tough times, and she values friends who understand her work and give feedback.

Joanna is allergic to cockroaches, and as of May 2022 her allergies make her not want a pet. She said she is too lazy to research alternative pets.

Nate won his first video game tournament in January 2022 and his second in late April. He expected his fourth tournament in May but has not said how it went. On 20 May he introduced Max, an adopted dog full of energy who is keeping his other pets active. He said pets make people happier and never let them down.

Food has come up often. In February Nate offered to send Joanna a coconut milk recipe, and in May Joanna described a dairy-free vanilla cake with strawberry filling and coconut cream frosting.

Both find nature calming. Joanna watched "Little Women" in February 2022 and called it amazing. In May she watched "The Lord of the Rings" trilogy on Nate's recommendation and said it was awesome. On 12 May she went hiking, found more trails in her town, and photographed Whispering Falls. Nate said he gets deep in thought about his life or new recipes when he relaxes, and he suggested they hike together sometime. He also mentioned he might write a drama and publish a screenplay. Joanna invited him onto the trails, and he agreed. No date has been set.

Open items: how Nate's fourth tournament went; whether Joanna's first screenplay was accepted; how the audition went; whether Nate and Joanna have gone hiking together; whether Joanna has shared her third script with anyone; and whether Joanna has read the fantasy book series Nate recommended.

Audrey and Andrew are friends who keep in touch in sporadic bursts, bonded by a love of nature and animals. They mostly discuss Audrey's dogs, Andrew's search for a dog and later his life with dogs, outdoor adventures, and Audrey's handmade jewelry. Their latest exchange was Session 24 on 19 October 2023. On 27 March 2023, Andrew had just started work as a Financial Analyst after a period apart. He had no pets, loved eagles, and hiked Fox Hollow on weekends. Audrey had three dogs, Pepper, Precious, and Panda, and said she could not live without them, which made Andrew a little jealous. Her family adopted a puppy, Pixie, on 2 April. Andrew considered getting a dog but found dog-friendly city places scarce. Audrey's 16 April pastry party proposal was never mentioned again. On 11 May she said she had four dogs. On 13 June Andrew finished a rock climbing class, and Audrey invited him on a trail walk, with no recorded outcome. On 26 June she moved to a home with a bigger backyard.

On 3 July Audrey said a dog training course was taking much of her time. On 11 July Andrew announced a German Shepherd puppy, Toby, taken home despite city living, and invited Audrey and her dogs on a hike, which she accepted. On 4 August he mentioned a camping trip with his girlfriend and Toby, and Audrey advised that German Shepherds need plenty of exercise. On 24 August he shared a photo of Toby, a small dog on a leash, which conflicts with the breed description and was never addressed. The hike and camping trip never came up again.

On 6 September Andrew said work stress had pushed outdoor activities aside. On 24 September Audrey described calming a dog that pulled so hard its leash broke. Andrew guessed it was Precious, which she did not confirm. On 1 October Andrew said he and his girlfriend would take Toby to the beach next month. Audrey mentioned "our hike with the dogs next month" and said she wanted to start birdwatching. Andrew offered to bring binoculars and to show her bike routes near the river. On 4 October Audrey said her dogs had swum in the ocean at the beach. Andrew replied with a photo of a stranger on a beach, presented as his last beach trip, then said he had not been to a beach in a while, a discrepancy. He said he misses being outdoors. On 6 October Audrey recalled a knee injury that once kept her from walking her dogs. Andrew asked about jewelry she had apparently mentioned earlier, but no earlier mention is recorded. Audrey makes jewelry from recycled materials such as bottle caps and buttons and donates part of her profits to an animal shelter.

On 13 October Andrew said that last Tuesday he, his girlfriend, and Toby had a good evening playing board games, but later called Friday night's board game session the nice break, an inconsistency. Audrey said she had baked cookies for neighbors with pup-friendly homes and showed a new flower tattoo added to her earlier tattoo of her four dogs. Andrew suggested a dog park outing, and Audrey said her dogs love the park. He called Toby a German Shepherd who loves sweaters, which does not resolve the breed conflict. Audrey admitted it had been a while since she walked her dogs and said she needs a hike with them as therapy. She then recalled good times when "we all" hiked with "my dog," which leaves unclear whether she means all her dogs or one.

On 19 October Audrey said she had gone to a pet store "last Monday" to buy toys for her dogs and shared a photo of a box of toys. Andrew said he had recently adopted a shelter dog he named Buddy, shared a photo of him on a couch, and said Buddy was still getting used to Toby. He said he never imagined pets would bring so much happiness, though Toby has been with him since July. Andrew said he and Buddy enjoy walks and new trails and would soon take both dogs hiking. Audrey said she could not wait for "our hike with the furry friends next month." Andrew shared photos of a cow on a dirt road and a red truck in a field, saying he wished he could take his dogs somewhere so far from the city. Audrey said she would research a similar spot for their hike, and Andrew agreed to look for one.

Andrew's arc runs from having no pets and hiking regularly, through his dog search and Toby's arrival, to work stress that pushed outdoor life aside. By 19 October he had a second dog and was talking about trails again. Audrey's household grew from three named dogs to four with Pixie, though her July description of four adult dogs conflicts with Pixie being a puppy. She moved to a bigger yard in June, took up birdwatching, and by late October was planning a scenic hike with her dogs.

Open items with no set date include the pastry party, the Fox Hollow visit, the trail walk, the August hike, the beach trip details, the birdwatching trip, the bike ride, the dog hike, the cafe and dog park outing, and the hike with the furry friends next month, for which Audrey is researching a location. It is unknown whether Toby and Audrey's dogs will ever meet, and Audrey still awaits a photo of Andrew's dog from May. Unresolved are the Toby breed conflict, the unconfirmed Precious name, the beach photo discrepancy, the knee injury and earlier jewelry mention, the Tuesday versus Friday board game date, the unclear "my dog" phrasing, the "never imagined" remark given Toby's July arrival, and the breed and location of Buddy and of the cow spot.

Joanna and Nate reconnected on 21 January 2022 after a long gap and have stayed friendly, warm, and encouraging. They keep in regular contact and support each other's projects, but no in-person meetup is confirmed. On 12 May 2022, Joanna invited Nate to hike the trails in her town. He said it sounded like a plan, but no date was set, and that hiking trip remains the main open plan between them. On 25 May 2022, Nate opened by noting it had "been ages" since they last talked.

Joanna enjoys writing, reading, movies, nature, cooking and baking, and time with friends. She isn't into video games and prefers dramas, emotionally driven films, and romantic comedies. Acting was her first passion, but she now focuses mostly on writing, and when asked about returning to acting she said "never say never." She is allergic to reptiles, furred animals, and cockroaches, has no pets, and avoids dairy.

Nate enjoys video games and movies, especially action and sci-fi, and he enjoys classics. He sees fantasy and sci-fi as an escape, plays mainly for fun, and has recently started playing with people outside his usual circle. He has two pet turtles, which calm him when he is nervous, and on 15 April he dyed his hair purple to stand out. His gaming wins so far are a first Counter-Strike: Global Offensive tournament in January 2022 and a local Street Fighter tournament on 2 May. He mentioned a fourth tournament for May but has not reported on it.

Joanna's writing has moved steadily forward. On 23 January she finished her first screenplay, a drama-romance, and planned to submit it to film festivals, though no results have been reported. On 18 March she finished a second screenplay, a drama about a thirty-year-old woman on a road trip of self-discovery after a loss, drawn from her own experiences. Nate told her not to quit, and no submission has been reported. On 24 March she auditioned for a writing gig and is still waiting, feeling hopeful but anxious. On 21 April she joined a writers group and began working on a script called "Finding Home." On 20 May she said she had finished a third screenplay, deeply personal, about loss, identity, and connection. She said it was hard to write but that she is proud of it, and she credited Nate's and her friends' support with making the journey easier. It is unclear whether this is "Finding Home" or a separate project.

Food has been an ongoing thread. On 7 February Nate shared a dairy-free chocolate berry cake, and Joanna recommended "Little Women," which neither has discussed since. On 25 February Joanna said she can no longer eat dairy, and on 15 April Nate delivered a dairy-free coconut milk ice cream recipe. On 2 May Joanna shared a dairy-free vanilla cake, crediting his advice, and said she has been testing dairy-free desserts for friends and family.

Pets have also come up. On 20 May Nate introduced Max, a dog he recently adopted. On 25 May he reported meeting a friendly local couple with a dog while walking Max, and they agreed to arrange doggy playdates. He also sent Joanna a photo of a stuffed animal as a reminder of good vibes, which she said she would cherish. Joanna has said her allergies mean she doesn't want a pet.

Recommendations have gone both ways. On 21 April Nate recommended a fantasy and sci-fi book series, and on 2 May Joanna said she had watched "The Lord of the Rings" trilogy at his suggestion and loved it. Neither has reported back on the book series or "Little Women."

On 12 May Joanna shared a photo of a waterfall at Whispering Falls, saying nature makes her feel calm and present and that these trails made her want to write a drama. Nate said he might write a drama himself and suggested hiking together.

On 25 May Joanna said she can't wait to show Nate her finished script, that she values his opinion, and that she will keep him updated. Nate replied that he is there to support her. The open threads are the hiking trip, the screenplay submissions and writing gig result, the "Finding Home" project, Nate's reported fourth tournament, and the book and film recommendations.

She is allergic to reptiles, furred animals, and cockroaches, has no pets, and has avoided dairy since 25 February.
