John and James are two gamers who first spoke on 17 March 2022 at about 3:47 pm. Their conversations are friendly and personal, covering games, programming, dogs, goals, travel, work, romance, cooking, and other hobbies. James usually shares projects, achievements, outings, and photos. John usually shares new hobbies, ventures, and experiences, and he has come to turn to James when stressed. There have been twenty-five sessions, dated 4, 8, 11, and 23 May; 13, 16, and 19 June; 9 and 22 July; 6 and 10 August; 21 and 26 August; 1 and 4 September; 18 September; and 20 September 2022. Some sessions describe the friendship as reaching back to childhood, which does not fit their first conversation in March 2022. This has never been explained.

James has considered programming central to his life since college. He has worked with Python and C++, built a website, and made game mods. He writes goals in a notebook and says tracking progress keeps him motivated. In Session 13 he started a course combining gaming and programming. He is developing a game based on a character he sketched as a child. In the first session he offered to involve John in its HTML work, but this has not come up since. His proposed dog-walking app was never mentioned again. In Session 22, on 1 September 2022, he announced that his Unity strategy game was finished, crediting John's encouragement. It is not stated whether this is the childhood character game. In Session 25 he said a streamed game drew kind comments that left him inspired.

James has three dogs: Max, a shepherd; Daisy, a Labrador; and Ned, a pup he adopted from a Stamford shelter in early April 2022. Introducing the dogs to one another has been hard but is slowly working. In Session 18 he took "his puppy" to the clinic on 5 August. The puppy is unnamed, and Ned is the likeliest candidate but unconfirmed. On 9 August he took all three dogs to a beach outing, where he met Samantha. He calls his pets "the source of my joy."

James has played many games. He praised The Witcher 3's story and atmosphere, and his team reached an online tournament semifinal, playing mostly Apex Legends. He has played a turn-based strategy game and won an online tournament, but neither game is named. He uses games to relax, compares them to therapy, and promised to share his thoughts on RPGs or MOBAs, which never came. He enjoys 2D puzzle adventures like The Legend of Zelda.

James's romantic life is now one of the most significant threads. In Session 6 he shared a drawing of a woman in armor kneeling on a rock, based on a stranger he passed around 6 April. He fell for her at first sight, and she remains unidentified. He met Samantha at the beach on 9 August, and she gave him her phone number. He planned to call on 11 August, but the call was never described. In Session 23, on 4 September, he reported that on 3 September, at the theater, he asked Samantha to be his girlfriend, and she agreed. She loves theater. He said recent weeks had brought good and bad moments that felt overwhelming, but he is happy with her. They had also visited McGee's bar, where she revealed she loves a good lager. Whether that was the planned 27 August meeting is not stated. James invited John to a baseball game next Sunday, which would be 11 September, and promised to show him what Samantha looks like. Whether John attended is not recorded. This is James's first romantic relationship in the memory.

James also took up cooking. Two days before 4 September he signed up for a cooking class, though he had never liked cooking. He made a good omelette on his first try, and the class covers meringue and dough at $10 per session. He hoped to treat John to one of his creations and credited John's encouragement.

Travel and family are major threads. In the first session John preferred arcades to bowling because his fingers are too big for bowling balls, and James proposed trying VR gaming "next Saturday," which was never confirmed. In Session 6 James said he had visited Italy, Turkey, and Mexico, and suggested a trip with John next year. In Session 16 he announced tickets to Toronto, with plans for Vancouver. In Session 17 he reported the trip went great and that he had reached Nuuk. Toronto and Vancouver were never mentioned again. He brought souvenirs for John and for someone named Jill, whose relationship to John is not stated. In Session 9 James named pepperoni as his favorite pizza, John named Hawaiian, and James urged John to try prosciutto. In Session 13 they had a football rivalry. James hopes Liverpool wins the title, while John, a Manchester City fan, predicted City would win. James bet that Liverpool would finish higher, John accepted, and the stakes were never specified, so the bet will be settled at season's end.

John's life has been full of projects. He once suggested building mobile applications together, which has not been revisited. He is taking a programming class to refresh HTML and CSS. In Session 7 he was stuck on a difficult algorithm assignment. In Session 8 he started freelance programming, building a website for a local business, and getting payments working was the hardest part. Neither problem has a reported resolution. In Session 10 he organized a CS:GO tournament that raised money for a nearby dog shelter, and the leftover money bought groceries that they cooked for homeless people. In Session 11 he volunteered for a charitable foundation working with kids. In Session 12 he took second place in a local tournament. In Session 13 he got his dream job, starting July 2022, though the employer and role were not named. In Session 17 he started learning chess, and James advised him to study opening moves. No update has come since.

In Session 18, John said he had left his IT job after three years. It was frightening, but he wanted work that made a difference and matched his values, and he now loves his new job. This may be the Session 13 dream job, but the sessions do not say so. He wants to organize computer game tournaments in his state, starting with CS:GO and later adding Fortnite, and James offered financial help or advice. John very much wants a pet but is not ready yet, and James's offer to help him find one still stands. In Session 14 he recommended The Stormlight Archive, The Kingkiller Chronicle, and The Expanse. In Session 15 he asked to visit James's volunteering organization, but no late June visit was confirmed. In Session 19 he said he had been playing strategy and RPG games and was hooked on The Witcher 3. In Session 20 he joined an online programming group of skilled coders who want to use technology for good. He said he was not returning to programming work, which had been a one-time experience. He still wants to host eSports competitions and sees gaming as an escape.

In Session 21, John said he had been helping his younger siblings build a simple text-based adventure game. James suggested meeting at McGee's Pub, and they agreed on 27 August, John's day off. In Session 22, John said teaching his siblings had been fulfilling. For the first time he said plainly that he was going through difficult times and that it was good to have someone like James. James replied that he was there to talk or vent to. The cause of John's stress has never been discussed. In Session 23 John said his parents had just started learning to code from him, drawing the family closer. He also bought Sennheiser headphones and a Logitech mouse, and he still plans a family gaming night with his siblings for September 2022. Whether it happens is open.

In Session 24, on 18 September 2022, John returned after about two weeks and said much had changed. He had taken up board games and enjoyed "Dungeons of the Dragon." He described a vivid dream about a medieval castle with a labyrinth of puzzles and traps, and James shared a guitar sketch. John is into electronic and rock music and used to play drums, and James used to play guitar. Neither had recordings of past jams.

In Session 25, on 20 September 2022 at 8:56 pm, John returned after a few days. He had started a portable smoker venture and welded one from metal. His biggest news was that he had made his first mobile game, a 2D adventure with puzzles and exploration, launching next month, in October 2022. He shared a screenshot and a photo of a demon with a sword that appears to come from the game. He said he had kept the project secret because he would have been very upset to tell James about "her" in advance and then have it fail. That remark is not explained. He recommended a game design book that helped with the puzzles, and said he learns from tutorials, developer forums, and the magazine James recommended. James offered to test the game, and John promised to let him know when testing is ready. John said his week had been chaotic, and James urged him to rest. John agreed to make time for himself.

Several items remain open as of Session 25. James has not shared his thoughts on the RPG John recommended or on RPGs and MOBAs, and his turn-based and tournament games are still unnamed. The VR outing, the trip with John next year, and the Toronto and Vancouver parts of his trip are unconfirmed beyond Nuuk. The stranger behind James's character is unidentified, and the identities of Jill, the cat, and the puppy are unknown. Whether John attended the 11 September baseball game, and whether the 27 August McGee's meeting happened, are not recorded. John's algorithm project, freelance payment problem, and chess study have no reported resolution, and his new job has no named employer or role. Whether he visited the volunteering organization is unknown, and he owes James his prosciutto impressions. The football bet is unresolved, and the cause of John's stress is not stated. The dog-walking app, HTML collaboration, and James's comic game have gone quiet. The mobile game's October launch and James's offer to test it are pending. John's portable smoker venture, eSports competitions, online programming group, and teaching of his siblings and parents are active, and whether the September family gaming night happens is open.

Maria and John are friends who check in periodically about volunteering, fitness, family, work, John's political ambitions, pets, and leisure. Twenty-eight sessions have taken place, from 17 December 2022 through 5 August 2023. Maria volunteers at a homeless shelter and a dog shelter, does aerial yoga, joined a nearby church in May, and started a new gym routine in June. John does kickboxing, has been a firefighting brigade member since late July, and has a growing involvement with veterans' causes. Maria keeps her own notes on local politics and asked to be kept posted on John's meetings with local leaders, which he agreed to.

John's main political goal remains local office focused on education and infrastructure, both lacking in the area where he grew up. On 1 January 2023 he said he had failed a military aptitude test, which left him stressed. On 25 February he announced he was running again, calling it a "last run." The office, election date, and launch have never been named. He later retook the aptitude test with strong results, and on 2 April said he had graduated and was considering policymaking. On 18 April he mentioned blogging and a convention, with no stated link to the office. On 6 May he said he had decided to run again, and Maria said she was fully behind him. That day he also proposed a community infrastructure project after a power cut, aimed at West County, his old area, and Maria agreed to help win neighborhood backing. On 20 May he said he was busy with a petition supporting military veterans, again with no stated link to the office.

John's finances have been a steady stress. His car broke down on 10 April. On 16 June he announced a promotion to assistant manager, a stepping stone to bigger things the memory does not name. On 5 July he said work often felt like an uphill battle, but Maria's support kept him going. On 22 July he said he was enjoying a new job with an encouraging team, though it is unconfirmed whether this was the June promotion. On 5 August he said he had lost his job at a mechanical engineering company after it tanked. He had been looking into tech opportunities, Maria's push had helped him consider a change, and he said he may have found a job at a tech company needing his mechanical skills for its hardware team. Whether he accepted it is unconfirmed. Maria responded with sympathy and encouragement.

Family matters have also come up. On 3 June the family said goodbye to Max, a dog they had owned for ten years, and they are considering adopting a rescue dog, which Maria encouraged. On 3 August John mentioned his children directly for the first time, saying a recent visit to a military memorial had moved them deeply. Maria said younger generations need to learn to remember those who served, and John agreed that teaching respect for veterans matters.

John's public activity has grown more visible. On 3 July he took part in a veterans' rights march. On 7 July he said a severe flood the previous week had ruined many homes in his old area because of poor infrastructure. He was gathering people to discuss repairs, and Maria agreed to join. The meeting's date, place, and organizers were not given. On 17 July he visited a veterans' hospital and met an elderly veteran named Samuel, whose resilience reminded him why he wanted to join the military. He described an organization he works with as a family that supports each other, without naming it. Whether he has enlisted is not confirmed.

His public service has also widened into the fire brigade. On 31 July John said Maria's shelter work had made him think about how he could help, so he had just joined a firefighting brigade, which he called intense but rewarding. Its first call-out, on 23 July, saved a family from a burning building, and the team felt like family, reminding him of his military service. He has not linked the brigade to the office. On 3 August he asked family and friends to join a virtual support group and act as military advocates. It is unconfirmed whether this is the organization from 17 July. On 5 August he said he had not volunteered much lately, though he cares about it, and recalled helping renovate a rundown community center back home last year.

Maria's own work and life have also featured across these sessions. She started volunteering at the homeless shelter a year before the memory's latest session, after seeing a family struggling on the streets, and the work is fulfilling despite being tough. On 3 August she shared a photo of a group around a table and a note from a shelter resident named Cindy, and John called her inspiring. Her recent life has included a car accident on 2 July, helping her cousin find housing after the cousin left home in a hurry, church activities, a church hike that gave her peace, and baking for the shelter. On 4 August she took up community work with church friends, which she found rewarding. She has offered encouragement and practical help on networking, events, the infrastructure project, the petition, the flood meeting, and the possible rescue dog.

Support runs both ways. John encouraged Maria when she opened up in session 20, and in session 23 he asked for her ideas. In session 28 he thanked her repeatedly. Maria and John agreed that teamwork can accomplish a great deal.

Several threads remain open. The memory does not establish whether the petition, march, project, convention, hospital visit, organization, support group, brigade, or flood meeting connects to the office, which remains unnamed. It does not say what the fundraiser raised, whether the tech job is confirmed, or whether John has enlisted. It does not say whether the family adopts a rescue dog, what Maria's struggle involves, or whether her cousin has found housing. The flood meeting's date, place, and link to the party invitation are also unknown.

The 15 October session opened with Dave describing a rollercoaster week, including a lost deal and doubts about whether his effort was wasted. Calvin offered generic encouragement. Calvin then announced the new Ferrari, and Dave asked for a photo, which Calvin promised to share soon.

Several things have shifted over time. In March Calvin planned Japan before Boston. By July he spoke as if he lived in a Japanese mansion, and by early September he had a Boston flight. By mid-September his album was out and a tour was coming, and by October he described meeting collaborators in Boston. His tone has stayed upbeat, but his replies have grown shorter and vaguer. Joanna and Nate reconnected on 21 January 2022 after a long gap and have stayed friendly, warm, and encouraging. They keep in regular contact and support each other's projects. On 25 May 2022 Nate said it had "been ages" since they last talked. On 5 June he mentioned noticing a Spider-Man pin on Joanna's purse "last time we saw each other," so they have met in person at least once.

Joanna enjoys writing, reading, movies, nature, cooking and baking, and time with friends. She isn't into video games and prefers dramas, emotionally driven films, and romantic comedies. Acting was her first passion, but she now focuses mostly on writing, and when asked about returning to acting she said "never say never." She is allergic to reptiles, furred animals, and cockroaches, has no pets, and has avoided dairy since 25 February. Her favorite superhero is Spider-Man.

Nate enjoys video games and movies, especially action and sci-fi, and he also enjoys classics. He sees fantasy and sci-fi as an escape and plays mainly for fun, though he has recently started playing with people outside his usual circle. He has two pet turtles, which calm him when he is nervous. On 15 April he dyed his hair purple, and on 20 May he introduced Max, a dog he recently adopted. His favorite superhero is Iron Man, and a toy Iron Man figure in his room reminds him to keep working on his goals.

Nate's competitive gaming has produced several wins, including a Counter-Strike: Global Offensive tournament in January 2022, a local Street Fighter tournament on 2 May, and a regional tournament the week before 3 June, where he met new people. Some of them want to hang out, and he agreed to help them improve. He is organizing a gaming party about two weekends after 3 June, inviting tournament friends, old friends, and former teammates, with custom controller decorations for guests.

Joanna's writing has moved forward, with setbacks. She finished a drama-romance screenplay on 23 January, a drama about a thirty-year-old woman's road trip after a loss on 18 March, and a third, deeply personal screenplay about loss, identity, and connection on 20 May, though it is unclear whether that is "Finding Home," which she began on 21 April after joining a writers group. On 24 March she auditioned for a writing gig and is still waiting. On 3 June she received a generic rejection letter from a major company with no feedback, and Nate encouraged her. It is unclear which screenplay was submitted. On 5 June she said bits she wrote for a screenplay appeared on the big screen the day before, which she found nerve-wracking but inspiring.

Food has been an ongoing thread. Nate has shared dairy-free recipes, including a chocolate berry cake on 7 February and a coconut milk ice cream on 15 April. On 2 May Joanna shared a dairy-free vanilla cake, crediting his advice, and said she has been testing dairy-free desserts for friends and family.

Pets have also come up. On 25 May Nate met a friendly local couple with a dog while walking Max, and they agreed to arrange doggy playdates. Joanna has said her allergies mean she does not want a pet.

Recommendations have gone both ways. On 21 April Nate recommended a fantasy and sci-fi book series. On 2 May Joanna said she had loved "The Lord of the Rings" trilogy at his suggestion. Neither has reported back on the book series, and Joanna's suggestion of "Little Women" is also unanswered.

On 5 June Nate said he should start a cork board like Joanna's, and she recommended it, adding that he should be ready to explain it to friends. Hers holds quotes, photos, and a framed family picture that reminds her of their encouragement every day.

Hiking has been a recurring plan. On 12 May Joanna invited Nate to hike the trails near her town, and he said it sounded like a plan, but no date was set. On 3 June she said she was hiking with friends that weekend and did not mention Nate.

The open threads are the hiking trip, the screenplay submissions and writing gig result, "Finding Home" and the third screenplay, the film with Joanna's words, Nate's mid-June party, the tournament friends, the cork board, and the recommendations.

John and Tim have talked across twenty-eight sessions, from 21 May 2023 to 7 January 2024. John is a basketball shooting guard who recently signed with the Minnesota Wolves, which he has confirmed as his team. His goals include improving his shooting, winning a championship, building his brand through endorsements, and eventually inspiring others, possibly through a foundation. Tim's interests center on Harry Potter, Game of Thrones, and fantasy novels, and he has recently taken up music. The two consistently encourage each other's dreams.

On 11 August he said he wanted to help disadvantaged kids. On 17 October he said the season was over and that he had been mentoring younger players. On 6 December he shared a trophy photo whose competition is unconfirmed. On 11 December he reported a career-high in assists against a rival, and on 16 December a close game won on the final buzzer. On 19 December he said he had landed a deal with a renowned outdoor gear company, with the company and terms not named.

John's personal life has come up as well. On 2 October he said he and his girlfriend had held a small greenhouse wedding. He named LeBron James his favorite player. In November he said he and his wife had road-tripped along the European coastline and offered to mail Tim his honey garlic chicken recipe, which is unconfirmed as sent. On 1 December he said he had started yoga, with Warrior II as his favorite pose. On 16 December he confirmed a foot injury that had cost him several games and said he was doing daily physical therapy.

Tim's activity has followed his reading, writing, and studies. In June he joined a fantasy literature forum. In August he spoke with a California Harry Potter fan about a possible collaboration, which remains open. On 2 October he recommended a Patrick Rothfuss novel to John, and on 13 October he suggested running shoes. He attended a UK Harry Potter conference, though his UK story did not go as he wanted. On 1 December a tough exam shook his confidence, and on 6 December he said he had started learning violin. On 8 December John named "Dune" as his current read and admitted he had not yet read George R. R. Martin's books, and Tim recommended "A Dance with Dragons."

In session 26, on 26 December, John said he had started doing seminars on sports and marketing and described organizing a basketball camp for kids "last summer," a claim that conflicts with his August statement. John's favorite character is Aragorn, and he said he had been to Paris and found the view from the Eiffel Tower incredible. Tim said he has not been yet.

In session 28, on 7 January 2024, Tim shared his biggest news. On 5 January he learned he had been accepted into a study abroad program, and next month he leaves for a semester in Galway, Ireland, chosen for its arts scene and Irish music. John and James are two gamers who first spoke on 17 March 2022 at about 3:47 pm. Their conversations are friendly and personal, covering games, programming, dogs, goals, travel, work, romance, cooking, and other hobbies. James usually shares projects, achievements, outings, and photos. John usually shares new hobbies, ventures, and experiences, and he has come to turn to James when stressed. There have been twenty-six sessions, dated 4, 8, 11, and 23 May; 13, 16, and 19 June; 9 and 22 July; 6 and 10 August; 21 and 26 August; 1 and 4 September; 18 September; 20 September; and 3 October 2022. Some sessions describe the friendship as reaching back to childhood, which does not fit their first conversation in March 2022. This has never been explained.

James has considered programming central to his life since college. He has worked with Python and C++, built a website, and made game mods. He writes goals in a notebook and says tracking progress keeps him motivated. In Session 13 he started a course combining gaming and programming. He is developing a game based on a character he sketched as a child, and in the first session he offered to involve John in its HTML work, but this has not come up since. His proposed dog-walking app was never mentioned again. In Session 22, on 1 September 2022, he announced that his Unity strategy game was finished, crediting John's encouragement. It is not stated whether this is the childhood character game. In Session 25 he said a streamed game drew kind comments that left him inspired.

James has three dogs: Max, a shepherd; Daisy, a Labrador; and Ned, a pup he adopted from a Stamford shelter in early April 2022. Introducing the dogs to one another has been hard but is slowly working. In Session 18 he took "his puppy" to the clinic on 5 August. The puppy is unnamed, and Ned is the likeliest candidate but unconfirmed. On 9 August he took all three dogs to a beach outing, where he met Samantha. He calls his pets "the source of my joy."

James has played many games. He praised the story and atmosphere of The Witcher 3, and his team reached an online tournament semifinal, playing mostly Apex Legends. He has also played a turn-based strategy game and won an online tournament, but neither game is named. He uses games to relax and enjoys 2D puzzle adventures such as The Legend of Zelda. He promised to share his thoughts on RPGs or MOBAs, but never did. In Session 26, on 3 October 2022, he said he had just bought a new video card and was excited to play again. He described himself as super into RPGs and asked John whether Cyberpunk 2077 was worth his attention. John said he had played it, found the world immersive and the story excellent, and recommended it. This is the first specific RPG James has named in the memory.

James's romantic life is now one of the most significant threads. In Session 6 he shared a drawing of a woman in armor kneeling on a rock, based on a stranger he passed around 6 April. He fell for her at first sight, and she remains unidentified. He met Samantha at the beach on 9 August, and she gave him her phone number. He planned to call on 11 August, but the call was never described. In Session 23, on 4 September, he reported that on 3 September, at the theater, he asked Samantha to be his girlfriend, and she agreed. She loves theater. He said recent weeks had brought good and bad moments that felt overwhelming, but he was happy with her. They had also visited McGee's bar, where she revealed she loves a good lager. Whether that was the planned 27 August meeting is not stated. James invited John to a baseball game on Sunday, 11 September, and promised to show him what Samantha looks like. Whether John attended is not recorded. This is James's first romantic relationship in the memory.

James also took up cooking. Two days before 4 September he signed up for a cooking class, though he had never liked cooking. He made a good omelette on his first try, and he hoped to treat John to one of his creations, crediting John's encouragement.

Travel and family are major threads. In the first session John preferred arcades to bowling, and James proposed trying VR gaming "next Saturday," which was never confirmed. In Session 6 James said he had visited Italy, Turkey, and Mexico, and suggested a trip with John next year. In Session 16 he announced tickets to Toronto, with plans for Vancouver. In Session 17 he reported that the trip went great and that he had reached Nuuk. Toronto and Vancouver were never mentioned again. He brought souvenirs for John and for someone named Jill, whose relationship to John is not stated. In Session 13 James and John had a football rivalry. James hopes Liverpool wins the title, while John, a Manchester City fan, predicted City would win. James bet that Liverpool would finish higher, John accepted, and the stakes were never specified, so the bet will be settled at season's end.

John's life has been full of projects. He once suggested building mobile applications together, which has not been revisited. He is taking a programming class to refresh HTML and CSS. In Session 8 he started freelance programming, building a website for a local business, and getting payments working was the hardest part. Neither that problem nor an earlier algorithm assignment has a reported resolution. In Session 10 he organized a CS:GO tournament that raised money for a nearby dog shelter. In Session 11 he volunteered for a charitable foundation working with kids. In Session 12 he took second place in a local tournament. In Session 13 he got his dream job, starting July 2022, though the employer and role were not named. In Session 17 he started learning chess, and James advised him to study opening moves. No update has come since.

In Session 18, John said he had left his IT job after three years. It was frightening, but he wanted work that matched his values, and he now loves his new job. This may be the Session 13 dream job, but the sessions do not say so. He wants to organize computer game tournaments in his state, starting with CS:GO and later adding Fortnite, and James offered financial help or advice. John very much wants a pet but is not ready yet, and James's offer to help him find one still stands. In Session 15 he asked to visit James's volunteering organization, but no visit was confirmed. In Session 20 he joined an online programming group of skilled coders who want to use technology for good. He said he was not returning to programming work, which had been a one-time experience, and he still wants to host eSports competitions. Session 26 complicates that statement.

In Session 21, John said he had been helping his younger siblings build a simple text-based adventure game. James suggested meeting at McGee's Pub, and they agreed on 27 August, John's day off. In Session 22, John said plainly that he was going through difficult times and that it was good to have someone like James. James replied that he was there to talk or vent to. The cause of John's stress has never been discussed. In Session 23 John said his parents had just started learning to code from him, drawing the family closer. He still planned a family gaming night with his siblings for September 2022. Whether it happened is open.

In Session 24, on 18 September 2022, John returned after about two weeks and said much had changed. He had taken up board games and described a vivid dream about a medieval castle with a labyrinth of puzzles and traps. He is into electronic and rock music and used to play drums, while James used to play guitar. Neither had recordings of past jams.

In Session 25, on 20 September 2022, John said he had started a portable smoker venture and welded one from metal. His biggest news was that he had made his first mobile game, a 2D adventure with puzzles and exploration, launching in October 2022. He said he had kept the project secret because he would have been very upset to tell James about "her" in advance and then have it fail. That remark is not explained. James offered to test the game, and John promised to let him know when testing was ready. John said his week had been chaotic, and James urged him to rest.

In Session 26, on 3 October 2022, John said he had been busy for a few weeks but was pushing through. He had received an email offering a volunteer role as a programming mentor for game developers with a game development non-profit, which he described as the perfect start to a career combining his two loves, gaming and helping people. He was excited to share his knowledge and boost his own skills. Whether he accepted the role, and how it relates to the Session 13 job, is not stated. James shared a photo of his new computer case with a red light, and the session ends with James promising to tell John what he thinks of Cyberpunk 2077.

Several items remain open as of Session 26. James has not yet reported on the RPG John recommended or on Cyberpunk 2077, and his turn-based and tournament games are still unnamed. The VR outing, the trip with John next year, and the Toronto and Vancouver parts of his trip are unconfirmed beyond Nuuk. The stranger behind James's character is unidentified, and the identities of Jill, the cat, and the puppy are unknown. Whether John attended the 11 September baseball game, and whether the 27 August McGee's meeting happened, are not recorded. John's algorithm project, freelance payment problem, and chess study have no reported resolution. His new job has no named employer or role, and it is unclear whether the mentoring role is separate from it. Whether he visited the volunteering organization is unknown, and he still owes James his impressions of prosciutto. The football bet is unresolved, and the cause of John's stress is not stated. The dog-walking app, HTML collaboration, and James's childhood character game have gone quiet. The mobile game's October launch and James's offer to test it are pending. John's portable smoker venture, eSports ambitions, online programming group, and teaching of his siblings and parents are active, and whether the September family gaming night happened is open.

Calvin and Dave are casual acquaintances who have talked across twenty-four sessions, from 23 March to 19 October 2023, always in a friendly, upbeat tone. Dave usually offers support, invitations, and help, and Calvin usually replies with enthusiastic praise. Calvin presents himself as a musician. Dave presents himself as a car enthusiast who became a shop owner and, by mid-September, a Boston resident with a finished vintage-car restoration.

Calvin's account has grown more expansive over time. On 23 March he mentioned a major life change and said he planned Japan before Boston, and on 26 March he said he had written new tunes. On 21 June he shared a mountain-town photo, calling it his living-room view in Japan, though he had not been there yet. On 7 July he said he was working with Japanese artists, and on 21 July that he was turning his mansion into a recording studio. On 3 August he named his red car's make, a Ferrari, but not the model, and said he had performed with "the boys" without naming them. On 14 August he said he had finished touring, ending in Japan, which conflicts with his earlier accounts. On 22 August he said he had a deal to keep working with Frank Ocean, whom he met at a Tokyo festival. On 31 August he started a music video shoot on a Miami beach. On 2 September he shared a boarding pass for a Boston flight. On 13 September he said his album was released and a tour was coming, naming no cities. On 4 October he claimed to have met artists in Boston. On 15 October he said he got a new Ferrari, sharing a photo of a black sports car, which conflicts with the red car of August.

Dave's account has also shifted. On 1 May he said he had opened his car shop. On 14 August he visited a San Francisco workshop and shared a photo of a broken-engine car he was restoring. On 15 September he said he had attended a rock concert "here in Boston," his first placement of himself there, and shared a photo of his finished vintage car. On 22 September he reported a strange noise from a vintage Mustang's engine, and both agreed to a jam session. On 4 October he asked how Calvin's Boston meeting was arranged; neither answered. On 8 October he called cars his therapy and his job, rooted in childhood hours in his dad's garage.

The 15 October session opened with Dave describing a rollercoaster week and doubts about whether his effort was wasted, and Calvin offered generic encouragement. Dave then said he had just returned from a music festival, giving no location or dates. Calvin announced the new Ferrari and promised to share its photo soon.

The 19 October session, four days later, was Calvin's longest telling yet. He said he had started touring with Frank Ocean and shared several concert photos, one of which he said was taken in Tokyo. He dated the partnership to "August last year" at a festival, which does not match his 22 August account. He said he is going to Tokyo next month after the tour ends, and that he was excited to explore Shibuya and Shinjuku. Dave did most of the asking, sharing internet photos of Tokyo streets and a ramen bowl from Boston, and inviting Calvin to try ramen. Calvin's replies were brief, and he said he had never tried ramen, though he earlier spoke of trying it again. He did not share the promised Ferrari photo or explain the Boston meeting.

Several things have shifted over time. In March Calvin planned Japan before Boston. By July he spoke as if he lived in a Japanese mansion, and by early September he had a Boston flight. By mid-September his album was out and a tour was coming, and by October he described meeting collaborators in Boston. By 19 October touring was underway, with a Tokyo trip after it. His tone has stayed upbeat, but his specifics have grown vaguer. Since 22 August Calvin has done most of the telling, while Dave has mostly listened, asked questions, and repeated invitations.

Open items include Calvin's unnamed Ferrari model, the conflict between the red car of August and the black car of October, and the still-unshared Ferrari photo. Also unresolved are the Japan living-room view, the unexplained "the boys" performance, and the tour timing, since he said on 14 August he had finished touring, on 13 September described one as upcoming, and on 19 October described one as underway. Whether Calvin has reached Boston is unconfirmed, and the meeting's arrangement and the artists' identities remain unclear. It is also unclear where Dave is based, whether the Mustang relates to his restoration, and how the Miami shoot fits Calvin's plans.

The most concrete plans are Calvin's Boston trip and Dave's promised attendance at a show, the ongoing tour and Calvin's Tokyo trip next month, Dave's garage invitation and mountain trip, the Miami video, and the agreed jam session. Calvin's next expected steps are to share the Ferrari photo, report on Tokyo and ramen, and explain the Boston collaboration. Dave is likely to follow up on the garage visit, the jam session, the Mustang's progress, and whether Calvin has tried ramen.

On 8 May 2023, at about 1:56 pm, Caroline and Melanie caught up. Melanie said she was swamped with her kids and work. Caroline said she had attended an LGBTQ support group the day before, on 7 May 2023, and found it very powerful, especially the transgender stories. It made her feel happy, thankful, and accepted, and gave her the courage to embrace herself. She plans to continue her education and explore career options, and she is most interested in counseling or mental health work so she can support people facing similar issues. Melanie said Caroline would make a great counselor because of her empathy. Caroline shared a photo of a dog walking past a wall with a painting of a woman. Melanie shared a photo of a sunset over a lake she painted in 2022, which is special to her. Caroline complimented its blended colors, and Melanie said painting helps her express her feelings and relax after a long day. Both agreed that relaxing and self-expression matter for self-care. Caroline then left to research career options, and Melanie went swimming with her kids.

On 25 May 2023, at about 1:14 pm, the two spoke again. Melanie said she had run a charity race for mental health "last Saturday," which would be 20 May 2023, and found it rewarding and thought-provoking. Caroline called the race great and said she was proud of Melanie. Melanie said self-care is really important, because looking after herself helps her look after her family. She carves out daily me-time for running, reading, or playing her violin, and called it a work in progress. She was thinking about a family camping trip in June 2023.

Caroline's update was a major one. She is researching adoption agencies, a long-held dream of giving a loving home to kids who need one. She shared a photo of one agency's sign and said she felt hopeful and optimistic. She chose the agency because it helps LGBTQ+ people adopt, and its inclusivity and support spoke to her. She knows single parenting will be tough but is up for the challenge. Melanie said she would be an awesome mom.

On 9 June 2023, at 7:55 pm, the two reconnected in Session 3. Caroline said she had given a talk at a school event the previous week. She shared her transgender journey, encouraged students to get involved in the LGBTQ community, and reflected on how far she has come since starting her transition three years earlier. She said the audience seemed inspired to be better allies. Melanie praised her courage. Both agreed that sharing vulnerable stories helps people feel less alone. Melanie said she wants to be courageous for her family, who motivate her. Caroline said her friends, family, and mentors are her rocks.

Caroline shared a photo from a recent meetup with friends, whom she has known for four years since moving from her home country, and who helped her through a tough breakup. Melanie said she is lucky to have her husband and kids, and shared a family photo in front of a waterfall. She said she and her husband have been married five years, and shared a photo from her wedding day. Melanie then shared a photo of a family picnic with games and good food. Both agreed that family time makes them feel most alive and happy.

Taken together, Caroline moved from exploring education and counseling careers in early May 2023, to pursuing single-parent adoption through an LGBTQ+-inclusive agency by late May, to speaking publicly about her transgender journey by June. She has repeatedly drawn strength from her friends, mentors, and community. Melanie moved from feeling swamped to building self-care into her routine, running a charity race, and planning a family camping trip while describing a happy married family life. Across all three sessions, the two women consistently encouraged each other, and Melanie repeatedly praised Caroline's empathy and courage.

Dave usually offers support, invitations, and help, and Calvin usually replies with enthusiastic praise. Calvin presents himself as a musician. Dave presents himself as a car enthusiast who opened a car shop and, by mid-September, described himself as a Boston resident with a finished vintage-car restoration.

On 14 August he said he had finished touring, ending in Japan, which conflicts with earlier accounts. He started a Miami beach video shoot on 31 August, shared a Boston flight boarding pass on 2 September, and on 13 September said his album was out and a tour was coming, naming no cities. On 4 October he claimed to have met artists in Boston. On 15 October he announced a new Ferrari, a black sports car that conflicts with August's red car, and promised a photo.

On 19 October Calvin said he had started touring with Frank Ocean and shared concert photos, one said to be from Tokyo. He dated the partnership to "August last year," which does not match his 22 August account. He said he would go to Tokyo next month after the tour, and he said he had never tried ramen, though he had earlier spoken of trying it again.

Dave's account has shifted too. On 1 May he said he had opened his car shop. On 14 August he shared a photo of a broken-engine car he was restoring. On 15 September he said he attended a rock concert "here in Boston," his first placement of himself there, and shared a photo of his finished vintage car. On 22 September he reported a strange noise from a vintage Mustang's engine, and both agreed to a jam session. On 4 October he asked how Calvin's Boston meeting was arranged, and neither answered. On 8 October he called cars his therapy and job, rooted in childhood hours in his dad's garage. On 15 October he said he had returned from a music festival, with no location given. On 19 October he shared Tokyo street photos and a Boston ramen bowl, and invited Calvin to try ramen.

In the 23 October session, Dave asked about the tour and how Calvin balanced work and personal life. Calvin called the tour incredible but gave no dates or places, and said he leans on friends and his team. He said his songs draw on people's struggles and that music is his own therapy. Dave shared a garage photo, said his interest began at age ten when he fixed a neighbor's old car, and said he restored a car last year, sold it to a collector, and now has a new project. Both shared concert crowd photos. Calvin did not mention the promised Ferrari photo, the Boston meeting, Tokyo, or ramen.

Several things have shifted over time. By July Calvin spoke as if he lived in a Japanese mansion, by early September he had a Boston flight, and by 19 October touring was underway with a Tokyo trip after it. His specifics have grown vaguer. Since 22 August Calvin has done most of the telling while Dave listens, asks questions, and repeats invitations. Open items include Calvin's unnamed Ferrari model, the conflict between the red and black cars, and the unshared Ferrari photo. Also unresolved are the Japan living-room view, the unexplained "boys" performance, and the tour timing, since Calvin said he had finished touring in August, described one as upcoming in September, and described one as underway in October. Whether Calvin has reached Boston is unconfirmed, as are the meeting's arrangement and the artists' identities. It is also unclear where Dave is based, whether the Mustang relates to his restoration, and how the Miami shoot fits Calvin's plans.

The most concrete plans are Calvin's Boston trip, Dave's promised attendance at a show, the ongoing tour and Calvin's Tokyo trip next month, Dave's garage invitation and mountain trip, the Miami video, and the agreed jam session. Calvin's next expected steps are to share the Ferrari photo, report on Tokyo and ramen, and explain the Boston collaboration. Dave is likely to follow up on the garage visit, the jam session, the Mustang, the new project, and whether Calvin has tried ramen.

Joanna and Nate reconnected on 21 January 2022 after a long gap and have stayed friendly, warm, and encouraging. They keep in regular contact and support each other's projects. On 5 June 2022 Nate mentioned noticing a Spider-Man pin on Joanna's purse "last time we saw each other," so they have met in person at least once. On 14 August (Session 18) Joanna opened with "long time no talk," and they caught up warmly.

Joanna enjoys writing, reading, movies, nature, cooking and baking, and time with friends. She isn't into video games and prefers dramas, emotionally driven films, and romantic comedies. Acting was her first passion, but she now focuses mostly on writing, and when asked about returning to acting she said "never say never." She is allergic to reptiles, furred animals, and cockroaches, has no pets, and has avoided dairy since 25 February. Her favorite superhero is Spider-Man.

Nate enjoys video games and movies, especially action, sci-fi, and classics. He plays mainly for fun and sees fantasy and sci-fi as an escape. He has two pet turtles, which calm him when he is nervous, and he is part of a vegan diet group. On 15 April he dyed his hair purple, and on 20 May he introduced Max, a dog he recently adopted. His favorite superhero is Iron Man. By 14 August he had started teaching people to make dairy-free desserts.

Nate's competitive gaming has produced several wins. In mid-June he held a gaming party for tournament and old friends, and by 24 June reported seven attendees. On 10 July he announced his fourth video game tournament win and said he is proud to earn money doing what he loves. No next party has been reported.

Joanna's writing has moved forward, with setbacks. She finished a drama-romance screenplay on 23 January, a road-trip drama on 18 March, and a deeply personal screenplay on 20 May, which may be "Finding Home," begun on 21 April. On 24 March she auditioned for a writing gig and is still waiting to hear back. On 3 June she received a generic rejection letter, and Nate encouraged her. On 5 June she said bits she wrote appeared on the big screen. On 24 June she submitted a screenplay to a film contest; the result is unknown. On 10 July she took a research road trip to Woodhaven, a small Midwest town that sparked ideas for her next script. She also said she had started her first book, a story exploring loss, redemption, and forgiveness.

On 14 August Joanna described writing as the biggest part of her life, with her journal as her rock. A stranger had written to her after reading a blog post about a hard moment in her life, saying her story had comforted them. Nate told her she was changing lives.

Food has been an ongoing thread. Nate has shared dairy-free recipes, including a chocolate berry cake on 7 February and a coconut milk ice cream on 15 April. John and James are two gamers who first spoke on 17 March 2022 at about 3:47 pm. Their conversations are friendly and personal, covering games, programming, dogs, goals, travel, work, romance, cooking, and other hobbies. James usually shares projects, achievements, outings, and photos. John usually shares new hobbies, ventures, and experiences, and he has come to turn to James when stressed. There have been twenty-seven sessions, the most recent on 13 October 2022. Earlier sessions fell on 4, 8, 11, and 23 May; 13, 16, and 19 June; 9 and 22 July; 6 and 10 August; 21 and 26 August; 1 and 4 September; 18 and 20 September; and 3 October 2022. Some sessions describe the friendship as reaching back to childhood, which does not fit their first conversation in March 2022. This has never been explained.

James has considered programming central to his life since college. He has worked with Python and C++, built a website, and made game mods. In Session 13 he started a course combining gaming and programming. He is developing a game based on a character he sketched as a child, and in the first session he offered to involve John in its HTML work, but this has not come up since. His dog-walking app was never mentioned again. In Session 22, on 1 September 2022, he announced that his Unity strategy game was finished, crediting John's encouragement. In Session 25 he said a streamed game drew kind comments. In Session 27, on 13 October 2022, he said he had released his first game to the gaming community, which was very fulfilling. He credited The Witcher 3's world and story for inspiring him and said he is now ready to make games in different genres. The session does not name the game or link it to his earlier projects.

James has three dogs: Max, a shepherd; Daisy, a Labrador; and Ned, a pup adopted from a Stamford shelter in early April 2022. Introducing them to one another has been hard but is slowly working. In Session 18 he took "his puppy" to the clinic on 5 August. The puppy is unnamed, and Ned is the likeliest candidate but unconfirmed. On 9 August he took all three dogs to a beach outing, where he met Samantha. He calls his pets "the source of my joy."

James has played many games. He praised the story and atmosphere of The Witcher 3, and his team reached an online tournament semifinal, playing mostly Apex Legends. He also won an online tournament playing a turn-based strategy game, though neither game is named. He enjoys 2D puzzle adventures such as The Legend of Zelda. In Session 26, on 3 October 2022, he said he had just bought a new video card, called himself super into RPGs, and asked whether Cyberpunk 2077 was worth his attention. John had played it and recommended it. This is the first specific RPG James has named. In the same session he shared a photo of his new computer case with a red light and promised to report his opinion of Cyberpunk 2077. He has not yet done so.

James's romantic life is one of the most significant threads. In Session 6 he shared a drawing of a woman in armor kneeling on a rock, based on a stranger he passed around 6 April. He fell for her at first sight, and she remains unidentified. He met Samantha at the beach on 9 August, and she gave him her phone number. He planned to call on 11 August, but the call was never described. In Session 23, on 4 September, he reported that on 3 September, at the theater, he asked Samantha to be his girlfriend, and she agreed. She loves theater. He said recent weeks had brought good and bad moments that felt overwhelming, but he was happy with her. They had also visited McGee's bar, where she revealed she loves a good lager. Whether that was the planned 27 August meeting is not stated. James invited John to a baseball game on Sunday, 11 September, and promised to show him what Samantha looks like. Whether John attended is not recorded. This is James's first romantic relationship in the memory.

James also took up cooking, signing up for a class two days before 4 September despite never having liked it. He made a good omelette on his first try and hoped to treat John to one of his creations.

In the first session John preferred arcades to bowling, and James proposed trying VR gaming "next Saturday," which was never confirmed. In Session 6 James said he had visited Italy, Turkey, and Mexico, and suggested a trip with John next year. In Session 16 he announced tickets to Toronto, with plans for Vancouver. In Session 17 he reported that the trip went great and he had reached Nuuk. Toronto and Vancouver were never mentioned again. He brought souvenirs for John and for someone named Jill, whose relationship to John is not stated. In Session 13 James and John had a football rivalry. James hopes Liverpool wins the title, while John, a Manchester City fan, predicted City would win. James bet that Liverpool would finish higher, John accepted, and the stakes were never specified, so the bet will be settled at season's end.

John's life has been full of projects. He once suggested building mobile applications together, which has not been revisited. He is taking a programming class to refresh HTML and CSS. In Session 8 he started freelance programming, building a website for a local business, and getting payments working was the hardest part. Neither that problem nor an earlier algorithm assignment has a reported resolution. In Session 10 he organized a CS:GO tournament that raised money for a nearby dog shelter. In Session 11 he volunteered for a charitable foundation working with kids. In Session 12 he took second place in a local tournament. In Session 13 he got his dream job, starting July 2022, though the employer and role were not named. In Session 17 he started learning chess, and James advised him to study opening moves. No update has come since.

In Session 18, John said he had left his IT job after three years to find work matching his values, and he now loves his new job. This may be the Session 13 dream job, but the sessions do not say so. He wants to organize computer game tournaments in his state, starting with CS:GO and later adding Fortnite, and James offered financial help or advice. John very much wants a pet but is not ready yet, and James's offer to help him find one still stands. In Session 15 he asked to visit James's volunteering organization, but no visit was confirmed. In Session 20 he joined an online programming group of skilled coders who want to use technology for good. He said he was not returning to programming work, which had been a one-time experience, and he still wants to host eSports competitions. Session 26 complicates that statement. John said he had received an email offering a volunteer role as a programming mentor for game developers with a game development non-profit, which he called the perfect start to a career combining gaming and helping people. Whether he accepted, and how it relates to the Session 13 job, is not stated. In Session 27 he said he and his programmer friends had organized an online competition the previous week, and it was awesome to see everyone show off their skills. His eSports and programming activities therefore appear to be ongoing.

In Session 21, John said he had been helping his younger siblings build a simple text-based adventure game. James suggested meeting at McGee's Pub, and they agreed on 27 August, John's day off. In Session 22, John said he was going through difficult times and that it was good to have someone like James, who replied that he was there to talk or vent to. The cause of John's stress has never been discussed. In Session 23 John said his parents had just started learning to code from him, drawing the family closer, and he still planned a family gaming night with his siblings for September 2022. Whether it happened is open.

In Session 24, on 18 September 2022, John returned after about two weeks, having taken up board games. He is into electronic and rock music and used to play drums, while James used to play guitar. Neither had recordings of past jams.

In Session 25, on 20 September 2022, John said he had started a portable smoker venture and welded one from metal. His biggest news was that he had made his first mobile game, a 2D adventure with puzzles and exploration, launching in October 2022. He had kept it secret because he would have been very upset to tell James about "her" in advance and then have it fail. That remark is not explained. James offered to test the game, and John promised to let him know when testing was ready. John said his week had been chaotic, and James urged him to rest.

Open items as of Session 27 are numerous. James has not yet reported on Cyberpunk 2077 or the RPG John recommended, and his turn-based and tournament games are unnamed. The VR outing, the next-year trip with John, and the Toronto and Vancouver legs are unconfirmed beyond Nuuk. The stranger behind James's drawing, the identities of Jill, the cat, and the puppy, and the link between his new game and earlier projects are unknown. Whether John attended the 11 September baseball game and whether the 27 August McGee's meeting happened are not recorded. John's algorithm project, freelance payment problem, and chess study have no reported resolution. His new job's employer and role are unnamed, and it is unclear whether the mentoring role is separate. Whether he visited the volunteering organization is unknown, and he still owes James his impressions of prosciutto. The football bet is unresolved, and the cause of John's stress is not stated. The dog-walking app, HTML collaboration, and childhood character game have gone quiet. The mobile game's October launch and James's offer to test it are pending. John's portable smoker venture, eSports ambitions, online programming group, and teaching of his family are active, and whether the September family gaming night happened is open.

John and James are two gamers who first spoke on 17 March 2022 at about 3:47 pm. Their conversations are friendly and personal, covering games, programming, dogs, goals, travel, work, romance, cooking, and other hobbies. James usually shares projects, achievements, outings, and photos. John usually shares new hobbies, ventures, and experiences, and he has come to turn to James when stressed. There have been twenty-eight sessions, the most recent on 21 October 2022. Earlier sessions fell on 4, 8, 11, and 23 May; 13, 16, and 19 June; 9 and 22 July; 6 and 10 August; 21 and 26 August; 1 and 4 September; 18 and 20 September; and 3, 13, and 21 October 2022. Some sessions describe the friendship as reaching back to childhood, which does not fit their first conversation in March 2022. This has never been explained.

James has considered programming central to his life since college. He has worked with Python and C++, built a website, and made game mods. In Session 13 he started a course combining gaming and programming. He is developing a game based on a character he sketched as a child, and he once offered to involve John in its HTML work, but this has gone quiet, as has his dog-walking app. In Session 22, on 1 September 2022, he announced his Unity strategy game was finished, crediting John's encouragement. In Session 27, on 13 October, he said he had released his first game to the gaming community and was now ready for different genres, inspired by The Witcher 3. That game was never named or linked to his earlier projects.

James has three dogs: Max, a shepherd; Daisy, a Labrador; and Ned, a pup adopted from a Stamford shelter in early April 2022. Introducing them has been hard but is slowly working. He took "his puppy," unnamed and possibly Ned, to the clinic on 5 August, and on 9 August he took all three to a beach, where he met Samantha. In Session 28 his mother visited with an army friend, and James shared a photo of the two beside an unidentified dog. The friend was described both as still serving and as retired, which went unaddressed.

James has played many games. He praised The Witcher 3's story and atmosphere, and his team reached an online tournament semifinal playing mostly Apex Legends. He also won an online tournament in an unnamed turn-based strategy game, and he enjoys 2D puzzle adventures such as The Legend of Zelda. As a child he played Super Mario and Zelda for hours on his first gaming system, a Nintendo console. In Session 26 he bought a new video card, called himself super into RPGs, and asked about Cyberpunk 2077, which John recommended. In Session 28, on 21 October, he said he had tried it on 20 October and found it great and addictive. John said the game has many unexpected turns, that its choices are hard and can be life-changing, and that James need not befriend every character. Around 18 October a power outage during the big reveal of an unnamed game cost James unsaved progress and hours of waiting.

James's romantic life is one of the most significant threads. In Session 6 he shared a drawing of a woman in armor kneeling on a rock, based on a stranger he passed around 6 April. He fell for her at first sight, and she remains unidentified. He met Samantha at the beach on 9 August, and she gave him her number. He planned to call on 11 August, but the call was never described. In Session 23, on 4 September, he reported that at the theater on 3 September he asked Samantha to be his girlfriend, and she agreed. She loves theater, and they had visited McGee's bar, where she revealed she loves a good lager. He said recent weeks had brought good and bad moments that felt overwhelming, but he was happy with her. He invited John to a baseball game on Sunday, 11 September, promising to show him Samantha; whether John attended is not recorded. Samantha has not appeared since, and the relationship's status is unreported. This is James's first romantic relationship in the memory.

James took up cooking, signing up for a class two days before 4 September despite never having liked it, and he made a good omelette on his first try. He hoped to treat John to one of his creations, and John still owes him his impressions of prosciutto. In Session 6 James had visited Italy, Turkey, and Mexico and suggested a trip with John next year. In Session 16 he announced tickets to Toronto, with plans for Vancouver; in Session 17 he reported he had reached Nuuk, and Toronto and Vancouver were never mentioned again. In Session 13 the two made a football bet. James hopes Liverpool wins the title, while John, a Manchester City fan, predicted City would win. James bet Liverpool would finish higher, John accepted, and the stakes were never specified. The VR outing James proposed in the first session was never confirmed.

John's life has been full of projects. He once suggested building mobile applications together, a idea not revisited. He is refreshing HTML and CSS in a class. In Session 8 he started freelance programming, building a website for a local business, and getting payments working was the hardest part. No resolution is reported for that problem or for an earlier algorithm assignment. In Session 10 he organized a CS:GO tournament that raised money for a dog shelter, and in Session 11 he volunteered for a charitable foundation working with kids. In Session 12 he took second place in a local tournament. In Session 13 he got his dream job, starting July 2022, though the employer and role were not named. In Session 17 he started learning chess, and James advised him to study opening moves; there has been no update since.

In Session 18 John said he had left his IT job after three years for work matching his values and now loves his new job. This may be the dream job, but the sessions do not say so. He wants to organize computer game tournaments in his state, starting with CS:GO and adding Fortnite later, and James offered financial help or advice. He very much wants a pet but is not ready yet, and James's offer to help him find one still stands. In Session 20 he joined an online group of skilled coders who want to use technology for good, and he said he was not returning to programming work, though he still wanted to host eSports. Session 26 complicates that: he received an email offering a volunteer role as a programming mentor for game developers with a game development non-profit, which he called the perfect start to a career combining gaming and helping people. Whether he accepted, and how it relates to his job, is unstated. In Session 25 he had started a portable smoker venture and welded one himself. In Session 28 he said he had organized a programming seminar the week before, with a great turnout. He learned various programming approaches, found ideas he had not yet tried, and promised James resources and tutorials. James said he was looking to branch out, and whether John sent them is not recorded.

In Session 21 John said he was helping his younger siblings build a text-based adventure game. James suggested McGee's Pub, and they agreed on 27 August, John's day off. In Session 22 John said he was going through difficult times, and James offered to listen. The cause of the stress has never been discussed. In Session 23 John said his parents had started learning to code from him, and he planned a family gaming night with his siblings for September; whether it happened is open. In Session 24, on 18 September, John returned after about two weeks, having taken up board games. In Session 25, on 20 September, he revealed his first mobile game, a 2D puzzle adventure launching in October 2022. He had kept it secret because he would have been very upset to tell James about "her" in advance and then have it fail. That remark is not explained. James offered to test the game, and John promised to let him know. Neither the launch nor the testing is mentioned in Session 28.

Open items as of Session 28 are numerous. James has not formally given his full opinion of Cyberpunk 2077, and his turn-based and tournament games remain unnamed. The VR outing, the next-year trip, and the Toronto and Vancouver legs are unconfirmed beyond Nuuk. Unknown are the stranger behind the drawing, the identities of Jill, the cat, and the puppy, and the link between his new game and earlier projects. Unrecorded are whether John attended the 11 September baseball game and whether the 27 August McGee's meeting happened. Samantha's status is unknown. The algorithm, payment, and chess items have no reported resolution. The new job's employer and role are unnamed, and whether the mentoring role is separate is unclear. Whether John visited the volunteering organization is unknown. The football bet is unresolved, and the cause of John's stress is not stated. The dog-walking app, HTML collaboration, and childhood character game have gone quiet. Pending are the mobile game's launch, James's testing offer, and the promised resources. Active are John's portable smoker venture, eSports ambitions, programming group, and teaching of his family, and whether the September family gaming night happened is open.

Melanie said she is lucky to have her husband and kids, to whom she has been married for five years, and both agreed that family time makes them feel most alive. On 27 June, Caroline shared a cross-and-heart necklace from her grandmother in Sweden. On 23 June, she attended an LGBTQ+ counseling workshop she found enlightening. Melanie introduced her dog, Luna, and cat, Oliver, and said running farther to de-stress has improved her mental health.

On 15 July 2023, Melanie said she took her kids to a pottery workshop "last Friday," roughly 14 July, and the family has been painting nature-inspired works together. Caroline said she attended an adoption council meeting "last Friday," which made her more determined to adopt. Melanie said flowers bring her joy and were part of her wedding decor, and that marrying her partner was the best part of the day. Caroline described a pride parade "a few weeks ago," where she felt proud and not alone, and said the best part was realizing she can be herself without fear. Melanie said creativity and family keep her at peace, and the family went camping in the forest. Across eight sessions, the two have consistently encouraged each other. Caroline has moved from exploring counseling careers toward adoption and public speaking, and Melanie has moved from feeling swamped to building self-care through running, reading, violin, pottery, and family outings.

Maria and John are friends who check in periodically about volunteering, fitness, family, work, John's political ambitions, pets, and leisure. Thirty-two sessions have taken place, from 17 December 2022 through 16 August 2023. Maria keeps her own local politics notes and asked to be kept posted on John's meetings with local leaders, which he agreed to.

Maria volunteers at a homeless shelter and a dog shelter, does aerial yoga, joined a nearby church in May, and started a new gym routine in June. She finds shelter work fulfilling despite its difficulty, and the shelter gave her a medal in session 29, which she called humbling. On 11 August she worked the shelter's front desk and described the joy of seeing people receive food or a bed. On 4 August she took up community work with church friends. Her recent life has also included a car accident on 2 July and helping her cousin find housing after the cousin left home in a hurry. The memory does not say whether the cousin has found housing.

Her pets have changed. In session 30 she described a white puppy named Coco. In session 31 she described a black puppy named Shadow, adopted from a shelter the week before, who is energetic and gets along with her other dog. The memory does not reconcile the two dogs.

John does kickboxing and has been in a firefighting brigade since late July, when its first call-out saved a family from a burning building. On 16 August he spoke as though he had only just joined, saying he was excited to help his community and impressed by the members' dedication and teamwork. He said the brigade's donation drive for canned food, toiletries, and clothes helped it buy a brand new fire truck, and he shared a photo of the truck. He said the work gave him a sense of purpose and that he felt it was his true calling. Maria said she was loving his newfound passion. On 13 August he also reported becoming a volunteer mentor at a local school, which he found rewarding.

John's main political goal remains a local office focused on education and infrastructure, both lacking where he grew up. On 1 January 2023 he said he had failed a military aptitude test, which left him stressed. On 25 February he announced he was running again, calling it a "last run." The office, election date, and launch have never been named. He later retook the test with strong results and said he had graduated. On 6 May he confirmed he would run, and Maria said she was fully behind him. That day he also proposed a community infrastructure project aimed at West County, his old area, and Maria agreed to help win neighborhood backing. On 20 May he said he was busy with a petition supporting military veterans. Neither the petition nor the blogging and convention he mentioned on 18 April has a stated link to the office.

Finances have been a steady source of stress. On 16 June John announced a promotion to assistant manager. On 5 August he said he had lost his job at a mechanical engineering company after it tanked, and that Maria's push had helped him consider a change. He may have found a job on a tech company's hardware team, but whether he accepted it is unconfirmed.

On 3 June the family said goodbye to Max, a dog they had owned for ten years, and they are considering adopting a rescue dog, which Maria encouraged. On 3 August John mentioned his children for the first time, saying a military memorial visit had moved them deeply. On 13 August he described his family as a close unit that supports him in hard times and enjoys hikes, picnics, board games, and movie nights.

John's public activity has grown more visible. On 3 July he took part in a veterans' rights march. On 7 July he said a severe flood had ruined many homes in his old area because of poor infrastructure, and he was gathering people to discuss repairs. Maria agreed to join, but the meeting's date and place were not given. On 17 July he visited a veterans' hospital and met an elderly veteran named Samuel, whose resilience reminded him why he had wanted to join the military. Session 15 took place at 2:56 pm on 25 October 2023. Sam said they were struggling to keep up with the new routine and felt pressured by family. Sam's arc runs from having no hobbies, to planning to paint, to eating healthier, cutting back on soda and candy, planning to lift with a trainer, trying kayaking, and now committing to a hike and a fitness push after a health scare. Unconfirmed items include the 16 September painting session, the lake day trip, finding a trainer and starting to lift, the dark chocolate swap, reading The Great Gatsby, the Lake Tahoe kayaking, and the hike.

Caroline and Melanie are friends who have kept in touch across eleven sessions, from 8 May to 14 August 2023, sharing personal changes, family life, community events and creative work.

Caroline: She is active in the LGBTQ community and wants a career in counseling or mental health, ideally supporting people with similar experiences. She started transitioning three years before June 2023 and says it has taught her to be herself without fear. She has long dreamed of having a family and has researched adoption agencies since May. After an adoption council meeting in mid-July she became more determined to adopt, but no agency has been chosen. She attended a pride parade on Friday 11 August and found it energizing. It reminded her to keep standing up for equality. She describes her art as a way to express her trans experience, represent inclusivity and speak up for LGBTQ+ people. She shared paintings including "Embracing Identity," about finding comfort and love in being yourself. She says painting helps her explore her transition and her changing body and teaches her to accept imperfection.

Melanie: She ran a charity race for mental health in May and runs farther to de-stress. She calls her pottery class therapy and took the kids to a pottery workshop on 14 July. The family paints nature scenes together and loves camping and hiking. She says creativity and family keep her at peace. Their camping trips are the highlight of summer, and they once watched the Perseid meteor shower and made wishes. She has a dog and a cat, Luna and Oliver. On 13 August she celebrated her daughter's birthday with a Matt Patterson concert. She wants to cultivate a loving, accepting environment for her kids.

Open threads as of 14 August 2023: no adoption agency has been chosen, the August art show outcome is unknown, and the activist group and mentoring work are ongoing. Melanie's reading and violin routine has not been mentioned since May.

On 27 August Sam reported a new diet and exercise routine, but on 11 September admitted that cravings remained a real struggle. After a 2 October check-up called their weight a serious health risk, Sam sent a distressed message on 8 October. Evan said he had lifted weights for about a year and asked whether Sam was interested. Sam said yes, and Evan advised good form, finding a trainer, and starting small.

Sam had gone to the emergency room with a severe stomachache, diagnosed as gastritis, which Sam called a wake-up call to prioritize nutrition and exercise. Evan recommended setting goals, choosing an enjoyable exercise, and finding a workout buddy, then proposed a hike soon. Sam responded enthusiastically, but no date or place was set.

Session 15 took place at 2:56 pm on 25 October 2023. Sam said they were struggling to keep up with the routine, felt pressure from family, and admitted impatience with fast results. Evan said encouragement should not become stress, shared that he had changed his diet and started walking regularly two years earlier, and advised taking it one day at a time. No new plans came out of this session.

Session 16 took place at 9:13 pm on 9 November 2023. Sam shared that they had become a Weight Watchers coach in their group, calling it a major accomplishment and a step toward better health. Evan congratulated them and said Sam inspires people. Evan apologized for missing some events due to personal challenges, shared a photo of a 1968 Kustom K-200A vintage guitar given to him by a close friend, and revealed that he lost his job last month when his company downsized. He is now job hunting, and Sam offered support. Later Evan shared a beach sunset photo from a peaceful spot near his home where he goes to relax, suggested visiting it together, and proposed going next month, in December 2023. Sam agreed, but no date was set.

On the creative side, Sam said on 11 September that they were still learning to draw but loved journaling and creative writing, which remains their main creative outlet. That day Evan proposed painting together on Saturday, 16 September 2023. Sam was excited, but the session is never confirmed. Evan also named "The Great Gatsby" as a mystery he could not stop thinking about, and Sam said they would read it sometime.

Sam's arc runs from having no hobbies, to planning to paint, to eating healthier, cutting back on soda and candy, planning to lift with a trainer, trying kayaking, committing to a hike and a fitness push after a health scare, and becoming a Weight Watchers coach. Sam still reports cravings and family pressure, and their health concerns have grown more serious. Evan's arc has shifted from encouraging Sam's health to facing his own job loss while still offering warmth and support.

Unconfirmed items include the 16 September painting session, the lake day trip, finding a trainer and starting to lift, the dark chocolate swap, reading The Great Gatsby, the Lake Tahoe kayaking, the October hike, and the December beach outing.
