Deborah and Jolene have chatted regularly since first meeting on 23 January 2023, supporting each other through grief, work stress, and self-care. Their conversations often return to mothers, nature, yoga, and work. Sessions 18 to 21 took place on 16, 19, 21, and 24 August 2023, Session 22 on 26 August, Session 23 on 30 August, Session 24 on 3 September, and Session 25 on 6 September 2023. Photo captions sometimes conflict with what was said aloud, so rely on the spoken content.

Deborah is a yoga teacher who lost her mother years before they met, and her father died suddenly around 25 January 2023. She sits on the bench by the living-room window where her mother used to read. After her friend Karlie died in mid-February, she found comfort in a garden of roses and dahlias. On 1 August she began a community cleanup project and has been raising funds for it. She has two cats, Max and Luna. In Session 23 she shared a photo of her husband, the first mention of a husband in these records. In Session 24 she called her yoga friends her second family. In Session 25 she said meditation is now part of her daily routine and accepted Jolene's hope to watch a sunrise together.

Jolene is an electrical engineer who lost her mother in 2022. She has a similar bench and window at her mother's house and wears a heart-shaped bird pendant her mother gave her in Paris. She keeps two pet snakes, Susie and Seraphim. She and her partner, together three years and not married, love console gaming, especially "It Takes Two," and on 17 August she bought him a console. Deborah has repeatedly suggested swapping some gaming for yoga, and Jolene says yoga has "seriously saved" her. She and Deborah agreed to visit a hidden lake dock together.

Work is a recurring theme for Jolene. In February she proposed a STEM volunteer program for underprivileged kids but never pursued it. On 2 March, overwhelmed by exams, she received Deborah's advice to set smaller goals and use a planner. Deborah also promised her a yellow coffee mug, whose arrival is not recorded, and introduced the Eisenhower Matrix. Her internship at a well-known engineering firm was rewarding but hard to balance, so Deborah recommended a few minutes of daily mindful breathing. On 1 August a project she had poured enormous work into crashed and she lost everything. Deborah described a breathing-and-grounding flow and promised a tutorial video. On 12 August Jolene said meditation had restored her clarity.

Sessions 18 through 22 traced Jolene's move from strain back toward balance. She struggled to juggle engineering, her relationship, and personal growth in Session 18, and planned a schedule for studies and hobbies in Session 19. By Session 20 she was "really finding [her] zen again." In Session 22 she said she wants to use her engineering talent for renewable solar energy and clean water, and she and her partner planned a meditation retreat together.

Session 23 was a lighter exchange built around photos. Jolene and her partner returned on 29 August from Rio de Janeiro, where they attended yoga classes. She regularly meditates at a nearby pond, which feels like a restart.

Session 24 was a catch-up conversation. Jolene said she has been focused on studying and her relationship, and she is grateful for a partner who encourages her goals. Several finals are coming up, and she is considering a trip afterward to recharge.

Session 25 was brief and upbeat. Jolene had signed up for a meditation course at a retreat near a lake and was eager to share it with her partner. She called meditation an easy habit that helps her stay balanced during studies, and said beach walks and glimpses of sunrise soothe her.

Whether Jolene has started a regular mindfulness practice now looks answered. Still open are the yellow mug, the STEM volunteer program, the Eisenhower Matrix, daily mindful breathing, swapping gaming for yoga, the lake dock visit, Deborah's tutorial video, Jolene's report on the new flow, the schedule for studies and hobbies, the post-finals trip, and the sunrise they hope to watch together. The retreat planned in Session 22 may be the lake retreat from Session 25, but this is not confirmed.

John and James are two gamers whose friendship has grown through personal conversations about games, programming, dogs, goals, travel, work, romance, cooking, and other hobbies. They first spoke on 17 March 2022 at about 3:47 pm. Some sessions describe the friendship as reaching back to childhood, which does not fit that first conversation, and this has never been explained. There have been thirty-one sessions, the most recent on 7 November 2022 at 8:57 pm. James usually shares projects, achievements, outings, and photos, while John shares new hobbies, ventures, and experiences. John turns to James when he is stressed.

James has considered programming central to his life since college, working with Python and C++, building a website, and making game mods. In Session 13 he started a course combining gaming and programming. He is developing a game based on a character he sketched as a child and once offered to involve John in its HTML work, but that project and his dog-walking app have gone quiet. On 1 September (Session 22) he announced that his Unity strategy game was finished, crediting John's encouragement. On 13 October (Session 27) he said he had released his first game to the gaming community and wanted to try other genres, inspired by The Witcher 3. That release has never been named or linked to his earlier projects.

James has three dogs: Max, a shepherd; Daisy, a Labrador; and Ned, a pup adopted from a Stamford shelter in early April 2022. Introducing them is slowly working. On 5 August he took an unnamed puppy, possibly Ned, to the clinic, and on 9 August he took all three to a beach, where he met Samantha. In Session 28 his mother visited with an army friend, described both as still serving and as retired, which was never addressed. In Session 29 he shared a photo of a man and two unidentified dogs in a field. On 4 November (Session 30) he began a road trip with his family and dogs. In Session 31 he said it was still underway. They had visited his friends Josh and Mark and stopped at an animal sanctuary full of rescue dogs, where he wanted to take them all home but reminded himself that three dogs are enough. How the trip ends is not recorded.

James has played many games. He praised The Witcher 3's story, and his team reached an online Apex Legends tournament semifinal. He also won an online tournament in an unnamed turn-based strategy game. In Session 26 he bought a new video card, called himself super into RPGs, and asked about Cyberpunk 2077, which John recommended. On 21 October he said he had tried it and found it great and addictive. James has not formally given his full opinion. In Session 30 he said he wanted to try the sports genre.

James's romantic life is one of the most significant threads. In Session 6 he shared a drawing of a woman in armor kneeling on a rock, based on a stranger he passed around 6 April and fell for at first sight; she remains unidentified. He met Samantha at the beach on 9 August, and she gave him her number. He planned to call on 11 August, but the call is never described. In Session 23, on 4 September, he reported that he had asked Samantha to be his girlfriend on 3 September and she agreed, and he said he was happy with her despite overwhelming good and bad moments. He invited John to a baseball game on 11 September, promising to introduce him to Samantha; whether John attended is not recorded. In Session 29, on 31 October, James announced that he and Samantha had decided to move in together. He called the decision mutual and well informed, and they rented an apartment near McGee's bar, which he admitted was one of their criteria. No move-in date has been given. This is his first romantic relationship in the memory, moving from dating to cohabitation in about two months. Samantha has not appeared directly since.

James took up cooking, signing up for a class despite never having liked it, and hopes to treat John to one of his creations. John still owes him his impressions of prosciutto. In Session 6 James had visited Italy, Turkey, and Mexico and suggested a trip with John the following year. In Session 16 he announced tickets to Toronto with plans for Vancouver, and in Session 17 he reported reaching Nuuk. Toronto and Vancouver were never mentioned again. In Session 13 the two made a football bet. James hopes Liverpool wins the title, while John, a Manchester City fan, predicted City would win. James bet Liverpool would finish higher, John accepted, and the stakes were never specified.

John's life has been full of projects. In Session 8 he began freelance programming, building a website for a local business. Getting payments working was the hardest part, and no resolution is reported for that or for an earlier algorithm assignment. In Session 13 he got his dream job starting July 2022, though the employer and role were not named. In Session 18 he said he had left his IT job after three years for work matching his values and loved his new job. This may be the dream job, but the sessions do not confirm it. In Session 30 he said he had won the regional chess tournament on or about 1 November, crediting his habit of anticipating opponents, his study of openings, and James's earlier advice. He shared a photo of a chess opening book, and James thanked him.

John wants to organize computer game tournaments in his state, starting with CS:GO and adding Fortnite later, and James offered financial help or advice. In Session 20 he joined an online group of coders who want to use technology for good, and he said he was not returning to programming work, though he still wanted to host eSports. In Session 26 he received an offer to be a volunteer programming mentor with a game development non-profit, which he called the perfect start to a career combining gaming and helping people. Whether he accepted is unstated. In Session 25 he started a portable smoker venture and welded one himself. In Session 28 he organized a programming seminar and promised James resources, which are not recorded as sent.

In Session 21 John was helping his younger siblings build a text-based adventure game, and James suggested meeting at McGee's Pub on 27 August, John's day off. Whether that meeting happened is not recorded. In Session 22 John said he was going through difficult times, and James offered to listen. The cause has never been discussed. In Session 25, on 20 September, John revealed a first mobile game, a 2D puzzle adventure set to launch in October 2022. He had kept it secret because he would have been very upset to tell James about "her" in advance and then see it fail, a remark never explained. James offered to test it, and John promised to let him know. Neither the launch nor the testing has been mentioned since. In Session 29, on 30 October, John reported a gaming tournament with friends that raised a decent amount for a children's hospital; the total is unstated. When James asked for news, the talk turned to his move with Samantha, and John said he was there whenever James needed him. In Session 30 John said he was hooked on FIFA 23 and proposed playing together after James practiced. That session has not yet been held.

In Session 31, on 7 November, John said he had spent a fun weekend working with a game developer to turn his ideas into an online board game, and he shared a photo of it. He said a demo would be released soon for feedback. James asked to be told when it was out so he could support it and share his thoughts. This venture is not clearly tied to the mobile puzzle game, the mentoring role, or the seminar. The conversation then turned to dogs. John said he still has not gotten one but really wants one, and both men praised dogs as daily sunshine. John shared a photo of his cousin's dog, Luna, which James admired, and then John abruptly signed off. A final photo of two people in front of a giant head is unidentified.

Open items remain numerous. James's turn-based and tournament games and the game he released on 13 October are unnamed. The VR outing, the next-year trip, and the Toronto and Vancouver legs are unconfirmed beyond Nuuk. The stranger behind the drawing, the identities of Jill, the cat, and the puppy, and the link between his new game and earlier projects are unknown. Whether John attended the 11 September baseball game and whether the 27 August McGee's meeting happened are unrecorded. The algorithm and payment problems have no reported resolution. The new job's employer and role are unnamed, and whether the mentoring role is separate is unclear. The football bet is unresolved, and the cause of John's stress is not stated. Pending items include the mobile game's launch, James's testing offer, the promised resources, the board game demo, FIFA 23, and the family gaming night, whose outcome is open. The 30 October hospital fundraiser total and James's road trip have no recorded outcomes. John's wish for a dog remains unfulfilled, and James's offer to help him find one still stands.

Joanna and Nate reconnected on 21 January 2022 and have stayed friendly, warm, and encouraging, often cheering on each other's projects. They have met in person at least once, since Nate mentioned a Spider-Man pin on Joanna's purse on 5 June. Session 24 took place on 21 October 2022, after Session 23 on 9 October.

Joanna enjoys writing, reading, movies, nature, baking, DIY crafts, and friends. She isn't into video games and prefers dramas, emotional films, and romantic comedies. Acting was her first passion, though she said "never say never" about acting again. She is allergic to reptiles, furred animals, and cockroaches, and has no pets now. She has avoided dairy since 25 February and called herself lactose intolerant on 5 September. Her favorite superhero is Spider-Man. She keeps an external drive for backups after a laptop crash in early September. On 9 October she recommended a fluffy couch, a weighted blanket, and dimmable lights for a cozy living room. She rated a classic movie she recently watched 9 or 10 out of 10, but has not named it. Her 6 October movie recommendation request is still unanswered. She has a stuffed dog named Tilly, a gift from Nate, named after a real dog she had to rehome in Michigan.

Nate enjoys video games and movies, especially action, sci-fi, and classics, and sees fantasy and sci-fi as an escape. His two pet turtles calm him when he is nervous, and he keeps fish he calls his "little dudes." He is part of a vegan diet group, dyed his hair purple on 15 April, and introduced Max, a dog he adopted, on 20 May. His favorite superhero is Iron Man. On 12 September he hosted a cooking show teaching vegan ice cream recipes. His gaming wins include a fourth tournament win on 10 July and an international win on 22 August, which let him make a living from gaming. On 6 October he reported a very big win, saved some of the prize money, and has no big plans for it. His mid-June gaming party had seven attendees, but no next party has been reported. On 9 October he attended a game convention and played Catan. He said gaming is his escape, so he doesn't get intensely competitive. On 21 October he said he felt stressed about tough competitors and was practicing for his next tournament.

Joanna's writing has moved forward with setbacks. She finished a drama-romance screenplay on 23 January, a road-trip drama on 18 March, and a deeply personal screenplay on 20 May, possibly "Finding Home," begun 21 April. She is still waiting to hear back on a writing gig she auditioned for on 24 March. On 3 June she received a generic rejection, and Nate encouraged her. On 24 June she submitted a screenplay to a film contest. A research road trip to Woodhaven on 10 July sparked ideas for her next script. On 22 August she shared her first book, about loss, redemption, and forgiveness, with a writers group and received great feedback. On 6 October she said she finished the book's writing. On 9 October Nate suggested a writing convention, and Joanna said she would look into it. On 21 October she reported another rejection from a production company. When Nate asked whether it was the film contest, she answered only "Yeah..", so the contest result is probably a rejection but is unconfirmed.

Food is a strong shared thread. Nate has shared dairy-free recipes, including coconut milk ice cream. On 2 May Joanna shared a dairy-free vanilla cake, crediting his advice. On 5 September she shared dairy-free chocolate coconut cupcakes, and on 14 September she asked for his ice cream recipe. On 6 October she said a new dairy-free recipe was a hit with her family and shared a photo of a raspberry tart. Her favorite dairy-free treat is a chocolate raspberry tart with an almond flour crust.

Recommendations have gone both ways. On 21 April Nate recommended a fantasy and sci-fi book series, and on 2 May Joanna said she loved "The Lord of the Rings" trilogy at his suggestion. Neither has reported back on that series. Her "Little Women" recommendation was closed on 6 October, when Nate said he loved it. On 22 August Joanna asked for relaxing fantasy series, and Nate recommended one; she asked him to report back. On 12 May Joanna invited Nate to hike trails near her town, but no date has been set.

Open threads include the hiking trip, the film contest result, the writing gig result, "Finding Home" and the third screenplay, the Woodhaven-inspired script, the first book's next steps, Nate's next tournament and party, his winnings, the writing convention, the Tilly photo discrepancy, the book recommendations, Joanna's movie request, and the classic movie's name.

Between 8 May and 17 August 2023, Melanie and Caroline consistently encouraged each other. In early May, Melanie said she was swamped with her kids and work, and shared a 2022 painting of a sunset over a lake that helps her relax. Caroline said an LGBTQ support group left her happy and accepted, and she began considering counseling. By late May, Melanie had run a charity mental health race on 20 May and found it rewarding, and she sets aside daily me-time for running, reading, or playing violin. Caroline was researching adoption agencies, a long-held dream, and chose one serving LGBTQ+ people. Both agree family time makes them feel most alive, and Caroline calls her friends, family, and mentors her rocks.

In June, Caroline spoke at a school event about her transgender journey, and Melanie praised her courage. Melanie took the family camping in the mountains the week of 19 June, and that week Caroline attended an LGBTQ+ counseling workshop and a pride parade that made her feel she belonged. On 6 July, Caroline said she was building a children's library for her future kids, and her favorite book is "Becoming Nicole" by Amy Ellis Nutt. On 15 July, Melanie's family took a pottery workshop and has been painting nature-inspired works together. The same day, Caroline attended an adoption council meeting that made her more determined to adopt. On 17 July she joined a mentorship program for LGBTQ youth and mentors a transgender teen. On 20 July she joined the activist group "Connected LGBTQ Activists," having missed her city's pride parade the weekend before.

In mid-August, Caroline said inclusivity and diversity are central to her art, which expresses her trans experience, and she shared "Embracing Identity," a painting about self-acceptance. On 17 August, she said a hike went badly when religious conservatives made remarks that upset her, though accepting people around her help. Melanie shared a finished pottery bowl, and both agreed that joyful things and supportive friends help them through hard times. Caroline offered a trip just the two of them to explore nature, and they agreed to plan something special.

In Session 13 on 23 August 2023, Caroline said she had applied to adoption agencies the week before, with help from an adoption advice group. She felt ready to give her love to a child, though parenting felt exciting and nerve-wracking. She has a guinea pig named Oscar. Melanie mentioned her cats Bailey and Oliver, and shared a photo of a black dog presented as Oliver, so the pet details should be confirmed. She shared a self-portrait of a woman with a blue face, saying painting makes her feel liberated, empowered, and therapeutic.

In Session 14 on 25 August 2023, Caroline said she had gone hiking the previous week and got into a bad spot with some people, so she apologized, and Melanie said that took courage and maturity. Melanie shared a flower-covered plate she made in pottery class the day before. Caroline has not tried pottery yet. She shared a sunset painting made after a beach visit, and Melanie said it conveyed serenity. Caroline said finding an accepting community has meant a great deal to her, and she described a rainbow flag mural as reflecting the courage of the trans community. She shared stained glass works, including a church window showing time changing lives, which represents her own journey as a transgender woman. She found a rainbow sidewalk for Pride Month while walking, and said art helps her express feelings. Melanie paints landscapes and still life, shared a sunflower painting, and said autumn is inspiring her. Caroline said she is putting together an LGBTQ art show "next month," where she will show her paintings. That conflicts with the earlier August 2023 reference, so the date should be confirmed.

SUMMARY:
January to March 2023: Jolene's mother gave her a pendant in 2010 in Paris and has since died. Deborah's father died around 25 January 2023. Jolene and her partner have been together three years but are unmarried. Jolene uses the Pomodoro Technique to manage burnout.

Spring to July 2023: Jolene finished her engineering project in May and started interning in June. Deborah started a running group, raised funds for a community cleanup, organized a July yoga event, and visited her mom's house, a place of mixed memories.

August 2023: Jolene's project crashed in late July, but she keeps going and tracks her workload in a bullet journal. She bought a game console for her partner on 17 August, and Battlefield 1 arrived the next week. They returned on 29 August from Rio de Janeiro, where they attended yoga classes. Jolene wants a sustainable engineering career in solar power or clean water. Deborah has two cats, Luna (5) and Max (8), and shared a photo of a man she called her husband. Her later beach-wedding remark suggests he is her husband, though this is not fully confirmed.

3 to 8 September 2023: Deborah considers her yoga friends her second family. Jolene is focused on finals and plans a recharging trip afterward. Her favorite game is "Monster Hunter: World," and she says meditation keeps her balanced. A storm forced Deborah to cancel her yoga getaway. The coffee date moved to Friday at 5, when Jolene will sort books from a bookcase.

12 September 2023: Jolene and her partner attended a few-week meditation retreat in Phuket, which helped her reflect on happiness, balance, and savoring the present. Both agreed small moments boost happiness. Deborah recalled a card game about cats she wants to play with Jolene. Camping and sunrise plans remain unconfirmed.

15 September 2023 (latest): Deborah reconnected with her late mother's old friends, whose stories moved her to tears. They looked through her mother's photos together, which deepened her appreciation for her mother. Deborah practices beach yoga as self-care. Jolene creates a calm yoga space with candles, essential oils, and soft music, and her room is her main place to relax. Jolene's pet is a snake named Susie, whom she has had for two years.

Recurring themes: grief, self-care, workload stress, yoga and meditation, mindfulness, engineering goals, setbacks, travel, gaming, pets, and planning shared activities.

Evan and Sam first met in person on 18 May 2023, shortly after Evan returned from a family trip to the Rockies. Evan is an enthusiastic watercolor painter and frequent traveler who encourages Sam to try new things. When they met, Sam had no hobbies. Conversations have since moved through health, creative pursuits, outdoor activities, and Evan's hardships.

The health thread began on 24 May, when a check-up showed Sam's weight was off target. On 6 June Evan suggested flavored seltzer and dark chocolate in place of sugary snacks. On 27 July, friends' mockery prompted Sam to cut back on soda and candy and start the gym. On 27 August Sam reported a new routine, but on 11 September admitted cravings remained a struggle. After a 2 October check-up called their weight a serious health risk, Sam sent a distressed message on 8 October. Evan said he had lifted weights for about a year and advised good form, finding a trainer, and starting small. In Session 13 on 14 October, Sam described a rough week after buying unhealthy snacks, along with work stress. Evan proposed kayaking, and Sam said they and "my mate" would try a nearby lake, later mentioning Lake Tahoe. Whether the kayaking happened is unconfirmed.

Session 14 took place at 1:50 pm on 17 October. Sam had gone to the emergency room with a severe stomachache, diagnosed as gastritis, which Sam called a wake-up call. Evan recommended setting goals and finding a workout buddy, then proposed a hike, but no date or place was set. Session 15 took place at 2:56 pm on 25 October. Sam said they were struggling to keep up with the routine and felt family pressure. Evan said encouragement should not become stress and advised taking it one day at a time.

Session 16 took place at 9:13 pm on 9 November. Sam shared they had become a Weight Watchers coach in their group, and Evan said Sam inspires people. Evan apologized for missing some events due to personal challenges and shared a photo of a 1968 Kustom K-200A vintage guitar. He revealed he had lost his job the previous month when his company downsized, and he is now job hunting. Sam offered support. Evan then shared a beach sunset photo from a peaceful spot near his home and proposed visiting together in December 2023. Sam agreed, but no date was set.

On the creative side, Sam said on 11 September they were still learning to draw but loved journaling and creative writing, which remains their main creative outlet. That day Evan proposed painting together on Saturday, 16 September 2023. Sam was excited, but the session was never confirmed. Evan also named "The Great Gatsby" as a mystery he could not stop thinking about, and Sam said they would read it sometime.

Session 17 took place at 7:30 pm on 21 November. Evan reported a health scare the previous week, when a check-up found something suspicious and he went to the hospital, but doctors said everything was fine. Evan said he stays in shape by hitting the gym. Sam said they had been dealing with discomfort that limited their movement and that diet changes were hard. Sam shared a photo of a book cover, calling it their go-to "feel good" flick, and proposed making it a habit to appreciate something each day. Evan shared photos of a small island where he grew up, calling it his happy place, along with beach and sunset scenes. No new plans were made.

Sam's arc runs from having no hobbies, to planning to paint, to eating healthier and planning to lift with a trainer, to committing to a hike after a health scare, and becoming a Weight Watchers coach. Sam still reports cravings, family pressure, and physical discomfort. Evan's arc has shifted from encouraging Sam's health to facing job loss and a frightening hospital visit while still offering warmth and support.

Unconfirmed items include the 16 September painting session, the lake day trip, finding a trainer and starting to lift, the dark chocolate swap, reading The Great Gatsby, the Lake Tahoe kayaking, the October hike, and the December beach outing.

In early October, Evan hurt his knee playing basketball with his kids and struggled to stay active. On 8 October, Sam's doctor called his weight a serious health risk. John and James first met on 17 March 2022, when John said he was glad to finally talk with James. They share a love of video games, though James finds them joyful while John mostly plays to relax. A 22 July session calls them classmates at age 10, which conflicts with the March meeting, so the origin of their shared history remains unclear. James has programmed since college, works with Python and C++, has built a website, and made game mods. He considers his dogs family and offered to help John find a pet, which John wants someday but is not ready for yet.

Early on, James proposed a dog walking and pet care app and a VR gaming session, most likely for 19 or 26 March, but the VR session is never confirmed. On 20 March James joined an online gamers' platform, calling gaming a shared language and a refuge in hard times. On 27 March John joined a CS:GO tournament, and on 4 April James reached the semifinals of an online tournament. On 12 April James adopted a pup named Ned. John offered to send James an RPG link, but sending is not confirmed.

In late April John said he had met three new friends in his programming course and dreamed of visiting Italy, which James has already seen. James offered to help pick a country for a trip together next year. On 23 April James helped John with a difficult algorithm assignment, still unresolved that day. Around 26 April John recommended The Name of the Wind, and James agreed to try an impostor game John suggested. On 29 April John took on freelance work building a local business website. On 4 May James said friends had helped him fix a bug in a nearly finished project. John invited his new friends to watch movies, and James agreed to join the next gathering. John also agreed to try prosciutto, which James had recommended. On 8 May John organized a CS:GO tournament that raised money for a dog shelter. On 11 May he volunteered to build a smartphone app for a charitable foundation, which led him to consider non-profit work.

On 20 May John took second place in a local tournament. On 23 May James finished a big project that required a new language. On 13 June John landed his dream job, starting in July 2022. John, a Manchester City fan, predicted City would win the title, while James hopes Liverpool does. James bet that Liverpool would finish higher, and John accepted; the bet is pending. On 16 June James said he was lucky to have at least two people who always help when he struggles. John recommended several fantasy and science fiction series, and James said he would check them out. On 19 June James began introducing his dogs Max, Daisy, and Ned. John asked James to take him to the charity where James had volunteered, and James agreed in principle to go the following weekend.

In July James said he had won an online gaming tournament and taken up surfing and rope jumping. John said he felt determined but overwhelmed, finding it hard to balance his personal and professional life. James bought tickets to Toronto, leaving 11 July and returning 20 July, and promised John a souvenir. On 22 July John said he had just started playing chess, and James gave him two tips: study opening moves and analyze your own games. James said his trip included Nuuk, Greenland, a new country for his bucket list. He brought souvenirs for John and Jill, then ended the chat, saying he was tired.

On 6 August 2022, John said he had left his IT job after three years to pursue work aligned with his values. He loves his new job and now wants to organize computer game tournaments in his state, starting with CS:GO and extending to Fortnite. James called the move brave, suggested trying different game genres, and offered financial help or advice. James then said he had taken his puppy, likely Ned, to the clinic for a routine checkup and vaccination. John praised James's care for his pets, which James said are the source of his joy.

In Session 19, on 10 August 2022, John said the earlier conversation had got him thinking about his passions and goals, and thanked James for encouraging him to try new game genres. He had been playing strategy and RPG games and was already thinking about organizing competitions for them. He had become hooked on The Witcher 3. James said that on 9 August he had taken his three dogs to a beach outing, where he met a woman named Samantha, who gave him her number. He planned to call her the next day, 11 August, and possibly ask her out. Whether he called or dated her is not yet known.

Open items: the VR session and RPG link are unconfirmed. James still owes his impressions of the game and must find next year's shared trip destination. John's algorithm problem and payment feature were unresolved as of their dates. James was to read The Name of the Wind and try the impostor game, John was to try prosciutto, and James agreed to attend the movie gathering, but none is confirmed done. John intends to organize more tournaments with no dates set. The volunteer visit remains unconfirmed. The Liverpool versus Manchester City bet is pending. James's planned call to Samantha is pending as of 10 August.

Between 8 May and 17 August 2023, Melanie and Caroline consistently encouraged each other. In early May, Melanie said she was swamped with her kids and work, and shared a 2022 painting of a lake sunset that helps her relax. Caroline said an LGBTQ support group left her happy and accepted, and she began considering counseling. By late May, Melanie had run a charity mental health race and found it rewarding, and she sets aside daily me-time for running, reading, or playing violin. Caroline was researching adoption agencies, a long-held dream. Both agree family time makes them feel most alive, and Caroline calls her friends, family, and mentors her rocks.

In June, Caroline spoke at a school event about her transgender journey, and Melanie praised her courage. That same week, Caroline attended an LGBTQ+ counseling workshop and a pride parade that made her feel she belonged. On 6 July, Caroline said she was building a children's library for her future kids. On 15 July, Melanie's family took a pottery workshop, and Caroline attended an adoption council meeting that made her more determined to adopt. On 17 July she joined an LGBTQ youth mentorship program and mentors a transgender teen. On 20 July she joined the activist group "Connected LGBTQ Activists."

In mid-August, Caroline shared "Embracing Identity," a painting about self-acceptance, and said inclusivity is central to her art. On 17 August, she said a hike went badly when religious conservatives made upsetting remarks, though accepting people around her help. Melanie shared a finished pottery bowl, and both agreed joyful things and supportive friends help in hard times. Caroline offered a trip just the two of them to explore nature, and they agreed to plan something special.

In Session 13 on 23 August 2023, Caroline said she had applied to adoption agencies the week before and felt ready to give her love to a child, though parenting felt exciting and nerve-wracking. She has a guinea pig named Oscar. Melanie mentioned cats Bailey and Oliver and shared a photo of a black dog presented as Oliver, so the pet details should be confirmed. Caroline shared a self-portrait of a blue-faced woman, saying painting feels liberating and therapeutic. In Session 14 on 25 August, Caroline apologized for a bad spot she got into with some people on a hike, and Melanie said that took courage and maturity. Melanie shared a flower-covered pottery plate; Caroline has not tried pottery. Caroline shared a beach sunset painting and a stained glass church window representing her own journey as a transgender woman. Melanie paints landscapes and still life and said autumn inspires her. Caroline said she is organizing an LGBTQ art show "next month," which conflicts with the earlier August reference, so the date should be confirmed.

In Session 15 on 28 August 2023, Melanie said she took her kids to a park the day before. Caroline said she has been volunteering at an LGBTQ+ youth center, where her own past loneliness made talking with young people meaningful, and she plans to keep volunteering and help with a talent show for the kids next month. Melanie loves live music and named the band "Summer Sounds." Caroline mostly plays acoustic guitar, which she uses to express her emotions, and her most meaningful song is "Brave" by Sara Bareilles. Melanie said she plays clarinet, which conflicts with her May mention of violin, so the instrument should be confirmed. Her favorite music includes Bach, Mozart, and Ed Sheeran's "Perfect."

She is lactose intolerant and allergic to cockroaches. Her stuffed dog Tilly, a gift from Nate, sits with her while she writes. Nate plays competitive video games, keeps turtles, cooks dairy-free desserts, and enjoys movies.

Joanna finished her first full screenplay in January 2022; the March audition outcome is unknown. A major company rejected her on 3 June, and bits she wrote appeared on screen on 5 June. She submitted a screenplay to a film contest on 24 June, with no reply reported. She finished a book in late September. A 14 September laptop crash wiped out unsaved work, so she now keeps an external drive. On 21 October she reported another rejection, from a production company, and said she would keep pushing forward. On 25 October she said another script she contributed to reached the big screen the previous Sunday, her third such time. She keeps character drawings to help her picture characters while writing, and draws ideas from people she knows, things she has seen, and her imagination.

Nate won tournaments in January, late April, 3 June, 10 July, 21 August (an international event), and late September 2022, and had a setback on 5 September. On 14 September he taught vegan ice cream recipes on his cooking show. His favorite is coconut milk ice cream. On 6 October he made Joanna a whiteboard drawing of encouraging words. He plays Cyberpunk 2077 nonstop and calls gaming his escape. On 21 October he felt stressed by tough competitors, was practicing for his next tournament, and said his turtles cheer him up. On 25 October he took his two turtles for a walk, said they eat vegetables, fruits, and insects and love fruit, and described one as adventurous and the other as reserved.

Joanna recommended "Little Women" to Nate. On 12 May she invited him hiking, but no date is set. On 22 August they swapped book recommendations. Nate suggested a writing convention, and she said she would look into it. For living room comfort, she suggested a long, fluffy couch, a weighted blanket, and dimmable lights.

Open items: the March audition result; whether the film contest entry gets a response; whether the production company rejection is that entry; whether Joanna's book gets published; whether they have gone hiking; whether Nate has started his drama; whether Joanna's family liked the ice cream and whether she made the recipe; whether Joanna has looked into writing conventions; how Nate's next tournament goes; and whether Nate will watch the movie with the character Joanna described.

Caroline and Melanie are friends who have kept in touch across fourteen sessions, from 8 May to 25 August 2023, sharing life changes, pets, community events, volunteering and creative work.

Caroline: She is active in the LGBTQ community and joined an activist group in July. She wants a career in counseling or mental health and has long dreamed of adopting. She applied to adoption agencies around 23 August, which feels exciting but nerve-wracking. Her art expresses her trans experience, and she finds painting therapeutic. Her guinea pig is Oscar. In the 25 August session she described an upsetting hike where she got into a bad spot with some people and tried to apologize. She also shared a sunset painting from a beach visit, a stained glass window about personal growth, and a rainbow sidewalk she found on a Pride Month walk. She loves drawing flowers and has not tried pottery yet.

Melanie: She ran a mental health charity race in May and runs to de-stress. Pottery and painting help her express feelings. She made a pottery plate on 24 August and shared a sunflower painting, and she is planning autumn-inspired works. She spent a day volunteering at a homeless shelter with her family. Her family paints nature scenes together and loves camping and hiking. Her pets are the dog Luna and the cats Oliver and Bailey. She wants to build a loving, accepting home for her kids.

Plans: On 17 August both agreed to plan a special summer outing, as a family or just the two of them. No date or destination has been set.

Open threads as of 25 August 2023: no adoption agency is confirmed as chosen. Caroline's LGBTQ art show is set for next month (September 2023), and its outcome is unknown. The summer outing has no details. The hiking apology has no known outcome. Melanie asked what led Caroline to transition, and Caroline described the acceptance she found in the community.

Deborah and Jolene have chatted regularly since first meeting on 23 January 2023, supporting each other through grief, work stress, and self-care. Their conversations often return to mothers, nature, yoga, and work. Sessions 18 to 21 took place on 16, 19, 21, and 24 August 2023, Session 22 on 26 August, Session 23 on 30 August, Session 24 on 3 September, Session 25 on 6 September, and Session 26 on 8 September 2023. Photo captions sometimes conflict with what was said aloud, so rely on the spoken content.

Deborah is a yoga teacher who lost her mother years before they met, and her father died suddenly around 25 January 2023. She sits on the bench by the living-room window where her mother used to read. After her friend Karlie died in mid-February, she found comfort in a garden of roses and dahlias. On 1 August she began a community cleanup project and has been fundraising for it. She has two cats, Max and Luna. In Session 23 she shared a photo of her husband, the first mention of one in these records. In Session 24 she called her yoga friends her second family, and in Session 25 she said meditation is now part of her daily routine. In Session 26 a storm cancelled a yoga getaway, and she said the setback reminded her to be grateful for small things.

Jolene is an electrical engineer who lost her mother in 2022 and has a similar bench and window at her mother's house. She and her partner, together three years and not married, love console gaming, especially "It Takes Two," and on 17 August she bought him a console. Deborah has repeatedly suggested swapping some gaming for yoga, and Jolene says yoga has "seriously saved" her.

Work is a recurring theme for Jolene. In February she proposed a STEM volunteer program for underprivileged kids but never pursued it. On 2 March, overwhelmed by exams, she received Deborah's advice to set smaller goals and use a planner. Deborah also promised her a yellow coffee mug, whose arrival is not recorded, and introduced the Eisenhower Matrix. When her internship proved hard to balance, Deborah recommended a few minutes of daily mindful breathing. On 1 August a project she had poured enormous work into crashed and she lost everything. Deborah described a breathing-and-grounding flow and promised a tutorial video. On 12 August Jolene said meditation had restored her clarity.

Sessions 18 through 22 traced Jolene's move from strain back toward balance. In Session 18 she struggled to juggle engineering, her relationship, and personal growth, and in Session 19 she planned a schedule for studies and hobbies. By Session 20 she was "really finding [her] zen again." In Session 22 she said she wants to use her engineering talent for renewable solar energy and clean water, and she and her partner planned a meditation retreat together.

Session 23 was a lighter photo-based exchange. Jolene and her partner had just returned from Rio de Janeiro, where they attended yoga classes, and she meditates at a nearby pond that feels like a restart. Session 24 was a catch-up in which she said she has been focused on studying and her relationship, and is grateful for a partner who encourages her goals. Finals are coming up, and she is considering a trip afterward to recharge. Session 25 was brief and upbeat. She had signed up for a meditation course at a lakeside retreat, called meditation an easy habit that keeps her balanced during studies, and said sunrise glimpses soothe her.

Session 26 turned to practical planning. Jolene and her partner are planning a camping trip to connect with nature and practice yoga. Asked how she manages a busy schedule, Jolene described a routine covering classes, studying, and personal time, with yoga and meditation keeping her balanced. Deborah wanted to hear more, so they arranged a coffee date. Monday and Wednesday at 4 fell through because Deborah had plans, so they settled on Friday at 5, when Jolene would be sorting books from a bookcase. Deborah accepted, looked forward to the date "next week," and asked Jolene to bring some interesting books. Since 8 September was a Friday, "next week" most likely means 15 September, but this was not restated and is unconfirmed.

Open threads include the yellow mug, the STEM volunteer program, the Eisenhower Matrix, daily mindful breathing, swapping gaming for yoga, the lake dock visit, Deborah's tutorial video, Jolene's report on the new flow, the post-finals trip, the sunrise they hope to watch together, the camping trip, the coffee date, and rescheduling the cancelled yoga getaway. Whether Jolene has started a regular mindfulness practice looks answered. The lake retreat from Session 25 may be the retreat planned in Session 22, but this is not confirmed.

Joanna and Nate reconnected on 21 January 2022 and have stayed friendly, warm, and encouraging, often cheering on each other's projects. They have met in person at least once, since Nate mentioned a Spider-Man pin on Joanna's purse on 5 June. The most recent session is Session 26 on 4 November 2022, and they have arranged an in-person visit for 5 November.

Joanna enjoys writing, reading, movies, nature, baking, DIY crafts, and friends. She isn't into video games and prefers dramas, emotional films, and romantic comedies. Acting was her first passion, though she said "never say never" about acting again. She is allergic to reptiles, furred animals, and cockroaches, and has no pets now. She has avoided dairy since 25 February and called herself lactose intolerant on 5 September. Her favorite superhero is Spider-Man. After a laptop crash in early September, she started keeping an external drive for backups. She rated a classic movie she recently watched 9 or 10 out of 10, but has not named it. Her 6 October movie request is still unanswered. She owns a stuffed dog named Tilly, a gift from Nate.

Joanna's writing has moved forward with setbacks. She finished several screenplays between January and May, including a possible "Finding Home" on 20 May. She is still waiting to hear back on a writing gig she auditioned for on 24 March. She received a generic rejection on 3 June and submitted a screenplay to a film contest on 24 June. A research trip to Woodhaven on 10 July sparked ideas for her next script. On 22 August she shared her first book, about loss, redemption, and forgiveness, with a writers group and received great feedback. She finished the book on 6 October. On 9 October Nate suggested a writing convention, and she said she would look into it. On 21 October she reported another rejection from a production company, and her answer to whether it was the film contest, "Yeah..", suggests that result is a rejection but unconfirmed. On 25 October she reported that a script she contributed to was shown on the big screen for the first time. On 4 November she said she had set up meetings with movie producers, who seemed interested in her script's self-discovery elements.

Nate enjoys video games and movies, especially action, sci-fi, and classics, and sees fantasy and sci-fi as an escape. His two pet turtles calm him when he is nervous, and he keeps fish he calls his "little dudes." He dyed his hair purple on 15 April and introduced Max, a dog he adopted, on 20 May. His favorite superhero is Iron Man. His gaming wins include a fourth tournament win on 10 July and an international win on 22 August, which let him make a living from gaming. On 6 October he reported a very big win and saved some of the prize money. His mid-June gaming party had seven attendees, but no next party has been reported. On 21 October he said he felt stressed about tough competitors and was practicing for his next tournament. On 25 October he said he took his two turtles for a walk and described their diet as vegetables, fruits, and insects, with a special love for strawberries. Some of his photo captions in that session do not match their images, so those images are unreliable. In Session 26 he said he had been helping friends reset high scores at the international tournament.

Food is a strong shared thread. Nate has shared dairy-free recipes, including coconut milk ice cream. On 2 May Joanna shared a dairy-free vanilla cake, crediting his advice. On 5 September she shared dairy-free chocolate coconut cupcakes, and on 6 October she shared a raspberry tart photo. Her favorite dairy-free treat is a chocolate raspberry tart with an almond flour crust. On 4 November Nate invited her to try his lactose-free coconut milk ice cream, and Joanna agreed to visit on 5 November, saying she would bring recipes to share.

Recommendations have gone both ways. On 21 April Nate recommended a fantasy and sci-fi book series, and on 2 May Joanna said she loved "The Lord of the Rings" trilogy at his suggestion. On 6 October Nate said he loved "Little Women," which Joanna had recommended. On 22 August Joanna asked for relaxing fantasy series, and Nate recommended one; she asked him to report back. On 12 May Joanna invited Nate to hike trails near her town, but no date has been set.

Open threads include the hiking trip, the film contest result, the writing gig result, the producer meetings, the third screenplay, the Woodhaven-inspired script, the first book's next steps, the writing convention, Nate's next tournament and party, his winnings, the screenplay shown on 23 October and its title, the Tilly photo discrepancy, the book recommendations, Joanna's movie request, the classic movie's name, and the 5 November visit and dessert.

Deborah and Jolene have chatted regularly since first meeting on 23 January 2023, supporting each other through grief, work stress, and self-care. Sessions 18 to 21 took place on 16, 19, 21, and 24 August 2023, Session 22 on 26 August, Session 23 on 30 August, Session 24 on 3 September, Session 25 on 6 September, Session 26 on 8 September, and Session 27 on 12 September 2023.

Deborah is a yoga teacher who lost her mother years before they met, and her father died suddenly around 25 January 2023. She sits on the bench by the window where her mother used to read, and she found comfort in a garden of roses and dahlias after her friend Karlie died in mid-February. On 1 August she began a community cleanup project and has been fundraising for it. She has two cats, Max and Luna. In Session 23 she shared a photo of her husband, the first mention of one. She called her yoga friends her second family, and in Session 27 she described a card game about cats, where players take cards one by one from a deck and then attack their opponent with them. She said they would play it with Jolene.

Jolene is an electrical engineer who lost her mother in 2022 and has a similar bench and window at her mother's house. She and her partner, together three years and not married, love console gaming, especially "It Takes Two," and on 17 August she bought him a console. Deborah has suggested swapping some gaming for yoga, which Jolene says has "seriously saved" her.

Work is a recurring theme for Jolene. She proposed a STEM volunteer program in February but never pursued it. On 2 March, overwhelmed by exams, she received Deborah's advice to set smaller goals and use a planner, and Deborah promised her a yellow coffee mug whose arrival is not recorded. Deborah also introduced the Eisenhower Matrix and recommended a few minutes of daily mindful breathing when an internship proved hard to balance. On 1 August a project she had poured enormous work into crashed and she lost everything. Deborah described a breathing-and-grounding flow and promised a tutorial video. On 12 August Jolene said meditation had restored her clarity.

Sessions 18 through 22 traced Jolene's move from strain back toward balance. In Session 18 she struggled to juggle engineering, her relationship, and personal growth, and in Session 19 she planned a schedule for studies and hobbies. By Session 20 she was "really finding [her] zen again." In Session 22 she said she wants to use her engineering talent for renewable solar energy and clean water, and she and her partner planned a meditation retreat together. Session 23 was a lighter photo-based exchange about a recent trip to Rio de Janeiro, where they attended yoga classes, and a nearby pond where she meditates that feels like a restart. Session 24 was a catch-up in which she said she has been focused on studying and her relationship, and is grateful for a partner who encourages her goals. Finals were coming up, and she was considering a trip afterward to recharge. Session 25 was brief and upbeat. She had signed up for a meditation course at a lakeside retreat, called meditation an easy habit that keeps her balanced during studies, and said sunrise glimpses soothe her.

Session 26 turned to practical planning. Jolene and her partner were planning a camping trip to connect with nature and practice yoga. Asked how she manages a busy schedule, Jolene described a routine covering classes, studying, and personal time, with yoga and meditation keeping her balanced. After Monday and Wednesday at 4 fell through because Deborah had plans, they arranged a coffee date for Friday at 5, when Jolene would be sorting books from a bookcase. Deborah asked her to bring interesting books. Since 8 September was a Friday, "next week" most likely means 15 September, though this was not restated and is unconfirmed.

Session 27 was a warm update after a gap in replies. Jolene said that the previous weekend she and her partner had traveled to a meditation retreat in Phuket for a few weeks, where nature, reflection, and a break from engineering helped her find inner peace. A session on releasing expectations and savoring the present stood out to her, and she admitted she often gets so consumed with hitting goals that she forgets to appreciate the journey. She now notices small pleasures like sunlight or good coffee and described "a new level of joy and happiness." Both women spoke of the value of a supportive community, and Jolene said she looks forward to meeting Deborah and playing the card game. Jolene did not mention the coffee date, so it is presumed to still be on.

Open threads include the yellow mug, the STEM volunteer program, the Eisenhower Matrix, daily mindful breathing, swapping gaming for yoga, the lake dock visit, Deborah's tutorial video, the post-finals trip, the sunrise they hope to watch together, the camping trip, the coffee date, the card game, and rescheduling the cancelled yoga getaway. Whether Jolene has started a regular mindfulness practice looks answered.

On 9 August James took his three dogs to a beach and met Samantha, who gave him her number; the outcome of his planned 11 August call is unknown. He said Civilization and Total War inspired him, and that balancing took trial and error. His takeaways were perseverance, patience, and the value of feedback. John said he was teaching his siblings to code. Near the end, John said he was going through difficult times and valued James's friendship; James offered to listen whenever John wanted to vent.

He said the recent days had brought good and bad moments, but he was happy with her. James invited John to a baseball game with Samantha the following Sunday, likely 11 September, and John agreed. Deborah and Jolene have chatted regularly since they first met on 23 January 2023, supporting each other through grief, work stress, and self-care. Sessions 18 to 21 took place on 16, 19, 21, and 24 August 2023, followed by Session 22 on 26 August, Session 23 on 30 August, Session 24 on 3 September, Session 25 on 6 September, Session 26 on 8 September, Session 27 on 12 September, and Session 28 on 15 September.

Deborah is a yoga teacher who lost her mother years before they met, and her father died suddenly around 25 January 2023. She sits on the bench by the window where her mother used to read, and she found comfort in a garden of roses and dahlias after her friend Karlie died in mid-February. On 1 August she began a community cleanup project and has been fundraising for it. She has two cats, Max and Luna, and a husband, first mentioned in Session 23. She calls her yoga friends her second family and described a cat-themed card game she hopes to play with Jolene.

Jolene is an electrical engineer who lost her mother in 2022 and has a similar bench and window at her mother's house. She and her partner, together three years and not married, love console gaming, especially "It Takes Two," and on 17 August she bought him a console. Deborah suggested swapping some gaming for yoga, which Jolene says has "seriously saved" her.

Work is a recurring theme. Jolene proposed a STEM volunteer program in February but never pursued it. On 2 March, overwhelmed by exams, she received Deborah's advice to set smaller goals and use a planner, and Deborah promised a yellow coffee mug whose arrival is not recorded. Deborah also introduced the Eisenhower Matrix and recommended daily mindful breathing. On 1 August a project Jolene had poured enormous work into crashed and she lost everything. Deborah promised a tutorial video for a breathing-and-grounding flow, and on 12 August Jolene said meditation had restored her clarity.

Sessions 18 through 22 traced Jolene's move from strain back toward balance. In Session 18 she struggled to juggle engineering, her relationship, and personal growth, and by Session 20 she was "really finding [her] zen again." In Session 22 she said she wants to use her engineering talent for renewable solar energy and clean water, and she and her partner planned a meditation retreat together. Session 23 was a photo exchange about a Rio de Janeiro trip that included yoga classes. In Session 24 she was focused on studying, with finals coming up and a post-finals trip under consideration. Session 25 was brief: she had signed up for a lakeside meditation course and said sunrise glimpses soothe her.

Session 26 turned to planning. Jolene and her partner were preparing a camping trip to connect with nature and practice yoga, and she described yoga and meditation as keeping her balanced during a busy routine. After Monday and Wednesday at 4 fell through, they arranged a coffee date for Friday at 5, when Jolene would be sorting books from a bookcase, and Deborah asked her to bring interesting books. Since 8 September was a Friday, that date is most likely 15 September, though this was never restated.

Session 27 was a warm update. Jolene said that she and her partner had spent a few weeks at a meditation retreat in Phuket, where she found inner peace. She admitted she often gets so consumed with goals that she forgets to appreciate the journey, and she now notices small pleasures like sunlight or good coffee. Both women valued supportive community, and she looked forward to meeting Deborah and playing the card game.

Session 28 on 15 September was a chatty, photo-driven exchange. Deborah said she had reconnected with her late mother's old friends, whose stories made her tear up, and that she spent the day reminiscing over her mother's photos. She also said she married on a beach where she discovered surfing. Jolene described a serene yoga space at home with candles and oils, said she and her partner had tried a flower-based meditation in Thailand, and called her bedroom her "little haven" for rest. She introduced her pet snake, Susie, whom she has had for two years, the first mention of a pet of hers. Jolene did not mention the coffee date, so it is presumed still on, though this remains unconfirmed.

Open threads include the yellow mug, the STEM volunteer program, the Eisenhower Matrix, daily mindful breathing, swapping gaming for yoga, the lake dock visit, Deborah's tutorial video, the post-finals trip, the sunrise they hope to watch together, the camping trip, the coffee date, the card game, and rescheduling the cancelled yoga getaway. Whether Jolene has a regular mindfulness practice looks answered, since she describes yoga and meditation as an established part of her routine.
